title: canon geo: artifact must carry everything a visual evidence card needs
description:
Canon does NOT render the card. Canon's job is that the ARTIFACT CARRIES ENOUGH, LOSSLESSLY, for a renderer outside canon to draw the decision WITHOUT A SECOND QUERY. If the renderer has to go back to the warehouse for geometry or for the rejected candidates, reproducibility is gone and the card stops being evidence.

DRIVER: operator 2026-08-14 called this a particularly important visual use case for OC-0048. Working mock built against a real case (237 Park Avenue, Manhattan): a ROOFTOP geocode that lands inside TWO genuine MapPLUTO lots, BBL 1012920026 (237 Park) and 1012920001 (245 Park), both ST_CONTAINS true. Geometry scores them identically and must abstain; the address channel breaks the tie. 157 five-borough CMBS points fall in more than one lot, max 4.

== WHAT THE ARTIFACT MUST CARRY (the actual requirements the mock exposed) ==

1. THE REJECTED CANDIDATES, WITH THEIR EVIDENCE. This is the big one. A card that
   shows only the winner is not evidence, it is an assertion. The 237 Park card is
   only persuasive because you can see 245 Park scored, and see WHY it lost. If the
   edge artifact retains only promoted edges, the card cannot be drawn. Verify what
   the current entity artifacts retain for losing pairs and extend if they drop them.

2. GEOMETRY RESOLVABLE FROM THE PINNED TILE DIGEST. The card renders from the same
   content-addressed tile that produced the decision (bd-1uld), so re-rendering a
   2019 decision yields 2019 geometry. This turns the bitemporal requirement into a
   visual guarantee. Rendering must never require a live warehouse call.

3. PER-OPERATOR EVIDENCE WITH LANE. Already the shape of EdgeEvidenceHit
   (operator_id, reason_code, score_units, lane, hard_cannot_link, explanation).
   The three lanes render as three distinct visual registers -- Support contributes
   to the total, AntiMerge is a veto shown separately, RelationHint shapes the typed
   output. Do not collapse lanes into one number for display convenience.

4. ABSTENTION AS AN EXPLICIT STATE, NOT AN ABSENT ROW. The card must be able to
   render 'canon declined to decide, and here is the tie it could not break'. That
   is a first-class visual, and it is the OC-0048 success criterion.

5. TILE IDENTITY AND THE HALO FLAG. Which cell anchored the decision, and whether
   the candidate sat in the halo, so the card can show why a neighbouring decision
   was discarded.

6. MULTI-CONTAINMENT CARDINALITY. How many lots contained the point, not just which
   one won. See bd-bmee.

== NON-GOALS ==
Canon does not ship a renderer, a web surface, or a map library. No geometry drawing
code in core. The deliverable is an artifact contract plus a documented worked example
that a separate renderer consumes.

== EXIT CRITERIA ==
- A written artifact contract listing exactly the fields a renderer needs
- Losing-candidate retention verified or implemented
- One fixture artifact for a real multi-lot case, sufficient to draw the card offline
- Confirmation that no field requires a live query to resolve

RELATED: bd-g3mw (evidence waterfall) is the non-spatial half of the same card and is
already scoped. bd-2jfj (evidence-signature grouping) is what makes visual review
affordable -- one card per PATTERN instead of per pair. This bead is separable from the
deferred workbench review orchestration: a renderer over an artifact can exist first.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
REALITY CHECK 2026-08-14 — REQUIREMENT 1 IS ALREADY SATISFIED. VERIFIED BY RUNNING THE
PIPELINE. THIS BEAD JUST GOT SUBSTANTIALLY CHEAPER.

REQUIREMENT 1 (THE REJECTED CANDIDATES, WITH THEIR EVIDENCE) — VERIFIED PRESENT.
This bead says "This is the big one ... Verify what the current entity artifacts retain
for losing pairs and extend if they drop them." Verified by executing
`canon entity run` against tests/fixtures/entity/cmbs/small_book/observations.csv:

  15 rows -> 14 surfaces -> 23 candidate pairs -> 23 EVIDENCE RECORDS

Every candidate pair produces an EdgeEvidenceRecord in evidence/evidence.jsonl,
INCLUDING pairs that score zero. Each carries left/right surface ids, pair_score_total,
score_breakdown with per-lane contributions and top_contributors, has_hard_cannot_link,
and a hits[] array where each hit has lane, namespace, operator_id, reason_code,
score_units, hard_cannot_link, explanation.

CONCLUSION: losing-candidate retention needs NO new machinery. Requirement 1 becomes a
CONTRACT-DOCUMENTATION task (state which artifact the renderer reads and pin its
version), not an implementation task. Retarget the effort saved at requirements 2 and 4.

REQUIREMENT 3 (PER-OPERATOR EVIDENCE WITH LANE) — SHAPE CONFIRMED, WITH ONE DEFECT.
EdgeEvidenceHit has exactly the fields this bead describes. The defect: existing
operators put their SEMANTICS IN A PROSE STRING. Observed verbatim from a real run:
  "explanation": "Candidate pair retained for review: 24 HOUR FITNESS USA, INC. <> 24 HR
   Fitness"
and in relation.rs:
  "relation hint relation={} left={} right={} handoff=review_and_ontology score_units={}"
A renderer would have to PARSE PROSE to recover the relation type or the compared values.
REQUIREMENT ADDED: geo operators must emit TYPED fields — measured value, threshold,
units, comparison outcome, and for spatial operators the geometry refs — alongside the
human explanation. The explanation is for humans; the card must not depend on it. This is
now also an exit criterion on bd-gs6n and bd-3soj.

REQUIREMENT 2 (GEOMETRY FROM THE PINNED TILE DIGEST) — UNCHANGED AND NOW HARDER.
Under BYOP (operator decision 2026-08-14, see bd-2kjx) there are TWO geometry sources:
our content-addressed tile and the client's licensed parcel layer. The card must render
both. Our side is digest-pinned. The client's side needs an equivalent pin — a content
digest of their supplied layer, recorded at run time — or a 2019 re-render silently uses
2026 client geometry and the bitemporal guarantee is a lie for half the drawing.
REQUIREMENT ADDED: the artifact records a content digest for EVERY geometry source,
including client-supplied ones.

NEW REQUIREMENT 7 — THE LICENSE BOUNDARY. This is the one BYOP genuinely creates.
Requirement 2 puts geometry at decision fidelity in the artifact. Under BYOP that
geometry includes the client's LICENSED parcel polygons (ATTOM/Regrid/LightBox). So the
artifact is license-encumbered and CANNOT round-trip to us. Consequences that must be
designed for, not discovered:
  - We cannot debug a client's run by asking for the artifact.
  - We cannot score a client's results centrally.
  - bd-2jfj's evidence-signature review CANNOT BE A HOSTED SERVICE for licensed layers;
    it must run locally or operate on a redacted projection.
  - "One card per pattern" review economics must work with the card rendered client-side.
REQUIRED: a declared redaction boundary — which artifact fields are license-encumbered,
which are safe to share (evidence scores, operator ids, reason codes, abstention states,
tile ids, and OUR geometry are all safe; client geometry and client row values are not) —
and a `canon geo redact` projection that produces the shareable subset while preserving
content-addressing integrity. This is cut as its own bead; this bead owns the field-level
classification.

NEW REQUIREMENT 8 — COVERAGE STATE ON THE CARD. Requirement 4 (abstention as an explicit
state) must distinguish the two abstention causes BYOP creates: "canon declined to decide
between these candidates" versus "the client's layer does not cover this tile, so there
were no parcel candidates at all." These render completely differently — one shows a tie,
the other shows an empty layer — and conflating them is the silent-error mode OC-0048
forbids. See the coverage-abstention bead.

EXIT CRITERIA — AMENDED:
- Written artifact contract listing exactly the fields a renderer needs, naming the
  artifact and pinning its version
- Losing-candidate retention CONFIRMED (done — document it, do not rebuild it)
- Typed operator evidence fields, not prose-parsed
- Content digest per geometry source, including client-supplied
- Field-level license classification (encumbered vs shareable)
- Coverage state distinguishable from decision abstention on the card
- One fixture artifact for a real multi-lot case (237 Park Avenue), sufficient to draw
  the card offline
- One fixture artifact for a BYOP partial-coverage case
- Confirmation that no field requires a live query to resolve

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
ARCHITECTURE SUPERSEDED 2026-08-15 — see docs/PLAN_CANON_GEO.md.

An adversarial multi-model design session produced a materially different architecture,
which then survived a red team that destroyed two intermediate designs. The tile is modelled
as a BOUNDED UNIVERSE and every piece of evidence is a CONSTRAINT; propagation runs to a
fixpoint; the residual model set IS the answer. There is no proposer channel.

THE THREE PROPERTIES THAT MATTER:
- CONFLUENCE. The fixpoint is independent of the order constraints are applied (Tarski 1955;
  Cousot & Cousot 1977; Apt 1999), so determinism is a theorem rather than an engineering
  effort.
- MONOTONICITY. Constraints only add and domains only shrink, so a tile resolved with four
  sources today and six next year yields a TIGHTER residual, never a contradicting one. The
  earlier answer was never wrong, only less resolved.
- STRUCTURAL ABSTENTION. The residual model set is the answer. No threshold anywhere.

THE KEY DESIGN RULE IS rho, THE SOUNDNESS DISCIPLINE. Every source attribute enters the
solver only through a declared versioned relaxation mapping it to the WEAKEST constraint the
source can actually support. An interpolated geocode becomes a 150m disc rather than a
location. A parcel ADDRESS becomes "one of this lot's addresses" rather than functional
equality. OWNERNAME equal PERMITS an assemblage; OWNERNAME different constrains NOTHING.
Every noisy channel is admitted only in its sound direction — which is what dissolved the
proposer dilemma that broke the two earlier designs.

AND THE COMMERCIAL CONSEQUENCE: if every rho is sound, the true assignment is in the model
set, so AN EMPTY MODEL SET IS A PROOF that a named source violated its own published error
model — attributable, falsifiable, and mailable to the vendor.

Read PLAN_CANON_GEO.md before starting any geo work. Section 11 carries the bead-by-bead
supersession table. Appendix A covers frozen-weight observers and imagery sources. APPENDIX
B RECORDS THE FIRST HARD MEASUREMENT, WHICH FALSIFIED A LOAD-BEARING CLAIM — read it before
trusting any performance number in the plan.

Raw session artifacts, including the red team and the adversarial reviews, are preserved
under docs/geo_design_session/ with a reading guide.

comments.text:
== 2026-09-02 STAGE SPEC (PLAN_CANON_GEO.md §19.3, §19.4, §19.6, §19.9 text for PK-D6c so no implementer needs the plan; coverage pass round 1) ==

MODULE SURFACE `src/geo/card.rs` (D6). Field lists are the required minimum; add `#[serde(default)]` fields only. Shared shape: `pub mod card;` and `pub use card::*;`; `GeoCardError { code: GeoCardErrorCode, message, detail }` with the generic variants plus the row below; `CANON_GEO_EVIDENCE_CARD_VERSION`, `canonical_evidence_card_bytes`, `validate_evidence_card_artifact`; schemas/canon.geo.evidence_card.v0.schema.json; a `--describe` entry; `canon geo card`; tests/geo_card.rs. Dependency direction: `card` consumes `explain` and `observer`; nothing consumes `card`.

| Item | Definition |
|---|---|
| Consumes | `GeoCompositionArtifact` (`hard_forced`, `residual_models`, `conflict_constraint_ids`), `GeoEvidenceCompilationArtifact`, `GeoExplanationArtifact`, `GeoImageTilePin`, `GeoTypedGeometry` |
| `GeoEvidenceCard` | `version`, `subject_id`, `ortho_pin: GeoImageTilePin`, `candidate_parcels: Vec<{ id, geometry_blake3 }>`, `forced: GeoCompositionBackbone`, `ambiguous_members: Vec<GeoEntityRef>`, `conflicting_records: Vec<GeoEvidenceRecordRef>`, `composition_blake3`, `evidence_blake3`, `explanation_blake3: Option<String>` |
| `pub fn build_evidence_card(subject_id: &str, composition: &GeoCompositionArtifact, evidence: &GeoEvidenceCompilationArtifact, explanation: Option<&GeoExplanationArtifact>, ortho: &GeoImageTilePin, geometry: &BTreeMap<String, GeoTypedGeometry>) -> Result<GeoEvidenceCard, GeoCardError>` | data only; `ambiguous_members` is the universe minus backbone minus members absent from every residual model |

How the description's requirements map onto the type (nothing is lost): (1) rejected candidates with their evidence: `candidate_parcels` carries every universe member, and `conflicting_records` plus the `evidence_blake3` chain to the compilation artifact's `admissions[]` (which retains every observation, including those that pruned a candidate) so a renderer draws the losers from the same artifact; (2) geometry resolvable from the pinned tile digest: `candidate_parcels[].geometry_blake3` and `ortho_pin.blake3`, both content-addressed, plus an additive `#[serde(default)] geometry_source_pins: Vec<GeoSourceReleasePin>` covering client-supplied (BYOP) layers so a 2019 re-render cannot silently use 2026 client geometry; (3) per-operator evidence with lane: reached through `evidence_blake3` (typed fields on `GeoEvidenceAdmission`, not prose); (4) abstention as an explicit state: `ambiguous_members` nonempty with `forced` present is the "declined to decide" visual, `conflicting_records` nonempty with `explanation_blake3` is the conflict visual; (5) tile identity and halo flag: additive `#[serde(default)] home_cell: Option<String>` and `halo_members: Vec<GeoEntityRef>`; (6) multi-containment cardinality: `candidate_parcels.len()`; (7) license boundary: the card carries digests, never client geometry bytes, and bd-pq5w's `canon geo redact` projection reads the card; (8) coverage state: additive `#[serde(default)] reach: GeoCandidateReachStatus` and `reach_none_reason: Option<String>` so "no candidates because the layer does not cover the tile" renders differently from a tie.

ERROR CODE (§19.4): | `card_artifact_mismatch` | `card::build_evidence_card` | composition, evidence, and explanation digests do not reference one another | refusal | T24 |. `detail["composition_blake3"]`, `detail["evidence_blake3"]`, `detail["explanation_evidence_blake3"]` carry all digests.

CONTRACT C21: `build_evidence_card` refuses when the composition, evidence, and explanation digests do not reference one another; `ambiguous_members` is the universe minus the backbone minus members absent from every residual model. C22, C23 (fixture-derived cards carry `fixture.` pins), C25 apply. THREAT TH22: fabricated sets, a card emitted without the composition and evidence artifacts that justify it, or with digests that do not chain; mitigation card digests must reference one another; covered by C21, T24, `card_artifact_mismatch`.

TESTS (§19.6): | T24 | D6 | unit | Demo 0 `solve.json` as composition, Demo 0 `evidence-compilation.json` as evidence, and an explanation artifact whose `evidence_blake3` is the digest of `negative-hard-chimera.json` instead | `build_evidence_card` returns `Err` code `card_artifact_mismatch` with `detail["evidence_blake3"]` naming both digests | with the explanation's `evidence_blake3` matching: `Ok`, `forced.parcels` equals the six case 4 parcels, `ambiguous_members.is_empty()`, `composition_blake3` equals the `solve.json` digest | C21; TH22 | `card_artifact_mismatch` |. | T26 | D3, D6 | adversarial | every artifact written by `scripts/geo_demo/demo0.sh` | `evidence-compilation.json`: every `admissions[].contract.source_dataset` starts with `fixture.`; no Demo 0 artifact is read by `frozen_e4_h7_gate()` or by any G-gate test; a card built from Demo 0 carries `ortho_pin` and `geometry_source_pins` beginning `fixture.` | a card from fixture input whose pins are relabeled to a live dataset name fails `validate_evidence_card_artifact` | C23; TH20 | none |. Required additional cases (bead-defined): (a) the ambiguous case: Demo 0 case 6 shape (parcel singleton, building doubleton) yields `ambiguous_members` equal to the two BINs and `forced.parcels` of length 1; (b) the reach-none case: `reach == None` yields `candidate_parcels.is_empty()`, `reach_none_reason.is_some()`, and no `forced` member, distinct from (a); (c) the 237 Park Avenue fixture (BBL 1012920026 and 1012920001, both containing the rooftop point) is committed as tests/fixtures/geo/card_237_park.json and yields `candidate_parcels.len() == 2` with `ambiguous_members.len() == 2` when the address channel is not admitted.
T27: file, line, literal.

LOGGING: every test logs `subject_id`, the three digests supplied and the digests each artifact references, `candidate_parcels` ids with geometry digests, `forced.parcels` and `forced.buildings`, `ambiguous_members`, `conflicting_records` ids, `reach`, and the pin `source_dataset` values; on refusal the code and the full `detail` map.

E2E script scripts/geo_demo/e2e_card.sh (`set -euo pipefail`; logs each command, exit code, artifact BLAKE3 into <work-dir>/run.log): (1) `bash scripts/geo_demo/demo0.sh --work-dir <dir>`; `bash scripts/geo_demo/e2e_explain.sh --work-dir <dir>` (bd-o0co); (2) `canon geo card --subject case_4 --composition <dir>/solve.json --evidence <dir>/evidence-compilation.json --explanation <dir>/explanation.json --ortho tests/fixtures/geo/fixture_pin_cc_by.json --geometry <dir>/geometry.json --emit json > <dir>/card.json`; `jq -e '(.forced.parcels | length) == 6 and (.ambiguous_members | length) == 0 and (.ortho_pin.license_id | startswith("fixture.") | not) and (.composition_blake3 | length) == 64'`; log the card summary; (3) scratch explanation with a foreign `evidence_blake3`: assert nonzero exit with `card_artifact_mismatch`; (4) `cargo test --test geo_card -- --nocapture`; `cargo test --test geo_schemas evidence_card_schema_matches_a_real_instance`; the §19.7 jq pin for `evidence_card`; the --describe check for `geo card`; the T27 `rg` line on src/geo/card.rs; whole-tree gates. (5) G6 clause "card artifact validates" (live): build one card per D1 cohort subject in the bd-2g4z population using the real NYC ortho pin and the bd-3ufk count rows; `canon geo card validate` over every card; post the count validated with the denominator.

RESERVATIONS (thread bd-101v): src/geo/card.rs, tests/geo_card.rs, tests/fixtures/geo/card_237_park.json, schemas/canon.geo.evidence_card.v0.schema.json, scripts/geo_demo/e2e_card.sh. Shared append-only touch points, reserve for the edit only: src/geo/mod.rs, src/geo/cli.rs (`geo card`, `geo card validate`), src/operator.rs, tests/geo_schemas.rs, the T27 scan list.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
== HONEST CREDIT (round 3: reward-hacking resistance, proof classes; PK-D6c evidence card, G6 third clause) ==

Cheapest false close: a card built from a composition artifact alone, with rendering code in card.rs and the Demo 0 card cited for "card artifact validates". Exploit / guard pairs:

(1) Gate self-weakening. EXPLOIT: build the card without checking that the three digests reference one another. GUARD (in bead): C21, T24 card_artifact_mismatch naming both digests. ADDED: validate_evidence_card_artifact also refuses when candidate_parcels contains an id absent from the composition universe, or when a forced member is absent from candidate_parcels (a card cannot show a winner it never showed as a candidate).

(11) Dependency smuggling / non-goal. EXPLOIT: PNG drawing or a map library in card.rs. GUARD: the card is data, not rendering; ADDED: the T27 line on card.rs also matches image, png, svg, and tiff crate symbols (same list as bd-35zz T33).

(2) Proof-class inflation. EXPLOIT: cite the Demo 0 card as the G6 clause. GUARD (in bead): T26 fixture. pins; the live clause is one card per bd-2g4z population subject with the real NYC pin and bd-3ufk rows, validated count over the population count.

(5) Tautological tests. GUARD (in bead): (a) case 6 two ambiguous BINs, (b) reach None empty candidates with a reason, (c) 237 Park two candidates. Note on the e2e jq: `(.ortho_pin.license_id | startswith("fixture.") | not)` asserts the license id is a real license id (cc_by_4_0) even on a fixture pin; the fixture marker is on source_dataset, not on license_id, so the assertion is consistent with C23.

(8) Scope-splitting. The redact projection (bd-pq5w) and review export (bd-2jfj) consume the card; they are not slices of it.

(12) Demo-path hard-coding. GUARD: T27.

PROOF CLASS (N07, C23): T24, T26, (a) to (c) are fixture; the 237 Park fixture is a fixture-labeled retained case; live cards over the population inherit the class of the composition and evidence artifacts (retained, derived from observed_snapshot) and the NYC pin (retained). May be cited as "cards validated n/n"; may NOT be cited as a characterization or accuracy.

USER VALUE: a reviewer or a buyer receives one artifact per loan from which a renderer draws the ortho, every candidate parcel including the losers, the forced set, the contested set, the conflicting source records, and the coverage state, without a second query, so the picture that justifies a ledger row is the same bytes the decision was made from. OUTPUT CONTRACT: the additive fields already listed (geometry_source_pins, home_cell, halo_members, reach, reach_none_reason) cover requirements 1 to 8; ADDED (additive): `subject_ref` (accession, loan_id) and `truth_plane` copied from the ledger row so the card joins to P1 without the run manifest.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
== RESOLUTION (round 4) ==

(1) C21 VERSUS THE E2E: comment 4's e2e step 2 builds the card for the resolved case 4 `solve.json` with `--explanation <dir>/explanation.json`, but e2e_explain.sh (bd-o0co) produces that explanation for the chimera CONFLICT request, and C21 refuses when the digests do not reference one another. CONTROLS: C21, defined exactly: `explanation.evidence_blake3 == BLAKE3(canonical evidence artifact)` AND `explanation.request_blake3 == composition.request_blake3`. A card with `explanation: None` is valid (explanation_blake3 None) and is the shape for every Resolved or Ambiguous subject, because explanation_not_conflict means no explanation exists for them. e2e step 2 therefore runs case 4 WITHOUT --explanation and asserts `.explanation_blake3 == null`; a new step 2b runs `canon geo solve --request <dir>/negative-hard-chimera-composition.json` and builds the chimera card with the chimera explanation, asserting `conflicting_records` nonempty and `explanation_blake3` set (the conflict visual). Step 3's foreign-evidence mismatch stays as the T24 negative.

(2) FIXTURE MARKER: the marker is `ortho_pin.source_dataset` (added to GeoImageTilePin by bd-ci1n's round-4 resolution), which is what comment 6 already says. T26's card clause reads "ortho_pin.source_dataset and geometry_source_pins[].source_dataset begin fixture."; the jq on license_id stays as the check that a license id is never used as the marker.

(3) Comment 6's added validate_evidence_card_artifact refusals (a candidate id absent from the composition universe; a forced member absent from candidate_parcels) use code `card_artifact_mismatch` with detail["member"], and are T24 halves (d) and (e) so the T table carries them.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
== TREE RECONCILIATION (round 5) ==

Verified: GeoCompositionArtifact hard_forced, residual_models, conflict_constraint_ids (src/geo/composition.rs:448-476); GeoTypedGeometry (src/geo/geometry_value.rs:211-223) with canonical_geometry_bytes (612) for geometry_blake3; GeoCompositionBackbone { parcels, buildings } (290); Demo 0 solve.json is solved from evidence-compilation.json and carries evidence_compilation.blake3 (demo summary payload_blake3_source = solve.evidence_compilation.blake3); bd-pq5w, bd-2jfj, bd-g3mw, bd-1uld exist.

MISMATCH 1 (round 4 item 1, C21 definition). CLAIM: "explanation.request_blake3 == composition.request_blake3". title: [CANON-V1/P06.12] Map arbitrary source schemas into observations and relationship facts
description:
## Background
Tables, disclosures, APIs, vendor files, and internal models all encode entity surfaces and roles differently. Canon needs declarative intake without learning each source's vocabulary.

## Technical Approach
Define a source-mapping package for CSV/TSV/JSONL/Parquet-style records: object IDs, raw entity surfaces, namespace-qualified anchors, context fields, typed subjects, roles/relationships, intervals, source locators, null/error policy, and profile selection. Parsing emits observations/facts only; identity decisions happen later.

## Success Criteria
- A new source shape is supported by a package and generic reader, not a custom CLI branch.
- Parsing, identity, and relationship assignment produce distinct artifacts.
- Unknown fields/roles and ambiguous cells are preserved or quarantined under declared policy.
- All outputs trace to source row/record and mapping digest.

## Test Plan
Use unrelated neutral schemas with nested/multi-value fields, amendments, missing columns, encoding noise, unknown roles, schema drift, and large streaming inputs. Verify no identity inference during parse.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/extensions/source_mapping.rs`
- `schemas/canon.source.mapping.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/extensions_source_mapping.rs`

## Considerations
Format-specific generic readers may live in Canon; actual source semantics remain external configuration or adapters.
notes:
## Demanding-deployment requirement ownership
Owns the source-mapping side of R2 and R5. Arbitrary source rows must map into separate observations, assignments, and relationships with source timestamp, validity/as-of context, and provenance. Renames and new spellings accrete as temporal aliases after resolution; mapping must not collapse history into the current name.

title: [CANON-V1/P08] Signed registry packages, OCI distribution, and concurrency-safe publication
description:
## Background
Registry knowledge should be portable and immutable. Existing S3 wrapper workflows have observed version-chain divergence between operator and Airflow writers. A generic content-addressed package/distribution model is preferable to making the core AWS-specific.

## Scope
Define Canon OCI media types and local package layout; attach audit/gold/strategy/provenance artifacts; implement pack/unpack/verify, publish/pull by digest, signing/trust policies, optimistic concurrency, offline mirrors, and backend boundaries. Evaluate native S3 only as one backend or wrapper outcome within this model.

## Success Criteria
A registry and its proofs can be verified locally, published immutably, pulled by digest, mirrored offline, and promoted without lost updates. Filesystem remains the default and no cloud dependency enters runtime lookup.

## Test Plan
Local OCI registry twins, digest/tag immutability, signature verification, concurrent publisher races, offline backup/restore, corrupted-layer refusals, and package-to-dbt/search replay parity.

title: canon geo: client-layer tile ingest — H3-index the client's licensed geometry inside canon
description:
OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-14: H3 INDEXING OF THE CLIENT'S LAYER HAPPENS IN CANON.

WHY: under bring-your-own-parcel (bd-2kjx) our tiles ship pre-indexed by H3 cell, but the
client's licensed parcel extract (ATTOM / Regrid / LightBox / county open data) does not.
Requiring the client to own H3 tooling to use canon geo defeats the product. Pure-Rust H3
ports exist (h3o) with no C bindings and deterministic behaviour, so canon can do this
itself.

THIS IS THE BOUNDARY WHERE UNTRUSTED, LICENSED, POSSIBLY-MALFORMED THIRD-PARTY GEOMETRY
ENTERS THE SYSTEM. Treat it as a security and correctness boundary, not a convenience
importer.

TASK: a command that takes the client's geometry file and produces a canon-native,
H3-indexed, content-addressed local tile set that composes with our downloaded tiles.

1. INPUT FORMATS. Decide the supported set and refuse everything else explicitly.
   RECOMMEND: GeoJSON and newline-delimited GeoJSON first (universal, text, inspectable);
   then GeoPackage or FlatGeobuf if a real client extract demands it. Shapefile is a
   multi-file format with a legacy encoding minefield — support it only if a paying
   client actually ships one, and if so, require the .prj.
2. CRS HANDLING. The client's extract will often NOT be WGS84 (county data is frequently
   State Plane). Require a declared CRS — from the file where the format carries it, or
   from an explicit flag — and REFUSE on absent or ambiguous CRS. Reproject into the
   canonical regime declared by the predicate-regime bead, and RECORD the transform and
   its library version in the tile provenance so replay reproduces it.
3. H3 ASSIGNMENT. Assign each parcel to cells at the tile resolution. A parcel is not a
   point: specify whether membership is by representative point, by centroid, by full
   cell cover, or by all cells the polygon intersects. RECOMMEND FULL INTERSECTION COVER
   FOR MEMBERSHIP (so a parcel spanning cells is visible in every tile it touches) PLUS A
   SINGLE DETERMINISTIC ANCHOR CELL (for halo reconciliation and mint-once semantics,
   bd-2b9d). Both must be recorded; the anchor rule must be a deterministic property of
   the geometry, never of input order.
4. COVERAGE DERIVATION. This ingest is where the coverage predicate comes from (see the
   coverage-abstention bead). Derive, per cell, whether the client's layer covers it.
   Deriving coverage from "cells containing at least one parcel" is WRONG — a genuinely
   empty covered cell (a park, a water lot) is indistinguishable from an uncovered one.
   Require an explicit coverage extent from the client (a boundary polygon, a county FIPS
   list, or an explicit declaration that the extract is complete for a named area), and
   REFUSE to guess. This is the single most important correctness decision in this bead.
5. VALIDATION AND REFUSAL. Apply the geometry refusal surface from the geometry-typed-
   value bead: self-intersecting rings, unclosed rings, mixed CRS, NaN/Inf, empty
   geometry, vertex budget. Report a validation summary — how many features accepted, how
   many refused, by reason — because a client whose extract is 8% invalid needs to know
   before they interpret their results.
6. VENDOR IDENTIFIER PRESERVATION. Preserve the vendor's own parcel identifier as an
   alias under a role-namespace that states ISSUER AND ROLE distinctly
   (attom:parcel:*, regrid:ll_uuid:*, county:apn:*). Per bd-67wx: a vendor's parcel ID is
   NOT the county's APN, and conflating them produces wrong joins across vendors.
7. MUTUAL-EXCLUSIVITY DECLARATION. The client must declare whether their layer is
   mutually exclusive within itself. It is FALSE for NYC-style condo aggregation (measured:
   a single point inside both a condo unit BBL and its parent lot) and may be true for a
   simple assessor extract. Canon must refuse to assume. Feeds the anti-merge scoping in
   bd-gs6n.
8. LOCAL AND LICENSED. The output stays on the client's machine. It is content-addressed
   like our tiles so decisions are replayable, but see the license-containment bead — it
   must be excludable from anything shared back.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- Ingest command producing content-addressed, H3-indexed local tiles from GeoJSON/NDJSON
- Declared-CRS requirement with refusal, reprojection recorded in provenance
- Membership cover + deterministic anchor cell, both recorded; anchor independent of
  input order
- Explicit coverage extent required; refusal rather than inference from parcel presence
- Validation summary with per-reason refusal counts
- Vendor identifiers preserved as role-and-issuer namespaced aliases
- Mutual-exclusivity declared, never assumed
- Round-trip test: ingest -> tile -> run produces identical decisions across two platforms

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
TILE PRE-STITCHING IS ALREADY UNDER WAY IN cmdrvl-curves, LANDING NOW 2026-08-14. Verified
by reading the in-progress beads. This confirms the pre-resolved-tile architecture and
supplies hard facts that change several canon geo assumptions.

== WHAT IS ACTUALLY LANDING ==

  cmdrvl-curves bd-30ho   OVERTURE MAPS, release 2026-07-22.0. Themes buildings,
                          building_parts, PLACES, addresses, divisions. Snowflake DDL
                          APPLIED (OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_HOT / _EXT /
                          OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURE_H3_COVERAGE plus 14 per-type views);
                          manifest scan running, 0 rows landed yet.
  cmdrvl-curves bd-1ssr   FEMA USA STRUCTURES, 135,321,228 features nationally. National
                          landing IN PROGRESS; DC / AK / AL complete, AR running.
                          FEMA_USA_STRUCTURES_HOT loaded and read back (DC = 64,701 rows).
  cmdrvl-curves bd-3fyv   MICROSOFT GLOBALML FOOTPRINTS, release 2026-07-24. Landing IN
                          PROGRESS: 179 of 2,415 US files, 5,219,860 rows at 14:45Z.
  cmdrvl-curves bd-11uu   HUD USPS ADDRESS VACANCIES -- **BLOCKED**, and not a tile source.
                          HUD restricts it to registered governmental/non-profit users and
                          the sublicense forbids selling, licensing or distributing the
                          data. DO NOT PLAN ANY CANON GEO CAPABILITY ON IT.

NOTE ON "FOURSQUARE OS PLACES": it arrives as OVERTURE'S PLACES THEME, not a separate
Foursquare landing. That is the POI level in bd-2cbs, and it is in the same table family as
Overture buildings.

== FINDING 1: THE LANDED H3 GRAIN IS r4 / r7 / r8. THERE IS NO r9. ==
All three sources partition by h3_r4 and carry H3_R7 and H3_R8 columns. The epic's default
tile is res-9 and it is NOT precomputed anywhere.

AND THERE IS A CONVENIENT COINCIDENCE WORTH DELIBERATELY EXPLOITING: an r8 cell is
approximately 0.737 km2 -- which is almost exactly the area the epic specifies for its WORK
UNIT (an r9 cell plus k-ring 1 = 7 cells = 0.737 km2). So the already-landed H3_R8 column is
essentially the intended work-unit size.
ACTION FOR bd-2b9d: reconsider r9-plus-k-ring versus r8-plus-k-ring as the work unit, now
that r8 is precomputed across every source and r9 is not. This does not change the
requirement to compute cells in canon with a vetted Rust library -- the Snowflake H3 helper
defects (edgar-elt br-2wir) still stand -- but it does mean the warehouse can prefilter at
r8 for free, and the resolution decision now has a third input alongside node count and
human legibility.

== FINDING 2: POLYGON-TO-CELLS RETURNS EMPTY FOR SMALL BUILDINGS. LIVE, MEASURED. ==
From bd-3fyv: "H3_POLYGON_TO_CELLS alone inserted only 116 coverage rows for 354,804 hot
rows because small buildings often contain no H3 r8 cell centroid." Fixed there by using a
guaranteed CENTROID_H3_R8 plus H3_TRY_POLYGON_TO_CELLS.

THIS IS DIRECTLY THE MEMBERSHIP QUESTION bd-10s2 AND bd-2b9d SPECIFY. At r8 or r9 a
building is much smaller than a cell, so "which cells does this polygon cover" is
degenerate: the standard polygon-to-cells contract returns cells whose CENTRES fall inside
the polygon, and for a building that set is almost always EMPTY.
CONSEQUENCE: membership must be CENTROID-ANCHORED with polygon coverage as a supplement for
the large-feature case (parcels, campuses, complexes), NOT the other way round. My earlier
recommendation on bd-10s2 -- "full intersection cover for membership plus a single
deterministic anchor cell" -- is right in intent but inverted in emphasis, and applying it
naively with polygon_to_cells would have silently produced empty membership for nearly every
building. Correct it there.

== FINDING 3: OUR OWN SOURCES CARRY LICENSE OBLIGATIONS. bd-pq5w IS SCOPED TOO NARROWLY. ==
I framed license containment entirely around the CLIENT's licensed parcel layer. The landed
research shows OUR side has obligations too, and they differ per source:
    Overture buildings, divisions      ODbL-1.0            <-- SHARE-ALIKE
    Overture places                    per-source mix of CDLA-Permissive-2.0, Apache-2.0,
                                       CC0-1.0; source license must be retained
    Overture addresses                 source-specific, incl. NAD Access and Usage License
    FEMA USA Structures                CC-BY-4.0, attribution to ORNL and FEMA Geospatial
                                       Response Office REQUIRED
    Microsoft GlobalML                 CDLA-Permissive-2.0 current release; older vintages
                                       need per-release revalidation
bd-30ho states plainly: "License segmentation by source array is REQUIRED before any derived
product ships. Treat as a build-time gate, not a later cleanup."

ODbL SHARE-ALIKE IS THE COMMERCIAL ISSUE AND IT NEEDS AN OPERATOR DECISION, NOT AN
ENGINEERING ONE. A tile is a derived product. If it mixes ODbL Overture buildings with
everything else, the derived tile may inherit share-alike obligations that are
incompatible with a paid distribution model. Options to evaluate deliberately:
  (a) segregate ODbL-derived features into a separately-licensed layer of the tile, with
      the license class carried per feature -- note OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_EXT ALREADY HAS
      LICENSE_CLASS AND LICENSE_TERMS COLUMNS, so the substrate for this exists;
  (b) build the commercial tile from the permissive sources only (FEMA CC-BY, Microsoft
      CDLA) and treat Overture as an internal enrichment;
  (c) accept share-alike and publish the tile openly.
REQUIRED IN bd-pq5w AND bd-1uld: license class per FEATURE in the tile artifact, and a
declared per-tile license posture that composes our obligations with the client's. The
artifact license boundary now has TWO directions, not one.

== FINDING 4: THE ATTRIBUTE CHANNELS FOR bd-272d ARE REAL, AND ONE IS MODELLED ==
Attribute anchoring needs class, size, floors, year. What is actually arriving:
    FEMA        OCC_CLS, PRIM_OCC (occupancy class), SQFEET, PROP_ADDR, UUID, BUILD_ID
    Overture    building class, height, num_floors, GERS id
    Microsoft   height (subset only), confidence, NO ID
    MapPLUTO    BLDGCLASS, LANDUSE, BLDGAREA, LOTAREA, NUMBLDGS, NUMFLOORS, YEARBUILT
So the six-field client contract has a counterpart on the tile side for every field except
YEAR BUILT, which only MapPLUTO supplies -- meaning year-built anchoring works in NYC and
degrades outside it until a national year source exists. Record that as a known national
limitation rather than discovering it later.

CRITICAL: FEMA OCCUPANCY IS MODELLED, NOT SURVEYED. bd-1ssr requires a provenance flag
"so downstream never treats it as surveyed." Attribute anchoring MUST carry that flag into
the evidence and weight modelled attributes below observed ones. A modelled occupancy class
driving a hard eliminative filter (bd-2zdz's assemblage type filter) would be a silent error
generator -- the filter is HARD, so a wrong modelled class removes the correct candidate
before anything is scored. Use modelled occupancy as SUPPORT evidence, never as a hard
filter, unless corroborated.

== FINDING 5: NO STABLE ID CONFIRMED FOR TWO SOURCES ==
Microsoft has no id at all -- bd-3fyv derives "a deterministic feature hash because no
stable id." Overture ADDRESSES are alpha with no stable GERS id either. This confirms
bd-2cbs rule 4 (alias-less participants) and extends it: the alias-less set is Microsoft
footprints AND Overture addresses, not just Microsoft.
A derived feature hash is NOT an alias and must not be minted into a registry -- it will
change whenever the geometry changes, which violates the tile identifier stability contract
in bd-12gh.

== FINDING 6: OVERTURE ADDRESSES CANNOT BE THE ADDRESS-SET SOURCE ==
bd-30ho: "Addresses theme is ALPHA -- do not build a contract against it yet," no stable
GERS id, multi-source licensing including NAD terms. US count 127,719,691.
So bd-35qg's address-set acquisition is NOT solved by Overture. NYC PAD or the per-BIN
addresses in the landed footprints file (bd-397d) remain the path, and the national story
stays open. Do not let the size of the Overture addresses count create false confidence.

== WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE WORKED-CASE CORPUS (bd-tccn) ==
The corpus can now stage its non-MapPLUTO pulls against REAL TABLE NAMES rather than
placeholders:
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.FEMA_USA_STRUCTURES_HOT              partially loaded (DC, AK, AL)
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.MICROSOFT_GLOBALML_BUILDING_FOOTPRINTS_HOT   partially loaded
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_HOT           DDL applied, 0 rows
    plus the *_FEATURE_H3_COVERAGE tables for each
NEW YORK IS NOT YET LOADED IN ANY OF THE THREE. FEMA is alphabetical by state and is at AR;
Microsoft is 179/2415 files; Overture has not started landing. So the full-tile version of
every case remains blocked, exactly as the corpus bead predicted -- but the blocker is now
a KNOWN COMPLETION DATE rather than an unlanded dataset, and the table names and column
shapes are already fixed enough to write the extraction queries against.

comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-14 — MY MEMBERSHIP RECOMMENDATION IN THIS BEAD IS INVERTED. Applying it
as written would silently produce EMPTY membership for nearly every building.

WHAT THIS BEAD SAYS: "RECOMMEND FULL INTERSECTION COVER FOR MEMBERSHIP (so a parcel spanning
cells is visible in every tile it touches) PLUS A SINGLE DETERMINISTIC ANCHOR CELL."

WHY IT IS WRONG IN PRACTICE: the standard polygon-to-cells contract returns cells whose
CENTRES fall inside the polygon. At r8 or r9 a building is far smaller than a cell, so that
set is almost always EMPTY.

MEASURED LIVE, not theorised — cmdrvl-curves bd-3fyv: "H3_POLYGON_TO_CELLS alone inserted
only 116 coverage rows for 354,804 hot rows because small buildings often contain no H3 r8
cell centroid." Their fix was a guaranteed CENTROID_H3_R8 plus H3_TRY_POLYGON_TO_CELLS.

CORRECTED RECOMMENDATION — THE EMPHASIS INVERTS:
  PRIMARY     CENTROID-ANCHORED membership. Every feature belongs to the cell containing
              its representative point. Reliable for every feature at every size, and it
              doubles as the deterministic anchor cell that halo reconciliation (bd-2b9d)
              needs for mint-once semantics.
  SUPPLEMENT  POLYGON COVERAGE for LARGE features only — parcels, campuses, complexes,
              anything genuinely spanning cells. This is where the original intent was
              right; it is simply the exception rather than the rule.
  REFUSE      a coverage computation that returns empty for a non-empty geometry. That is
              the defect above, and it should surface as a refusal rather than as silently
              absent membership.

The anchor rule must still be a deterministic property of the geometry, never of input
order or of which source supplied the feature.

NOTE FOR THE INGEST CONTRACT: this applies to the CLIENT's layer too. A client parcel
extract will contain both small lots (centroid suffices) and large assemblages (coverage
needed), so the ingest must apply both and record which rule produced each membership row.

title: [CANON-V1/P07.2] Rebase entity cluster and link modes onto shared native stages
description:
## Background
The useful two-tape linkage capability must survive, but a second engine duplicates parsing, candidates, evidence, artifacts, errors, and write-back. Cluster and link are execution shapes over common primitives.

## Technical Approach
Implement shared observation intake, indexes, blocking, evidence operators, budgets, evaluation, artifacts, review, audit, and promotion. Keep typed mode metadata for undirected clustering versus directional cross-dataset linkage and preserve link field correspondence, unmatched/ambiguous semantics, and gold scoring. Expose the final CLI under one entity namespace.

## Success Criteria
- Cluster and link emit one artifact/evidence family and share refusal/no-mutation contracts.
- Existing link fixtures retain decision and metric parity before legacy cutover.
- Mode-specific semantics remain typed rather than hidden in conditional field conventions.
- No strategy, review, audit, apply, or registry-write implementation is duplicated.

## Test Plan
Run frozen entity and old resolve fixtures through both paths, compare artifacts/decisions, then exercise shared operator unit tests and subprocess mode journeys. Log every parity delta.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/entity/run.rs`
- `src/entity/link.rs`
- `src/resolve/mod.rs`
- `tests/entity_link.rs`

## Considerations
Consolidation does not mean forcing directional linkage into transitive clustering. Preserve the semantic distinction inside one engine.

title: [CANON-V1/P03.3] Package strategies with pinned dependencies and reproducible manifests
description:
## Background
A script hash alone does not capture interpreter, dependencies, entrypoint, capabilities, fixtures, schema, or provenance. A champion cannot be safely reused if its execution environment is implicit.

## Technical Approach
Define a content-addressed strategy package with typed manifest, entrypoint digest, runtime contract, exact dependency lock, declared capabilities, fixture corpus hashes, expected audit metrics, provenance, license, and optional signature references. Add deterministic pack, unpack, inspect, and verify operations that share the registry package substrate where possible.

## Success Criteria
- Two equivalent source trees pack to identical bytes and digest.
- Verification detects entrypoint, dependency, fixture, manifest, and path-normalization tampering.
- A strategy can be selected and audited entirely from its pinned package.
- Packages cannot escape their root or smuggle undeclared executables through links or generated paths.

## Test Plan
Golden-test package bytes across reordered files and workspaces; mutate each component; test path traversal, duplicate names, symlink/hard-link edge cases, missing runtimes, and read-only verify.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/strategy/package.rs`
- `schemas/canon.strategy.package.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/strategy_package.rs`

## Considerations
Reuse general package primitives from the registry lane, but retain distinct media types and semantic verification.

title: [CANON-V1/P06.15] Make review semantics and evidence presentation extensible
description:
## Background
Different domains need distinct labels, evidence panels, escalation rules, and relationship choices, while the underlying review actions must remain safe and machine-verifiable.

## Technical Approach
Define review-policy and presentation packages that map opaque ontology/namespace/relation IDs into labels, evidence groups, required rationale, risk tiers, two-person rules, and allowed actions. Generic actions remain same, distinct, related, successor, alias-scope, assignment, new entity, defer, and reject; imports compile to typed patches.

## Success Criteria
- A domain can change presentation and escalation without changing patch semantics.
- No presentation action can convert relation-only evidence into identity implicitly.
- High-risk overrides require declared approvals and remain hash-bound.
- Unknown package IDs render safely as opaque values rather than being dropped.

## Test Plan
Generate/import neutral review packs for conflicting IDs, related-distinct, temporal succession, new entity, assignment, and reviewer disagreement. Test tampering, stale policy, accessibility, offline behavior, and no partial writes.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/extensions/review_policy.rs`
- `schemas/canon.review.policy.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/extensions_review_policy.rs`

## Considerations
Canon owns safe actions and verification; domain packages own labels, contextual panels, and escalation policy.
notes:
## Ownership boundary
bd-14m6 owns the canonical review schema, static renderer, import validator, receipts, and typed patch compilation. This bead owns only extension-package labels, evidence grouping, allowed-action policy, and escalation/approval rules consumed by that infrastructure. Its tests must use the shared renderer/importer and must not create a second HTML template or decision format.

title: [CANON-V1/P11.7] Record privacy-safe performance and quality baselines
description:
## Background
Without durable baseline artifacts, regressions in speed, memory, artifact size, unresolved rates, candidate explosion, or review yield become anecdotes.

## Technical Approach
Define a versioned benchmark/quality result schema with build/tool/hardware/corpus digests, stage timings, peak memory, I/O, candidate/evidence counts, abstention/quality metrics, cache outcomes, and privacy classification. Add deterministic comparison with configurable regression bands and historical trend export. Never record raw identity values by default.

## Success Criteria
- Every benchmark and acceptance journey emits a comparable baseline artifact.
- Comparisons separate corpus/hardware/tool changes from actual performance deltas.
- Sensitive fields are structurally excluded or redacted by policy.
- CI blocks only on evidence-backed stable thresholds and reports noisy/incomparable runs honestly.

## Test Plan
Create improvement/regression/noise/hardware-change/corpus-change fixtures, validate comparison math and redaction, and run repeated benchmark samples to calibrate bands.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/telemetry.rs`
- `schemas/canon.baseline.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/baseline_compare.rs`

## Considerations
Telemetry is local artifact generation, not hosted collection. Canon must not phone home.

title: canon geo: as-of resolution and the tile-refresh identifier stability contract
description:
bd-67wx STATES THE RULE. NOTHING IMPLEMENTS IT. AND BYOP MAKES ID STABILITY A PUBLISHED
CONTRACT RATHER THAN A LOCAL CONCERN.

TWO HALVES.

== HALF 1: AS-OF RESOLUTION ==

bd-67wx rule 5 says "BITEMPORAL. As-of resolution, consistent with OC-0046's no-lookahead
requirement. 'Which cluster did this alias belong to in 2019' must be answerable." That is
a rule with no implementation and no bead. OC-0048 reinforces it: "MapPLUTO version
archive (bd-33t6) is treated as MANDATORY, not optional. BBLs are not stable: mergers,
apportionments and condo declarations change them. A current-only snapshot cannot resolve
a 2017 Annex A whose BBL no longer exists, AND WILL SILENTLY MATCH THE WRONG SUCCESSOR
LOT."

That last clause is the danger and it is a silent-error mode, not a coverage gap. Resolving
a 2017 tape against a 2026 parcel layer does not fail — it succeeds, wrongly, and looks
confident.

REQUIRED:
- Resolution takes an AS-OF date. The tile digest already pins geometry (bd-1uld); this
  bead makes the as-of explicit in the request and the artifact rather than implicit in
  which tile happened to be downloaded.
- Refusal when the requested as-of predates the earliest available tile vintage, rather
  than silently using the earliest.
- The BBL / parcel-identifier CHANGE LEDGER as a consumable input. cmdrvl-curves bd-33t6
  produces it by diffing consecutive MapPLUTO vintages; OC-0048 observes "that ledger is
  arguably worth more than any single vintage." Canon must consume it to answer "this 2017
  BBL became these two BBLs in 2021."
- Under BYOP the same problem applies to the CLIENT's layer, which has its own vintage and
  likely NO change ledger. Require the client to declare their layer's vintage (already in
  the ingest descriptor) and REFUSE to answer as-of queries outside it rather than
  extrapolating.

== HALF 2: TILE-REFRESH IDENTIFIER STABILITY — A PUBLISHED CONTRACT ==

bd-67wx rule 3 says minting is a promotion event, and rule 4 says never reuse, never
silently reassign. Correct — but written for a single local registry. Under BYOP, tile-
shipped cmdrvl:building:* ids are minted at OUR promotion, at tile build time, BEFORE ANY
CLIENT RUN. Every client registry aliases into them.

IF A TILE REFRESH REASSIGNS AN ID, EVERY CLIENT REGISTRY BREAKS SILENTLY — their alias now
points at a different building, and nothing in their pipeline notices.

REQUIRED — a published tile identifier contract:
  MAY   add new clusters
  MAY   retire a cluster WITH A TOMBSTONE, so stale references fail loudly (bd-67wx rule 4)
  MAY   split a cluster, retiring the prior id with a tombstone that names the successors
  MAY   merge clusters, retaining both prior ids as aliases pointing at the survivor
  NEVER reassign an existing minted id to different geometry
  NEVER reuse a retired id

REQUIRED — a CONFORMANCE TEST that diffs consecutive tile vintages and FAILS on
reassignment. This is the same diff shape as the MapPLUTO version-archive work
(cmdrvl-curves bd-33t6), and it is the thing that makes the contract real rather than
aspirational. Without an automated gate, a refresh pipeline will violate it within a year
and nobody will find out until a client's exposure report is wrong.

REQUIRED — a client-side detection path: on tile refresh, the client can ask "which of my
aliases now point at tombstoned or changed clusters" and get a typed answer. A contract
the client cannot verify is not a contract.

NOTE ON REUSE: canon already has the right machinery — entity/patches.rs and
anti_merge.rs exist for exactly this class of correction, and bd-67wx rule 4 names them.
Reuse them; do not build a parallel tombstone mechanism.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- As-of parameter on geo resolution, carried into the artifact, with refusal outside the
  available vintage range for BOTH our tiles and the client's declared layer
- Parcel-identifier change ledger consumed, with a worked case: a 2017 BBL that split
- Published tile identifier contract, written
- Automated vintage-diff conformance gate that fails on reassignment or id reuse
- Client-side tombstone/change detection command
- A no-lookahead test: resolving an as-of-2017 request must not use any fact dated after
  2017, consistent with OC-0046

title: canon geo discovery handoff — protocol-neutral catalog/acquisition requests and verified receipts
description:
WHY

A source-generic engine still needs an efficient way for an agent to discover what a region offers and obtain bounded inputs. Canon must make that handoff precise without embedding Reveal MCP, Snowflake, S3, HTTP, credentials, or vendor clients inside the deterministic build.

DELIVER

Implement canon_geo_discovery_request.v0, canon_geo_acquisition_request.v0, and canon_geo_acquisition_receipt.v0 as protocol-neutral contracts consumed and emitted by the planner/run manifest.

A discovery request names required evidence classes/entity levels, geography, as-of/release policy, minimum fields and semantics, coverage question, and metadata/result byte ceilings. An acquisition request pins the chosen source instance/release, spatial subset, projection, columns, row/byte ceilings, ordering/pagination contract, and required receipt fields.

External executors may use Reveal catalog discovery, cmdrvl-data/Snowflake, S3, local files, or future services. Canon validates returned local artifacts and receipts but never holds credentials or reaches the network.

Receipts preserve executor/tool identity, source release, normalized executed request or query digest, query/request id, bounded subset, pagination state, row count, declared denominator, result/source digests, observed bytes, proof class, and terminal state such as COMPLETE, ZERO_ROWS, TIMEOUT, CANCELED, PARTIAL, or UNREADABLE_COLUMNS.

ACCEPTANCE

- The agent can start from an unknown region by requesting metadata/catalog discovery before any data scan.
- Table/list/describe metadata and an actual bounded column read are separate receipt capabilities; metadata count alone cannot prove column readability.
- Requests require explicit release selection and bounded geography before warehouse/data execution.
- Pagination completeness is represented and a truncated key listing cannot silently become complete inventory.
- ZERO_ROWS is a typed finding distinct from inability to execute; a positive-path gate can explicitly require nonzero.
- TIMEOUT/CANCELED/PARTIAL receipts preserve query/request ids and resume/retry guidance without being presented as live success.
- Source/result digests and denominators survive into the regional inventory and run manifest.
- Credentials, connection strings, and secrets never enter artifacts or semantic hashes.
- Fixture, retained, and live proof classes remain distinct.
- Equivalent receipts from different executor protocols normalize into the same source-generic contract where their semantics match.

title: Instrument-grain canon registry: adopt external open ID (FIGI/CUSIP/LEI) where it exists, mint IN-* where it doesn't
description:
Extend Canon to an INSTRUMENT-GRAIN canonical registry (issuer + tranche/lien/type), adopting an
external open ID where one exists and minting a stable Canon ID where it does not.

CONTEXT (operator, 2026-07-10): BDC SOI is the case where "everybody wishes there was an industry ID
for these instruments." Current canon (PLAN_BDC_ENTITY_REGISTRATION.md) mints IC-* at the ISSUER
grain only -- IC- + blake3(normalized_company_name). The user wants instrument grain: "1st lien of
ACME vs equity of ACME" is a multi-column identity (issuer + instrument discriminator), which is the
assignment-vs-identity split (bd-3bst): the ISSUER is the identity, each tranche is a typed assignment
that also deserves a stable ID so cross-quarter continuity + the DealCharts time series (bd-vmh) can
key on it.

EMPIRICAL FINDING (this session): our parsed SOI holdings carry ZERO external identifier columns (no
cusip/isin/figi/lei anywhere in cmdrvl-soi), and DERA XBRL SOI tags a name breadcrumb + numerics, no
CUSIP either. This confirms the canon doc's "80%+ of BDC investments are private -- no CUSIP, no FIGI,
no Bloomberg ticker; the portfolio company name is the only identifier." So at instrument grain these
are NOT in FIGI and cannot even be /mapping-looked-up (no CUSIP to map).

DESIGN (adopt-where-exists, mint-where-absent -- the operator's stated rule):
1. Instrument canon ID = deterministic function of (issuer_canon_id, instrument discriminator:
   lien/seniority + investment_type + maybe maturity/tranche label). blake3-content-addressed like
   IC-*, new prefix (e.g. IN-*). Stable + reviewable, same immutability contract as the slug.
2. EXTERNAL ID ADOPTION: where an open standard ID exists (FIGI/CUSIP/ISIN for the ~20% broadly
   syndicated instruments; LEI for the issuer), store it as an ALIAS/anchor on the registry entry --
   NEVER as the canonical ID (the canonical ID must be stable even when no external ID exists). Reuse
   the OpenFIGI enrichment provider already designed (registry/provider.rs; OpenFIGI API key in .env
   + config.toml; semantic twin in twinning/docs). FIGI eligibility rules gate which investment types
   are worth a lookup (syndicated/unitranche, not private 1st/2nd lien to a private borrower).
3. Because 80%+ have no external ID, CMD+RVL's IN-* namespace effectively BECOMES the missing
   industry ID for private-credit instruments -- provenance-backed (every ID traces to a filing +
   source_page). That is a wedge, not a workaround.

This is the "pull external IDs into the Canon instrument registry" plan the operator asked for.
Relates: canon PLAN_BDC_ENTITY_REGISTRATION.md, bd-3bst (assignment-vs-identity), the R6

title: [CANON-V1] Compile uncertain identity evidence into exact, reusable registries
description:
## Background
Canon already contains the pieces of a category-defining identity compiler: exact versioned lookup, native entity and record-linkage evidence, anti-merge constraints, audit/review/promotion, registry exports, and canonical strategy selection. The program goal is to make those pieces one truthful, executable, domain-neutral open-source product.

The product thesis is: evidence may be plural and uncertain, but promoted canonical knowledge must be deterministic, reviewed, versioned, explainable, distributable, and exactly replayable. Canon must remain a standalone Rust package. It exposes generic extension contracts; an operator's industry vocabularies, identifiers, sources, policies, corpora, and registries remain out-of-tree inputs.

## Program Outcomes
- One artifact-backed entity engine with generic clustering and cross-dataset linkage modes.
- One project compiler that pins inputs, profiles, strategies, registries, gates, outputs, and proofs.
- Registry packages that preserve and strengthen dbt-seed and searchable-index exports.
- Canon strategy retained as typed, safe, canonical procedural knowledge.
- A privacy-aware unresolved inbox and impact-ranked review flywheel.
- Temporal and scoped identity facts compiled into exact as-of snapshots.
- Generic extension contracts for vocabularies, namespaces, profiles, providers, review policies, relationships, and projections.
- Native evidence generation by default; optional external matchers only through a stable evidence boundary.
- Agent, SDK, packaging, benchmark, documentation, and release surfaces generated from the executable contract.

## Open-Source Boundary
Canon contains no industry-specific enums, conditionals, default thresholds, public-source clients, bundled knowledge, or product ontology. A demanding out-of-tree deployment—structured-finance counterparties for the initiating operator—must be expressible entirely through public generic contracts. It may be used as private acceptance evidence, but its vocabulary, source adapters, corpora, and registry data do not become Canon runtime behavior.

## Non-Negotiable Invariants
Core lookup remains exact byte match after ASCII trim. Same inputs and pinned artifacts produce byte-stable outputs. Ambiguity abstains. Hard cannot-link evidence vetoes positive similarity. Relationships and assignments never imply same-as. Promotion requires explicit versioning, current snapshot checks, audit evidence, and mutation-safe writes. Existing dbt-seed and search-index exports remain first-class.

## Success Criteria
All child lanes reach executable acceptance gates; a nontrivial out-of-tree domain deployment succeeds without changes to Canon core; the public CLI and machine contract agree; real subprocess E2E tests execute every advertised command; measured scale replaces virtual-only claims; packages verify and deploy to dbt/search consumers; exact knowledge demonstrably accretes across repeated projects.

## Test and Release Expectations
Every implementation bead includes unit, integration, refusal/no-mutation, determinism, and E2E coverage proportional to risk. The final gate runs fmt, clippy, all tests, real benchmark tiers, contract parity, package verification, offline replay, and cross-platform smoke checks with detailed logs.
notes:
## Feature-preservation firewall
- Exact lookup and row-preserving apply remain the production runtime contract (bd-1hum, bd-5xvd).
- dbt-seed generation is retained and strengthened, not replaced (bd-1m1o).
- searchable SQLite index generation is retained and strengthened, distinct from internal caches (bd-34f3).
- `canon strategy` remains a first-class command family for canonical procedural knowledge (bd-eb9s, bd-1f1o).
- Cross-dataset record linkage survives as generic `canon entity link`; only the duplicate top-level engine/namespace is consolidated after parity (bd-11ai, bd-24l9).
- Native Rust cluster/link/review is the complete default path (bd-wv6j).
- OpenRefine, Splink, and Dedupe integration is intentionally blocked on native acceptance and remains optional, evidence-only, and non-mutating (bd-3ofg through bd-1sf0).

title: canon geo D7: Franklin County deed-grain truth plane, pinned recorder source and truth-scoring input for E5
description:
PACKET PK-D7-truth (stage D7 entry condition) from docs/PLAN_CANON_GEO.md §19.5 row D7 and §18.3 IN list ("E5 in Franklin County with deed-grain truth and the tier curve (bd-s07o)"), minted 2026-09-02 in the coverage pass. §19.5 D7 entry condition: "G1 passed; bd-s07o Franklin parcel plane landed; deed-grain truth source pinned". The parcel plane landed 2026-09-01 (cmdrvl-curves bd-2opq; 494,043 admitted parcels, PIP reach 147/151). The deed-grain truth source had no owner: bd-s07o's comment records "Franklin's available truth is deed-grain rather than a bulk mortgage-amount plane" and nothing pins it. This bead pins it and turns it into a labeled truth plane E5 can score against. It carries the full design so no implementer needs the plan document.

== WHY ==
bd-179b's doctrine: truth must come from evidence that does not come from the address channel, and truth planes are reported separately and never pooled. In NYC that plane is ACRIS (mortgage amount, date, lender against a BBL). Franklin County has no ACRIS; its independent plane is the Recorder's deed and mortgage index keyed by parcel number (the Auditor parcel id the landed plane already carries). A mortgage instrument recorded against a parcel id, matched to a known CMBS loan by amount and recording-date window with uniqueness required and non-unique matches discarded and counted (bd-179b rule), is a deed-grain truth row with no address in the join. Without it the E5 tier curve (G7, T16) has coverage and abstention per tier but no precision column, and the plan forbids publishing precision without an independent truth set.

== SOURCE PIN (acquisition outside Canon; cross-repo landing) ==
The Franklin County Recorder index is landed by cmdrvl-curves (file a cross-link bead there under thread CROSS-E5-DEED with this bead id; the landing pins the bulk download ETag or SHA-256, release date, and license text hash exactly as bd-2opq did for parcels). Until it lands, this bead's Canon-side work runs against a `fixture.` deed index (tests) and the truth plane stays `refusal-only` for live scoring; label the bead `refusal-only` if it must close before the landing, and file the follow-up. Canon consumes: `{ instrument_id, instrument_type (mortgage, deed, release), parcel_ids: Vec<String> (Auditor parcel numbers, one instrument may cover several), recording_date, amount_cents: Option<i64>, lender_party_blake3, borrower_party_blake3, source_release, row_blake3 }` as `canon_geo_deed_index_rows.v0` (additive contract, shared shape, owned by src/geo/evaluation.rs where `GeoTruthPlane` lives; parties are digests, never clear text, matching the H.7 export discipline).

== TRUTH PLANE ==
Add `GeoTruthPlane::DeedGrainInstrument` (additive enum variant; every `match` on the enum in evaluation.rs, ledger rollups, and inspect gains an arm; the existing planes are unchanged). Truth derivation `pub fn derive_deed_truth(loans: &[GeoLedgerLoanRef with amount_cents and origination window], deeds: &[GeoDeedIndexRow], window_days: u32) -> Result<GeoDeedTruthArtifact, GeoEvaluationError>` producing `canon_geo_deed_truth.v0`: per loan `{ loan_id, matched_instrument_ids, parcel_ids (the truth set), match_kind: Unique | NonUniqueDiscarded | NoMatch, amount_exact: bool, date_delta_days: Option<u32> }`, plus counts `{ loans, unique, non_unique_discarded, no_match }` with `unique + non_unique_discarded + no_match == loans`. Only `Unique` rows become truth; the discarded count is reported (bd-179b: "a smaller clean truth set beats a larger contaminated one"). Round-amount loans are labeled `round_amount: true` and reported as their own stratum so the NYC non-round vs round separation (I09) carries to Franklin.

== SCORING INPUT FOR E5 ==
`canon geo evaluate --population <franklin population> --truth <deed-truth.json> --truth-plane deed_grain_instrument` scores the solver residuals against the deed parcel sets exactly as the H.7 path scores against ACRIS: truth-in-residual by exact membership predicate, backbone accuracy, false merges, abstentions, each with the declared denominator; the T16 tier-curve artifact (bd-s07o) gains a `precision_by_plane` block keyed by `GeoTruthPlane` with `DeedGrainInstrument` for Franklin and never a pooled figure.

== ERROR CODES (additions to `GeoEvaluationErrorCode`; class per §19.4) ==
| `deed_truth_non_unique` | `derive_deed_truth` | more than one instrument matches a loan within the window | abstention: `match_kind = NonUniqueDiscarded`, counted, no truth row |
| `deed_truth_address_join_detected` | `derive_deed_truth` input validation | a deed row carries any address field, or a loan ref carries `asserted_address` in clear | refusal (the join must be amount, date, parcel id only; bd-179b circularity rule); `detail["field"]` |
| `deed_truth_plane_pooled` | `evaluate` with `--truth-plane` | a population evaluation would combine `DeedGrainInstrument` rows with another plane in one count | refusal (mirrors `ledger_truth_plane_pooled`) |

== CONTRACTS AND THREATS SERVED ==
C22, C23 (fixture deed rows carry `fixture.franklin.deeds`), C24, C25 (no `franklin`, `39049`, or `epsg:3735` literal in src/geo/evaluation.rs or any generic module; the county enters only through the population and inventory artifacts; T27 scan unchanged in scope), N06, N07, I09, TH12, TH19, TH20, TH21.

== TESTS (tests/geo_deed_truth.rs; each test logs on failure) ==
| T48 (bead-defined, extends §19.6) | D7 | unit | a fixture deed index of 12 rows (`fixture.` release) and 6 loan refs: 3 with one unique amount-and-date match, 1 with two candidate instruments in the window, 1 with none, 1 round-amount unique | `unique == 4`, `non_unique_discarded == 1`, `no_match == 1`, sum 6; the round loan's row has `round_amount == true`; only unique rows carry `parcel_ids` | an implementation that keeps the first of two non-unique matches reports `unique == 5` and fails; a loan ref with an address field refuses `deed_truth_address_join_detected` with `detail["field"]` | LOG on failure: per loan the candidate instrument ids, amounts, date deltas, the match kind, and the three counts |
| T49 (bead-defined) | D7 | e2e | the fixture population from tests/geo_e5_franklin_parcel.rs with the T48 truth artifact | `canon geo evaluate --truth-plane deed_grain_instrument` emits per-plane precision fields keyed `deed_grain_instrument`; no field pools it with `address_derived_control`; every count has a denominator | an evaluation request naming two planes in one count refuses `deed_truth_plane_pooled` | LOG on failure: the plane keys present, the counts per plane, the denominators, the evaluation artifact BLAKE3 |
| T27 (existing scan) | D7 | adversarial | src/geo/evaluation.rs and the twelve generic modules | no county literal introduced by this bead | | LOG: file, line, literal |

== E2E SCRIPT (scripts/geo_demo/e2e_deed_truth.sh; `set -euo pipefail`; logs each command, exit code, artifact BLAKE3 into <work-dir>/run.log) ==
1. `canon geo truth derive-deed --loans tests/fixtures/geo/deed_truth_loans_fixture.json --deeds tests/fixtures/geo/deed_index_fixture.json --window-days 45 --emit json > <dir>/deed-truth.json`; log the four counts.
2. `canon geo evaluate --population <fixture franklin population> --truth <dir>/deed-truth.json --truth-plane deed_grain_instrument --emit json > <dir>/evaluation.json`; log per-plane precision fields and denominators.
3. `cargo test --test geo_deed_truth -- --nocapture`; `cargo test --test geo_schemas deed_index_rows_schema_matches_a_real_instance deed_truth_schema_matches_a_real_instance`; `cargo test --test geo_e5_franklin_parcel franklin_instance_names_do_not_enter_the_generic_geo_engine`; whole-tree gates.
4. Live (not CI; after the cmdrvl-curves landing): run the checked-in scripts/geo_measurements/e5_franklin_deed_truth_export.sql through cmdrvl-data (record query ids or label `observed`), derive truth, evaluate the Franklin population from bd-s07o, and post the per-plane counts here and on bd-s07o; the T16 tier-curve artifact then carries `precision_by_plane`.

== RESERVATIONS ==
tests/geo_deed_truth.rs, tests/fixtures/geo/deed_index_fixture.json, tests/fixtures/geo/deed_truth_loans_fixture.json, scripts/geo_measurements/e5_franklin_deed_truth_export.sql, scripts/geo_demo/e2e_deed_truth.sh, schemas/canon.geo.deed_index_rows.v0.schema.json, schemas/canon.geo.deed_truth.v0.schema.json. Shared touch points, reserve for the edit only: src/geo/evaluation.rs (additive variant, two types, one function; coordinate with bd-1g4x and bd-s07o on thread bd-s07o), src/geo/cli.rs (`geo truth derive-deed`, `--truth-plane` on `geo evaluate`), src/operator.rs, tests/geo_schemas.rs, scripts/geo_measurements/README.md and manifest.json.

bd-s07o (E5 gate, entry "deed-grain truth source pinned") depends on this bead. This bead depends on bd-3mo1 (harness conventions) only; the cross-repo landing is tracked by the CROSS-E5-DEED thread and is not a Beads dependency in this repo.

ANTI-REWARD-HACKING (AGENTS.md, binding): no address in the truth join; non-unique matches are discarded and counted, never adjudicated into truth; fixture deeds are never cited as E5 precision; the plane is never pooled. Code and tests ship together. No new todo!() scaffolds.

(12) Demo-path hard-coding. GUARD: no franklin, 39049, epsg:3735 in evaluation.rs or any generic module (T27).
