title: [CANON-V1/P13.1] Post-core starter pack: BDC issuer resolution
description:
## Background
Package the private BDC issuer deployment used to exercise bd-kkh5 R1-R5 as a standalone, out-of-tree Canon pack after the core v1 release. This is a production use case and worked example; it does not grant structured-finance awareness to Canon core.

## Scope
- Define domain-owned roles for issuer, filer, holding, and instrument or tranche.
- Map SOI-style rows into observations, assignments, relationships, and source provenance.
- Preserve raw, legal-name, and dba or operating-name views.
- Package conservative evidence and promotion policy plus an independently adjudicated starter corpus.
- Distribute through the signed P08 package contract.
- Exclude tournament parsing, source acquisition, proprietary data, and automatic promotion from the pack.

## Technical approach
Normalization may remove punctuation and well-justified legal suffixes in derived views, but it must preserve the original string and protected legal or organizational terms. It must never blanket-strip SPV, Bidco, Holdco, numbered-company, or similar tokens that may distinguish entities. Tranches remain assignments or instruments, not duplicate organizations. Industry and cross-filer co-holding are contextual evidence only; neither is identity authority or a universal cannot-link. Authoritative identifiers or reviewed constraints are the only hard veto sources.

The gold corpus must be human-adjudicated, provenance-bearing, sealed before evaluation, and separated from policy tuning and holdouts. The pack emits evidence through generic Canon contracts and cannot write registry truth directly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Clean install runs the sealed BDC fixture without changing Canon core.
- R1-R5 are exercised with provenance and temporal/as-of behavior.
- Raw, legal, and dba views survive round-trip inspection.
- Known SPV/Bidco/Holdco and same-name/different-entity cases do not false-merge.
- Candidate and decision metrics meet declared thresholds on an untouched holdout.
- No domain vocabulary appears in core source.

## Test plan
- Golden tests for typed views, tranche separation, temporal aliases, and protected tokens.
- Must-link and cannot-link evaluation on the sealed corpus with leakage checks.
- Ablations for co-holding and industry context.
- Install/verify/run/uninstall tests through P08 signatures and digests.
- Domain-neutrality scan over Canon core.

## File and reservation boundaries
Implementation belongs in a standalone pack or private deployment repository plus public, license-safe fixtures. Reserve exact pack and documentation files; do not edit core to accommodate BDC rules.

## Considerations
The pack may contain private local acceptance data that cannot ship publicly. Public fixtures must be synthetic or appropriately licensed while preserving the same contract. A starter corpus is evidence, not truth by assertion.

title: canon registry default-id-scheme: persist prefix convention in registry.json
description:
Add `canon registry default-id-scheme` to persist a registry's self-authored canonical ID convention in `registry.json`.

Purpose:
- A self-authored registry usually has one canonical namespace such as `PPL`, `IC`, or `CPTY`. Storing the convention makes the registry self-describing and lets `next-id` and `mint` work without repeating `--prefix` every time.

CLI:
`canon registry default-id-scheme --registry <DIR> --prefix <PREFIX> [--zero-pad <N>] [--strict] [--bump patch|minor|major | --next-version <VER>] [--emit json|plain]`

Behavior:
- Read `registry.json` as a JSON object and set `default_id_scheme` to `{ "prefix": <PREFIX>, "zero_pad": <N> }`.
- Validate `PREFIX` as `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*$` and `zero_pad` as an integer from 1 through 20. Default width is 3.
- Preserve all existing `registry.json` fields and formatting can change only through pretty JSON serialization.
- Version update uses the same mutually exclusive `--next-version` or `--bump` rules as add-entry, defaulting to patch when the current version is bumpable.
- Increment no mapping entries. `entry_count` should remain unchanged because this is registry metadata, not a mapping addition.
- Inspect existing `canonical_id` values. By default, emit warnings for IDs that start with the prefix namespace but do not conform to the scheme. With `--strict`, refuse instead of writing.
- Write `registry.json` atomically or leave the original bytes unchanged on failure.
- Do not mutate mapping files or `_index.sqlite`.
- Do not add new witness behavior in this bead.
- Ensure `next-id` without a prefix and `mint` without `--canonical-id` or `--prefix` consume the configured scheme.

Output:
- Default `--emit json`: emit `canon_registry_default_id_scheme.v0` with registry version before/after, previous scheme, new scheme, warning counts, and touched file.
- `--emit plain`: print `<PREFIX>-<zero_pad width>` style summary plus newline, for example `PPL-3`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Setting the scheme writes `default_id_scheme` to `registry.json` and bumps the registry version without changing `entry_count`.
- Unknown `registry.json` fields survive unchanged.
- Invalid prefixes, zero padding outside 1..20, and unchanged/non-bumpable versions refuse with recovery guidance.
- `--strict` refuses when existing in-namespace canonical IDs do not conform; non-strict mode writes and records warnings in the JSON receipt.
- `canon registry next-id --registry <DIR>` uses the configured scheme when no prefix is supplied.
- `canon registry mint --registry <DIR> --canonical-type <TYPE> --with-alias ...` uses the configured scheme when no canonical ID or prefix is supplied.
- JSON receipt shape is covered by a golden fixture for `canon_registry_default_id_scheme.v0`.
- The command writes only `registry.json`; mapping files and `_index.sqlite` are unchanged.
- Quality gate passes: `cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test`.
notes:
Target files:
- src/registry/id_scheme.rs (new)
- src/registry.rs (add module/export and extend metadata helpers; there is no src/registry/mod.rs in this repo)
- src/registry/next_id.rs (fallback behavior, if not already complete)
- src/registry/mint.rs (fallback behavior, if not already complete)
- src/cli.rs (wire subcommand)
- src/lib.rs (minimal dispatch only)
- operator.json (add command contract if implemented in this bead)
- tests/registry_id_scheme.rs (new)

Implementation notes:
- This bead should land after next-id and mint to avoid parallel edits to the same modules.
- `default_id_scheme` is metadata for self-authored registries. It must not alter lookup matching semantics.
- Keep the field optional; existing registries without it must continue to load and resolve exactly as before.
close_reason: Implemented canon registry default-id-scheme as a metadata-only registry.json writer. Validates prefix and zero_pad, bumps version without changing entry_count, preserves unknown registry fields, records non-strict warnings for in-namespace out-of-scheme IDs, supports --strict refusal, leaves mappings and _index.sqlite untouched, and proves next-id/mint consume the stored scheme. Evidence: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test; target/debug/canon --describe includes default-id-scheme; br dep cycles --json returned count 0.

title: [CANON-V1/P13.2] Post-core starter pack: CMBS tenant resolution
description:
## Background
Build a second hand-authored starter pack for tenant-name resolution across rent rolls and leases. It exercises a different entity archetype from BDC issuers—chains, stores, franchisees, legal tenants, locations, and landlords—but remains a structured-finance-adjacent use case. It must not be presented as proof of cross-industry generality.

## Scope
- Define domain-owned roles and relationships for tenant, legal obligor, brand or chain, franchisee, store or location, landlord, lease, and source row.
- Preserve store numbers, location identifiers, dba relationships, and franchise relationships rather than collapsing them into names.
- Package source mappings, typed normalization views, evidence policy, and an adjudicated starter corpus.
- Distribute through P08 as an independent package.
- Exclude document extraction, rent-roll parsing, and automatic registry promotion.

## Technical approach
Map each source row into observations and typed assignments. Preserve raw strings and protected numeric or location features. Treat chain affiliation and franchise relationships as typed evidence, not identity equivalence. Legal tenant, operating brand, franchisee, and individual store can be related while remaining distinct entities. All scoring and decisions pass through generic Canon evidence, review, and promotion contracts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A clean install resolves the sealed CMBS tenant fixture without core edits.
- Chain, franchisee, legal tenant, and store/location identities remain distinguishable.
- Store numbers and location signals improve disambiguation without becoming universal match keys.
- Holdout candidate recall and decision quality meet declared thresholds.
- Documentation accurately calls this a second finance archetype, not cross-domain proof.

## Test plan
- Golden tests for chain/franchise/store/legal-tenant relationship shapes.
- Adversarial same-brand/different-franchisee and same-name/different-location cases.
- Leakage-safe holdout evaluation and feature ablations.
- P08 install, signature, digest, compatibility, and uninstall checks.
- Domain-neutrality scan over Canon core.

## File and reservation boundaries
Implementation belongs in a standalone pack or deployment repository with license-safe fixtures. Reserve exact files and keep all CMBS vocabulary outside core.

## Considerations
Brand similarity can be strong relationship evidence while being dangerous identity evidence. The corpus must represent franchise and multi-location negatives, not only easy aliases.

title: canon geo: geocode plausibility — use the tile to refute its own input, and adjudicate competing geocodes
description:
OPERATOR INSIGHT 2026-08-14: THE TILE CAN REFUTE ITS OWN INPUT. THIS IS A CAPABILITY,
NOT AN ERROR PATH.

"Geocodes are hard to trust, and there is going to be some cases where the geocode we're
provided is just flat out wrong. It's not in the tile set at all. So it's an abstain or
refuse, and there's a lot of validity to when we're only looking at one tile and its
surrounding tiles being able to say: this geocode and this address are nowhere in here."

Everything else in canon geo runs FORWARD: take the geocode, pull the tile, generate
candidates, score, decide or abstain. This runs BACKWARD — it uses the tile as EVIDENCE
ABOUT THE INPUT. It is cheap, purely local, entirely deterministic, and it catches a
population that accuracy_type cannot.

== THE PROOF CASE, FROM REAL DATA ==
"241/249 West 74th Street" carries two geocodes from two different geocoding services:
  (40.7777640, -73.9755480)  range_interpolation  parsed "241 W 74th St"
  (40.7615050, -73.9859030)  ROOFTOP              parsed "241 W 49th St"  <- ~25 blocks off
The second is at the HIGHEST confidence tier and is flatly wrong.

Pull the tile plus k-ring at each point and ask a single question: DOES ANYTHING IN THIS
NEIGHBOURHOOD CARRY THE ASSERTED STREET? At the first point, West 74th Street is present.
At the second, it is not. THE TILE REFUTES THE GEOCODE. No ground truth, no external
service, no ML — just the tile the cascade already had to download.

== WHY TILE SCOPING IS WHAT MAKES IT WORK ==
Street names repeat across boroughs; there is a Broadway in every one. The question is not
"does this street name exist anywhere" (useless) but "DOES THIS STREET EXIST HERE"
(decisive). A res-9 cell plus k-ring 1 is ~1 km across, and a street that does not appear
anywhere in a 1 km neighbourhood is a street you are not standing on. The blocking unit
doubles as the plausibility window, which is the third distinct job the tile is doing —
after blocking (bd-2b9d) and the map viewport (bd-101v).

== THE CHECK, IN ORDER OF COST ==
1. STREET PRESENCE. Does any entity in the tile + k-ring carry the asserted street name
   (normalized)? Cheapest and strongest.
2. HOUSE-NUMBER RANGE. Does the asserted number fall within the range of numbers observed
   on that street in the neighbourhood? Catches "241 West 74th" pointing at the 1600 block.
3. ADDRESS-SET MEMBERSHIP. For multi-address assertions, does ANY member of the asserted
   set appear? (Requires the address-set source, bd-35qg, to be strong.)
4. ATTRIBUTE COHERENCE. Does anything in the neighbourhood plausibly match on size, type
   or year built? Weakest, but it is what discriminates the two failure directions below.

== IT DISCRIMINATES TWO FAILURE DIRECTIONS THAT NEED DIFFERENT REMEDIES ==
  GEOCODE IS WRONG    the tile has coherent content, but NOTHING matches the assertion on
                      ANY channel. Remedy: re-geocode. This is the 241/249 W 49th case.
  ADDRESS IS WRONG    the geocode lands cleanly on a rooftop and the tile has a coherent
                      property there matching on OTHER channels (size, type, name) but not
                      on address. Remedy: fix the source record.
  BOTH PLAUSIBLE      abstain.
Conflating these produces the wrong advice to the client, and the advice is the product.

== IT ADJUDICATES BETWEEN COMPETING GEOCODES ==
The geocode table's grain is property x SOURCE x ASOF — multiple geocoding services
appended, not upserted (verified 2026-08-14; see the correction on bd-tccn). So a property
may carry SEVERAL candidate points from INDEPENDENT services. That independence is
valuable: when two services disagree, the tile is a deterministic referee. Pull the tile at
each candidate, apply the checks above, and keep the point its own neighbourhood supports.
Where several survive or none do, abstain.
This is strictly better than the usual heuristics (highest accuracy_score, most recent
asof, preferred source), all of which pick a winner without evidence.

== THE EXPANDING SEARCH: DIAGNOSTICS, NOT REPAIR ==
When the geocode is refuted, expanding the k-ring can often find where the asserted address
actually is. That is genuinely valuable OUTPUT — "412 rows in your book have geocodes more
than 500 m from anything matching their address, and here is where each probably belongs"
is a report a client can act on the day they receive it, and no competing product produces
it.
BUT IT IS NOT RESOLUTION. Per canon doctrine the workbench proposes and review promotes. A
relocated point is a CANDIDATE carrying its displacement distance and its supporting
evidence, never a silent correction. Bound the expansion explicitly (a declared max k) and
refuse rather than searching outward indefinitely.

== ABSTENTION VOCABULARY ADDITIONS (extends bd-786w) ==
  GeocodeRefutedByTile      nothing in the neighbourhood supports the asserted address
  AddressRefutedByTile      the point is coherent but the assertion is not supported
  CompetingGeocodes         multiple candidate points, none decisively supported
  GeocodeUnlocatable        refuted, and the bounded expanding search found no better home
Each carries the tile id, the checks that ran, and what was found instead — so the card
(bd-101v) can render "we looked here and here is what is actually there."

== WHY THIS MAY BE THE HIGHEST-VALUE-PER-EFFORT ITEM IN THE EPIC ==
1. It needs NO data that is not already required — the tile and the client's own row.
2. It catches silent errors that accuracy_type provably misses. The proof case is ROOFTOP
   tier, which every tier-based calibration would trust.
3. It converts an unexplained miss into an ACTIONABLE finding with a named remedy, which is
   the difference between "we could not key 6% of your book" and "6% of your book has bad
   geocodes and here they are."
4. It is a REFUSAL, which is canon's native and strongest posture.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- The four checks implemented as geo evidence operators emitting structured (not prose)
  evidence
- Tile-scoped street presence proven on the 241/249 West 74th Street case: the W 49th point
  refuted, the W 74th point supported
- Both failure directions discriminated, with a fixture for each
- Competing-geocode adjudication, with a test that it beats highest-accuracy_score and
  most-recent-asof heuristics on a labelled set
- Bounded expanding search emitting candidates with displacement distance, never silent
  correction; refusal at the declared bound
- Four abstention reasons implemented and carried into the artifact
- Reported as a first-class rate alongside coverage, precision, abstention, multi-candidate
  and false-merge
close_reason: Absorbed by bd-7hze (stage D4 retry loop) and materialize-address-evidence street-absence refutation (Appendix M.2): the tile refuting its own input is an abstention that triggers bounded re-geocode and retry (L.5), not a separate plausibility scorer.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-14 (SECOND) — "COMPETING GEOCODING SERVICES" WAS NOT ESTABLISHED. IT
CAME FROM AN LLM INTERPRETATION, NOT FROM THE DATA. Operator caught it.

WHAT THE BEAD SAID: that the geocode table carries points from "SEVERAL candidate points
from INDEPENDENT services," and that their independence is what makes cross-source
disagreement valuable evidence.

THE PROVENANCE OF THAT CLAIM: Loom asserted "the ETL pipeline runs multiple geocoding
services (NYC and Census TIGER)." I did not verify it before writing it down. OC-0048
states plainly that the CMBS geocodes come from GEOCODIO — a single service — and records
a frozen Geocodio account (br-1zo6) as the backfill blocker.

THE LITERAL VALUES, NOW VERIFIED, for the two "241/249 West 74th Street" rows:
                   ROW 1                                          ROW 2
  SOURCE           "TIGER/Line(R) dataset from the US Census      "City of New York"
                    Bureau"
  ASOF             2025-01-01                                     2026-08-01
  CENSUS_YEAR      2024                                           2025
  PROPERTY_NAME    "Alfie Arms Corp."   (trailing period)         "Alfie Arms Corp"
  LAT/LON          40.7777640 / -73.9755480                       40.7615050 / -73.9859030
  ACCURACY_TYPE    range_interpolation                            rooftop
  ACCURACY_SCORE   1.00                                           0.92
  STREET           "W 74th St"                                    "W 49th St"

MOST LIKELY READING, STILL UNVERIFIED AND FLAGGED AS SUCH: those SOURCE strings are
GEOCODIO'S UNDERLYING-ADDRESS-DATASET ATTRIBUTION, not separate vendors. Geocodio returns a
per-result `source` naming the dataset that produced the match, and "TIGER/Line(R) dataset
from the US Census Bureau" is one of its stock strings. One service, two runs, different
underlying datasets matched.
DO NOT HARDEN THIS EITHER. Verify against Geocodio's documentation. It is the same class of
unverified-vendor-semantics problem bd-bmee already flags for accuracy_type ("asserted from
general knowledge, NOT verified against their documentation"), and both should be settled
in the same pass.

THE ACTUALLY VERIFIED AND MORE USEFUL FINDING — A TRAILING PERIOD DUPLICATES THE ROW.
PROPERTY_NAME is part of the table's grain. "Alfie Arms Corp." and "Alfie Arms Corp"
differ by ONE PUNCTUATION MARK, and that is what makes this two rows rather than one. Two
upstream records naming the same property slightly differently, geocoded 19 months apart,
landing 1.8 km apart.
This is a NAME-NORMALIZATION problem sitting upstream of the geo problem — and it is
squarely what canon entity's existing machinery is for (bd-2cbs rule 3). Deduplicating the
book by normalized property name BEFORE geo runs is cheap, uses shipped capability, and
directly shrinks the denominators bd-14co has to report. Add it to the corpus as its own
observation.

ALSO VERIFIED AND WORTH KEEPING: ACCURACY_SCORE and ACCURACY_TYPE DISAGREE about which row
to trust. Score says row 1 (1.00 vs 0.92); tier says row 2 (rooftop beats
range_interpolation). The tier — the field every convention trusts, and the one bd-bmee's
tier analysis is built on — points at the WRONG row. Neither field alone is a safe selector.

WHAT SURVIVES IN THIS BEAD, UNCHANGED AND STILL THE POINT:
The capability does not depend on WHY multiple rows exist. Whatever the mechanism —
separate vendors, one vendor across vintages, or duplicate upstream records — a property
can carry SEVERAL candidate points that disagree, and THE TILE CAN ADJUDICATE BETWEEN THEM
WITH EVIDENCE where accuracy_score, accuracy_type, most-recent-asof and preferred-source
all pick a winner without any. The 241/249 proof case stands exactly as written: the tile at
the West 49th point contains no West 74th Street and refutes it; the tile at the West 74th
point supports it.

REQUIRED EDIT: strike "independent services" from the adjudication section and replace with
"multiple candidate points for one property, whatever their provenance." Do not claim
independence as a property of the evidence until the mechanism is verified — independent
sources disagreeing IS stronger evidence than one source varying, but that strength has to
be earned by verification, not assumed.

PROCESS NOTE FOR THIS CORPUS: two claims in this session came from Loom's prose
interpretation rather than from returned values, and both were wrong. When building the
worked-case corpus (bd-tccn), TAKE LITERAL COLUMN VALUES AND RECORD THE QUERY. Prose
summaries from any LLM tool are a lead to verify, never a finding to cite. This matters
more here than usual because the corpus is meant to be the thing everything else is
designed against.

  SOURCE_GEOM_CRS, SOURCE_CHANNEL, SOURCE_FILENAME, ROW_PAYLOAD, LOADED_AT

CONSEQUENCES:
- MapPLUTO publishes roughly ninety fields; the landed table projects about twenty and puts
  the remainder in ROW_PAYLOAD. Anything not projected requires digging into ROW_PAYLOAD,
  which is a different access pattern and a different cost.
- THE SIX-FIELD CLIENT CONTRACT IS SATISFIED BY PROJECTED COLUMNS, which is good news:
  building size -> BLDGAREA, year built -> YEARBUILT, property type -> BLDGCLASS + LANDUSE.
  No ROW_PAYLOAD dig needed for the core cascade.
- UNIT COUNTS (UnitsTotal, UnitsRes) ARE NOT PROJECTED. Assemblage subset-sum for
  multifamily (case 7) may want them. Confirm they exist in ROW_PAYLOAD before designing
  around them.

=========================================================================
2. BBL IS STORED AS A STRING WITH A TRAILING ".0" AND IS NOT JOIN-READY.
=========================================================================
Literal returned value: "BBL": "1014477501.0"

This is a direct problem for canon. Core lookup is EXACT BYTE MATCH AFTER ASCII-TRIM, so
"1014477501" would NOT resolve against "1014477501.0". Any registry built from this column
without normalization silently fails to match the identifier every other NYC source uses,
and every downstream join against ACRIS, PLUTO, or the footprints file has the same
exposure.
REQUIRED: BBL normalization is a declared, versioned step in the ingest, not an incidental
cast. It belongs in the geo profile's normalization vocabulary alongside the geometry
canonicalization, and it needs a negative test.

=========================================================================
3. CASE 6 IS A CONDO, AND THE CONDO TRAP IS LIVE IN IT.
=========================================================================
Literal rows for BBL prefix 10144775:

  BBL 1014477501.0  "305 EAST 72 STREET"  BLDGCLASS RM  LOTAREA 37,800
                    BLDGAREA 194,949  NUMBLDGS 2  NUMFLOORS 17  YEARBUILT 1961
                    OWNERNAME "305/72 CONDOMINIUM"
  BBL 1014477502.0  "1355 1 AVENUE"       BLDGCLASS RM  LOTAREA  5,100
                    BLDGAREA 102,719  NUMBLDGS 1  NUMFLOORS 31  YEARBUILT 2009
                    OWNERNAME "UNAVAILABLE OWNER"

FOUR THINGS THIS ESTABLISHES:
a) OWNERNAME "305/72 CONDOMINIUM" and the 75xx lot range confirm these are CONDO BILLING
   BBLs. The condo trap named in OC-0048 and measured in the multi-lot fan-out is present
   in the very property picked to illustrate a different case.
b) A PRIOR CLAIM IS CORRECTED. I wrote that five asserted addresses "resolve to ONE BBL."
   Not established. At least two condo BBLs sit here with DIFFERENT street frontages —
   East 72 Street and 1 Avenue. The property's a/k/a set names E 72nd, 2nd Avenue and
   E 73rd; 1 Avenue is a fourth frontage not in that set. The containment test still has to
   be run properly.
c) YEARBUILT 1961 vs 2009 ON ADJACENT CONDO LOTS IS A LIVE REDEVELOPMENT SIGNAL — exactly
   the case hypothesised on bd-gs6n, that a large year-built spread on overlapping or
   adjacent footprints is a TEMPORAL finding rather than a match failure. It is real and it
   is in the first property examined closely.
d) NUMBLDGS 2 on one condo BBL. The building level is still needed and the BBL-to-BIN
   bridge (landed, bd-397d) is still the next pull.

=========================================================================
4. THE TABLE IS STRUCTURALLY BITEMPORAL ALREADY.
=========================================================================
RELEASE, RELEASE_DT, VALID_FROM_RELEASE_DT, VALID_TO_RELEASE_DT, IS_CURRENT_RELEASE are all
present. The landing contract (cmdrvl-curves bd-qbno) was built for multiple releases even
though OC-0048 records that only the current one is loaded.
CONSEQUENCE: the as-of machinery bd-12gh and bd-1oy8 need does not require a schema change,
only additional releases. Check `SELECT DISTINCT RELEASE, RELEASE_DT` before assuming case
9's temporal arc is blocked — cmdrvl-curves bd-33t6 may be closer to done than the outcome
document states.

=========================================================================
5. REPROJECTION PROVENANCE IS ALREADY RECORDED. THIS DIRECTLY SERVES bd-3nc7.
=========================================================================
GEOM_CRS and SOURCE_GEOM_CRS are projected columns. So the EPSG:2263 -> WGS84 transform
that the predicate-regime bead has to reason about is documented in the table itself rather
than needing archaeology. Read those columns first when starting bd-3nc7.

=========================================================================
6. H3_R7 AND H3_R8 ARE PRESENT. H3_R9 IS NOT.
=========================================================================
The epic's default tile is res-9. It is not precomputed. Canon computes it itself, which is
what bd-2b9d already requires for a separate reason — the Snowflake H3 helpers returned
malformed boundaries and a bad k-ring (edgar-elt br-2wir). Both reasons now point the same
way: compute r9 in canon with a vetted Rust H3 library, and treat the warehouse H3 columns
as a coarse prefilter at most.

=========================================================================
7. GEOCODIO SOURCE SEMANTICS — CONFIRMED BY OPERATOR.
=========================================================================
Geocodio reports the underlying address dataset that produced each match. So SOURCE values
like "TIGER/Line(R) dataset from the US Census Bureau" and "City of New York" are
per-result attribution from ONE service, not competing vendors — and MULTIPLE SOURCED
GEOCODES PER PROPERTY ARE EXPECTED AND NORMAL.
This VINDICATES the capability in bd-1a12 while keeping the retraction of the mechanism.
SOURCE becomes usable EVIDENCE: a local authoritative dataset and a national interpolated
one carry different reliability.
BUT NOTE THE COUNTEREXAMPLE ALREADY IN HAND: on "241/249 West 74th Street" the
"City of New York" sourced row is the WRONG one (W 49th St, rooftop, score 0.92) and the
TIGER/Line row is right (W 74th St, range_interpolation, score 1.00). So SOURCE is not a
safe selector either, any more than ACCURACY_TYPE or ACCURACY_SCORE are. Three fields, none
individually decisive, all disagreeing — which is precisely the argument for letting the
tile adjudicate.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
ARCHITECTURE SUPERSEDED 2026-08-15 — see docs/PLAN_CANON_GEO.md.

An adversarial multi-model design session produced a materially different architecture,
which then survived a red team that destroyed two intermediate designs. The tile is modelled
as a BOUNDED UNIVERSE and every piece of evidence is a CONSTRAINT; propagation runs to a
fixpoint; the residual model set IS the answer. There is no proposer channel.

THE THREE PROPERTIES THAT MATTER:
- CONFLUENCE. The fixpoint is independent of the order constraints are applied (Tarski 1955;
  Cousot & Cousot 1977; Apt 1999), so determinism is a theorem rather than an engineering
  effort.
- MONOTONICITY. Constraints only add and domains only shrink, so a tile resolved with four
  sources today and six next year yields a TIGHTER residual, never a contradicting one. The
  earlier answer was never wrong, only less resolved.
- STRUCTURAL ABSTENTION. The residual model set is the answer. No threshold anywhere.

THE KEY DESIGN RULE IS rho, THE SOUNDNESS DISCIPLINE. Every source attribute enters the
solver only through a declared versioned relaxation mapping it to the WEAKEST constraint the
source can actually support. An interpolated geocode becomes a 150m disc rather than a
location. A parcel ADDRESS becomes "one of this lot's addresses" rather than functional
equality. OWNERNAME equal PERMITS an assemblage; OWNERNAME different constrains NOTHING.
Every noisy channel is admitted only in its sound direction — which is what dissolved the
proposer dilemma that broke the two earlier designs.

AND THE COMMERCIAL CONSEQUENCE: if every rho is sound, the true assignment is in the model
set, so AN EMPTY MODEL SET IS A PROOF that a named source violated its own published error
model — attributable, falsifiable, and mailable to the vendor.

Read PLAN_CANON_GEO.md before starting any geo work. Section 11 carries the bead-by-bead
supersession table. Appendix A covers frozen-weight observers and imagery sources. APPENDIX
B RECORDS THE FIRST HARD MEASUREMENT, WHICH FALSIFIED A LOAD-BEARING CLAIM — read it before
trusting any performance number in the plan.

Raw session artifacts, including the red team and the adversarial reviews, are preserved
under docs/geo_design_session/ with a reading guide.

comments.text: Operator design decision: TRACT-BOUNDED RETRY is the v1 loop — no coordinate API required. The tract is a bounded universe of the same epistemic shape as the tile (jurisdiction-defined, integer-keyed GEOID, versioned), so retry = refute -> address->tract via geo MCP as landed (exact match) -> assemble tract cells -> normal pipeline over the tract's candidate set with address as existential membership evidence. Guards: (1) chimera/parsed-address membership check BEFORE trusting tract (tract inherits address-string risk); (2) rho scales with match_quality (exact -> tract; weaker -> tract+neighbors); (3) PIN TRACT VINTAGE — 2010 vs 2020 GEOIDs (MapPLUTO CT2010-era vs FEMA 2020 TRACT_GEOID) is the same silent-join defect class as H3 INTEGER/TEXT; (4) representative-address gap persists until PAD (bd-28kn).

title: Resolve v0 assertion operators
description:
Implement the pure assertion and candidate-filter operators used by canon resolve scoring.

Scope:
- Add src/resolve/assertions.rs.
- Implement exact: byte-equal after ASCII trim.
- Implement tolerance_pct: abs(a - b) / max(abs(a), abs(b)) <= tolerance with explicit zero handling.
- Implement tolerance_abs: abs(a - b) <= tolerance.
- Implement range: numeric candidate filter within range_pct.
- Implement date_range: supported deterministic date parsing and day-window comparison.
- Implement prefix: one trimmed string is prefix of the other.
- Implement canon_match as a deterministic exact-registry comparison helper that resolves both sides through an already-loaded registry/lookup context, without adding any fuzzy behavior to core lookup.
- Return structured AssertionResult data with passed, score contribution, operator, fields, weight, and detail values suitable for output evidence.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests cover every operator, boundary values, invalid type parsing, missing values, zero values, and deterministic detail rendering.
- Property-style tests or table-driven tests cover symmetry for numeric tolerance operators and reflexivity for exact.
- Scores are always bounded in [0.0, 1.0] before weighting.
- Required assertion failure semantics are represented for scoring but the final scoring policy can be implemented by the scoring bead.
- No runtime network calls, no fuzzy matching, and no locale-sensitive parsing.

Target files:
- src/resolve/assertions.rs
- src/resolve/types.rs if shared result structs are scaffolded there

Reservation guidance:
- Reserve only assertion-related files.

title: [CANON-V1/P07.R6h] Credit exact prepared-surface collapse in native link decisions
description:
## Background
Public native link decision derivation flattens observation-to-surface bindings into reference and target ID sets before classifying targets. An exact shared prepared surface can therefore resolve to one incumbent with zero candidate support but still be emitted as unmatched. PLAN_CANON defines prepared_surface_collapse as a first-class attachment lane with no candidate-rank or recall credit.

## Technical Approach
Retain target/reference binding identity at prepared-surface grain in entity_link_decision_records_from_solve. Permit a match only when exactly one reference and the target share the exact hash-bound prepared surface, the solve entity is resolved_existing, and all hard-cannot-link, conflict, soft-warning, and multiple-reference guards pass. Keep ordinary threshold matching unchanged. Emit an explicit prepared_surface_collapse assertion/disposition with zero candidate score rather than pretending candidate evidence exists. Refresh strict alias-withholding fixture decisions from the updated solve and committed lineage.

## Success Criteria
- Exact shared-surface reference/target observations deterministically produce one match even with zero candidate support.
- Collapse receives no candidate-rank or candidate-recall credit and is explicitly distinguishable from threshold evidence matches.
- Distinct-surface zero-support cases remain unmatched.
- Hard/soft anti-merge and multiple-reference cases never auto-match.
- Review-export rederivation remains byte/semantic parity with emitted link decisions.
- Strict alias-withholding fixture has one collapse attach and one honest non-incumbent abstention under committed publication lineage.

## Test Plan
Add neutral public link coverage for shared-surface collapse and negative safety guards; rerun entity_alias_withholding, CLI smoke/link integration, fmt, strict Clippy, and full cargo test.

## RESERVATIONS
- src/lib.rs
- tests/cli_smoke.rs
- tests/entity_alias_withholding.rs
close_reason: Guarded exact prepared-surface collapse now attaches only one safe resolved incumbent, emits zero candidate credit, preserves anti-merge and multi-reference abstention, and passes neutral, alias-withholding, and full quality gates.

title: [CANON-V1/P09.10] Deferred decision: review delivery transports
description:
## Background
Agent-orchestrated email crowdsourcing is one plausible way to deliver Canon review packets to domain experts, but it is only an idea. Core review and promotion must not depend on email, a UI, a ticketing system, active learning, or any other transport.

## Scope
Retain the future choices: direct CLI/file review, agent-operated email, a third-party or OpenRefine-compatible client, ticketing/approval systems, a custom UI, or no additional delivery layer. Core owns stable review packets, structured decision import, ledger receipts, stale/tamper refusals, audit, promotion, and replay.

## Technical Approach
Do no transport implementation before final v1 acceptance. Later, choose from observed review volume, privacy/disclosure constraints, expert-routing needs, and operator workflow. A selected transport becomes an out-of-core sidecar or client over the generic artifacts. Email, if selected, requires authorization, redaction, thread/candidate binding, reply parsing, spoof/tamper defense, idempotency, bounce/timeout/reassignment, retention, and real-service E2E.

## Acceptance Criteria
- No review delivery transport blocks or appears in core acceptance.
- CLI and offline files alone complete review, import, audit, promotion, and replay.
- The decision document records all options without selecting email or forbidding future clients.
- Any later client has zero direct registry/promotion authority and uses stable generic contracts.
- This bead remains blocked until final v1 acceptance.

## Test Plan
Before any later selection, scan release dependencies and docs to prove transport independence. A future selected sidecar must add protocol, security, stale/tamper, idempotency, failure, and real-service E2E matrices.

## RESERVATIONS
- docs/DECISION_REVIEW_VIA_EMAIL_CROWDSOURCING.md

## Considerations
Transport-neutral artifacts maximize open-source adoption and let agent workflows evolve independently of Canon core.

description:
Context:
XEW-P008 can prove instrument identity collapse in SEC filings by freezing canon/OpenFIGI materialization into a local snapshot before pack generation. In the MSFT 2026-04-29 10-Q proof, XEW found three securities collapsed under weak identity ticker=MSFT and exchange=NASDAQ: common stock, 3.125% Notes due 2028, and 2.625% Notes due 2033.

Observed provider gap:
canon registry build --source openfigi currently supports CUSIP, ISIN, and SEDOL seed columns with id_type=ID_CUSIP|ID_ISIN|ID_SEDOL, but OpenFigiMappingJob only sends idType and idValue. It does not pass through OpenFIGI mapping filters such as exchCode, micCode, currency, marketSecDes, securityType, or securityType2.

Why this matters:
The MSFT common stock seed US5949181045 maps to many venue-level OpenFIGI candidates. OpenFIGI can resolve it deterministically when the mapping request includes exchCode=US, returning exactly figi=BBG000BPH459, compositeFIGI=BBG000BPH459, shareClassFIGI=BBG001S5TD05, ticker=MSFT, exchCode=US. Without the exchange filter, canon correctly marks the seed ambiguous and refuses to guess. This is correct behavior, but it blocks fully automated registry materialization for the P008 demo/corpus.

Concrete evidence from 2026-06-09 run:
- canon OpenFIGI ISIN materialization for seeds XS1001749289 and XS0922885362 resolved the MSFT notes to BBG005NPW5Z2 and BBG004HDR2M6.
- canon materialization for common stock seed US5949181045 reported ambiguous_count=1 and failure_count=1 because multiple plausible FIGI rows were returned.
- Direct OpenFIGI mapping with body [{"idType":"ID_ISIN","idValue":"US5949181045","exchCode":"US"}] returned one deterministic common-stock row: BBG000BPH459.
- A local proof snapshot composed from the two canon-resolved note rows plus the exchange-filtered common-stock row let cmdrvl-xew prove the MSFT pack with registry_status_counts={"resolved":3}, no_live_openfigi=true, no_live_sec=true, and verify-pack passed.

Implementation goal:
Allow canon registry build --source openfigi to pass deterministic OpenFIGI mapping filters through from provider config and/or seed rows so provider-backed registry maintenance can disambiguate venue-level candidates without heuristics.

Suggested behavior:
- Support provider-config pass-through for OpenFIGI mapping fields: exchCode, micCode, currency, marketSecDes, securityType, securityType2, includeUnlistedEquities, and other stable mapping filters already modeled by OpenFIGI v3.
- Prefer explicit static provider-config for corpus-wide filters, e.g. --provider-config exchCode=US for US listed equity corpora.
- Consider optional per-row seed columns for mixed corpora, e.g. isin,exchCode,marketSecDes, while preserving deterministic request construction and clear provenance.
- Record all non-secret provider filters in _build.json. Redact secrets as today.
- Keep current refusal behavior for true ambiguity. Filters narrow the request; they must not introduce guessing.
- Preserve the provider boundary: live OpenFIGI calls are maintenance-time materialization only. Normal canon lookup and XEW pack generation must consume local registry files/snapshots only.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A registry build using seed US5949181045 with id_type=ID_ISIN and exchCode=US materializes a single FIGI mapping to BBG000BPH459 and captures composite/share-class data if canon supports those mapping files.
2. Existing CUSIP/ISIN/SEDOL builds without filters behave exactly as before, including ambiguous_match diagnostics.
3. Unit/smoke tests cover OpenFIGI request JSON including filters, _build.json provenance, and ambiguity preservation.
4. A twinning-backed test should exercise filtered OpenFIGI mapping without contacting api.openfigi.com.
5. README/docs/PLAN_CANON.md document when to use provider filters and reiterate that provider-backed registries are static materialization artifacts, not just-in-time lookups.

Related downstream use case:
cmdrvl-xew XEW-P008 Instrument Identity Collapse for MSFT 10-Q accession 0001193125-26-191507. This enhancement lets the clean demo show all three weakly-collapsed instruments resolved through canon/OpenFIGI materialization before XEW consumes the local snapshot.

Added provider unit tests, CLI smoke coverage for ID_ISIN + exchCode=US, and updated the twinning smoke command to exercise filtered mapping when the local fixture is present. title: canon geo [ambition-3]: correlation clustering over the existing Support/AntiMerge lanes (deterministic pivot)
description:
THE OBJECTIVE canon'S EVIDENCE MODEL WAS ALREADY SHAPED FOR, WITHOUT ANYONE SAYING SO.

BLOCKED ON THE RESIDUAL HARNESS.

THE OBSERVATION THAT MAKES THIS BEAD WORTH WRITING: correlation clustering is the problem
of partitioning a graph whose edges carry POSITIVE (should be together) and NEGATIVE
(should be apart) weights, minimizing total disagreement. canon's evidence model ALREADY
PRODUCES EXACTLY THAT GRAPH AND HAS FROM THE START:
  ScoreLane::Support     positive weight, integer ScoreUnits
  ScoreLane::AntiMerge   negative weight, with hard_cannot_link as the infinite case
  ScoreLane::RelationHint  zero weight by construction — related but not same
Verified in src/entity/score.rs and src/entity/edge.rs; EdgeEvidenceRecord already carries
pair_score_total, a per-lane score_breakdown, and has_hard_cannot_link.

So this is not importing foreign machinery. It is naming the objective the existing
artifact already encodes, and solving it properly instead of by threshold.

WHY IT BEATS THE CURRENT APPROACH: threshold-and-transitively-close is the default
clustering method and it has two well-known pathologies that geo will hit hard.
  CHAINING — A~B and B~C both clear the threshold, so A~C is asserted even though A and C
  are 400 m apart and have a hard negative between them. In a dense tile with many
  near-duplicate footprints this produces one giant wrong cluster.
  THRESHOLD BRITTLENESS — one number decides every merge, so the whole tile's behaviour
  swings on a calibration constant.
Correlation clustering optimizes GLOBAL agreement instead, and it respects hard negatives
structurally rather than hoping the threshold does.

NOTE: canon already depends on petgraph, so graph machinery is in-tree.

THE METHOD, AND THE DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT:
- The exact problem is NP-hard. Do NOT reach for an LP or SDP relaxation first.
- USE THE DETERMINISTIC PIVOT ALGORITHM (KwikCluster, Ailon-Charikar-Newman) WITH A
  DETERMINISTIC PIVOT ORDER. The standard analysis randomizes pivot selection for its
  3-approximation guarantee; randomization is FORBIDDEN here because replay must be
  byte-identical. Substituting a deterministic pivot order (a total order on surface ids,
  or descending by summed positive weight) FORFEITS THE PROBABILISTIC GUARANTEE. That is
  an acceptable trade — canon's promise is determinism, not an approximation ratio — but it
  MUST BE STATED HONESTLY in the artifact and the docs. Do not quote a 3-approximation
  bound for a deterministic variant that does not have one.
- MEASURE THE OBJECTIVE, DO NOT ASSERT IT. Report achieved disagreement cost alongside the
  clustering, and on small tiles compare against a brute-force optimum to characterize the
  real gap on real data. That is the honest way to claim quality.
- HARD CANNOT-LINK IS A CONSTRAINT, NOT A LARGE NEGATIVE WEIGHT. A finite weight can be
  overridden by enough positive evidence, which would let the solver merge two buildings
  500 m apart if enough weak signals accumulated. Enforce structurally.

INTERACTION WITH THE CARDINALITY PRIOR (bd-2kjx claim 3, as corrected 2026-08-14): "a tile
has approximately N buildings but an unbounded number of overlapping LEGAL parcels once
condos are included, so the prior applies PER ENTITY TYPE, not per tile." Correlation
clustering does not take a cluster count, which is a genuine advantage over k-style methods
here. But the per-entity-type prior remains a DIAGNOSTIC: a building clustering that
produces 3N clusters is wrong by construction and should be flagged even if it optimizes
the objective, because that means the evidence is wrong rather than the solver.

WITHIN-SOURCE MUTUAL EXCLUSION AS A CONSTRAINT: where a source DECLARES itself mutually
exclusive (see the client-ingest bead — it is declared, never assumed, and it is FALSE for
NYC condo lots), every within-source pair gets a structural cannot-link. That is a large,
free constraint set that prunes the search substantially.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- Deterministic pivot correlation clustering over the existing Support/AntiMerge lanes
- Hard cannot-link enforced structurally, with a test that overwhelming positive evidence
  cannot override it
- Achieved disagreement cost reported per tile; brute-force optimum comparison on small
  tiles
- The forfeited approximation guarantee stated honestly in docs and artifact
- Declared within-source mutual exclusion applied as a constraint set
- Per-entity-type cardinality diagnostic
- Chaining regression: a fixture where threshold-and-close produces one wrong giant cluster
  and correlation clustering does not
- Residual re-measured or reverted
close_reason: SUPERSEDED — ambition lane retired by measurement. Appendix L (E1-E3, 2026-08-16): point re-ranking is not the dominant failure mode (0/7 tile-addressable wins; 72/79 labeled failures unreachable/representation cases), so the residual harness gate this lane waited on resolved AGAINST it. PLAN_CANON_GEO.md section 11: assignment and clustering become named global constraints with exact propagators; bd-2kjx.3's factorized exact residual solver (src/geo/composition.rs) now does exact composition without search. Any revival must come from a measured E4/E5 residual that names this technique, not from this bead.

title: [CANON-V1/P09.8] Deferred option: Rust learned-predicate blocking
description:
## Background
Learned selection of blocking predicates could improve candidate recall per comparison budget, but the existing exact/token/ngram/sparse native lane must be measured first. This technique cannot precede or substitute for P12 candidate-recall forensics.

## Technical Approach
If a sealed failure slice justifies it after core acceptance, implement deterministic selection over a declared library of generic predicates. Optimize training must-link coverage under explicit pair, posting, memory, and runtime budgets. Pin training labels, split, predicate vocabulary, tie-breaking, objective, selected set, and artifact digest. Apply the learned artifact only to candidate generation; scoring, constraints, review, and promotion remain independent.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The learned predicate artifact never reads acceptance holdouts and reproduces exactly from pinned training inputs.
- Candidate recall improves materially on untouched evaluation data within declared budgets.
- Every selected predicate reports marginal recall, comparison cost, suppressed postings, and protected-feature effects.
- Overfit, empty, infeasible, hot-bucket, or tampered artifacts refuse or fall back according to explicit policy.
- No domain literal or learned alias enters Canon defaults.

## Test Plan
Greedy-set-cover parity fixtures; deterministic ties; redundant/conflicting predicates; rare and hot buckets; train/eval leakage; adversarial hard negatives; duplicate inflation; budget refusal; untouched-corpus recall and resource ablation.

## RESERVATIONS
No files while deferred. A selected packet must name candidate/index modules, artifact schema, fixtures, and current oracle/source pins.

## Considerations
High recall with an unbounded candidate universe is failure. This option is accepted only if it beats simpler native operators.

title: [SPLINK-STEAL/S4] entity block preflight: pre-run candidate cardinality and skew report
description:
## Problem this solves Blocking problems currently surface as mid-run refusals (E_ENTITY_CANDIDATE_BUDGET, E_ENTITY_INDEX_LIMIT) after real compute has been spent. On 100k+ row corpora (BDC investment names, CMBS tenants) the operator needs per-operator candidate-pair estimates and worst-block skew BEFORE executing, so strategies can be tuned cheaply and budget refusals become rare instead of routine during the grind. ## Build canon entity block preflight --profile

--strategy [--sample-pct N] [--emit json|summary] - Per blocking operator, in strategy order: estimated candidate count, marginal and cumulative (mirroring the run-path dedup semantics so numbers match reality). - Top-K largest blocks with their blocking-key values (skew hunting: the "JOHN SMITH" blocks). - Budget-headroom verdict against the configured candidate/index budgets: pass / tight / would-refuse. - Deterministic sampling when sample-pct < 100: hash-mod row selection, never RNG. ## Splink reference (clone at /Users/zac/Source/opensource/splink) - splink/blocking_analysis.py — count_comparisons_from_blocking_rules (deterministic 5% sample default, marginal + cumulative counts), n_largest_blocks (skew report) - docs/topic_guides/blocking/performance.md ## How to test - Engineered-skew fixture: a dominant block value appears in top-K with correct count. - Exactness at 100% sampling: estimates equal the real block stage's counts on the same fixture (parity with src/entity/block.rs diagnostics). - Determinism across runs and row shuffles at any sample-pct. - Budget verdict flips correctly when strategy budgets are lowered below the estimate. - Read-only guarantee: no work-dir mutation (or only the single preflight artifact when --work-dir passed explicitly). ## Doctrine constraints Read-only report; exit 0 report emitted / 2 refusal; deterministic sampling only. Distinct from bd-3j1e (declarative blocking for record-link scoring) and bd-1cvi (deferred learned-predicate blocking) — this bead only counts and reports. ## RESERVATIONS - src/entity/block_preflight.rs (new; shared helpers may touch src/entity/block.rs) - tests/entity_block_preflight.rs

title: Project skeleton + core types
description:
Pre-swarm foundation. Create Cargo.toml, src/main.rs, src/lib.rs with module stubs and ALL shared types that cross module boundaries. Must compile before agents start. This is the contract 8 agents code against.

Cargo.toml: name=canon, version=0.1.0, edition=2024. [[bin]] name=canon path=src/main.rs. Deps: clap 4 (derive), csv 1, serde 1 (derive), serde_json 1, rusqlite (bundled), blake3 1. Dev-deps: tempfile 3, assert_cmd 2, predicates 3. Release profile: opt-level=z, lto=true, codegen-units=1, panic=abort, strip=true.

src/main.rs: #![forbid(unsafe_code)], parse args via cli::Cli, call canon::run(), map exit code (0/1/2).

src/lib.rs: #![forbid(unsafe_code)], mod declarations (cli, input, registry, lookup, output, refusal, witness). pub fn run(cli: cli::Cli) -> Result<u8, Box<dyn Error>> stub returning Ok(0).

=== OUTPUT MODULE SPLIT (CRITICAL FOR PARALLELISM) ===

The output module MUST be a directory, not a flat file:
- src/output/mod.rs: pub mod json; pub mod csv;
- src/output/json.rs: stub for JSON emission (bd-2p4 agent's target)
- src/output/csv.rs: stub for CSV emission (bd-37k agent's target)

This split enables bd-2p4 and bd-37k to work in parallel without file conflicts.

=== SHARED TYPES (all pub, derives noted) ===

CRITICAL: Mapping.input and Mapping.canonical_id hold RAW byte values (no u8:/hex: prefix). Identifier encoding is applied ONLY by the JSON output module at serialization time. This keeps the in-memory types format-agnostic — CSV output reads raw values directly.

Output types:
- Outcome { Resolved, Partial, Unresolved, Refusal } — #[serde(rename_all = "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE")] so Resolved => "RESOLVED", etc.
- Mapping { input: String, canonical_id: String, canonical_type: String, rule_id: String, confidence: String } — NOTE: input/canonical_id are RAW values. JSON output applies u8:/hex: encoding via a custom serialization wrapper, NOT via the Mapping struct's Serialize impl.
- UnresolvedEntry { input: Option<String>, reason: String } — input is RAW or None for special reasons
- RegistryMeta { id: String, version: String, source: String } — source is CLI arg verbatim
- Summary { total: usize, resolved: usize, unresolved: usize }
- CanonOutput { version: String, outcome: Outcome, registry: Option<RegistryMeta>, summary: Option<Summary>, mappings: Vec<Mapping>, unresolved: Vec<UnresolvedEntry>, refusal: Option<Refusal> }

Refusal types:
- RefusalCode enum: EIo, EEncoding, ECsvParse, EBadRegistry, EColumnNotFound, EParse, EEmptyInput, ETooLarge, EEmitFormat, EColumnExists — custom Serialize to emit "E_IO", etc.
- Refusal { code: RefusalCode, message: String, detail: serde_json::Value, next_command: Option<String> }

Cross-module types (the 8-agent contract):
- InputFormat enum { Csv, Jsonl }
- SpecialReason enum { EmptyValue, NullValue, MissingField, NonScalarValue } — Display impl yields "empty_value", etc.
- InputValues { values: HashMap<String, ()>, special: HashMap<SpecialReason, usize>, format: InputFormat, delimiter: Option<u8> }
- Registry { meta: RegistryMeta, db_path: PathBuf }
- ResolveResult { mappings: Vec<Mapping>, unresolved: Vec<UnresolvedEntry>, summary: Summary }

Module stubs created: src/cli.rs, src/input.rs, src/registry.rs, src/lookup.rs, src/output/mod.rs, src/output/json.rs, src/output/csv.rs, src/refusal.rs, src/witness.rs. Each stub includes placeholder function signatures AND a #[cfg(test)] mod tests {} block.

VERIFICATION: cargo check must pass after this bead. All stubs compile, all types resolve.
acceptance_criteria:
cargo check --all-targets passes.
cargo fmt --check passes.
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings passes.
All 7 module files exist as stubs (cli.rs, input.rs, registry.rs, lookup.rs, output.rs, refusal.rs, witness.rs).
All shared types compile with appropriate derives (Serialize, Deserialize, Debug, Clone as needed).
Cross-module types present: InputFormat, SpecialReason, InputValues, Registry, ResolveResult.
canon::run() compiles and returns Ok(0).
src/main.rs calls run() and maps exit codes.
Module stubs have placeholder function signatures that match the pub fn exports in each feature issue.
notes:
Dev-dependency addition: proptest 1 (for property-based invariant testing in tests/properties.rs). Also add assert_cmd 2 and predicates 3 for integration tests. Design note: InputValues.values uses HashMap<String, ()> per spec. An agent may use IndexSet or HashSet internally but the cross-module contract type should remain HashMap for serde compatibility and ordering control.

CRITICAL: The Cli struct stub in src/cli.rs must include ALL fields listed in bd-3w0's description (input, registry, column, emit, canon_column, map_out, max_rows, max_bytes, no_witness, version, describe, schema) with correct types. This struct is the primary cross-bead contract — bd-27y reads cli.emit, cli.column, cli.registry, etc. Derive Cli struct fields from bd-3w0's description, function signatures from each feature bead's description.
close_reason: Project scaffold complete - Cargo.toml with edition 2024, all shared types defined in lib.rs, output module split for parallelism, all stub files created with test blocks. cargo check passes.

title: strategy CLI contract: key selection, grade selection, and lifecycle subcommands
description: Extend clap CLI structs and dispatch plumbing for task-keyed strategy operations and lifecycle commands. Current CLI requires --schema for resolve/register and requires --verify/--assess/--airlock for register. bd-a43 requires resolve --task <name> --skill <SKILL.md> and a register flow that can be operator-attested without proof tooling. RESERVATIONS: src/cli.rs, src/lib.rs.
design:
Recommended CLI: strategy resolve accepts exactly one key selector, --schema <PROFILE.json> or --task <TASK>; strategy register accepts exactly one key selector; register accepts --grade operator-attested|proof-attested; operator-attested register requires --operator and --reason and does not require proofs; proof-attested register requires --verify, --assess, and --airlock exactly as today. Add strategy update, strategy deprecate, strategy promote, strategy list, and strategy explain subcommands, or equivalent names matching the spec.

Manual validation is fine where clap groups are too tangled; refusals must be canon envelopes, not panics. Mutating commands should parse the documented witness suppression/override surface. Read-only list/explain should reject mutation-only flags and should never require proof artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: task resolve CLI parses; task operator-attested register CLI parses; list/explain parse with typed key and filter options; lifecycle commands parse with next-version and operator/reason requirements; existing schema-keyed proof-attested register/resolve CLI tests continue to parse; invalid combinations refuse, including both --task and --schema, neither key selector, invalid grade/status filters, operator-attested without operator/reason, proof-attested without proofs, task resolve with schema-only flags, and read-only commands with mutation-only flags; help and typed structs are clear enough for operator.json documentation.
notes: This bead wires arguments and dispatch. Core behavior can remain placeholder/refusal until behavior beads land.
close_reason: Implemented strategy v1 typed keys, operator/proof attestation grades, lifecycle, catalog/explain, receipts/witness, lint/diff/docs/tests; verified cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test, cargo build --release --locked, and UBS on changed files.

title: Resolve v0 tape loader and record projection
description:
Implement row-preserving tape loading for canon resolve reference and target tapes.

Background:
- canon resolve takes exactly two tapes: reference first, target second.
- Each tape can be CSV, TSV, JSONL, or NDJSON using the same format conventions as the rest of canon where practical.
- The strategy declares identity columns and structural columns used by filters and assertions.

Scope:
- Add src/resolve/tape.rs or equivalent module.
- Load reference and target tapes into deterministic Record structs containing side label, composite ID, source row index or source row ID, and BTreeMap attributes.
- Construct composite IDs from strategy-declared id_columns using a stable separator and explicit escaping or validation.
- Validate that identity columns and all strategy-referenced fields exist in the appropriate tape.
- Refuse empty tapes with E_EMPTY_TAPE.
- Refuse missing columns with E_COLUMN_NOT_FOUND and include side, missing column, and available columns in detail.
- Support max row and max byte limits if the scaffold exposes them.
- Keep parsing local and deterministic; no type inference beyond storing raw values and source provenance.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests cover CSV, TSV, JSONL/NDJSON, composite IDs, missing columns, empty tapes, duplicate composite IDs, row ordering, and stable attribute maps.
- The loaded record order is deterministic: file order captured for provenance, sorted composite order available for graph/scoring.
- The loader reuses existing input patterns where reasonable but does not mutate behavior of core input parsing.

Target files:
- src/resolve/tape.rs
- src/resolve/types.rs if needed
- tests/fixtures/resolve/tapes/** only if fixture adjustments are needed

Reservation guidance:
- Reserve only tape-loader files and exact fixture files touched.
close_reason: Implemented resolve tape loader in src/resolve/tape.rs: CSV/TSV and JSONL/NDJSON loading, required-column validation from strategy fields, deterministic composite IDs with separator validation, duplicate-ID refusal, empty-tape refusal, max-row/max-byte enforcement, file-order records plus sorted-ID view, and loaded tape summaries. Added unit coverage for CSV/JSONL fixtures, missing columns, empty tapes, duplicate/invalid IDs, row/byte limits, deterministic ordering, and two-tape loading. Validated with cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo test.

title: canon geo D6: dated collateral existence, vintage observations bound into physical collateral ledger rows
description:
PACKET PK-D6-dated (stage D6) from docs/PLAN_CANON_GEO.md §18.2 CMBS capabilities table row 2 and §18.4 kinds table rows 4 and 5, minted 2026-09-02 in the coverage pass. The capability "Dated collateral existence proof (the structure described in the 2019 offering document is not present in the 2024 ortho)" is built from "P1 plus the imagery observer lane" and waits on G6. No bead joined the two: the ledger row (bd-u0y1) carries `last_observed_present: Option<GeoValidTimeInterval>` but ledger.rs does not consume observer.rs (§19.3 dependency direction: adjudicate and card consume observer; exposure and collision consume ledger), and nothing filled the field. This bead owns the join. It carries the full design so no implementer needs the plan document.

== WHY ==
P1's row definition (§18.2): "the dated image vintage at which each structure was last observed present". A B-piece buyer running a workout wants to know whether the building the 2019 Annex A describes still stands. Today nobody can answer at loan grain because nobody has the building set (P1) and nobody has dated observations bound to it (D6). §18.4: `present_at_vintage` / `absent_at_vintage` are closed valid-time interval observations, diagnostic until the temporal solver lands, hard only as "absent at v implies not the 2019 structure" once dated. The Allen/STP temporal solver is DEFERRED (bd-1oy8) with trigger "the observer lane supplies dated existence observations for a population". This bead is that trigger's producer: it reports, it never constrains composition.

== DESIGN (respects the §19.3 dependency direction) ==
The join lives in a new generic module src/geo/existence.rs that consumes `observer` (rows) and `ledger` (rows) and is consumed by nothing else (like `inspect`). ledger.rs and observer.rs are not modified beyond additive `#[serde(default)]` fields (permitted by §19.3 "implementers may add #[serde(default)] fields, never remove or rename").
- Additive fields on `GeoLedgerRow` (bd-u0y1 schema updated additively): `building_last_observed: BTreeMap<String, GeoValidTimeInterval>` (per building id, the latest vintage with a `PresentAtVintage` row whose `window_blake3` matches the building's window), `absent_after_reference: Vec<GeoExistenceFlag>`, `existence_observation_ids: Vec<String>`.
- `GeoExistenceFlag { building_id, reference_vintage: GeoValidTimeInterval (the offering document date or the source release date the building set was asserted at), absent_vintage: GeoValidTimeInterval, observation_id, observer_id, diagnostic: bool (always true until bd-1oy8 lands; the field exists so the flip is a schema-visible event) }`.
- `pub fn bind_existence(row: &GeoLedgerRow, observations: &GeoObservationRowsArtifact, windows_by_building: &BTreeMap<String, String>, reference_vintage: &GeoValidTimeInterval) -> Result<GeoLedgerRow, GeoExistenceError>`: for each building in `building_set`, select rows with `kind` in `{PresentAtVintage, AbsentAtVintage}` whose `window_blake3` equals `windows_by_building[building]`; `last_observed_present` on the row becomes the MINIMUM over buildings of each building's latest present vintage (the vintage at which EVERY structure in the set was last seen; per-building detail stays in `building_last_observed`); an `AbsentAtVintage` row with `vintage.start > reference_vintage.end` for a building in the set produces a `GeoExistenceFlag`. A row with `reach == None` or an empty `building_set` is returned unchanged with `existence_observation_ids` empty (abstention, code `existence_no_building_set`). Rows from observers whose contract `output_kinds` does not include the vintage kinds are refused (`existence_observer_kind_mismatch`). The function never touches `residual_model_count`, `claim_class`, `hard_forced`, or `status`: a test asserts byte equality of those fields before and after.
- `canon geo existence --ledger <ledger.json> --observations <rows.json> --windows <map.json> --reference-vintage <YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD> --emit json`: emits the same `canon_geo_collateral_ledger.v0` artifact with the additive fields populated; `validate_ledger` (bd-u0y1) still passes.
- Deal rollup: `GeoDealRollup` gains additive per-truth-plane `absent_after_reference: u64` and `existence_unobserved: u64` counts; never a pooled total (I09, C14).

== ERROR CODES (module enum `GeoExistenceErrorCode`; class per §19.4) ==
| `existence_no_building_set` | `bind_existence` | `reach == None` or empty `building_set` | abstention: row unchanged, `existence_observation_ids` empty |
| `existence_observer_kind_mismatch` | `bind_existence` | an observation row's observer contract lacks `PresentAtVintage` or `AbsentAtVintage` in `output_kinds`, or the row is not in `diagnostic_only_ids` of its artifact | refusal; `detail["observation_id"]`, `detail["observer_id"]` |
| `existence_window_unbound` | `bind_existence` | a building in `building_set` has no entry in `windows_by_building` | abstention per building: building listed under `existence_unobserved` in the rollup; refusal when every building is unbound |
| `existence_would_constrain` | `bind_existence` | any composition field on the row differs after binding (guards the "diagnostic until bd-1oy8" rule) | refusal |

== CONTRACTS AND THREATS SERVED ==
C11 (vintage kinds stay diagnostic), C13 (rows with reach None carry no sets and gain nothing here), C14 (per-plane counts only), C22 (additive schema fields), C23, C25, I08, I09, N04, N05, N07, TH10 (a vintage observation cannot become a hard constraint through this path), TH12, TH22.

== TESTS (tests/geo_existence.rs; each test logs on failure) ==
| T38 (bead-defined, extends §19.6) | D6 | unit | a ledger row from Demo 0 case 4 (buildings `1006494` to `1006499`, `fixture.` pins); observation rows: `PresentAtVintage` 2022 and 2024 for five buildings, `PresentAtVintage` 2022 and `AbsentAtVintage` 2024 for `1006499`; `reference_vintage` 2019 | `last_observed_present == 2022 interval` (the minimum over buildings); `building_last_observed["1006494"] == 2024`; `absent_after_reference == [{ building_id: "1006499", absent_vintage: 2024, diagnostic: true }]`; `residual_model_count`, `claim_class`, `hard_forced`, `status` byte-identical before and after | an implementation that sets `last_observed_present` to the MAXIMUM (2024) fails; an `AbsentAtVintage` 2018 row (before the reference) must produce no flag | LOG on failure: per building the present and absent vintages seen, the computed minimum, the flag list, and a diff of the composition fields before and after |
| T39 (bead-defined) | D6 | unit | T38 row with `reach == None` and no sets; a second row whose observation comes from a contract with `output_kinds == [StructureCountInWindow]` only | first returns the row unchanged with `existence_no_building_set` as the abstention reason; second refuses `existence_observer_kind_mismatch` with `detail["observer_id"]` | a row whose observation id is absent from `diagnostic_only_ids` refuses the same code with `detail["observation_id"]` | LOG on failure: reach, building_set length, the observer contract's `output_kinds`, the `diagnostic_only_ids` list |
| T40 (bead-defined) | D6 | e2e | Demo 0 ledger of one synthetic accession over the T07 15 cases, observations for 3 buildings | `validate_ledger` passes after binding; the rollup's per-plane `absent_after_reference` and `existence_unobserved` sum to the observed counts, and no field named `total` serializes | a rollup that pools planes refuses `ledger_truth_plane_pooled` (bd-u0y1 code) | LOG on failure: the rollup per plane, the rows' truth planes, the count of rows bound, the ledger BLAKE3 before and after |

== E2E SCRIPT (scripts/geo_demo/e2e_existence.sh; `set -euo pipefail`; logs each command, exit code, artifact BLAKE3 into <work-dir>/run.log) ==
1. `bash scripts/geo_demo/demo0.sh --work-dir <dir>`; `bash scripts/geo_demo/e2e_ledger.sh --work-dir <dir>` (bd-u0y1) to produce `<dir>/ledger.json`.
2. Copy tests/fixtures/geo/existence_fixture_rows.json (vintage rows under `fixture.` pins) to <dir>.
3. `canon geo existence --ledger <dir>/ledger.json --observations <dir>/existence-rows.json --windows <dir>/windows.json --reference-vintage 2019-01-01..2019-12-31 --emit json > <dir>/ledger-dated.json`; log per row `last_observed_present`, the flag count, and `jq` equality of `residual_model_count` and `claim_class` between the two ledgers (exit 1 on any difference).
4. `canon geo ledger validate --ledger <dir>/ledger-dated.json`; `cargo test --test geo_existence -- --nocapture`; `cargo test --test geo_schemas collateral_ledger_schema_matches_a_real_instance`; whole-tree gates.
5. Live (not CI): the same over the G3 deal ledger with the NYC count observer's vintage rows; commit the dated ledger as retained evidence and post the flag count per truth plane on this bead and on bd-1oy8 (its trigger record).

== RESERVATIONS ==
src/geo/existence.rs, tests/geo_existence.rs, scripts/geo_demo/e2e_existence.sh, tests/fixtures/geo/existence_fixture_rows.json. Shared append-only touch points, reserve for the edit only: src/geo/mod.rs, src/geo/cli.rs (`geo existence`), src/operator.rs, tests/geo_schemas.rs, schemas/canon.geo.collateral_ledger.v0.schema.json (additive properties only; coordinate on thread bd-u0y1), the T27 scan list.

Depends on bd-u0y1 (ledger rows), bd-ci1n (observation rows), and the count observer bead (the only producer of vintage rows). bd-1oy8 depends on this bead (trigger).

ANTI-REWARD-HACKING (AGENTS.md, binding): a flag is a diagnostic report, never a composition change; do not add a `Forbid` from an absent vintage (that is bd-1oy8's work under its trigger). Fixture vintages are never cited as existence proof. Code and tests ship together. No new todo!() scaffolds.

title: [CANON-V1/P02] Project manifest and resumable identity compiler lifecycle
description:
## Background
Thirty-plus subcommands expose powerful plumbing but require operators to preserve hashes, paths, strategies, suites, and handoffs manually. A project manifest should make any identity program declarative and reproducible without hiding stage artifacts.

## Scope
Specify Canon project manifests and lockfiles; implement init/validate/plan/run/review/promote/apply/export lifecycle commands; build a deterministic DAG; resume only from hash-valid artifacts; pin registry, strategy, profile, policy, and extension dependencies; and surface dry-run plans, mutation boundaries, outputs, and recovery commands.

## Success Criteria
A fresh operator can configure and execute a complete neutral identity project from one manifest, and an out-of-tree domain project uses the same contract. Reruns reuse valid artifacts, reject stale state, and produce the same bytes. Plumbing commands remain available for inspection.

## Test Plan
Manifest/schema goldens, path and secret handling, plan determinism, crash/resume, stale locks, dry-run no-write behavior, neutral end-to-end project compilation, and optional private extension conformance with detailed stage logs.

title: [CANON-V1/P03.8] Prove strategies remain canonical, safe, reusable knowledge
description:
## Background
Keeping `canon strategy` is compelling only if one audited procedure can be selected reproducibly, reused across unrelated projects, improved through comparison, and explained without hidden execution authority.

## Technical Approach
Build an end-to-end fixture with two schema-compatible neutral inputs, multiple candidate strategy packages, a deterministic tournament, explicit promotion, project pinning, isolated audit, and explain/diff output. Then load an unknown external profile package to prove selection depends on typed contracts rather than built-in vocabulary.

## Success Criteria
- Exact-task and compatible-schema selection choose the expected champion with a verifiable chain.
- Tampered or capability-expanding packages are rejected before execution.
- Unrelated projects reuse one strategy digest and produce compatible evidence contracts.
- Every subprocess, artifact hash, metric, filesystem delta, and refusal path is logged.

## Test Plan
Run pack, verify, register, audit, tournament, promote, select, explain, project lock, and evidence execution through subprocesses. Include bad signature, timeout, stale audit, incompatible kind, unknown extension, and concurrent promotion cases.

## RESERVATIONS
- `tests/strategy_end_to_end.rs`
- `tests/fixtures/strategies/v1`
- `README.md`

## Considerations
Acceptance demonstrates procedural reuse, not merely registry CRUD, a mocked runner, or one industry's fixture vocabulary.

title: [CANON-V1/P07.7] Prove the standalone native engine at real scale and offline
description:
## Background
The native path cannot be called standalone if headline scale is based on virtual probes, direct module calls, or external engines. Operators need measured end-to-end behavior with realistic skew and artifacts.

## Technical Approach
Build streaming and bounded-memory execution for intake, indexes, blocking, evidence merge, solve/link, review selection, and artifact publication. Define benchmark tiers culminating in at least 500k real observations plus multi-source linkage, with heavy duplicate buckets, sparse anchors, Unicode, and hard negatives. Record wall time, peak RSS, disk I/O, artifact sizes, cache behavior, and determinism.

## Success Criteria
- The installed CLI completes published tiers without Python, network, or optional adapters.
- Configured budgets refuse before runaway allocation and partial outputs cannot masquerade as complete.
- Second runs demonstrate validated cache reuse and changed inputs invalidate exact descendants.
- Benchmark claims link to reproducible commands, corpus generator/version, hardware, and raw metrics.

## Test Plan
Run cold/warm, shuffled, skewed, low-memory, disk-pressure, interrupted/resumed, and read-only variants. Query outputs and compare hashes rather than only timing internal functions.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/entity/index.rs`
- `src/entity/block.rs`
- `src/entity/run.rs`
- `benches/entity_native.rs`
- `tests/entity_scale_e2e.rs`

## Considerations
Synthetic scale establishes systems behavior, not real-domain accuracy. Accuracy is evaluated through operator-owned gold corpora.

title: canon geo inspect — one-call status, explanation, comparison, and exact next actions
description:
WHY

Agents need one compact situation report, not a forensic tour of leaf artifacts. Existing doctor surfaces report generic binary health, not the epistemic or computational state of a Geo run.

DELIVER

Implement canon geo inspect --run RUN with optional --component ID, --compare OTHER_RUN, and --recommend-next. JSON is canonical; summary rendering is a projection.

The default response reports question/profile identity, requested and supported grains, pinned releases, phase state, reusable artifacts, coverage gaps, candidate reach, rho admission dispositions, component distribution, exactness/backbone/residual/conflict state, reconciliation, independent truth status, deterministic resource usage, budget remaining, blockers, and ordered next actions.

Every next action carries an exact command or acquisition request, required inputs, preconditions, expected output contract, deterministic cost ceiling, reason it can change the answer, and continuation state. Deep component views link summaries back to evidence and constraints without rerunning solve. Comparison explains evidence, invalidation, residual, backbone, claim-class, and resource-reuse deltas.

ACCEPTANCE

- Read-only inspection completes without rerunning acquisition, materialization, compilation, solving, or evaluation.
- Availability, coverage, candidate reach, admission, solver exactness, reconciliation, truth quality, and cost are separate fields.
- Negative test: exact solver output with unreachable truth cannot be summarized as an accurate resolution.
- Negative test: a matching payload digest cannot be summarized as semantic reconciliation proof.
- Negative test: a fixture or retained receipt is labeled by its actual proof class and never as fresh live proof.
- Missing/corrupt artifacts identify the first invalid dependency and a recovery command.
- Default output is bounded and paginates/addresses component detail rather than dumping unbounded models.
- Help, schema, operator manifest, exit semantics, and next-command metadata agree.

title: [CANON-V1/P03.7] Migrate existing strategy registries directly to typed v1
description:
## Background
The repository already has useful strategy registry behavior and fixtures. The new type system should preserve knowledge without perpetuating mixed v0/v1 code paths or compatibility wrappers.

## Technical Approach
Inventory every current schema/task entry and fixture, assign its typed kind, package its executable and dependencies, generate expected v1 receipts, and update callers, CLI schemas, tests, docs, and examples directly. Emit an offline migration plan and verify it before explicit write. Require deletion approval before removing legacy-only files.

## Success Criteria
- All maintained fixtures and examples operate solely through typed v1 contracts after migration.
- Unmappable or semantically ambiguous entries are reported, not guessed.
- No dual-read, fallback, wrapper, or indefinite v0 branch remains.
- Migrated champion selection and audit outcomes match frozen expectations.

## Test Plan
Run migration dry-run twice, inspect proposed files and hashes, then exercise every migrated fixture through select, explain, audit, and project lock. Search code/docs for legacy schema identifiers and record justified historical references.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/strategy.rs`
- `src/cli.rs`
- `tests/strategy_registry.rs`
- `docs/PLAN_CANON.md`

## Considerations
Because this is early development, prefer a clean direct contract change. Actual deletion of legacy files still requires the explicit permission mandated by AGENTS.md.
