title: [CANON-V1/P11.6] Build a locked release preflight and artifact verification workflow
description:
## Background
A release should be impossible when code formatting, warnings, tests, contracts, packages, docs, benchmarks, or generated artifacts disagree. Current green tests alone are not sufficient.

## Technical Approach
Implement one local/CI release preflight that runs Rust 2024 toolchain checks, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, all required tests/features, command-contract parity, schema/golden checks, package build/verify, offline native acceptance, safety matrix, benchmark smoke thresholds, license/dependency audit, clean-tree reproducibility, and release artifact smoke tests. Use locked dependencies and record a signed/checksummed report.

## Success Criteria
- The same preflight command runs locally and in CI with named optional/external exclusions.
- Any failed gate blocks packaging/publishing and identifies exact reproduction commands.
- Built binaries/packages are tested from release artifacts, not only the workspace target.
- Version, lockfile, changelog/release notes, schemas, and media types agree.

## Test Plan
Deliberately break one gate of each class in isolated fixtures/workflow tests, run clean preflight, install produced artifacts into a fresh temp environment, and execute smoke/verify journeys.

## RESERVATIONS
- `xtask/src/main.rs`
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`
- `scripts/release-preflight.sh`
- `tests/release_artifact.rs`

## Considerations
Prefer an existing Rust task runner/file if present; creating scripts or xtask files requires confirming the repository's current structure and no-file-proliferation rule.

title: canon strategy audit — verify frozen scripts against deterministic suites
description:
Add an audit command for frozen strategy scripts before registration or promotion.

Context:
canon strategy register validates proof artifact decisions and hashes, but the project still lacks a native audit surface that can run or evaluate a frozen script against a locked suite and produce the proof artifact expected by registration.

Acceptance Criteria:
- CLI: canon strategy audit --schema <PROFILE.json> --script <SCRIPT> --suite <DIR> [--emit json|summary].
- Emits canon_strategy_audit.v0 with script hash, schema fingerprint, suite hash, deterministic output hash, pass/fail metrics, and gate decision.
- Supports at least fixture-based expected-output checks and repeatability checks for the same input.
- Produces proof fields compatible with canon strategy register verify/assess/airlock expectations or clearly documents how those artifacts are derived.
- Refuses malformed suites or nondeterministic outputs with structured refusals.
- Tests cover passing, failing, malformed suite, and deterministic repeatability cases.

Emits canon_strategy_audit.v0 with script hash, schema fingerprint, suite hash, deterministic output hash, pass/fail metrics, and proof fields compatible with strategy register verify/assess/airlock. Supports expected stdout/exit checks and repeatability refusal for nondeterministic outputs. title: [CANON-V1/P00.9] Prove single-engine cutover with an executable no-theatre operator journey
description:
## Background
The cutover is complete only when real binaries execute every stage and downstream handoff. Static command strings and direct module calls are insufficient evidence.

## Technical Approach
Create a neutral fixture-backed subprocess journey covering profile selection, prepare, index, block, evidence, solve/cluster, run equivalence, review export/import, audit, promote, exact apply, and explain. Capture command, exit code, stdout/stderr route, artifact hashes, mutation diff, runtime, and next-command validation. Run twice for byte stability and once with stale/tampered failures. Prove core lookup and registry exports are unchanged.

## Success Criteria
- Every advertised entity command is executed, not merely parsed.
- Run wrapper and manual stages agree.
- Final applied output resolves only reviewed/promoted entities and preserves raw fields.
- Legacy engine selection is impossible and legacy artifacts refuse explicitly.
- A detailed acceptance transcript is available in CI logs.

## Test Plan
Run one small normal-CI journey plus a larger release tier; inject faults at each mutation boundary; cover cross-platform paths/encodings; and regression-test exact lookup plus dbt/search exports.

No network, Python, model runtime, or domain package is required in native acceptance. Obtain explicit written permission before deleting obsolete files.

title: [CANON-V1/P12.6] Build evidence ablation and failure-driven improvement loop
description:
## Background
A resolver can look sophisticated while most of its measured lift comes from exact aliases or name similarity. Canon needs evidence that each retrieval and scoring family improves real same-entity decisions, and a disciplined loop that converts misses into general capabilities rather than domain-specific patches.

## Technical Approach
Build reproducible ablations for exact alias, normalized name, character and token similarity, TF-IDF or equivalent sparse retrieval, trusted identifiers, address and web-domain anchors, contextual co-occurrence, source priors, relationship evidence, and the union of candidate operators. Report candidate recall, decision precision and recall, abstention, calibration, review volume, runtime, and memory by evaluation stratum and ambiguity class. Every false negative, false positive, and avoidable abstention receives a stage-local reason code: normalization, retrieval, evidence extraction, scoring, constraint, cluster, link, or policy. Improvements must be expressed as generic operators or external profile configuration and re-run against unchanged development suites; sealed holdouts remain untouched until a declared gate.

## Success Criteria
- Name-only, retrieval-only, anchor-only, contextual, relationship-aware, and full-system baselines are comparable from one public command.
- Reports show marginal quality and resource impact for every evidence family.
- At least the largest miss classes have reproducible fixtures and an owner bead before thresholds are tuned.
- Relationship evidence cannot silently become an equivalence merge signal.
- Domain strings, identifiers, or thresholds do not enter Canon defaults as a benchmark shortcut.
- Machine output identifies which stage lost each labeled true pair or admitted each false merge.

## Test Plan
Use planted cases where each evidence family is uniquely necessary, misleading, absent, duplicated, and contradictory. Shuffle input and evidence order; run cold and warm caches; remove one feature family at a time; verify invariant accounting and deterministic artifact digests. Confirm hidden-label files are never read by candidate generation or solving.

## RESERVATIONS
- src/entity/eval.rs
- src/entity/evidence.rs
- src/entity/candidate.rs
- tests/entity_evidence_ablation.rs
- tests/fixtures/canon_v1/quality/ablation_cases.json
- docs/ENTITY_EVALS_AND_PERFORMANCE.md

## Considerations
Ablation is diagnostic, not a license to add every feature. Prefer the smallest general feature that removes a measured failure class without increasing severe false merges.

title: [SPLINK-STEAL/S9] namekit/strategy ops: damerau-levenshtein, transposed-digit dates, reversal views
description:
## Problem this solves
Specific error families in the queued corpora have known cheap deterministic detectors that canon lacks:
1. Transposed characters/digits — plain Levenshtein counts a transposition as 2 edits and overweights it; Damerau-Levenshtein counts 1. Canon namekit has levenshtein_normalized/jaro_winkler/dice_sorensen/token_sort_ratio/token_set_ratio but NO damerau variant.
2. Date digit transpositions — maturity/origination dates in BDC/CMBS tapes ("2031-01-12" vs "2031-01-21") fail calendar-distance checks but are trivially caught by damerau<=1 on the STRING form.
3. Reversed name-part order — "SMITH JOHN" vs "JOHN SMITH" style reversals need a reversal view to block and score.
Each detector shrinks the escrow band for a real error class instead of forcing looser global thresholds.

## Build
a) Add DamerauLevenshteinNormalized to namekit similarity metrics: extend SimilarityMetric enum + rapidfuzz adapter in src/namekit/similarity.rs (rapidfuzz-rust supports it), same integer NAMEKIT_SCORE_SCALE, cutoff, and ASCII/Unicode path rules; extend the rapidfuzz parity fixture corpus.
b) Date evidence op variant: on calendar-distance miss, compare canonical string forms with damerau<=1; hit scores as its own authored band and is recorded distinctly in evidence artifacts (so explain/S7 shows "transposed-digit date match", never conflated with a real date-range hit).
c) Normalization view op(s) for token reversal usable in blocking and support evidence (reversal view on two-token names), strategy-authored like existing views.

## Splink reference (clone at /Users/zac/Source/opensource/splink)
- splink/internals/comparison_level_library.py — DamerauLevenshteinLevel (:431), ColumnsReversedLevel (:363, note symmetrical option)
- splink/internals/comparison_library.py — DateOfBirthComparison (:712; damerau<=1 on string form BEFORE calendar bands is the exact trick), ForenameSurnameComparison (:1090)

## How to test
- Damerau parity fixtures alongside existing rapidfuzz_metrics.jsonl conventions (tests/namekit_similarity.rs).
- Transposed-date fixture: string-form pair hits the new band while the plain date_range op misses; evidence artifact labels it distinctly.
- Reversal-view fixture: reversed names block+score only when the strategy enables the view.
- Absent-config no-op: strategies not using the new ops produce byte-identical artifacts (regression guard).
- Determinism replay.

## Doctrine constraints
All ops deterministic, integer-scored, strategy-authored; no default-behavior changes; similarity remains support evidence only (cannot override cannot-link/anchor conflicts per docs/namekit/similarity-decision.md guardrails).

## RESERVATIONS
- src/namekit/similarity.rs
- src/entity/evidence.rs
- tests/namekit_similarity.rs
- tests/entity_domain_ops.rs

title: [SPLINK-STEAL] Splink capability steals: minimize review burden, canon standalone
description:
## Background
Operator direction 2026-07-26: large entity-resolution projects are queued (BDC loan/investment names + instrument types; CMBS tenants, sponsors, servicers — see starter packs bd-18zf, bd-19rv). Concern: the entity workbench escrows too much to human review for corpus-scale grinding.

Head-to-head analysis of Splink 5.0.0.dev4 (local clone pinned at /Users/zac/Source/opensource/splink) concluded: canon's matching operators are already competitive (rapidfuzz metrics, TF-IDF cosine, ngram blocking). The review-burden gap is (1) calibration — hand-guessed integer weights force conservative thresholds, (2) review ergonomics — per-item review instead of per-pattern, (3) candidate diagnostics — budget problems surface mid-run instead of preflight. Splink's grinding power comes from calibrated weights (EM + term-frequency adjustment), not stronger comparators.

## Goal
Land bounded standalone features so canon ALONE grinds the queued corpora at the fixed canon.entity.quality.v1 gates (auto-link precision >= 0.995, recall >= 0.98, zero critical false merges) with minimum human review. End state: Splink not needed for most use cases; canon runs standalone.

## Doctrine guardrails (bind every child)
- Exact lookup kernel untouched; all work is workbench/build-time.
- Deterministic: integer score units, byte-stable artifacts, no floats across artifact boundaries, no wall-clock or randomness (hash-based sampling only).
- Anything learned or suggested emits PROPOSALS (reports, proposed strategy YAML); the operator reviews and freezes them as versioned inputs. Zero decision/registry/promotion authority for any new component.
- Cannot-link, protected tokens, anchor conflicts, budgets, and review gates cannot be overridden by any new evidence, weighting, or calibration.

## Relationship to existing beads
- bd-2q7r / P09 (deferred matcher techniques) remains the deep post-v1 lane: bd-1rlk (full Fellegi-Sunter/EM evidence operator), bd-3ofg (generic external-matcher adapter contract), bd-tv1m (active-learning review prioritization), bd-1cvi (learned-predicate blocking). Children here are the pragmatic near-term slice and do NOT select those options or grant any external tool authority.
- bd-3q3k (P12.7 cost-sensitive band calibration) is the acceptance-grade successor of the S1 sweep.
- bd-fung (P04.8) and closed bd-14m6 own the review substrate that S2/S7/S10 extend — no second renderer, no second decision-import format.

## Ordering
- P1: S1 gold threshold sweep, S2 pattern-grouped review
- P2: S3 value-level frequency evidence, S4 blocking preflight, S5 external-candidate import recipe (disposable Splink bridge, docs+fixtures only)
- P3: S6 EM weight suggestion, S7 waterfall decomposition, S8 unlinkables, S9 domain comparison ops, S10 cluster shape metrics
- P4: S11 score-pair primitive

Children are standalone: any can be taken up independently in any order; no hard inter-child dependencies. Shared-file coordination noted per bead (S1/S6 share calibrate.rs; S2/S7 share review_export.rs — serialize if concurrently in flight).

title: [CANON-V1/P01.5] Preserve and strengthen dbt-seed registry export
description:
## Background
dbt seed generation is an explicit retained capability and a primary way canonical knowledge enters warehouse transforms. V1 must strengthen provenance and package linkage without breaking deterministic rows or anti-collapse scaffolds.

## Technical Approach
- Port dbt-seed export onto the shared backend.
- Embed registry/package id, version, digest, canonical IRI provenance, source file, rule, alias kind, and normalized key in deterministic columns or companion metadata as appropriate.
- Preserve optional schema.yml and anti-collapse SQL generation.
- Add project-manifest output selection and post-promotion invocation.

## Success Criteria
- Current dbt-seed fixtures remain semantically compatible.
- Seeds are stable across paths and cache states.
- Generated dbt scaffolds execute and detect canonical collapse.
- Consumers can trace every row to an immutable registry package.

## Test Plan
- Golden CSV/schema/SQL comparisons.
- Run generated dbt tests in a fixture project where tooling is available; otherwise validate SQL contract deterministically.
- Filter, quoting, Unicode, and large-registry tests.
- Old/new export regression.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/registry/export.rs`
- `tests/registry_export_dbt.rs`
- `tests/fixtures/registry_export/dbt/expected_seed.csv`
- `tests/fixtures/registry_export/dbt/expected_schema.yml`
- `tests/fixtures/registry_export/dbt/expected_tests.sql`

## Considerations
- Do not put secrets or raw provider responses in dbt metadata.
- Document whether provenance is columns, comments, or sidecars.
- Keep namespace mandatory where it prevents cross-domain collapse.

description:
## Background
Canon needs strong positive, negative, and contextual evidence while allowing each deployment to decide which fields and combinations matter. A product-specific score function would defeat the extension boundary.

## Technical Approach
Define an evidence-policy package that maps profile fields/views/namespaces/relations to generic exact, token, vector, structural, temporal, anchor, context, protected-conflict, and cannot-link operators. Separate candidate generation, evidence emission, decision thresholds, abstention, and review rules. Require typed evidence IR output from every operator.

## Success Criteria
- A new policy can combine supported primitives without modifying engine dispatch.
- Positive, negative, contextual, and missing evidence remain separate and explainable.
- Hard vetoes and auto-decision authority are explicit policy clauses, not implicit weights.
- Unsupported capabilities are rejected at plan time.

## Test Plan
Run boundary, ablation, hard-negative, missing-field, conflicting-anchor, resource-limit, and package-version fixtures across multiple neutral profiles. Snapshot explanations and determinism.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/extensions/evidence_policy.rs`
- `schemas/canon.evidence.policy.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/extensions_evidence_policy.rs`

## Considerations
Canon supplies safe primitives and orchestration; the operator owns domain thresholds and evidentiary meaning.
notes:
## Demanding-deployment requirement ownership
Owns the generic operator side of R4. Repeated co-observation or co-holding across independent sources may contribute contextual evidence only when represented generically, provenance is retained, and a sealed-corpus ablation demonstrates lift. It is never identity authority, a hard match, or a promotion bypass.

title: canon geo: property as a first-class minted entity — document-scoped, tile-spanning, membership abstention
description:
RESOLVES A DIRECT SPEC CONFLICT AND SCOPES GENUINELY DIFFERENT WORK.

THE CONFLICT: bd-67wx says "RECOMMEND DEFERRING cmdrvl:property:* IN v1 ... Do not invent
an entity we cannot verify." OC-0048's Keying section says "Property | the loan document |
no external authority | **Yes** — cmdrvl:property:*" and states: "Property is nevertheless
first-class, by operator decision 2026-08-14. An earlier draft deferred it ... That
reasoning was sound about VERIFICATION and wrong about SCOPE: the CMBS tape IS a list of
properties, every corpus this outcome keys is a property list, and the buyer's file is a
property list. Deferring the entity while shipping a per-row location column does not
remove the ambiguity — it relocates it into the client's join, where it is worse because
it is invisible."

OC-0048 IS THE LATER DECISION AND GOVERNS. bd-67wx has been annotated. This bead owns the
work.

WHY PROPERTY IS NOT JUST A THIRD INSTANCE OF THE PARCEL/BUILDING PATTERN — four ways it
genuinely differs:

1. IT IS NOT SPATIALLY LOCAL. Parcels and buildings resolve within one H3 tile; that is
   the entire basis of bd-2b9d's blocking and of the epic's "embarrassingly parallel"
   claim. A PROPERTY CAN SPAN TILES — a loan on a campus, a portfolio property, a
   multi-parcel assemblage. The tile-local blocking strategy DOES NOT APPLY, and pretending
   it does will silently truncate collateral. Property blocking must be by DOCUMENT
   (deal/loan/project id) first and geography second.
2. ITS BOUNDARY IS ASSERTED, NOT INFERRED. The loan document defines its own collateral.
   Provenance for a property is THE DOCUMENT. The correct posture toward a conflicting
   document is A SECOND ASSERTION, NOT AN OVERWRITE — two deals may describe overlapping
   collateral differently and both are correct as of their own documents.
3. ABSTENTION IS ABOUT MEMBERSHIP, NOT LOCATION (OC-0048's phrasing). "We know where these
   three parcels are; we are not certain all three are in this property." That is a
   different abstention shape than every other geo abstention and needs its own reason
   code (see the coverage-abstention bead's vocabulary).
4. THE REGISTRY CANNOT HOLD IT AS ONE ROW. OC-0048 flags this explicitly and leaves it
   open: "A property spanning three parcels cannot be one registry row without either
   fan-out or collapse — the same pathology this document rejects when it rejects the wide
   crosswalk. So the property answer necessarily lives partly in the RELATION GRAPH, which
   is workbench output rather than registry output."

THE OPEN QUESTION THIS BEAD MUST ANSWER — and it is the most consequential product
question in the epic: IS THE RELATION GRAPH PART OF THE DELIVERED PRODUCT, OR INTERNAL
WORKBENCH STATE? bd-3soj leaves it open at the API boundary. It cannot stay open, because
the property answer is unusable without it.
  Option A — registry only. The property alias resolves to a minted cmdrvl:property:* id,
    and members are discoverable only by consulting the workbench artifact. Preserves
    canon's flat-and-exact runtime promise perfectly. Weak product: the client gets an id
    with no way to ask what is in it.
  Option B — registry plus a published relation projection. The registry stays flat and
    exact; a DERIVED, REGENERABLE membership view ships alongside it (exactly the
    "derived convenience view" bd-67wx already sanctions for the crosswalk). Nothing
    probabilistic reaches runtime lookup; the graph is a published artifact with its own
    version.
  RECOMMEND OPTION B. It is consistent with the doctrine bd-67wx already sets for the
  crosswalk, it keeps the runtime promise intact, and it is the difference between
  shipping an identifier and shipping an answer. But decide deliberately and record it —
  this sets the precedent for whether canon ever publishes graph output.

ALSO IN SCOPE:
- Property-to-member relation types over the vocabulary bd-3soj defines (a property
  CONTAINS parcels and buildings; note the direction differs from building PART_OF parcel).
- What happens when two source documents assert overlapping but unequal collateral —
  the second-assertion posture from point 2, implemented, not just described.
- The `Various` address population: Annex A rows recorded as `Various` never geocoded and
  are, in many cases, EXACTLY the multi-property rows this entity type exists to model.
  They need the Annex A parse (edgar-elt br-6iii), not geometry. Record the dependency.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- bd-67wx updated to mint property in v1; the contradiction closed in both places
- Document-first blocking strategy for property, with the tile-local assumption explicitly
  disclaimed
- Membership abstention reason code implemented
- A written, recorded decision on Option A vs B for the relation graph as product
- Conflicting-assertion behaviour implemented with both assertions retained
- A fixture: one loan whose collateral spans three parcels in two H3 tiles, resolving to
  one property cluster with correct membership and no fan-out

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
OPERATOR INSIGHT 2026-08-14 — PROPERTY IS CONSTITUTED, NOT RESOLVED. THIS SETTLES THE
WOBBLE AND CHANGES THE ID CONSTRUCTION.

THE OBSERVATION: "property" is singular and plural at once — a property is one asset, my
property is a holding. The domain word carries both because THE THING IS A SET.

WHAT FOLLOWS, AND IT RESOLVES WHAT bd-67wx AND OC-0048 KEPT DISAGREEING ABOUT:

PARCEL and BUILDING are RESOLVED ENTITIES. They have external authorities (BBL, BIN,
Overture GERS, FEMA UUID), so "is this the same one as that one?" is a real question with
a checkable answer. canon geo resolves them, and that is where all the uncertainty lives.

PROPERTY HAS NO AUTHORITY. The document names it. So THERE IS NO IDENTITY QUESTION TO
ADJUDICATE at the property layer — only MEMBERSHIP. OC-0048 already says property
abstention is about membership rather than location; this explains why, and the why is
what makes it designable.

bd-67wx's original instinct ("do not invent an entity we cannot verify") and OC-0048's
correction ("property is first-class; the CMBS tape IS a list of properties") are BOTH
RIGHT and were only in tension because both treated property as a third instance of the
same pattern. It is not the same pattern:

  cmdrvl:parcel:*    a CLUSTER of aliases     identity IS the cluster; source IDs are
  cmdrvl:building:*                            participants bound by evidence
  cmdrvl:property:*  a SET of clusters         members are already-minted cluster IDs;
                                               constituted by a document, not resolved

First-class does NOT mean resolved-independently. Property gets minted and it is the unit
the client cares about, AND it is derived from members that were resolved beneath it.

== THE RESULT THAT FALLS OUT: PROPERTY IDENTITY REDUCES TO SET EQUALITY ==

If the property IS the set, then two documents describe the same property IF AND ONLY IF
their member sets are equal, over stable minted IDs. That is EXACT.

  same property            member sets equal
  refi that added a lot    superset — exactly computable
  two deals overlapping    exact intersection, no adjudication
  collateral released      subset

THERE IS NO PROBABILISTIC MATCHING AT THE PROPERTY LAYER AT ALL. All uncertainty is spent
below, resolving parcels and buildings. Above that line it is set algebra over stable IDs.
canon's runtime promise survives completely intact, because nothing at the property layer
needs to guess.

This also makes bd-1oid's "second assertion, not an overwrite" posture TRIVIAL rather than
hard: you do not reconcile conflicting documents, you mint two sets and let set algebra
describe their relationship. Conflict detection becomes a set operation, not a decision.

MINTING RULE THAT FOLLOWS: mint one cmdrvl:property:* PER DOCUMENT ASSERTION. A 2015 deal
and a 2022 refi describing the same collateral get two IDs, which is CORRECT — they are
two collateral packages. If their member sets happen to be equal, that is DISCOVERABLE
EXACTLY at query time and needs no resolution step. Do not attempt to adjudicate "same
property across documents"; that would reintroduce the identity question this construction
just eliminated.

== IT GENERALIZES UPWARD ==
A portfolio is a set of properties — same construction one level up, same `contains`
relation (bd-3soj), no new entity type. That the construction generalizes without
special-casing is evidence it is the right one.

== WHAT IT ADDS: TWO DIFFERENT TEMPORAL SHAPES ==
A parcel cluster's IDENTITY is stable and its ALIASES accrete over time. A property's
MEMBERSHIP changes — collateral released, adjacent lot acquired, parcel split. Those
version differently and bd-12gh must model BOTH shapes, not one. "Which cluster did this
alias belong to in 2019" and "what were this property's members in 2019" are different
queries against different mechanisms.

== CONSEQUENCE FOR THE OUTPUT SURFACE (bd-kwmc) ==
The genuinely valuable queries are set operations over minted IDs, and they are exact:
does deal A's collateral intersect deal B's; is this HUD project a subset of this CMBS
property; what is the union of parcels a sponsor touches. That is the whole cross-corpus
join OC-0048 promises, and it is arithmetic rather than inference.

title: [CANON-V1/P10.3] Add deterministic Arrow and Parquet registry projections
description:
## Background
Analytical users may prefer columnar data for large registries, facts, relations, assignments, evidence summaries, and unresolved queues. This should be another backend, not a new semantic model.

## Technical Approach
Implement Arrow schema definitions and deterministic Parquet projection through the shared export backend. Pin field ordering/types/nullability, dictionary/statistics/row-group/compression settings that affect bytes, provenance metadata, and extension columns. Support streaming writes with explicit memory/row-group limits.

## Success Criteria
- Parquet/Arrow rows agree with JSON/dbt/search projections on IDs and registry snapshot.
- Equivalent inputs produce deterministic logical content and, where tooling permits, byte-stable output under pinned writer settings.
- Unknown domain extension IDs and temporal fields round-trip without loss.
- Export is offline, bounded, atomic, and never mutates the registry.

## Test Plan
Read generated files with an independent Arrow implementation, compare tables, shuffle inputs, test nulls/Unicode/large sets/extensions, corrupt metadata, and measure memory. Document any unavoidable byte nondeterminism while enforcing logical hashes.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/registry/export_parquet.rs`
- `schemas/canon.export.parquet.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/export_parquet.rs`

## Considerations
Dependency weight should be feature-gated and justified; a subprocess bridge may be preferable if a Rust dependency is disproportionate.

title: [CANON-V1/P00] Contract truth and single artifact-backed entity engine
description:
## Background
The public entity namespace currently selects between a legacy org-derived runtime and a newer artifact-backed workbench based on optional flags. Several downstream commands deserialize the legacy artifact shape while both shapes claim the same schema version. Machine metadata, help text, docs, and checked-in runbooks also disagree. This lane establishes one source of truth before new capability is built.

## Scope
Inventory every public and internal contract; define a single versioned artifact family; remove invocation-dependent engine selection; wire every advertised entity stage to the artifact-backed implementation; make the complete lifecycle executable; generate or verify help, operator metadata, schemas, refusals, and docs from the real command model.

## Success Criteria
There is one entity engine, one artifact contract per version, no active org terminology, no advertised-but-missing commands, and a subprocess E2E journey proves prepare/index/block/edge/solve/run/review/audit/promote/apply/explain. Core exact lookup remains byte-identical.

## Test Plan
Golden schema snapshots, CLI contract parity, stale/wrong-artifact refusals, no-mutation tests, deterministic repeated runs, and full operator-journey subprocess tests with stage logs and hashes.

title: canon registry next-id: deterministic id-allocator for self-authored registries
description:
Add `canon registry next-id [PREFIX]` as a read-only helper for self-authored registries.

Purpose:
- Operators who own a registry need a deterministic way to choose the next canonical ID under a local convention such as `PPL-001`, `IC-002`, or `CPTY-00042`.
- This command does not create an entity and does not mutate registry files. It only inspects the current flat mapping entries and suggests the next available ID.

CLI:
`canon registry next-id [PREFIX] --registry <DIR> [--zero-pad <N>] [--emit plain|json]`

Behavior:
- Read `registry.json` and all flat mapping files using the same discovery exclusions and filename ordering as the normal registry loader: all root `*.json` except `registry.json` and `_build.json`; subdirectories ignored.
- Validate `PREFIX` as `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*$`.
- If `PREFIX` is omitted, read `registry.json.default_id_scheme.prefix` and `zero_pad` when present; otherwise refuse with a next-command that includes an explicit prefix.
- `--zero-pad` overrides the scheme width for this read-only suggestion. Default width is 3.
- Collect distinct `canonical_id` values, filter IDs matching exactly `<PREFIX>-<digits>`, compute the numeric max, and return max + 1 padded to the selected width.
- If no matching IDs exist, return `<PREFIX>-001` or the selected zero-padded equivalent.
- Refuse if any canonical ID starts with `<PREFIX>-` but the suffix is not all ASCII digits. This prevents silently skipping malformed IDs inside the selected namespace.
- Do not write registry files, do not update `_index.sqlite`, and do not add new witness behavior in this bead. Keep side effects read-only.

Output:
- Default `--emit plain`: print only the suggested ID plus newline, for shell composition.
- `--emit json`: emit `canon_registry_next_id.v0` with `registry`, `scheme`, `current_max`, `next_id`, `entry_count_matching_prefix`, and `warnings` fields.
acceptance_criteria:
- `canon registry next-id PPL --registry <DIR>` returns `PPL-001` for a valid empty registry.
- Existing IDs are scanned across all root mapping files and the command returns max + 1 deterministically.
- Duplicate canonical IDs are counted once for max computation, while `entry_count_matching_prefix` reports distinct IDs in the namespace.
- `--zero-pad` is honored, including widths larger than 3.
- Omitted prefix uses `registry.json.default_id_scheme` when present and refuses with a concrete next-command when absent.
- Malformed in-namespace IDs such as `PPL-ABC` or `PPL-12A` cause a refusal; out-of-namespace IDs are ignored.
- JSON output matches a golden fixture for `canon_registry_next_id.v0`.
- Plain output contains only the ID and newline.
- The command has no filesystem writes except normal Beads/test fixture setup; `_index.sqlite` is not created as a side effect of next-id.
- Quality gate passes: `cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test`.
notes:

title: canon geo: entity lifecycle — buildings are born and die, containment is temporal, one BBL is many collateral positions
description:
OPERATOR CASE 2026-08-14 — THE ONE THAT BREAKS BBL-AS-THE-ANSWER.

"A property could start as just a parcel and end up as a parcel with seven buildings one
year later. And then it could be financed in two separate ways. Building one goes into a
REIT, building two goes into CMBS, and building three has an RCA sales comp on it."

This single case falsifies three assumptions that are load-bearing elsewhere in the epic.

== 1. ENTITIES ARE BORN AND DIE. THE TILE IS NOT A STATIC SCENE. ==
A parcel persists (until merger or apportionment). BUILDINGS DO NOT — they are constructed
and demolished. A bare parcel in 2019 and a seven-building parcel in 2020 are the same
parcel cluster with a completely different containment graph beneath it.

So as-of resolution is THREE distinct queries, not one, and bd-12gh currently models only
the first and third:
  (a) DID THIS ENTITY EXIST AT TIME T?              existence interval per cluster
  (b) WHAT CONTAINED WHAT AT TIME T?                the containment graph is itself
                                                     temporal — NEW, unmodelled
  (c) WHAT WAS THIS PROPERTY'S MEMBERSHIP AT TIME T? the set model (bd-67wx/bd-1oid
                                                     comments 2026-08-14)
A resolution that returns today's containment graph for a 2019 assertion is not merely
stale — it is confidently wrong, and it looks identical to a correct answer.

== 2. THE PARCEL IS NOT THE UNIT OF FINANCIAL INTEREST. THE BUILDING IS. ==
Seven buildings on one BBL, financed separately: a REIT holds one, a CMBS trust holds
another, a third shows up as an RCA sales comp. THEY ALL SHARE A BBL AND THEY ARE NOT THE
SAME COLLATERAL.

CONSEQUENCE — RESOLVING AT THE PARCEL LEVEL CREATES FALSE MERGES ACROSS CORPORA. Collapsing
those three positions onto one BBL and treating them as one property would double-count
exposure, corrupt holder attribution (OC-0047), and corrupt pool composition (OC-0046).
The cross-corpus join this outcome exists to enable would be POISONED BY THE VERY KEY IT
SHIPS. This is the strongest possible argument for the entity-level model — levels cannot
collapse, and a BBL column is not the deliverable.

== 3. THE PROVING GROUND'S METRIC CAN PASS WHILE THE PRODUCT FAILS. ==
bd-bmee scores "assign a BBL to CMBS collateral, scored against PLUTO." In this case ALL
THREE positions resolve to the SAME CORRECT BBL and all three score as correct — while the
actual question (WHICH BUILDING?) goes entirely untested. The kill criterion could be
satisfied by a system that cannot do the thing the product is for.
BBL is what can be scored against free ground truth. BUILDING is what the client needs.
Those are different, and the evaluation must say so. See the amendment filed on bd-bmee.

== WHAT TO BUILD ==
1. EXISTENCE INTERVALS on building-level clusters: first-observed / last-observed, and
   where authoritative sources exist, actual birth and death dates.
2. TEMPORAL CONTAINMENT EDGES. building part_of parcel is valid over an interval, not
   forever. The typed relation artifact (bd-3soj) needs validity bounds.
3. CONSTRUCTION SIGNALS — ALREADY REGISTERED FOR NYC AND CURRENTLY TREATED AS SIDE DATA.
   OC-0048's channel list carries two that are actually the temporal spine of the building
   level:
     dob permits and job filings (BIS + DOB NOW)  -- construction pipeline
     certificates of occupancy                    -- a CO is a building's birth certificate
   These are not enrichment. They are how the building level gets a clock. Reclassify them.
4. DEMOLITION VERSUS COVERAGE GAP. Cross-source presence disagreement (FEMA 2019 has it,
   Overture 2022 does not) may be a demolition rather than a data-quality problem. Combine
   per-source vintage (bd-2cbs rule 6), year-built, and CO/permit records to distinguish
   them; ABSTAIN where they cannot be distinguished. Silently treating a demolition as a
   coverage gap, or a coverage gap as a demolition, are both silent errors.
5. NEW-CONSTRUCTION COLD START. A building completed after every source's vintage exists in
   the client's book and in NO tile. That is a COVERAGE abstention with a specific,
   reportable cause and a specific remedy (refresh the tile), and it must not be reported
   as an unresolvable row. Distinguish it in the abstention vocabulary (bd-786w).

== INTERACTION WITH THE ASSEMBLAGE MODE (bd-2zdz) ==
Subset-sum over building areas is only valid AT A POINT IN TIME. A property asserted in
2019 against a parcel that gained six buildings by 2020 will fail its size constraint
against a current tile, and the failure will look like a wrong assemblage rather than a
temporal mismatch. Assemblage scoring must run against the tile vintage matching the
assertion's as-of, or abstain.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- Existence intervals on building clusters, sourced where authoritative and observed
  otherwise
- Validity bounds on containment relations; "what contained what at T" answerable
- DOB permits and certificates of occupancy consumed as building-lifecycle evidence
- Demolition vs coverage-gap discrimination, with abstention where indistinguishable
- New-construction cold start as its own abstention reason with a stated remedy
- Assemblage scoring bound to the assertion's as-of vintage
- Worked fixture: one BBL, bare in year 0, seven buildings in year 1, three of them in
  three different corpora — resolving to three DISTINCT properties sharing one parcel,
  with no false merge

title: [CANON-V1/P03.2] Separate profiles, linkage maps, policies, and frozen executable strategies
description:
## Background
Entity profile YAML, old linkage YAML, review thresholds, and frozen champion scripts currently resemble one another while carrying different authority and risk. That confusion encourages duplicate engines and accidental execution.

## Technical Approach
Define explicit schemas/references for entity profiles, cross-dataset field maps, evidence policies, review/promotion policy, and executable strategy packages. Linkage consumes a typed field map plus evidence-strategy reference; clustering consumes a profile plus evidence strategy; neither treats arbitrary YAML as executable. Artifact headers record every independent digest.

## Success Criteria
- Configuration, policy, and executable code are distinguishable by type/schema.
- No entity mode accepts a strategy of the wrong kind.
- Changing one object invalidates exactly the correct descendants.
- Old linkage YAML has a lossless generic destination without retaining a second engine.

## Test Plan
Create neutral paired fixtures differing in one contract dimension; assert type refusals and cache invalidation. Also replay maintained historical linkage/profile fixtures strictly as parity inputs, proving their vocabulary creates no core branch.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/entity/profile.rs`
- `src/entity/contracts.rs`
- `src/resolve/strategy.rs`
- `schemas/canon.entity.profile.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/strategy_entity_boundary.rs`

## Considerations
Do not nest every object into one giant manifest. Independent objects stay content-addressed and composable; historical fixtures are migration evidence, not built-in semantics.
notes:
## Domain-neutrality invariant
`canon entity link` is a generic two-or-more-dataset record-linkage mode. Core types and operators may reference only observations, sources/tapes, field mappings, namespaces, candidate blocks, evidence, constraints, decisions, and provenance. Structured-finance terms, identifiers, source adapters, thresholds, and role semantics live exclusively in versioned profiles, strategies, vocabularies, provider packs, and evaluation corpora. Add a source/contract conformance test that rejects domain vocabulary or conditional behavior in the core engine. Structured-finance fixtures prove the abstraction under a demanding use case; they do not define it.

title: [CANON-V1/P01.2] Move registry SQLite indexes to content-hash-keyed external cache
description:
## Background
Normal exact lookup currently creates _index.sqlite inside the registry and invalidates it with version plus mtimes. This prevents truly read-only registry mounts and can return stale data when bytes change without a newer mtime.

## Technical Approach
- Key derived indexes by verified registry/package content hash under the managed Canon cache root.
- Open immutable registries read-only and create no files beside them.
- Build indexes through temporary files and atomic rename; validate schema version and source digest before reuse.
- Define cache eviction and diagnostics without making cache presence part of domain output.

## Success Criteria
- Exact lookup succeeds from a read-only registry on all supported platforms.
- Content changes always invalidate the cache; mtime-only changes do not.
- Corrupt or partial indexes rebuild safely or refuse according to policy.
- Mapping output is byte-identical with cold, warm, absent, or unwritable cache.

## Test Plan
- Read-only permission and archive extraction tests.
- Backdated/preserved-mtime mutation regression.
- Corrupt SQLite and interrupted-build tests.
- Cold/warm determinism and concurrency tests.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/registry.rs`
- `src/paths.rs`
- `src/lookup.rs`
- `tests/registry_cache.rs`

## Considerations
- Do not record raw identifier values in cache diagnostics.
- Support an explicit no-cache/in-memory mode.
- Avoid unbounded cache growth.

title: entry_count mismatch warning should suggest the correct count
description:
## Problem

When \`registry.json\` has a stale \`entry_count\`, canon warns:

```
Warning: registry.json entry_count (19) differs from actual count (29)
```

This is helpful but could go one step further: tell the user what to set it to, or offer to fix it.

## Observed behavior (spring11 session)

Built a CRE field-name registry with 29 aliases but set \`entry_count: 19\` by mistake. Got the warning on every run until manually editing registry.json.

## Suggestion

Either:
1. Include a fix hint: \`Warning: registry.json entry_count (19) differs from actual count (29). Update to "entry_count": 29\`
2. Or just treat entry_count as advisory/optional and drop the warning (since canon rebuilds the index from aliases.json regardless)

## Notes

- canon 0.1.0
- Warning correctly goes to stderr (JSON on stdout is clean) — good
- The "Building registry index" message also goes to stderr — good
- Very minor polish, canon is the most polished tool in the suite

title: [CANON-V1/P09.7] Deferred option: Rust Fellegi-Sunter/EM evidence operator
description:
## Background
Fellegi-Sunter scoring and EM-estimated parameters may improve ambiguous linkage, but Canon does not yet have evidence that this technique is needed beyond its accepted native baseline. This is an option, not a v1 commitment and not a claim of Splink parity.

## Technical Approach
If selected after core acceptance, create a source-pinned Rust implementation packet. Specify comparison levels, priors, m/u estimation, initialization, smoothing, missingness, term-frequency treatment, convergence, degenerate cells, numeric representation, deterministic ordering, corpus dependence, and model artifact format. Use a pinned reference oracle and layered differential fixtures. Emit typed uncertain evidence with per-field waterfalls and zero decision or promotion authority.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Source, license, behavior inventory, oracle, inputs, outputs, parameters, and numeric floor are pinned.
- Same model artifact and inputs replay deterministically under the declared platform contract.
- Training never reads sealed acceptance labels and the artifact records the candidate/training corpus digest.
- P12 ablation proves useful marginal lift without severe false merges or unacceptable calibration/resource regressions.
- Unsupported or degenerate estimation refuses explicitly without mutation.

## Test Plan
Reference parity for comparison patterns and parameter estimation; missing/rare/constant fields; zero counts; smoothing boundaries; shuffled inputs; convergence/non-convergence; cross-platform numeric floor; adversarial hard negatives; sealed-corpus ablation and replay.

## RESERVATIONS
No Canon files while deferred. Following cmdrvl-tabfm, a selected port must first name its repository/module skeleton, provenance ledger, spec, oracle harness, fixture paths, and refusal taxonomy.

## Considerations
A known mathematical technique is not equivalent to complete third-party-tool behavior. Name any intentionally unported capabilities.

title: [CANON-V1/P11.5] Enforce read-only, offline, concurrency, and platform safety matrices
description:
## Background
Many guarantees are cross-cutting and easily regress: read commands should not mutate, offline runs should not connect, concurrent publication should not lose data, and path/atomic semantics differ across platforms.

## Technical Approach
Create a reusable black-box safety harness that snapshots filesystem metadata, intercepts or denies network, launches concurrent subprocesses, injects signals/failures, and runs supported-platform path/permission cases. Apply it to lookup, verify, plan, explain, inbox read, package read, project run, promotion, exports, cache, and optional servers/adapters as appropriate.

## Success Criteria
- Every command declares and empirically matches its mutation/network/concurrency class.
- Read-only commands leave content, mtimes, permissions, and owned-state inventories unchanged.
- Offline policy catches attempted connections rather than trusting code inspection alone.
- Platform-specific limitations are documented and fail closed where required guarantees are unavailable.

## Test Plan
Run Linux/macOS CI where available, read-only trees, no-network namespace/firewall harnesses, concurrent writers/readers, signals, permission/Unicode/symlink cases, and compare declared versus observed effects.

## RESERVATIONS
- `tests/safety_matrix.rs`
- `src/operator.rs`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

## Considerations
Tests must not delete arbitrary user content; all destructive fault fixtures live inside owned temporary directories.

title: canon geo: wire N-source multisource to a command surface (it is library-only today)
description:
ON THE CRITICAL PATH. FOUND BY REALITY CHECK 2026-08-14.

THE FINDING: bd-2kjx's strongest reuse claim — "multisource.rs: N-SOURCE link
materialization ... A geo tile carries six sources; this is solved" — is HALF TRUE. The
types and logic are real, well-designed, and tested. But NO COMMAND CAN INVOKE THEM.

VERIFIED:
  src/entity/multisource.rs  884 LOC. EntityMultisourceInput{name, role, rows_path,
    row_count, local_id_column, anchor_namespace}; EntitySourceRole =
    {CanonicalReference, Reference, Target, Peer}; EntitySourceComparison with per-pair
    max_candidate_rows; EntityMultisourceLinkArtifact with comparison_graph and
    consistency; EntityAnchorConflict; complete_comparison_graph().
  grep multisource src/cli.rs src/lib.rs src/main.rs  ->  NO MATCHES.
  Only caller: tests/entity_multisource.rs.
  The shipped CLI is strictly two-tape: `canon entity link <REFERENCE> <TARGET>`.

WHY GEO CANNOT PROCEED WITHOUT IT: a BYOP tile carries six to seven named sources in one
run — Overture building GERS, FEMA USA Structures, Microsoft GlobalML footprints, NYC /
MapPLUTO where free, the CLIENT's licensed parcel layer, and the CLIENT's property book.
Two-tape link cannot express that. Running C(7,2) = 21 pairwise two-tape links and
merging afterwards is NOT equivalent: it loses the comparison-graph budget enforcement,
loses cross-source consistency diagnostics, loses anchor-conflict abstention, and
produces a merge step with no artifact contract — which is precisely the fan-out-or-
collapse pathology bd-67wx rejects in the wide crosswalk.

TASK: wire the existing multisource machinery to a command surface.
1. COMMAND SHAPE. Named sources rather than positional tapes. Something of the form
     canon geo run --source <NAME>=<PATH>:<ROLE> ... --strategy ... --registry ...
   with the comparison graph either complete-by-default (complete_comparison_graph()
   already exists) or explicitly declared. DECIDE whether this lands as `canon geo run`
   only, or whether `canon entity` also gains an N-source form — RECOMMEND GEO ONLY for
   now, so entity's shipped contract does not change and the geo lane can iterate.
2. ROLE SEMANTICS FOR GEO. Map the four existing roles onto the BYOP shape and record it:
   the client's property book is the TARGET (the thing being keyed); our tile sources are
   PEERS (mutually comparable, none authoritative); the client's parcel layer is a
   REFERENCE (authoritative for parcel identity within its coverage, but only within its
   coverage); CANONICAL_REFERENCE is reserved and should probably go UNUSED in v1 —
   nothing in a BYOP tile is globally canonical, and pretending otherwise would let one
   vendor's parcel silently win. Record that reasoning; do not just pick roles.
3. PER-PAIR BUDGETS. EntitySourceComparison already supports max_candidate_rows per pair.
   Geo needs this genuinely, not decoratively: the client-parcels x our-footprints pair
   is dense and bounded by tile, while client-book x client-parcels is sparse. Wire the
   budgets through and surface them in diagnostics.
4. ABSTENTION VOCABULARY. EntityMultisourceAbstentionReason currently has EXACTLY ONE
   VARIANT: AnchorConflict. Geo needs more. The coverage cases are scoped in their own
   bead; this bead owns extending the enum and keeping the artifact contract versioned
   when it grows.
5. ARTIFACT VERSIONING. EntityMultisourceLinkArtifact is currently library-internal and
   has never been a published contract. Publishing it through a CLI makes it a contract.
   Version it deliberately, declare it in the geo contracts module (bd-3ccc), and add it
   to the artifact chain so its hash participates in replay.

DO NOT FORK. The point of this bead is that multisource.rs is GOOD and the only thing
wrong with it is reachability. Wire it; do not reimplement it in src/geo/.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- An N-source geo command that runs a tile with >=3 named sources end to end
- Roles assigned with recorded reasoning, CANONICAL_REFERENCE deliberately unused-or-
  justified
- Per-pair candidate budgets enforced and visible in diagnostics
- The multisource link artifact published as a versioned contract in the artifact chain
- A test asserting that 3-source composition is NOT equivalent to three pairwise 2-source
  runs — specifically that anchor-conflict abstention fires in the composed run and
  cannot fire in the pairwise runs
- Two-tape `canon entity link` behaviour unchanged (regression)
close_reason: N-source Geo materialization is publicly runnable, versioned, hash-bound, budgeted, atomically published, and fully tested; the impossible pairwise-conflict criterion was corrected with a theorem-level regression.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
RE-SCOPE 2026-08-14 — THE JUSTIFICATION IN THIS BEAD'S BODY IS NOW WRONG, THOUGH THE WORK
IS STILL NEEDED.

WHAT THE BODY ARGUES: "a BYOP tile carries six to seven named sources in one run — Overture
building GERS, FEMA USA Structures, Microsoft GlobalML footprints, NYC/MapPLUTO, the
CLIENT's licensed parcel layer, and the CLIENT's property book. Two-tape link cannot express
that."

WHY THAT IS NO LONGER THE RIGHT ARGUMENT: under the pre-resolved-tile architecture the four
public sources are reconciled BEFORE the tile ships. The client run then has THREE named
participants — pre-resolved building anchors, the client's parcel layer, and the client's
property book — not seven.

THE WORK IS STILL REQUIRED. Three named sources with distinct roles still cannot be
expressed by `canon entity link <REFERENCE> <TARGET>`, which is strictly two-tape. And
multisource.rs is still library-only: grep for `multisource` in cli.rs/lib.rs/main.rs
returns nothing, and the only caller is tests/entity_multisource.rs. So the wiring is real
work that still has to happen.

WHAT CHANGES:
1. SCALE. Three participants, not seven. C(3,2)=3 comparison pairs rather than 21. The
   per-pair budget machinery matters less; the ROLE SEMANTICS matter more.
2. ROLES BECOME SHARPER, NOT VAGUER. Under the original framing I recommended leaving
   CANONICAL_REFERENCE unused because "nothing in a BYOP tile is globally canonical." That
   reasoning INVERTS under a pre-resolved tile: the tile's building anchors ARE canonical
   for the building level, because we minted them and every client shares them. Revisit
   that recommendation — CanonicalReference is probably now the correct role for
   tile-shipped clusters, and getting it wrong would let a client's vendor parcel silently
   outvote a shared anchor.
3. IF bd-3foo LANDS ON OPTION C (canon runs at tile build), THEN N-SOURCE IS NEEDED ON BOTH
   SIDES — four sources at tile build, three at client run — and this bead serves both.
   That strengthens the case for doing it well rather than minimally.

the role semantics until that decision lands; the wiring and the artifact contract can
proceed.

title: Resolve v0 strategy parser and validator
description:
Implement parsing, validation, canonical hashing, and typed representation for canon resolve strategy YAML.

Background:
- docs/PLAN_STRUCTURAL_RESOLUTION.md defines strategies as the mutable tournament artifact.
- A strategy maps reference columns to target columns, declares composite identity columns, candidate filters, assertion operators, weights, thresholds, ambiguity gap, and max candidate controls.
- This parser is the contract that makes later scoring deterministic and auditable.

Scope:
- Add src/resolve/strategy.rs.
- Parse YAML with serde_yaml into typed structs.
- Validate required fields: strategy_id, strategy_version, entity_type, identity.reference.id_columns, identity.target.id_columns, assertions, match_threshold, ambiguity_gap.
- Validate threshold and weight ranges.
- Validate supported operators for candidate filters and assertions.
- Validate operator-specific parameters such as tolerance, range_pct, days.
- Compute and expose a BLAKE3 content hash from the exact strategy bytes.
- Preserve deterministic ordering in any normalized representation.
- Emit resolve-specific strategy errors that map to refusal E_BAD_STRATEGY.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests cover valid minimal and CMBS-like strategies.
- Unit tests cover malformed YAML, missing required fields, unknown operators, invalid threshold ranges, invalid negative weights, invalid operator parameters, and stable content hashes.
- The parser does not inspect tapes yet; cross-tape column existence validation belongs to tape/load orchestration or a later integration point.
- cargo fmt --check and cargo test for strategy tests pass.

title: [CANON-V1/P09.6] Deferred proof that optional matcher seams remain isolated
description:
## Background
If Canon later implements an optional matcher or interoperability seam, that seam must remain removable. This proof is intentionally post-v1 and cannot block the core release that establishes the native baseline.

## Technical Approach

Compare native artifacts and mutation inventories. Inspect default dependency and package graphs for accidental runtime coupling.

- Removing the optional component leaves native outputs and accepted workflows unchanged.
- Optional failures cannot mutate project inputs, reviews, decision ledgers, registries, exports, or witnesses.
- Core binary and installation do not acquire an undeclared runtime, network, model, or license obligation.
- Support claims clearly distinguish experimental optional evidence from native acceptance.
- This bead is not a prerequisite of v1 release preflight.

## Test Plan
Execute clean and failure matrices from installed artifacts; inspect dependency trees and network/filesystem traces; compare exact native outputs; reproduce evaluation and isolation reports.

title: [CANON-V1/P12.4] Prove incumbent attachment with counterfactual alias-withholding benchmarks
description:
## Background
Reviewed registries already contain valuable same-entity judgments, but ordinary exact replay cannot show whether Canon could have discovered those aliases. Withholding accepted aliases creates a realistic counterfactual benchmark from existing knowledge.

## Technical Approach
For each eligible canonical entity, create a base registry snapshot that omits one reviewed alias while retaining the entity, other aliases, trusted identifiers, and permissible context. Present the withheld surface as an unseen observation and ask the public entity engine to attach it, abstain, or reject it. Prevent leakage through mapping files, search indexes, caches, normalization patches, generated corpora, and display-name copies. Stratify by punctuation/case, abbreviation, legal suffix, word order, OCR-like noise, DBA, reviewed rename, and evidence-rich versus name-only cases. Treat predecessor, parent, subsidiary, and division labels according to explicit gold relation policy rather than assuming equality.

## Success Criteria
- Every eligible withheld alias produces a reproducible trial bound to the clean base registry digest.
- Results report candidate rank, decision, evidence lanes, abstention, review action, and exact replay after approved promotion.
- Exact lookup against the base snapshot proves the alias truly was absent.
- Holdout generation never uses the withheld value in strategy or package inputs.
- Aggregate results meet the discovery-quality contract without hiding per-class failures.

## Test Plan
Run tiny planted registries plus a larger reviewed fixture; deliberately leak aliases through each prohibited channel and require refusal. Shuffle entity and alias order, rerun cold/warm, and compare trials. Promote a correct reviewed attachment in a sandbox and prove subsequent exact resolution.

## RESERVATIONS
- src/evaluation/alias_withholding.rs
- tests/entity_alias_withholding.rs
- tests/fixtures/canon_v1/quality/alias_withholding/

## Considerations
Some aliases are only knowable through human or external evidence. Those should abstain or enter review; the benchmark must not reward unsupported guessing.

title: canon registry mint: compose next-id + add-entry for one-shot self-authored mints
description:
Add `canon registry mint` as the one-shot self-authored entity creation workflow built from `next-id` and `add-entry` internals.

Purpose:
- Make the common workflow ergonomic: choose or provide a canonical ID, add one or more starting aliases for that ID, bump registry metadata once, validate once, and emit a receipt.
- `mint` creates durable registry knowledge only through mapping entries. It must not create an invisible allocated ID that cannot resolve later.

CLI:
`canon registry mint --registry <DIR> [--canonical-id <ID> | --prefix <PREFIX>] --canonical-type <TYPE> --with-alias <FILE=INPUT:RULE_ID>... [--bump patch|minor|major | --next-version <VER>] [--no-lint] [--emit json|plain]`

Behavior:
- Require at least one `--with-alias`. Refuse no-alias mints; reserving unused IDs would require a separate documented allocation sidecar and is out of scope for this bead.
- If `--canonical-id` is omitted, call the internal next-id allocator using `--prefix` or `registry.json.default_id_scheme`. `--prefix` overrides the configured default for this operation.
- Parse `--with-alias` by splitting once at `=` and then splitting the right side at the last `:`. This lets inputs contain colons while keeping `rule_id` required and non-empty.
- Each alias file must satisfy the same validation as `add-entry`: existing root-level `.json`, no path traversal, not `registry.json` or `_build.json`.
- Validate all aliases and all target files before writing anything. Duplicate inputs against existing registry entries or within the mint request must refuse.
- Apply one registry version change for the entire mint. Do not call an add-entry path that bumps once per alias.
- Version update uses the same mutually exclusive `--next-version` or `--bump` rules as add-entry, defaulting to patch when the current version is bumpable.
- Increment `entry_count` by the number of alias entries actually added and preserve all other `registry.json` fields.
- If lint is enabled, validate the final proposed registry once and abort on lint errors; warnings/info appear in the receipt.
- Commit all touched alias files plus `registry.json` atomically as a unit, or restore byte-for-byte originals on failure.
- Do not directly mutate `_index.sqlite`; let the normal loader rebuild from mapping files and the bumped version.
- Do not add new witness behavior in this bead.

Output:
- Default `--emit json`: emit `canon_registry_mint.v0` with `canonical_id`, `canonical_type`, alias entries added, registry version before/after, touched files, lint summary, and warnings.
- `--emit plain`: print only the minted canonical ID plus newline.
acceptance_criteria:
- Mint without `--canonical-id` uses the next-id allocator and writes at least one resolvable alias.
- Mint with `--canonical-id` skips allocation but still validates the ID and writes aliases.
- Mint with zero `--with-alias` refuses and writes nothing.
- Multiple aliases across one or more alias files are committed with one registry version bump and one `entry_count` update.
- Duplicate alias input in the existing registry or within the mint request refuses before writing.
- Prefix override beats `default_id_scheme` for the allocation only; the receipt records the scheme used.
- Lint errors or write errors roll back all touched files byte-for-byte.
- JSON receipt shape is covered by a golden fixture for `canon_registry_mint.v0`.
- Round-trip tests prove all added aliases resolve through the normal exact lookup path after mint.
- Quality gate passes: `cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test`.
notes:
Target files:
- src/registry/mint.rs (new)
- src/registry.rs (add module/export only; there is no src/registry/mod.rs in this repo)
- src/registry/next_id.rs (reuse allocator API only)
- src/registry/add_entry.rs (reuse planning/write helpers only)
- src/cli.rs (wire subcommand)
- src/lib.rs (minimal dispatch only)
- operator.json (add command contract if implemented in this bead)
- tests/registry_mint.rs (new)

Implementation notes:
- This bead depends on `bd-1ot` and `bd-ayw`. Do not duplicate their parsing and validation logic.
- No hidden allocation table in this bead. If unused-ID reservations become necessary, create a separate plan and registry sidecar first.
- Keep this in the registry-maintenance family, not a workbench. No evidence graph, no scoring, no matching.
close_reason: Implemented canon registry mint by composing next-id allocation with add-entry validation/write helpers. Supports explicit IDs or allocation by prefix/default scheme, repeated FILE=INPUT:RULE_ID aliases with colon-safe parsing, one version/count update, multi-file atomic restore, lint receipt, operator contract, golden fixture, prefix override, duplicate/zero-alias refusals, and round-trip lookup coverage. Evidence: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test; target/debug/canon --describe includes registry mint; br dep cycles --json returned count 0.

title: [CANON-V1/P05.6] Explain and diff temporal identity across snapshots
description:
## Background
When an alias resolves differently between two dates or registry versions, operators need more than a mapping diff: they need the business-time and knowledge-time reason.

## Technical Approach
Add temporal query, explain, and diff artifacts that trace a surface or entity across fact validity, recorded corrections, policy versions, compiled snapshots, and relationships. Classify deltas as new fact, expired fact, correction, retraction, policy change, scope change, conflict, or canonical remap. Expose stable JSON and concise timelines.

## Success Criteria
- Every changed exact result has a minimal causal fact/policy chain.
- Valid-time and known-time comparisons are visibly distinct.
- No-change queries still identify the compiled snapshot and supporting fact set.
- Large diffs paginate deterministically and can filter by entity type, scope, source, and change class.

## Test Plan
Golden-test mergers, renames, late corrections, source conflicts, policy changes, and unchanged histories. Verify cursor stability, explanation minimization, and read-only behavior.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/temporal/explain.rs`
- `src/temporal/diff.rs`
- `tests/temporal_explain.rs`

## Considerations
An explanation should not imply legal conclusions beyond the supplied source assertions and policy.

title: canon geo [ambition-1]: exact optimal assignment (Hungarian/JV) over integer scores — the honest baseline
description:
THE HONEST BASELINE THE FANCY METHODS MUST BEAT. DO THIS BEFORE ANY SPECTRAL OR ENTROPIC
METHOD.

BLOCKED ON THE RESIDUAL HARNESS. Do not start without a measured tie population.

WHY THIS FIRST: bd-2kjx's ambition list names permutation synchronization, correlation
clustering and Sinkhorn. All three are approximations to problems whose EXACT solution is
sometimes affordable. At the epic's own stated scale — approximately 167 nodes per tile
across six sources — OPTIMAL BIPARTITE ASSIGNMENT IS EXACTLY SOLVABLE IN POLYNOMIAL TIME
AND IS FULLY DETERMINISTIC. Reaching for a relaxation before trying the exact method is
the reward-hacking pattern AGENTS.md calls conformance metastasis, applied to math:
choosing the impressive tool over the correct one.

THE METHOD: Hungarian algorithm / Jonker-Volgenant, on the cost matrix formed by the
cascade's existing pair scores.
  - O(n^3). At n ~ 167 that is ~4.6M operations per tile. Trivially affordable.
  - EXACT, not approximate. Returns the provably minimum-cost assignment.
  - DETERMINISTIC given deterministic tie-breaking — and canon already has the right
    substrate: ScoreUnits is an INTEGER type (u32, scale 10,000), so the cost matrix is
    integral and the classic float-accumulation nondeterminism of assignment solvers does
    not arise. This is a genuine, unearned advantage of canon's existing integer boundary
    and should be called out in the implementation.
  - TIE-BREAKING MUST BE SPECIFIED, not left to iteration order. Equal-cost assignments
    exist and are common in geometry (two identical footprints). Break by a deterministic
    total order on surface ids. An unspecified tie-break is a determinism bug.

WHAT IT BUYS OVER GREEDY PAIRWISE ACCEPTANCE: the cascade as designed accepts pairs
independently. That can produce globally incoherent results — surface A takes its best
match B, leaving C with nothing even though the assignment {A-D, C-B} has lower total cost
and is correct. This is exactly the CARDINALITY PRIOR the epic names ("a tile has
approximately N buildings; a clustering producing 3N is wrong by construction") turned into
an enforceable constraint rather than a diagnostic.

SCOPE:
1. Bipartite assignment between two named sources within a tile, over the existing pair
   scores. Cost = ENTITY_SCORE_SCALE minus pair score, with hard-cannot-link pairs given
   an infeasible cost rather than a large finite one (a large finite cost can still be
   chosen when the alternative is worse; infeasible cannot).
2. RECTANGULAR AND UNBALANCED CASES ARE THE NORM, not the exception. Sources have
   different cardinalities, and not every feature has a counterpart. Support explicit
   NON-ASSIGNMENT with a declared abstention cost, so the solver can leave a surface
   unmatched rather than being forced into its least-bad option. GETTING THIS WRONG
   CONVERTS ABSTENTIONS INTO SILENT ERRORS, which is the exact failure mode the whole
   outcome exists to prevent.
3. EMIT THE ASSIGNMENT AS EVIDENCE, NOT AS A VERDICT. Per canon doctrine the solver
   proposes; review promotes. The assignment result is a scored proposal with a named
   operator and reason code, visible in explain and on bd-101v's card. If you cannot
   explain a match by pointing at assertion scores, it does not ship — and "the global
   assignment preferred this" IS a pointable reason, provided the alternative cost is
   reported alongside.
4. REPORT THE MARGIN. For each assignment, the cost delta to the next-best alternative
   assignment. A near-zero margin is a TIE and should abstain rather than accept. This is
   the cheapest possible tie detector and it comes free from the solver.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: anything multi-way. Three-plus-source global consistency is the
permutation-synchronization bead. Keep this one exact and bipartite.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- Deterministic Hungarian/JV over integer ScoreUnits costs, with specified tie-breaking
- Infeasible (not merely expensive) encoding of hard-cannot-link
- Unbalanced/rectangular support with explicit non-assignment at a declared abstention cost
- Margin-to-next-best reported per assignment; near-zero margin abstains
- Cross-platform determinism test on a tie-heavy fixture
- Residual re-measured: the tie and silent-error categories must MOVE, or this gets
  reverted rather than defended
close_reason: SUPERSEDED — ambition lane retired by measurement. Appendix L (E1-E3, 2026-08-16): point re-ranking is not the dominant failure mode (0/7 tile-addressable wins; 72/79 labeled failures unreachable/representation cases), so the residual harness gate this lane waited on resolved AGAINST it. PLAN_CANON_GEO.md section 11: assignment and clustering become named global constraints with exact propagators; bd-2kjx.3's factorized exact residual solver (src/geo/composition.rs) now does exact composition without search. Any revival must come from a measured E4/E5 residual that names this technique, not from this bead.

WHAT I ASSUMED WHEN WRITING IT: that canon geo performs multi-source reconciliation at

WHAT IS NOW LIKELY: the tile ships PRE-RESOLVED. cmdrvl-curves is co-locating the big four

title: [CANON-V1/P02.4] Compile manifests into deterministic dry-run execution DAGs
description:
## Background
Before spending hours linking millions of observations or mutating a registry, an operator needs a truthful view of stages, cache hits, expected artifacts, review gates, and proposed writes.

## Technical Approach
Implement `canon project plan` as a pure compiler from manifest plus lockfile into a typed DAG. Nodes cover intake, normalize, index, block, evidence, solve/link, evaluate, review, promote, exact replay, and exports. Every node declares content-hash inputs, outputs, limits, cache eligibility, side effects, dependencies, and refusal conditions. Emit stable JSON plus an intelligible terminal summary.

## Success Criteria
- Repeated planning is byte-stable and performs no writes outside an explicitly requested plan artifact.
- The DAG detects cycles, missing producers, incompatible modes, output collisions, and impossible review policy before execution.
- Plan output distinguishes computation, external materialization, review pauses, and mutation gates.
- Agents can identify runnable nodes and exact next commands without parsing prose.

## Test Plan
Golden-test minimal, multi-source, two-tape linkage, temporal snapshot, cached, and invalid DAGs. Compare workspace trees before and after dry-run. Log node ordering, graph hash, cache decisions, and refusal diagnostics.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/project/plan.rs`
- `schemas/canon.project.plan.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/project_plan.rs`

## Considerations
Planning must not probe live providers. Any materialization requirement is an explicit node whose network policy and output digest become part of execution.
close_reason: Implemented reserved project dry-run DAG planner module, schema, and focused integration tests. Evidence: cargo test --test project_plan passes 10 tests; cargo fmt --check passed during quality gate. Broader cargo clippy and cargo test are currently blocked by unrelated unreserved active-bead changes in src/entity/review_import.rs, src/lib.rs, and tests/canon_v1_contract_inventory.rs.

title: canon geo: tile artifact format and offline provider build
description:
Two phases, forced apart by PROVIDER_SDK.md: 'hidden network access is always
a conformance failure because acquisition stays outside the deterministic
offline build.'

ACQUISITION (network, outside canon): a geo MCP server serves CONTENT-ADDRESSED
tile artifacts keyed by H3 cell. Clients pull only the cells covering their book.

PROVIDER BUILD (offline, deterministic, inside canon): the downloaded tile is
the provider's SOURCE. Emits typed facts with full provenance -- source_digest,
source_path, record ordinal, field-level locators -- and DECLARES ITS SUBSET
PREDICATE (the H3 cell set plus k-ring buffer), so 'why is this row in my tile'
is answerable by construction.

WHY THE CONSTRAINT HELPS: the tile digest makes resolution reproducible and
auditable, exact replay works, and the client can re-run offline forever.
Refreshed tiles are the recurring product, the same way registry versions
already are.

OPEN: is the tile artifact a DataBook? It has the shape (content-addressed,
typed, provenance-carrying) and DataBook infrastructure exists.

Depends on: skeleton
Parent: bd-2kjx
