comments.author: zac
comments.text:
RENDERING CONSUMER 2026-08-14 (see new bead bd-101v): the tile artifact is also the SOURCE FOR THE VISUAL EVIDENCE CARD, not only for the resolution run.

This strengthens the case for content-addressing rather than complicating it. Because the tile is pinned by digest, a card re-rendered years later shows the geometry AS IT WAS when the decision was made — the bitemporal requirement becomes a visual guarantee instead of a caveat. A renderer that re-queries the warehouse for geometry breaks that and must be refused.

REQUIREMENT ADDED: the tile must carry geometry at sufficient fidelity to draw, for EVERY candidate considered — including the ones that lost. A tile that keeps only the geometry of promoted entities cannot support the card.

CAUTION FROM THE MOCK: geometry simplified for DRAWING must never be the geometry used for the DECISION. While building the mock I simplified MapPLUTO polygons to ~2 m to keep coordinate lists short, and the simplified shapes no longer supported the containment result that full-precision ST_CONTAINS returns — I initially read the simplified geometry as contradicting the two-lot finding, and was wrong. If the tile ships one simplified geometry for both purposes, exact predicates (bd-15ba) are silently defeated. Carry decision geometry at full precision; derive any display simplification separately and label it.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
REALITY CHECK 2026-08-14 — BYOP MEANS TWO GEOMETRY SOURCES, NOT ONE. THIS BEAD MODELS
ONE.

ARCHITECTURE SETTLED (operator decision 2026-08-14, see bd-2kjx): canon geo is
parcel-source agnostic. We serve tiles of OUR datasets (Overture building GERS, FEMA USA
Structures, Microsoft GlobalML footprints, NYC/MapPLUTO where free — four to five at
launch). The CLIENT brings their own licensed parcel layer (ATTOM/Regrid/LightBox),
which may be PARTIAL, plus their property book. Canon composes the graph across both,
locally, on the client's machine.

WHAT THAT CHANGES IN THIS BEAD:

1. THE SUBSET PREDICATE BECOMES AN INTERSECTION. This bead's best idea — "DECLARES ITS
   SUBSET PREDICATE (the H3 cell set plus k-ring buffer), so 'why is this row in my
   tile' is answerable by construction" — must now compose two predicates: OUR tile's
   cell set AND the client's coverage predicate. The answerable question becomes "why is
   this row in my tile, and is this tile fully covered by both sources." A tile where
   our side is complete and the client's layer is absent is a DIFFERENT STATE from a
   tile where both are present and nothing matched. See the new coverage-abstention bead.

2. ASYMMETRIC TRUST AND PROVENANCE. Our tile is content-addressed, digest-pinned, and
   auditable by us. The client's layer is opaque to us — we do not know its vintage, its
   generalization, its capture method, or whether it is mutually exclusive within itself.
   The tile artifact format must carry a per-source provenance block that can express
   BOTH: full provenance for our sources, and a client-declared descriptor
   (vendor, vintage, CRS, coverage extent, mutual-exclusivity flag) for theirs. Canon
   must refuse rather than assume defaults for the client descriptor.

3. LICENSE CONTAINMENT IS NOW A HARD ARTIFACT REQUIREMENT. This bead's own comment
   already requires that the tile carry geometry at drawing fidelity for EVERY candidate
   including losers, and bd-101v requires geometry at DECISION fidelity in the artifact.
   Under BYOP those artifacts will contain the client's licensed parcel geometry. That
   makes the artifact LICENSE-ENCUMBERED: it cannot round-trip to us for debugging,
   scoring, or hosted review. See the new license-containment bead — this bead owns the
   format change (a per-source redaction/exclusion boundary that survives content
   addressing), that bead owns the policy.

4. THE PROVIDER-BUILD CONSTRAINT STILL HOLDS AND IS NOW EASIER TO SATISFY. PROVIDER_SDK.md
   forbids network access inside a provider build. Under BYOP the client's layer arrives
   as a local file, not a fetch, so both geometry sources are local at build time. Good.

RETAINED AND REINFORCED FROM THE EXISTING COMMENT:
- Content addressing makes a re-rendered 2019 decision show 2019 geometry. Correct, and
  it is now the ONLY mechanism that makes as-of resolution visually honest. Do not weaken.
- DECISION GEOMETRY AT FULL PRECISION; display simplification derived separately and
  LABELLED. The mock's ~2 m simplification silently contradicted a full-precision
  ST_CONTAINS result. If one simplified geometry serves both purposes, bd-15ba's exact
  predicates are defeated. This is now doubly important because the client's vendor may
  ALREADY have generalized their parcels — so the tile must record whether incoming
  geometry is source-fidelity or vendor-simplified, and refuse to treat vendor-simplified
  geometry as decision geometry without an explicit operator acknowledgement.

OPEN QUESTION — IS THE TILE A DataBook? Now leaning YES, and BYOP is the reason. The tile
is content-addressed, typed, provenance-carrying, and must express a per-source privacy
boundary — which is exactly the three-axis privacy model (owner x tenant x audience)
that DataBook already carries. Reusing it gets the license-containment boundary for free
rather than inventing a parallel mechanism. Decide explicitly in this bead.

EXIT CRITERIA — AMENDED:
- Tile artifact format with per-source provenance blocks supporting both full-provenance
  (ours) and client-declared (theirs)
- Subset predicate expressed as an intersection, with coverage state per source per cell
- Decision geometry at full precision; display geometry derived, labelled, and never
  substitutable
- A source-fidelity vs vendor-simplified flag on incoming geometry, with refusal on
  silent substitution
- Losing candidates' geometry retained (already required; note that the EVIDENCE side of
  this is verified working — canon retains all candidate pairs as evidence records)
- License boundary expressible in the format and preserved under content addressing
- Explicit DataBook yes/no decision recorded

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
REFINEMENT 2026-08-14 — CROSS-REPO HANDOFF. This bead correctly places ACQUISITION outside
canon, but nothing records who owns the other side, and canon cannot create beads in
another repo. Recording the handoff here so it is not lost.

TWO PIECES LIVE OUTSIDE THIS REPO:

1. THE GEO MCP SERVER (serves content-addressed tiles keyed by H3 cell) belongs in
   geo-ddp/geo-mcp-server, which is the established home for the estate's geo MCP tools.
   NOT cmdrvl-geo, which is an unrelated map UI. A bead is needed there for: tile serving
   by cell, content addressing, digest pinning, the cell-set subset predicate, and refresh
   semantics that honour the tile identifier stability contract.

2. OUR TILE BUILD PIPELINE (Overture building GERS, FEMA USA Structures, Microsoft GlobalML
   footprints, NYC/MapPLUTO) belongs in cmdrvl-curves, which is the current NYC landing
   path and already owns the shared geometry landing contract (bd-qbno, closed) that all
   geo sources follow. A bead is needed there for building tiles from the landed sources
   at the resolution bd-2b9d settles.

THE CONTRACT BETWEEN THEM AND CANON IS THIS BEAD'S TILE ARTIFACT FORMAT. Specify the format
first; both external pieces are then implementations against it rather than negotiations.
That ordering matters — if the pipeline ships before the format is settled, canon inherits
whatever shape the pipeline happened to produce.

ALSO NOTE THE TILE-IDENTIFIER STABILITY CONTRACT (see the as-of/ID-stability bead): the
refresh pipeline in cmdrvl-curves is the thing that would VIOLATE it, and the conformance
gate that diffs consecutive vintages needs to run THERE, in the pipeline, not only here.
A contract enforced only on the consuming side is not enforced.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
TILE PRE-STITCHING IS ALREADY UNDER WAY IN cmdrvl-curves, LANDING NOW 2026-08-14. Verified
by reading the in-progress beads. This confirms the pre-resolved-tile architecture and
supplies hard facts that change several canon geo assumptions.

== WHAT IS ACTUALLY LANDING ==

  cmdrvl-curves bd-30ho   OVERTURE MAPS, release 2026-07-22.0. Themes buildings,
                          building_parts, PLACES, addresses, divisions. Snowflake DDL
                          APPLIED (OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_HOT / _EXT /
                          OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURE_H3_COVERAGE plus 14 per-type views);
                          manifest scan running, 0 rows landed yet.
  cmdrvl-curves bd-1ssr   FEMA USA STRUCTURES, 135,321,228 features nationally. National
                          landing IN PROGRESS; DC / AK / AL complete, AR running.
                          FEMA_USA_STRUCTURES_HOT loaded and read back (DC = 64,701 rows).
  cmdrvl-curves bd-3fyv   MICROSOFT GLOBALML FOOTPRINTS, release 2026-07-24. Landing IN
                          PROGRESS: 179 of 2,415 US files, 5,219,860 rows at 14:45Z.
  cmdrvl-curves bd-11uu   HUD USPS ADDRESS VACANCIES -- **BLOCKED**, and not a tile source.
                          HUD restricts it to registered governmental/non-profit users and
                          the sublicense forbids selling, licensing or distributing the
                          data. DO NOT PLAN ANY CANON GEO CAPABILITY ON IT.

NOTE ON "FOURSQUARE OS PLACES": it arrives as OVERTURE'S PLACES THEME, not a separate
Foursquare landing. That is the POI level in bd-2cbs, and it is in the same table family as
Overture buildings.

== FINDING 1: THE LANDED H3 GRAIN IS r4 / r7 / r8. THERE IS NO r9. ==
All three sources partition by h3_r4 and carry H3_R7 and H3_R8 columns. The epic's default
tile is res-9 and it is NOT precomputed anywhere.

AND THERE IS A CONVENIENT COINCIDENCE WORTH DELIBERATELY EXPLOITING: an r8 cell is
approximately 0.737 km2 -- which is almost exactly the area the epic specifies for its WORK
UNIT (an r9 cell plus k-ring 1 = 7 cells = 0.737 km2). So the already-landed H3_R8 column is
essentially the intended work-unit size.
ACTION FOR bd-2b9d: reconsider r9-plus-k-ring versus r8-plus-k-ring as the work unit, now
that r8 is precomputed across every source and r9 is not. This does not change the
requirement to compute cells in canon with a vetted Rust library -- the Snowflake H3 helper
defects (edgar-elt br-2wir) still stand -- but it does mean the warehouse can prefilter at
r8 for free, and the resolution decision now has a third input alongside node count and
human legibility.

== FINDING 2: POLYGON-TO-CELLS RETURNS EMPTY FOR SMALL BUILDINGS. LIVE, MEASURED. ==
From bd-3fyv: "H3_POLYGON_TO_CELLS alone inserted only 116 coverage rows for 354,804 hot
rows because small buildings often contain no H3 r8 cell centroid." Fixed there by using a
guaranteed CENTROID_H3_R8 plus H3_TRY_POLYGON_TO_CELLS.

THIS IS DIRECTLY THE MEMBERSHIP QUESTION bd-10s2 AND bd-2b9d SPECIFY. At r8 or r9 a
building is much smaller than a cell, so "which cells does this polygon cover" is
degenerate: the standard polygon-to-cells contract returns cells whose CENTRES fall inside
the polygon, and for a building that set is almost always EMPTY.
CONSEQUENCE: membership must be CENTROID-ANCHORED with polygon coverage as a supplement for
the large-feature case (parcels, campuses, complexes), NOT the other way round. My earlier
recommendation on bd-10s2 -- "full intersection cover for membership plus a single
deterministic anchor cell" -- is right in intent but inverted in emphasis, and applying it
naively with polygon_to_cells would have silently produced empty membership for nearly every
building. Correct it there.

== FINDING 3: OUR OWN SOURCES CARRY LICENSE OBLIGATIONS. bd-pq5w IS SCOPED TOO NARROWLY. ==
I framed license containment entirely around the CLIENT's licensed parcel layer. The landed
research shows OUR side has obligations too, and they differ per source:
    Overture buildings, divisions      ODbL-1.0            <-- SHARE-ALIKE
    Overture places                    per-source mix of CDLA-Permissive-2.0, Apache-2.0,
                                       CC0-1.0; source license must be retained
    Overture addresses                 source-specific, incl. NAD Access and Usage License
    FEMA USA Structures                CC-BY-4.0, attribution to ORNL and FEMA Geospatial
                                       Response Office REQUIRED
    Microsoft GlobalML                 CDLA-Permissive-2.0 current release; older vintages
                                       need per-release revalidation
bd-30ho states plainly: "License segmentation by source array is REQUIRED before any derived
product ships. Treat as a build-time gate, not a later cleanup."

ODbL SHARE-ALIKE IS THE COMMERCIAL ISSUE AND IT NEEDS AN OPERATOR DECISION, NOT AN
ENGINEERING ONE. A tile is a derived product. If it mixes ODbL Overture buildings with
everything else, the derived tile may inherit share-alike obligations that are
incompatible with a paid distribution model. Options to evaluate deliberately:
  (a) segregate ODbL-derived features into a separately-licensed layer of the tile, with
      the license class carried per feature -- note OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_EXT ALREADY HAS
      LICENSE_CLASS AND LICENSE_TERMS COLUMNS, so the substrate for this exists;
  (b) build the commercial tile from the permissive sources only (FEMA CC-BY, Microsoft
      CDLA) and treat Overture as an internal enrichment;
  (c) accept share-alike and publish the tile openly.
REQUIRED IN bd-pq5w AND bd-1uld: license class per FEATURE in the tile artifact, and a
declared per-tile license posture that composes our obligations with the client's. The
artifact license boundary now has TWO directions, not one.

== FINDING 4: THE ATTRIBUTE CHANNELS FOR bd-272d ARE REAL, AND ONE IS MODELLED ==
Attribute anchoring needs class, size, floors, year. What is actually arriving:
    FEMA        OCC_CLS, PRIM_OCC (occupancy class), SQFEET, PROP_ADDR, UUID, BUILD_ID
    Overture    building class, height, num_floors, GERS id
    Microsoft   height (subset only), confidence, NO ID
    MapPLUTO    BLDGCLASS, LANDUSE, BLDGAREA, LOTAREA, NUMBLDGS, NUMFLOORS, YEARBUILT
So the six-field client contract has a counterpart on the tile side for every field except
YEAR BUILT, which only MapPLUTO supplies -- meaning year-built anchoring works in NYC and
degrades outside it until a national year source exists. Record that as a known national
limitation rather than discovering it later.

CRITICAL: FEMA OCCUPANCY IS MODELLED, NOT SURVEYED. bd-1ssr requires a provenance flag
"so downstream never treats it as surveyed." Attribute anchoring MUST carry that flag into
the evidence and weight modelled attributes below observed ones. A modelled occupancy class
driving a hard eliminative filter (bd-2zdz's assemblage type filter) would be a silent error
generator -- the filter is HARD, so a wrong modelled class removes the correct candidate
before anything is scored. Use modelled occupancy as SUPPORT evidence, never as a hard
filter, unless corroborated.

== FINDING 5: NO STABLE ID CONFIRMED FOR TWO SOURCES ==
Microsoft has no id at all -- bd-3fyv derives "a deterministic feature hash because no
stable id." Overture ADDRESSES are alpha with no stable GERS id either. This confirms
bd-2cbs rule 4 (alias-less participants) and extends it: the alias-less set is Microsoft
footprints AND Overture addresses, not just Microsoft.
A derived feature hash is NOT an alias and must not be minted into a registry -- it will
change whenever the geometry changes, which violates the tile identifier stability contract
in bd-12gh.

== FINDING 6: OVERTURE ADDRESSES CANNOT BE THE ADDRESS-SET SOURCE ==
bd-30ho: "Addresses theme is ALPHA -- do not build a contract against it yet," no stable
GERS id, multi-source licensing including NAD terms. US count 127,719,691.
So bd-35qg's address-set acquisition is NOT solved by Overture. NYC PAD or the per-BIN
addresses in the landed footprints file (bd-397d) remain the path, and the national story
stays open. Do not let the size of the Overture addresses count create false confidence.

== WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE WORKED-CASE CORPUS (bd-tccn) ==
The corpus can now stage its non-MapPLUTO pulls against REAL TABLE NAMES rather than
placeholders:
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.FEMA_USA_STRUCTURES_HOT              partially loaded (DC, AK, AL)
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.MICROSOFT_GLOBALML_BUILDING_FOOTPRINTS_HOT   partially loaded
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_HOT           DDL applied, 0 rows
    plus the *_FEATURE_H3_COVERAGE tables for each
NEW YORK IS NOT YET LOADED IN ANY OF THE THREE. FEMA is alphabetical by state and is at AR;

title: strategy mutation receipts and witness parity for registry writes
description:
Bring strategy registry mutations up to canon's audit posture by emitting explicit mutation receipts and appending witness ledger records where canon's normal witness policy applies. The new operator-attested path is lightweight, but it still freezes scripts and changes registry state; those state changes need hashable receipts and witness parity with the rest of the tool.

Expected implementation scope: receipt structs/output for strategy register/update/deprecate/promote, before/after registry hashing, witness record construction, non-secret provenance fields, and e2e assertions. RESERVATIONS: src/strategy_registry.rs, src/lib.rs, src/witness.rs, tests/cli_smoke.rs, operator.json if output schemas change.
design:
Every successful mutating strategy command should emit a deterministic receipt containing operation, registry id, before_version, after_version, before_registry_hash, after_registry_hash, typed key, grade/status before and after when applicable, script id/path/language/content hash, proof artifact hashes when present, operator attestation hash when present, source file, entry order, and next suggested commands.

Witness records should chain through the existing witness machinery, honor the existing witness suppression/override contract, avoid recording script bytes or secret values, and degrade consistently with existing non-fatal witness failure behavior if that is the established policy. Resolve/list/explain remain read-only and should not append mutation witness records.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: register/update/deprecate/promote success JSON includes a stable receipt with before/after registry hashes and no raw script bytes; witness ledger append is proven in a temp HOME/EPISTEMIC_WITNESS e2e test for at least one successful mutation; --no-witness or the documented equivalent suppresses witness append without changing the mutation receipt; witness failure behavior matches existing canon commands; receipts are deterministic under injected timestamps; operator.json documents receipt schemas and witness semantics.
notes: Do not make witness append a hidden dependency for resolving strategies. This bead covers state-changing registry operations only.
close_reason: Implemented strategy v1 typed keys, operator/proof attestation grades, lifecycle, catalog/explain, receipts/witness, lint/diff/docs/tests; verified cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test, cargo build --release --locked, and UBS on changed files.

title: Input parsing (CSV + JSONL)
description:
Parse both CSV and JSONL input formats in src/input.rs. Return a unified InputValues structure (unique values + special-case classifications) consumed by the lookup engine.

CSV parsing:
- csv crate (streaming). Header required, UTF-8 BOM stripped.
- Delimiter auto-detected (same algorithm as rvl: sniff first 8KB for comma/tab/pipe/semicolon frequency).
- --column specifies column name. Must exist (else E_COLUMN_NOT_FOUND).
- Skip blank records (all fields empty after ASCII-trim).
- ASCII-trim values before collection. Empty after trim => classify as empty_value (no lookup).

JSONL parsing:
- One JSON object per line. --column specifies field name.
- Missing field => classify as missing_field.
- null value => classify as null_value (not string-coerced to "null").
- Object/array value => classify as non_scalar_value.
- Numbers/booleans coerced to JSON string representation (42 => "42").
- String values ASCII-trimmed. Empty after trim => classify as empty_value.
- Stdin support (- for JSONL only; CSV requires seekable input).

Format detection:
- .csv and .tsv => CSV parser.
- .jsonl and .ndjson => JSONL parser.
- Unrecognized or missing extension => E_PARSE refusal.

=== I/O BUDGET ENFORCEMENT ===

--max-bytes (Option<u64>): For regular files, check file size BEFORE reading (stat the file, compare, refuse E_TOO_LARGE if over). For stdin (JSONL only), count bytes during streaming and refuse E_TOO_LARGE as soon as the limit is exceeded.

--max-rows (Option<usize>): Count raw data rows during streaming (including duplicates, excluding header for CSV and excluding blank records). Refuse E_TOO_LARGE if the count exceeds the limit. This is an I/O budget, not a cardinality limit.

Both checks use refusal code E_TOO_LARGE with detail indicating which limit was hit and what the actual value was.

=== EMPTY INPUT CHECK ===

After parsing completes, if values is empty AND special is empty, refuse with E_EMPTY_INPUT. This covers: header-only CSV, empty JSONL file, CSV where all rows are blank records. This check MUST happen here (not in run()) so the zero-values-zero-specials case never reaches the lookup engine.

=== ENCODING ERRORS ===

Non-UTF-8 files that fail decoding => refuse E_ENCODING (not E_CSV_PARSE). Malformed-but-UTF-8 CSV => E_CSV_PARSE. The distinction matters for the next_command recovery guidance.

Output: InputValues struct containing:
- values: HashMap<String, ()> of unique non-special input values
- special: HashMap<SpecialReason, usize> counts of empty_value/null_value/missing_field/non_scalar_value
- format: InputFormat enum (Csv/Jsonl) for downstream emit-mode validation
- delimiter: Option<u8> — the detected CSV delimiter (Some for CSV, None for JSONL). Required by the CSV output module to preserve delimiter in --emit csv mode.
acceptance_criteria:
TARGET FILE: src/input.rs only. Include #[cfg(test)] mod tests.
Tests:
- CSV column extraction with correct values
- JSONL field extraction with correct values
- Format detection by extension (.csv, .tsv, .jsonl, .ndjson, unknown => E_PARSE)
- Special reason classification (empty_value, null_value, missing_field, non_scalar_value)
- Dedup: duplicate input values collapsed to one entry in HashMap
- Delimiter detection: comma, tab, pipe correctly identified and stored in InputValues.delimiter
- --max-rows enforcement: refuse E_TOO_LARGE when row count exceeds limit
- --max-bytes enforcement: refuse E_TOO_LARGE when file size (or stdin bytes) exceeds limit
- E_EMPTY_INPUT: header-only CSV, empty JSONL, all-blank-records CSV => refuse E_EMPTY_INPUT
- E_ENCODING vs E_CSV_PARSE: non-UTF-8 file => E_ENCODING, malformed CSV => E_CSV_PARSE
VERIFICATION: cargo test -- input
close_reason: Input parsing complete - comprehensive CSV and JSONL parsing with format detection, auto delimiter detection, I/O budget enforcement, comprehensive error handling, stdin support for JSONL, extensive test coverage. Quality gate passes with 9 new tests.

title: canon geo: threshold and decision-band calibration — cost-sensitive, per-tier, per-source-pair
description:
REFINEMENT GAP 2026-08-14: nothing owns where the geo thresholds come from.

Every operator in bd-gs6n and bd-1zph carries a threshold — distance_lt bound, iou_gt
threshold, area_ratio band, size_ratio band, year_built tolerance, and the score at which
the cascade auto-links, abstains, or routes to review. bd-uilx specifies that a
channel-agreement rule with decision bands must exist. NOTHING SPECIFIES WHERE THE NUMBERS
COME FROM. Hand-picked thresholds are exactly the "calibration constant that swings the
whole tile's behaviour" pathology the correlation-clustering bead warns about, and they are
unfalsifiable in review.

DO NOT BUILD A NEW CALIBRATION MECHANISM. canon already has two, both open, both applicable:
  bd-3qfq  [SPLINK-STEAL/S1] entity calibrate sweep: gold-driven threshold selection report
  bd-3q3k  [CANON-V1/P12.7] Calibrate auto-link, abstention, and review bands with
           cost-sensitive risk
This bead's job is to make geo a CONSUMER of those, and to supply what geo uniquely needs
that a name-matching calibration does not.

WHAT GEO NEEDS THAT THE EXISTING CALIBRATION WORK DOES NOT COVER:

1. THE COST ASYMMETRY IS EXTREME AND MUST BE STATED. A false merge in geo means a loan is
   attributed to the wrong building — wrong exposure, wrong owner, wrong comps, and it
   propagates into OC-0045/0046/0047 which all consume this key. An abstention means a
   human looks at a map for ten seconds. These costs differ by orders of magnitude, and
   cost-sensitive band selection (bd-3q3k) is therefore not a refinement here, it is the
   whole design. Bands must be chosen at a declared cost ratio, and the ratio must be
   recorded in the artifact so a reviewer can see what tradeoff produced the answer.

2. GROUND TRUTH EXISTS AND IS FREE — USE IT. PLUTO gives address-to-BBL truth for the
   entire NYC book (858,602 rows). That is a far richer gold set than the hand-labelled
   pairs name-matching calibration usually gets. Sweep against it.

3. THRESHOLDS ARE PER-TIER, NOT GLOBAL. The measured geocode distribution makes this
   unavoidable: rooftop hits a lot 99.92% of the time, range_interpolation 50.52%,
   street_center 30.38%, intersection 8.70%. A distance_lt bound appropriate for an
   interpolated point in the right-of-way is absurdly permissive for a rooftop point.
   Calibrate per accuracy tier and REFUSE to apply a tier's thresholds to a row whose tier
   is undeclared (see bd-uilx: a geocode without a declared tier cannot be auto-accepted).

4. THRESHOLDS ARE PER-SOURCE-PAIR. Under BYOP we do not know the client's vendor
   characteristics. A distance bound tuned on MapPLUTO-vs-Overture may be wrong for
   ATTOM-vs-Overture. Support per-source-pair overrides, and make the DEFAULT conservative
   (abstain more) rather than permissive, because the failure direction matters.

5. THE NEAREST_ROOFTOP_MATCH TIER NEEDS ITS OWN TREATMENT. 688 NYC rows, 100% lot-hit rate,
   worst house-number agreement of the rooftop tiers. Geometry is maximally confident and
   may be pointing at the neighbour. A calibration that optimizes overall precision will
   happily accept this tier because it "works"; a cost-sensitive one that weights silent
   error properly should route much of it to review. This tier is the single best test of
   whether the calibration is honest.

6. CALIBRATION ARTIFACTS ARE VERSIONED AND PINNED. The thresholds used by a run are part of
   its reproducibility surface, exactly like the registry version and the tile digest. A
   re-run with different bands is a different answer and must be visibly so.

ANTI-REWARD-HACKING: do not tune thresholds until the scored set looks good. The sweep
reports a curve; the operator picks a point on it at a declared cost ratio; the pick is
recorded with its justification. Moving the threshold after seeing the score, without
restating the cost ratio, is gate self-weakening.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- Geo consumes bd-3qfq's sweep and bd-3q3k's cost-sensitive bands rather than duplicating
- Declared cost ratio recorded in the run artifact
- Per-tier and per-source-pair thresholds, with conservative defaults and refusal on
  undeclared tier
- Sweep run against PLUTO ground truth with the curve published
- nearest_rooftop_match treated as its own calibration slice with its behaviour justified
- Calibration artifact versioned and pinned into the run's reproducibility surface
close_reason: Superseded by §3.2 band-versus-threshold rule and §18.3: there are no decision thresholds to calibrate; softness lives in declared rho bands (population, calibration digest, falsification rule) and observer error characterization (bd-ci1n). Calibration of bands is part of each admitting bead.

title: [CANON-V1/P07.1] Define one typed evidence IR for all native and adapter producers
description:
## Background
Clustering, cross-dataset linkage, exact anchors, external suggestions, and review patches currently risk producing incompatible records. A single intermediate representation is the key seam between uncertain evidence and deterministic decisions.

## Technical Approach
Define `canon.evidence.v1` records for observations, candidate scopes, pair/hyperedge/record-link support, anti-merge veto, context-only evidence, missingness, provenance, operator identity/version, policy reference, numeric/categorical payloads, temporal/scope metadata, and deterministic ordering. Separate evidence facts from solver decisions and promotion authority.

## Success Criteria
- Every native operator and optional adapter can express its output without untyped blobs.
- Positive, negative, veto, context, and missing evidence are mechanically distinct.
- Evidence IDs and canonical bytes are stable across shards and producer order.
- Unknown namespaced operator payloads survive only through declared schema extensions and cannot grant authority.

## Test Plan
Round-trip every variant; merge shuffled/sharded evidence; fuzz malformed values, NaN/infinity, oversized payloads, unknown extensions, and provenance gaps. Golden-test bytes and hashes.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/evidence/mod.rs`
- `src/evidence/types.rs`
- `schemas/canon.evidence.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/evidence_contract.rs`

## Considerations
The IR captures claims, not verdicts. Solver and review policies remain explicit consumers.

title: EPIC: canon geo agent control plane — question to resumable exact answer and next evidence
description:
DELIVERY OBJECTIVE

Turn the implemented Geo leaf capabilities into one agent-operable, offline, source-generic system. The normative design is docs/CANON_GEO_AGENT_ARCHITECTURE.md. Today an agent must hand-assemble requests, remember command order, infer phase state from files, and decide reuse manually. This epic ships executable contracts and commands that make those responsibilities explicit.

SYSTEM CONTRACT

question + compiled capabilities + regional inventory + resolution profile + deterministic budget
  -> costed plan
  -> immutable resumable run revisions
  -> bounded sections
  -> independent candidate-reach gate
  -> rho admission and actual incidence components
  -> small exact residuals
  -> ownership reconciliation
  -> separate availability, reach, admission, solver, truth, and cost planes
  -> explanation and cheapest potentially decision-changing next evidence

BOUNDARIES

- Core dispatches typed evidence classes, entity levels, relations, and contract versions, never vendor names.
- Regional inventories and adapters carry source instances, releases, coverage, lineage, coordinate contracts, and licenses.
- Acquisition remains outside the deterministic offline Canon build.
- A geography may lack parcels. Current parcel/building composition remains an explicit implementation limit until bd-2cbs closes it.
- H3 is blocking and ownership metadata, never geometric truth.
- Exact solving is tile plus controlled halo, then incidence components, then small residuals. No national or 500k-candidate monolith.
- More hard evidence narrows the model set or makes it empty. Source count is not confidence.
- Counterfactual model-count separation is not expected value of information without calibrated outcome probabilities.
- Resource fallback is controlled by deterministic counters, never wall-clock timing.

EPIC EXIT

An agent can start from one typed question and one regional inventory, obtain a deterministic offline plan, execute or resume it, inspect one compact machine-readable run state, distinguish all epistemic planes, reuse unaffected artifacts after evidence accretes, and receive exact next commands. Full-stack, parcel-typical, parcel-free minimal, contradiction, missing-coverage, and interruption/resume scenarios pass without fixtures being represented as live proof.

title: [CANON-V1/P13.5] Prove pack portability on an independent non-finance domain
description:
## Background
The BDC issuer and CMBS tenant packs exercise different relationship shapes but share a structured-finance context and some operator assumptions. Before Canon claims that the pack ecosystem generalizes across domains, run the same package contract against an independently selected, public, non-finance entity-resolution problem.

## Scope
- Select one public, license-compatible non-finance dataset with real ambiguous identities and independently adjudicable truth.
- Author its ontology, source mapping, typed views, evidence policy, and sealed corpus as an out-of-tree pack.
- Record which core and package-contract changes, if any, the exercise demands.
- Add a small invented neutral fixture for contract-level edge cases.
- Exclude optimizing the core specifically for the chosen dataset or importing its vocabulary into core.

## Technical approach
Choose the dataset only after documenting license, entity semantics, temporal behavior, positive and hard-negative coverage, and evaluation budget. Freeze train, development, and untouched holdout partitions before policy tuning. Build the pack without copying assumptions from either finance pack. Any proposed generic contract change must be justified by at least two distinct packs, pass the domain-neutrality scan, and land through its own bead.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The independently authored pack installs and runs through the same P08 and Canon contracts as the finance packs.
- Core requires no use-case vocabulary or conditionals.
- Candidate recall, pairwise or cluster decision quality, calibration, abstention, and determinism meet declared pre-registered thresholds on the untouched holdout.
- The report distinguishes portable mechanisms from dataset-specific policy.
- Cross-domain claims cite this proof rather than treating two finance archetypes as sufficient.

## Test plan
- License and provenance audit before corpus ingestion.
- Sealed split and leakage audit.
- End-to-end install, verify, map, normalize, retrieve, score, decide, review, promote, and export test as applicable.
- Adversarial hard-negative and temporal cases.
- Source scan and package diff against both finance packs.

## File and reservation boundaries
All domain data, vocabulary, policies, and fixtures live in the standalone pack. Reserve exact files. Canon core may change only under a separate generic-contract bead with cross-pack evidence.

## Considerations
A benchmark can reward shortcuts or contain noisy labels. Report label uncertainty and negative evidence honestly. One non-finance pack is evidence of portability, not proof of universality.

title: canon geo: address_match and address_range operators
description:
TWO operators, not one. This is the originating problem.

address_match -- normalization: case, abbreviation expansion (St/Street,
  Ave/Avenue), directionals, unit/suite handling, punctuation. The existing
  exact operator is brittle here ('123 Main St' != '123 MAIN STREET').

address_range -- parse '100-101 Main Street' as a range [100,101] on Main St and
  test containment.

WHY BOTH ARE REQUIRED: '100 Main Street' vs '100-101 Main Street' is the
motivating case, and STRING SIMILARITY CANNOT DECIDE IT. Edit distance says
near-identical, but they may be one property written as a range OR two
different buildings on the same block. Only range parsing plus geometry
separates those.

USE AS AN INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE CHANNEL. Parsed-address agreement is evidence
independent of the geocode. Require geometry and address channels to AGREE, or
abstain -- that is what makes the answer trustworthy rather than a black box.

Depends on: skeleton
Parent: bd-2kjx
close_reason: Superseded: query-side address parsing is bd-158y (regular-grammar parse forest, all readings held as a domain) and lot-side membership is PAD via materialize-address-evidence (Appendix M). address_match/address_range as scored operators contradict §7.1.

comments.author: zac
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-14 (measured on real NYC data via Loom) — THE RANGE RULE AS WRITTEN IS WRONG FOR QUEENS.

This bead says: parse '100-101 Main Street' as a range [100,101] and test containment. That is correct for Manhattan/Brooklyn-style addresses. IT IS WRONG FOR QUEENS.

Queens uses a HYPHENATED GRID CONVENTION where '42-15 Crescent Street' is a SINGLE atomic house number: 42 is the nearest cross-street, 15 is the position on the block. It is NOT a range from 42 to 15 (which would be inverted and meaningless). Parsing it as a range produces garbage on the entire borough.

MEASUREMENT: in the NYC CMBS geocode set joined to MapPLUTO, 1,130 of 2,107 house-number disagreements (54%) had a non-purely-numeric geocode house number, and the ten most frequent values were all Queens-grid hyphenates: 42-15 (48), 41-25 (32), 28-07 (24), 43-22 (20), 27-28 (18), 43-31 (16), 45-02 (15), 39-01 (14), 42-20 (14), 27-14 (13).

REQUIRED CHANGE: address_range must be borough/locale aware before it parses a hyphen. A hyphen means RANGE in some jurisdictions and GRID POSITION in others. The operator needs an explicit convention input (or a refusal) rather than a single global hyphen rule. Per canon doctrine this is a refuse-rather-than-guess case: if the convention for a locale is unknown, do not parse the hyphen.

This does not weaken the motivating case. '100 Main' vs '100-101 Main' still cannot be decided by string similarity. It adds a second case the operator must distinguish: '42-15' is one address, not two.

comments.author: zac
comments.text:
SECOND CORRECTION 2026-08-14 — THE ADDRESS CHANNEL NEEDS AN ADDRESS SET PER LOT, AND MapPLUTO CANNOT SUPPLY IT.

This bead assumes an address channel exists to corroborate geometry. On the NYC proving ground the obvious source for it — MapPLUTO's ADDRESS field — is NOT adequate, and this changes the data requirements.

MapPLUTO carries ONE representative address per tax lot. Large lots legitimately carry many. Measured examples from the CMBS join where the point is almost certainly on the correct lot yet the addresses differ:
  geocode 1633 BROADWAY            vs MapPLUTO 1657 BROADWAY
  geocode 1540 BROADWAY            vs MapPLUTO 1568 BROADWAY
  geocode 330 WEST 42ND STREET     vs MapPLUTO 334 WEST 42 STREET
  geocode 388 BRIDGE STREET        vs MapPLUTO 360 BRIDGE STREET
  geocode 9 WEST FORDHAM ROAD      vs MapPLUTO 2167 GRAND CONCOURSE  (corner lot, two frontages)

Comparing a property address against a single canonical lot address MANUFACTURES DISAGREEMENT on exactly the large multi-address and corner lots that dominate the CMBS book. A naive comparison scored these as mismatches; they are not.

REQUIRED: the address channel needs the SET of addresses valid for a lot, not one. Candidate sources — NYC PAD (Property Address Directory, DCP), or the building footprints file which carries per-BIN addresses. NEITHER IS LANDED. This is an acquisition gap that the 2026-08-14 NYC landings did not cover; see cmdrvl-context bd-1g1h.

Until an address-set source exists, address_match against MapPLUTO ADDRESS alone will produce a high false-disagreement rate and must not be used as the corroboration channel this bead depends on.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
REALITY CHECK 2026-08-14 — THIS BEAD IS BLOCKED ON DATA NOBODY OWNS, AND ITS PARSER MUST
BE DETERMINISTIC.

1. THE CORROBORATION CHANNEL HAS NO SOURCE AND NO OWNING BEAD. This bead's own
   2026-08-14 comment establishes that MapPLUTO carries ONE representative address per
   tax lot, that large and corner lots legitimately carry many, and that comparing
   against a single canonical lot address MANUFACTURES DISAGREEMENT on exactly the
   multi-address lots that dominate the CMBS book (1633 vs 1657 BROADWAY; 9 WEST FORDHAM
   vs 2167 GRAND CONCOURSE). It names NYC PAD or the per-BIN footprint addresses as
   candidates and states NEITHER IS LANDED.

   That comment points at cmdrvl-context bd-1g1h. VERIFIED: OC-0048 marks bd-1g1h
   "superseded 2026-08-14: all three gaps closed" — and the three gaps it closed were
   MapPLUTO, Building Footprints, and ACRIS. THE ADDRESS-SET GAP IS NOT AMONG THEM AND
   IS NOW ORPHANED. No open bead owns it.

   CONSEQUENCE: this bead's stated purpose — an independent address channel that
   corroborates geometry, which OC-0048 identifies as the mechanism that recovers the
   interpolated geocode tier — CANNOT BE DELIVERED against MapPLUTO ADDRESS alone. A
   new acquisition bead has been cut. This bead should depend on it.

2. NO STATISTICAL PARSER. libpostal is the obvious tool and MUST NOT BE USED: it is a
   C library with a large statistical model, and statistical parsing is
   non-reproducible-by-construction across model versions. Determinism is canon's core
   promise. Use a DETERMINISTIC RULE TABLE — USPS Publication 28 street-suffix
   abbreviations, directionals, and secondary-unit designators — shipped as data, with
   the table version recorded in the artifact so a re-parse years later is reproducible.

3. THE QUEENS CORRECTION GENERALIZES FURTHER THAN THE EXISTING COMMENT SAYS. The comment
   correctly establishes that a hyphen means RANGE in Manhattan/Brooklyn and GRID
   POSITION in Queens (measured: 1,130 of 2,107 house-number disagreements, 54%, had
   non-purely-numeric geocode house numbers; the ten most frequent were all Queens
   hyphenates). Under BYOP the same problem recurs nationally and worse, because we will
   not know the client's jurisdictions in advance. Hyphenated and compound house numbers
   appear with different semantics in many places (grid conventions, fractional
   addresses like 12 1/2, alphanumeric suffixes like 100A, and genuine ranges).

   REQUIRED: address_range takes an EXPLICIT LOCALE CONVENTION INPUT resolved per
   jurisdiction from a declared table, and REFUSES to parse a hyphen when the convention
   for that locale is unknown. Refuse rather than guess. The convention table lives in
   the profile, not core (see bd-15ba: predicates in core, conventions in profiles).

4. THE SIX-FIELD CLIENT INPUT CONTRACT CHANGES THIS BEAD'S LEVERAGE (operator decision
   2026-08-14). Address is now one of six declared inputs alongside geocode, geometry,
   building size, year built, and property type. That means address is no longer the
   ONLY corroboration channel — size, year built, and property type are independent
   attribute channels that can also reject a wrong candidate. This MATTERS because it
   gives the interpolated tier a second path: where the address-set source is missing or
   the locale convention is unknown, size/year/type agreement can still discriminate
   between two candidate lots. Design address_match to be ONE VOTER in a multi-channel
   agreement rule, not the sole tiebreaker. Abstain when channels disagree; that is the
   trustworthy behavior this bead already argues for.

EXIT CRITERIA — AMENDED:
- address_match with a versioned deterministic normalization table (USPS Pub 28), table
  version recorded in the artifact
- address_range with an explicit per-locale convention input and a documented refusal
  when the convention is unknown
- Negative test: '42-15 Crescent Street' must NOT parse as range [42,15]
- Negative test: '100 Main' vs '100-101 Main' must not resolve on string similarity alone
- Multi-address lot test: a lot with an address SET must not score as disagreement when
  the property address matches any member
- The operator emits structured evidence (parsed components, matched member, convention
  used, table version), not a prose explanation string

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
REFINEMENT 2026-08-14 — ADDRESS PARITY IS A LOCALE CONVENTION, AND address_range NOW HAS A
SECOND JOB.

1. PARITY BELONGS IN THE CONVENTION TABLE. In Manhattan, odd and even house numbers are on
   OPPOSITE SIDES of the street: 101/103/105 is one frontage, 102/104 the other. An office
   property recorded as "100-105 Broadway" whose surviving candidates are all odd is
   almost certainly a ONE-SIDE ASSEMBLAGE with a sloppy range endpoint, not a two-sided
   property.
   Parity is real, usable signal and it is JURISDICTION-DEPENDENT exactly like the Queens
   hyphenate rule this bead already handles. Put it in the same declared locale convention
   table. Never hardcode it — parity conventions are not universal, and a locale whose
   convention is unknown must REFUSE to apply a parity inference rather than guess.

2. address_range IS ALSO A CARDINALITY DETECTOR, NOT ONLY A MATCHER. A parsed range implies
   the property spans MULTIPLE addresses and therefore probably multiple parcels. That
   makes this operator one of the three cheap, address-channel-independent-of-geometry
   detectors for how much of the book is multi-parcel — the number that decides whether
   assemblage is the main event or a tail case. Emit the parsed interval and its width as
   structured evidence so the cardinality distribution can be computed from operator
   output rather than re-parsed downstream.

3. THE RANGE IS AN INTERVAL, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES ASSEMBLAGE TRACTABLE. See the
   assemblage bead: ordering candidates by address along the frontage turns subset
   selection from 2^N into N(N+1)/2 intervals. This operator produces the ordering key.
   Its output is therefore load-bearing for a solve mode, not just a scoring channel —
   design the evidence shape accordingly (emit the interval endpoints and the parity, not
   a boolean match).

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
NEW FAILURE MODES FOUND IN REAL DATA 2026-08-14 (see bd-tccn for the full case extracts).
These are not hypotheses; they are named rows.

1. THE CHIMERA PARSE — A SYNTHESIZED ADDRESS NO SOURCE ASSERTS.
   The parser takes a HOUSE NUMBER from one street and a STREET NAME from another,
   producing an address that appears nowhere in the input and may legitimately belong to a
   different property.
     "199, 201, 203, 205 FIRST AVENUE AND 349 & 351 EAST 12TH STREET ..."
        -> NUMBER 199, STREET "E 12th St", range_interpolation
     "241/249 West 74th Street"
        -> NUMBER 241, STREET "W 49th St", ROOFTOP     (74 -> 49 transposition)
     "47-19/47-27 a/k/a 47-27 Little Neck Parkway"
        -> NUMBER 47-10, nearest_rooftop_match          (47-10 is in no source address)
   This is DISTINCT from "the parser picked the first of several addresses," which is
   lossy but honest. A chimera is fabricated.
   REQUIRED: address_match must test whether the parsed address is A MEMBER OF THE ASSERTED
   ADDRESS SET and refuse to corroborate when it is not. That check is cheap, entirely
   local to the client's own row, needs no external data, and would have caught all three
   rows above. It should be one of the first operators built.

2. MULTI-ADDRESS FIELDS ARE A SIX-SEPARATOR PROBLEM AND ARE ~7-8% OF THE NYC BOOK.
   Measured counts in the five boroughs: '/' 297, ',' 129, '&' 93, ' AND ' 44,
   ' A/K/A ' 9, plus bare whitespace ("54-40   54-44 Little Neck Parkway").
   This bead currently scopes normalization and RANGES. It does not scope multi-address
   fields at all, and they are the larger population.

3. THE QUEENS COUNT IS 756 ROWS, AND THEY ARE NOT RANGES.
   756 five-borough rows carry a hyphen in the parsed NUMBER, and the sampled population is
   entirely Queens (36081) grid addresses — 47-27 Little Neck Pkwy, 196-12 67th Ave. A
   range rule applied here produces garbage on 756 rows. Confirms this bead's 2026-08-14
   correction with a hard count.

4. COMPLEX MULTI-STREET PROPERTIES NEVER PARSE AT ALL.
   The hardest rows degrade to accuracy_type = 'place' with NULL NUMBER and NULL STREET, so
   they never enter the geometric pipeline in either direction. They are invisible to the
   hit-rate metric. See the denominator note filed on bd-14co.

5. ONE PROPERTY CAN CARRY MULTIPLE GEOCODE ROWS THAT DISAGREE WITH EACH OTHER.
   "241/249 West 74th Street" has two: one range_interpolation in the roadbed at
   (40.7777640, -73.9755480), and one ROOFTOP at (40.7615050, -73.9859030) roughly 25
   blocks away on the wrong street. Cross-row disagreement within a single property is a
   free, purely local detection signal and is currently unmodelled anywhere in the epic.

title: [CANON-V1/P13] Post-core domain-pack ecosystem and adoption tooling
description:
## Background
Canon's domain-neutral engine deliberately leaves ontology, source mapping, normalization policy, evidence policy, and adjudicated examples outside core. That clean boundary creates an adoption cost: a new operator starts from a blank package. P13 is a post-core adoption lane that turns proven deployments into reusable, independently installable packs without weakening the firewall.

P13 starts only after bd-2i2q completes the Canon v1 no-theatre release. The BDC issuer and CMBS tenant packs are valuable structured-finance archetypes, but they are not by themselves evidence of cross-industry generality.

## Scope
- Produce hand-built, out-of-tree starter packs using the signed, content-addressed P08 package contract.
- Prove the same package interface with a neutral or non-finance portability fixture before making a cross-domain ecosystem claim.
- Explore a suggestion-only kit-builder after at least two hand-built packs exist.
- Add catalog metadata over P08 distribution only after package trust and compatibility semantics are proven.
- Keep pricing, marketplace governance, hosted services, and proprietary pack policy out of this epic.

## Technical approach
Each pack owns domain vocabulary, mappings, protected terms, evidence policy, corpus provenance, and compatibility metadata. Canon core consumes only generic package and evidence contracts. The sidecar may propose files and candidate labels but never writes trusted policy, gold labels, or registry state without explicit human confirmation. Distribution reuses P08 OCI digests and signatures rather than inventing a second transport.

## Success Criteria
- Every P13 artifact is installable and removable without changing Canon core.
- A source scan finds no BDC, CMBS, finance, tenant, issuer, or pack-specific rules in core crates.
- At least one neutral or non-finance portability proof exercises the same pack contract.
- Documentation distinguishes two finance archetypes from genuine cross-domain evidence.
- P13 remains absent from the bd-2i2q release critical path.

## Test plan
- Install each pack into a clean Canon environment and run its sealed fixture.
- Run package digest, signature, compatibility, and provenance checks through P08.
- Run the domain-neutrality/source-scan gate against core.
- Compare declared capabilities and outputs across the finance packs and the neutral/non-finance proof.
- Confirm the v1 release plan and ready queue do not depend on P13.

## File and reservation boundaries
P13 may add out-of-tree pack, catalog, sidecar, fixture, and documentation files. It must not add domain terms or rules to Canon core crates. Reserve exact files before implementation.

## Considerations
Starter packs are product-quality examples and production assets, not hidden core behavior. A generated scaffold is untrusted until reviewed. Corpus licenses, provenance, leakage controls, revocation, and compatibility are part of the pack contract, not afterthoughts.

title: canon geo D4: E1 gross-class (40) and condo (31) point lists committed as typed fixtures with a validation test
description:
PACKET PK-D4-fixtures (stage D4 entry condition) from docs/PLAN_CANON_GEO.md §19.5 row D4 and §18.1 item 1, minted 2026-09-02 in the coverage pass. §19.5 D4 entry condition: "the E1 gross-class and condo point lists committed as fixtures". Gate G4 measures "the recovery rate of the retry loop on the 40 gross-class points with fresh geocodes; condo flips independently confirmed on the 31 points". No bead owned the fixtures; bd-7hze (retry.rs) and bd-2fed (condo.rs) both read them and neither commits them. This bead does. It is a data capability with a schema and a validation test, gating two named feature beads; it is not a report.

== WHY ==
§18.1: "E1 found 72/79 labeled failures unreachable by any tile-local solver (40 gross-location inputs, 32 condo ledger residues)". Appendix M.4 measured the PAD condo crosswalk on 31 missing-geometry condo points and Appendix L.6 measured 0/40 recovery from already-landed geocodes. Those two named populations are the G4 denominators. They exist today only as SQL archaeology in docs/geo_design_session/ and scripts/geo_corpus/; a denominator that lives in prose can be silently re-drawn. tests/fixtures/geo/ holds five files and none is these lists.

== DELIVERABLES ==
1. tests/fixtures/geo/e1_gross_class_points.json, contract `canon_geo_point_population.v0` (additive contract, shared shape per §19.3, owned by src/geo/retry.rs since retry is its first consumer): `{ version, population_id: "e1.gross_class.40", source_dataset: "fixture.e1.gross_class" (C23), selection_query_blake3 (the checked-in SQL under scripts/geo_measurements/e1_gross_class_points.sql), release_pins: [MapPLUTO 26v1, PAD 26B, the geocode batch id], points: Vec<{ point_id, subject_id, loan_key, asserted_address_blake3 (the address bytes are NOT committed in clear; the digest binds the row to the warehouse without exporting the tape), landed_geocode: { lon_e7: i64, lat_e7: i64, accuracy_type, source_attribution }, home_cell_r9, refuter_fired: bool (the M.2 street-absence refuter), e1_failure_class: "gross" }> sorted by point_id }`. Exactly 40 points; the test pins the count.
2. tests/fixtures/geo/e1_condo_points.json, same contract, `population_id: "e1.condo.31"`, `e1_failure_class: "condo"`, plus per point `pip_lot_bbl`, `pad_billing_bbl_candidates: Vec<String>`, `pad_unit_bbl`, `block`, `billing_equals_pip: bool` (M.4 found this true on 10/31; the test pins 10). Exactly 31 points.
3. scripts/geo_measurements/e1_gross_class_points.sql and e1_condo_points.sql (bd-3mo1 conventions) that regenerate both lists from the pinned releases; their BLAKE3 values are the `selection_query_blake3` fields.
4. `validate_point_population_artifact` (retry.rs, shared shape): refuses `invalid_input` with `detail["field"]` on empty or unsorted points, duplicate point ids, missing `selection_query_blake3`, a `source_dataset` not starting with `fixture.` for a file under tests/fixtures/geo/ (C23 enforced at the type), or a coordinate outside the NYC bounding box in E7 integers.
5. schemas/canon.geo.point_population.v0.schema.json and the `point_population_schema_matches_a_real_instance` test in tests/geo_schemas.rs.

== ERROR CODES ==
| `invalid_input` | `validate_point_population_artifact` | as listed above | refusal; `detail["field"]` |

== CONTRACTS AND THREATS SERVED ==
C22, C23 (fixture pins by construction), C24 (the denominators 40 and 31 are constants in the test, not in src/), N07, TH19 (a changed count fails the test; the SQL digest binds the list to its query), TH20, TH21 (no point id or BBL literal from these files may appear in src/geo/retry.rs or condo.rs; T27 scan extended with `e1.gross_class` and `e1.condo`).

== TESTS (tests/geo_point_population.rs; each test logs on failure) ==
| T44 (bead-defined, extends §19.6) | D4 | unit | both fixture files | `points.len() == 40` and `== 31`; sorted, unique ids; every `source_dataset` starts with `fixture.`; `selection_query_blake3` equals the BLAKE3 of the checked-in SQL file; condo file has exactly 10 `billing_equals_pip == true`; every point has a nonempty `home_cell_r9` and `loan_key` | a scratch copy with one point removed fails on count; one with `source_dataset = "nyc.pad.26b"` refuses `invalid_input` with `detail["field"] = "source_dataset"` | LOG on failure: file, `points.len()`, the first unsorted or duplicate id, the expected and actual SQL digests, the `billing_equals_pip` count |
| T45 (bead-defined) | D4 | determinism | `canonical_point_population_bytes` on both files, serialized twice and after a JSON key reorder of the input | byte-identical | a `HashMap`-ordered implementation is caught by the reorder | LOG on failure: both BLAKE3 values and the first differing byte offset |

== E2E SCRIPT (scripts/geo_demo/e2e_point_population.sh; `set -euo pipefail`; logs each command, exit code, BLAKE3 of each file into <work-dir>/run.log) ==
1. `b3sum scripts/geo_measurements/e1_gross_class_points.sql scripts/geo_measurements/e1_condo_points.sql` and `jq -r .selection_query_blake3` of both fixtures; compare and log.
2. `canon geo retry validate-population --population tests/fixtures/geo/e1_gross_class_points.json` and the condo file; log counts.
3. `cargo test --test geo_point_population -- --nocapture`; `cargo test --test geo_schemas point_population_schema_matches_a_real_instance`; the jq schema pin from §19.7 for `point_population`; whole-tree gates.
4. Regeneration check (live, not CI): run both SQL files through cmdrvl-data, canonicalize, and `diff` against the committed fixtures; any difference is recorded as a source drift with the release pins, never patched into the fixture by hand.

== RESERVATIONS ==
tests/fixtures/geo/e1_gross_class_points.json, tests/fixtures/geo/e1_condo_points.json, scripts/geo_measurements/e1_gross_class_points.sql, scripts/geo_measurements/e1_condo_points.sql, tests/geo_point_population.rs, scripts/geo_demo/e2e_point_population.sh, schemas/canon.geo.point_population.v0.schema.json. Shared append-only touch points, reserve for the edit only: src/geo/retry.rs (the type and validator; coordinate on thread bd-7hze, land here first if bd-7hze has not started), tests/geo_schemas.rs, scripts/geo_measurements/README.md and manifest.json.

bd-7hze (retry loop, G4 recovery denominator), bd-2fed (condo bridge, the 31-point confirmation), and the G4 measurement bead depend on this bead.

ANTI-REWARD-HACKING (AGENTS.md, binding): the lists are regenerated by the SQL or not at all; no point is added or removed to move a recovery rate; the counts 40 and 31 are test constants. Code, schema, fixtures, and tests ship together. No new todo!() scaffolds.

title: Build deterministic org candidate blocks
description:
Implement the deterministic org candidate-blocking engine.

Using the scaffolded strategy, projection, and incumbent-memory types, emit `canon_org_block.v0` candidate pairs with canonical `(left_row_id, right_row_id)` ordering and registry-aware block hits. Implement the validated BDC v1 blocking operators from the plan: `exact_view`, `rare_token_overlap`, `shared_anchor`, and `registry_alias_match`.

Keep the work in `src/org/block.rs` only with inline unit tests that construct direct in-memory fixtures rather than depending on parser implementations.

## Acceptance Criteria
`src/org/block.rs` emits deterministic `canon_org_block.v0` records with no duplicate pairs and canonical pair ordering.
The validated BDC v1 blocking operators are implemented and emit the expected `block_hits`.
Block artifacts carry the scaffolded strategy and registry-snapshot provenance fields.
Inline unit tests cover each blocking operator, canonical pair ordering, and duplicate suppression.

## Notes

title: [CANON-V1/P04.1] Define a privacy-aware unresolved inbox artifact
description:
## Background
Unresolved values are currently an output condition, but they should become the highest-value input to the next registry improvement cycle. Without a stable artifact, teams repeatedly rediscover the same unknown identities and lose provenance.

## Technical Approach
Define `canon.unresolved.inbox.v1` as an appendable deterministic event model containing normalized surface fingerprints, source/project/run references, profile and field role, namespace hints, reason code, candidate summary, temporal scope, first/last seen, occurrence aggregation, and optional privacy class. Separate raw-value retention from stable fingerprints and define redaction, encryption hooks, retention, export, and merge semantics.

## Success Criteria
- Every unresolved exact lookup, cluster/link abstention, and rejected candidate maps to a typed reason.
- Repeated-run events merge deterministically while preserving source/time provenance.
- Sensitive raw values can be omitted or sequestered without destroying dedupe/impact analysis.
- The schema has explicit versioning, canonical ordering, and verification.

## Test Plan
Round-trip redacted/retained neutral fixtures; merge reordered shards; test hash collision handling, Unicode, time boundaries, incompatible privacy policy, corrupt references, and byte determinism.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/inbox/mod.rs`
- `src/inbox/types.rs`
- `schemas/canon.unresolved.inbox.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/inbox_contract.rs`

## Considerations
The inbox is evidence about missing coverage, not a shadow registry; it cannot silently create identity assertions.

title: [CANON-V1/P03.6] Run deterministic strategy tournaments without training on the holdout
description:
## Background
Canonical procedural knowledge should improve from evidence, but ad hoc tuning encourages overfitting and makes a promoted champion impossible to justify.

## Technical Approach
Add a tournament contract that separates train/tune/holdout corpora, enumerates bounded parameter candidates deterministically, runs each through the isolated audit runner, computes domain metrics plus abstention and resource costs, and emits a ranked comparison without auto-promoting. Hash corpus partitions and prohibit reading holdout labels during candidate generation.

## Success Criteria
- Repeated tournaments produce the same candidate order, metrics, ranking, and report.
- A candidate cannot access labels or files outside its declared partition and package.
- Champion recommendations expose metric tradeoffs, regressions, hard-negative failures, and uncertainty.
- Promotion remains an explicit separate operation with named threshold policy.

## Test Plan
Use a synthetic strategy with a tempting overfit parameter to prove holdout isolation. Shuffle corpus order, repeat runs, test ties and resource failures, and compare reports byte-for-byte.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/strategy/tournament.rs`
- `schemas/canon.strategy.tournament.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/strategy_tournament.rs`

## Considerations
Canon should evaluate deterministic candidates, not become an opaque AutoML system. Keep search bounded, inspectable, and optional.

title: [CANON-V1/P12.3] Measure candidate recall before scoring and emit actionable miss forensics
description:
## Background
If the true pair never enters the candidate set, no evidence model or solver can recover it. Aggregate cluster scores hide this failure. Candidate retrieval therefore needs its own release gate and operator-visible error analysis.

## Technical Approach
Instrument block and index output with per-operator and union recall at configurable K, true-pair rank distributions, candidate counts, suppressed postings, cap effects, exact-bucket behavior, and missed-pair reason codes. Attribute every miss to absent normalized evidence, operator coverage, posting suppression, candidate cap, profile mapping, anchor conflict, or malformed gold. Produce privacy-safe examples keyed by stable observation IDs. Compare exact views, token and character n-grams, sparse TF-IDF, sorted-neighborhood, trusted anchors, and packaged extension operators without granting any operator merge authority.

## Success Criteria
- Evaluation reports candidate recall at 1, 5, 10, 25, and 50 plus the union and marginal contribution of each operator.
- Every gold must-link absent at K=50 has a deterministic forensic record and next action.
- Exact-known, withheld-alias, novel-cluster, and directional-link candidate metrics remain separate.
- Candidate caps and large-bucket suppression are visible and never silently lower recall.
- Instrumentation adds no raw sensitive payload to public telemetry and does not cause pair explosion.

## Test Plan
Use planted pairs found by exactly one operator, by multiple operators, beyond a cap, inside a suppressed common bucket, and by no operator. Verify ranks, union recall, attribution, deterministic ordering, privacy redaction, and bounded memory. Run the public CLI against the neutral corpus and inspect emitted artifacts.

## RESERVATIONS
- src/entity/block.rs
- src/entity/index.rs
- src/entity/telemetry.rs
- tests/entity_candidate_recall.rs
- tests/fixtures/canon_v1/quality/candidate_recall/

## Considerations
This bead measures retrieval rather than improving it. Evidence-policy changes belong in later failure-driven work so baseline and treatment remain distinguishable.
notes:
## Demanding-deployment acceptance
Owns R1 retrieval verification. Measure candidate recall@50 (plus the declared retrieval cutoffs) across raw, legal-name, dba or operating-name, protected-token, and temporal-alias cases. Exact aliases and sealed holdout labels must not leak into candidate generation or tuning.

title: Registry loading + SQLite index
description:
Implement registry loading and SQLite index building in src/registry.rs.

Loading:
- Read registry.json from --registry path. Parse into RegistryMeta (id, version, description, updated, entry_count).
- Discover mapping files: all *.json in directory except registry.json. Flat directory only (subdirs ignored). Non-JSON files ignored.
- Validate each mapping file: must be a JSON array of objects, each with { input, canonical_id, canonical_type, rule_id }. Malformed => return E_BAD_REGISTRY.
- Log stderr warning if entry_count in registry.json differs from actual discovered entry count.

SQLite index:
- Derived index stored as _index.sqlite inside the registry directory.
- Schema: entries(input TEXT, canonical_id TEXT, canonical_type TEXT, rule_id TEXT, source_file TEXT, entry_order INTEGER).
- Entries ordered by (source_file ASC, entry_order ASC) for first-match-wins precedence.
- Staleness check: compare registry.json version string + max file mtime of *.json files against metadata table in SQLite.
- Auto-rebuild when stale. Log rebuild to stderr.
- If registry dir is not writable (can't create _index.sqlite), fall back to in-memory SQLite (build once per run, log warning).

Return type: Registry { meta: RegistryMeta, db_path: PathBuf } (the db_path points to _index.sqlite; lookup module opens it).

Error cases:
- Missing registry dir => E_IO
- Missing registry.json => E_BAD_REGISTRY
- Malformed mapping files => E_BAD_REGISTRY
- Empty registry (valid format, zero entries) => load succeeds (zero entries is valid; outcome will be UNRESOLVED)
acceptance_criteria: TARGET FILE: src/registry.rs only. Include #[cfg(test)] mod tests. Test: registry.json parsing, mapping file discovery, SQLite index build, staleness check, E_BAD_REGISTRY cases. VERIFICATION: cargo test -- registry
close_reason: Registry loading complete - full implementation with registry.json parsing, SQLite index creation with staleness checking, mapping file validation, comprehensive error handling, write permission fallback, and complete test coverage. Quality gate passes.

title: [CANON-V1/P00.10] Prove the resolve-to-entity-link cutover contract
description:
## Background
The implemented `canon resolve` workbench contains valuable two-tape record-linkage behavior, but as a sibling product it duplicates the entity workbench's strategy, artifact, evidence, refusal, review, and registry-write concepts. The word "resolve" is also overloaded by exact lookup and strategy selection. The capability must survive while the second public engine and mental model do not.

## Technical Approach
Own the cutover contract around the shared-engine implementation in bd-11ai. Inventory every `canon resolve` flag, input field, operator, artifact field, outcome, metric, refusal, write-back behavior, fixture, documentation claim, and operator/schema surface; assign each a typed destination under generic `canon entity link`; define the golden parity comparator; update callers and public contracts only after the shared native implementation passes it. Require explicit user approval before deleting legacy files. Do not add a compatibility shim: once parity is proven, change callers directly.

## Success Criteria
- Every useful v0 capability has one named generic destination or an explicitly justified rejection.
- Frozen cross-tape fixtures demonstrate decision, unmatched/ambiguous, gold-metric, refusal, and exact-replay parity.
- The final CLI/schema/help/operator/docs expose one entity workbench namespace.
- No structured-finance or other industry vocabulary is hardcoded into link mode.
- No legacy file is removed without the explicit deletion authorization required by AGENTS.md.

## Test Plan
Run old and new public subprocesses against frozen neutral and historical fixtures before cutover; compare canonicalized decisions, gold metrics, refusal codes, determinism, mutation intent, and exact replay. Exercise happy, partial, ambiguous, malformed strategy, budget refusal, read-only, and no-mutation paths. Log commands, fixture hashes, exit codes, artifact hashes, and every accepted parity exception.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/cli.rs`
- `src/lib.rs`
- `src/resolve/mod.rs`
- `tests/resolve_end_to_end.rs`
- `tests/resolve_golden.rs`
- `docs/IDENTITY_ARCHITECTURE.md`

## Considerations
This bead is the migration firewall, not a second implementation task. Cross-dataset linkage is a generic execution mode with typed directionality; the engine implementation belongs to bd-11ai.
notes:
## Domain-neutrality invariant
`canon entity link` is a generic two-or-more-dataset record-linkage mode. Core types and operators may reference only observations, sources/tapes, field mappings, namespaces, candidate blocks, evidence, constraints, decisions, and provenance. Structured-finance terms, identifiers, source adapters, thresholds, and role semantics live exclusively in versioned profiles, strategies, vocabularies, provider packs, and evaluation corpora. Add a source/contract conformance test that rejects domain vocabulary or conditional behavior in the core engine. Structured-finance fixtures prove the abstraction under a demanding use case; they do not define it.

Review55 tightening 2026-07-11: blocker remains sound in the current dirty tree. src/cli.rs now has entity link/evidence and src/resolve/mod.rs has native link/parity hooks, so the smallest safe handoff is a parity-harness-only slice: reserve tests/resolve_end_to_end.rs, tests/resolve_golden.rs, and exact resolve fixture/golden paths touched; read src/resolve/mod.rs but do not change CLI/docs/operator surfaces in that slice. Full resolve-to-entity-link cutover still needs the shared-file window already listed in comments, especially src/cli.rs, src/lib.rs, docs/IDENTITY_ARCHITECTURE.md, operator.json, and help fixtures. Do not remove or hide CanonCommand::Resolve until bd-np37/operator/help contract work is coordinated.
close_reason: Cutover contract converged: one public entity-link namespace, executable shared-engine behavior, frozen parity and mutation proofs, domain-neutral tripwire, and adversarial PASS.

title: [CANON-V1/P10.2] Compile portable exact-lookup artifacts for constrained runtimes
description:
## Background
Some consumers need read-only exact lookup without SQLite, filesystem mutation, or the full workbench. A compiled portable artifact can expand Canon's reach while preserving exact semantics.

## Technical Approach
Design a deterministic immutable lookup artifact containing normalized keys, canonical IDs/types, rule/provenance references, registry digest, collision checks, and format version. Evaluate sorted mmap table, perfect hash, and optional WASM-compatible representation against size/build/runtime tradeoffs. Readers perform no cache writes and verify the root digest.

## Success Criteria
- Portable lookup results and unresolved reasons match canonical registry/SQLite backends exactly.
- Build output is deterministic and rejects duplicate/conflicting keys.
- Reader is read-only, bounded, and usable without network or temp files.
- Format choice is justified with measured size/latency/memory and simple long-term verification.

## Test Plan
Generate artifacts for tiny, Unicode, collision, and large registries; compare every key against canonical lookup, corrupt sections, test mmap/read-only/WASM target where supported, and benchmark cold/warm behavior.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/registry/export_lookup.rs`
- `src/portable_lookup.rs`
- `tests/portable_lookup.rs`

## Considerations
A new format must earn its maintenance cost; SQLite search and flat mappings remain supported rather than replaced.

- Every exported row traces to the package digest.

Run cross-platform public subprocess E2E with an offline guard, dbt-compatible and SQLite consumer checks, repeated-run determinism, read-only source inspection, and cache corruption/rebuild.
