comments.text:
TILE PRE-STITCHING IS ALREADY UNDER WAY IN cmdrvl-curves, LANDING NOW 2026-08-14. Verified
by reading the in-progress beads. This confirms the pre-resolved-tile architecture and
supplies hard facts that change several canon geo assumptions.

== WHAT IS ACTUALLY LANDING ==

  cmdrvl-curves bd-30ho   OVERTURE MAPS, release 2026-07-22.0. Themes buildings,
                          building_parts, PLACES, addresses, divisions. Snowflake DDL
                          APPLIED (OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_HOT / _EXT /
                          OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURE_H3_COVERAGE plus 14 per-type views);
                          manifest scan running, 0 rows landed yet.
  cmdrvl-curves bd-1ssr   FEMA USA STRUCTURES, 135,321,228 features nationally. National
                          landing IN PROGRESS; DC / AK / AL complete, AR running.
                          FEMA_USA_STRUCTURES_HOT loaded and read back (DC = 64,701 rows).
  cmdrvl-curves bd-3fyv   MICROSOFT GLOBALML FOOTPRINTS, release 2026-07-24. Landing IN
                          PROGRESS: 179 of 2,415 US files, 5,219,860 rows at 14:45Z.
  cmdrvl-curves bd-11uu   HUD USPS ADDRESS VACANCIES -- **BLOCKED**, and not a tile source.
                          HUD restricts it to registered governmental/non-profit users and
                          the sublicense forbids selling, licensing or distributing the
                          data. DO NOT PLAN ANY CANON GEO CAPABILITY ON IT.

NOTE ON "FOURSQUARE OS PLACES": it arrives as OVERTURE'S PLACES THEME, not a separate
Foursquare landing. That is the POI level in bd-2cbs, and it is in the same table family as
Overture buildings.

== FINDING 1: THE LANDED H3 GRAIN IS r4 / r7 / r8. THERE IS NO r9. ==
All three sources partition by h3_r4 and carry H3_R7 and H3_R8 columns. The epic's default
tile is res-9 and it is NOT precomputed anywhere.

AND THERE IS A CONVENIENT COINCIDENCE WORTH DELIBERATELY EXPLOITING: an r8 cell is
approximately 0.737 km2 -- which is almost exactly the area the epic specifies for its WORK
UNIT (an r9 cell plus k-ring 1 = 7 cells = 0.737 km2). So the already-landed H3_R8 column is
essentially the intended work-unit size.
ACTION FOR bd-2b9d: reconsider r9-plus-k-ring versus r8-plus-k-ring as the work unit, now
that r8 is precomputed across every source and r9 is not. This does not change the
requirement to compute cells in canon with a vetted Rust library -- the Snowflake H3 helper
defects (edgar-elt br-2wir) still stand -- but it does mean the warehouse can prefilter at
r8 for free, and the resolution decision now has a third input alongside node count and
human legibility.

== FINDING 2: POLYGON-TO-CELLS RETURNS EMPTY FOR SMALL BUILDINGS. LIVE, MEASURED. ==
From bd-3fyv: "H3_POLYGON_TO_CELLS alone inserted only 116 coverage rows for 354,804 hot
rows because small buildings often contain no H3 r8 cell centroid." Fixed there by using a
guaranteed CENTROID_H3_R8 plus H3_TRY_POLYGON_TO_CELLS.

THIS IS DIRECTLY THE MEMBERSHIP QUESTION bd-10s2 AND bd-2b9d SPECIFY. At r8 or r9 a
building is much smaller than a cell, so "which cells does this polygon cover" is
degenerate: the standard polygon-to-cells contract returns cells whose CENTRES fall inside
the polygon, and for a building that set is almost always EMPTY.
CONSEQUENCE: membership must be CENTROID-ANCHORED with polygon coverage as a supplement for
the large-feature case (parcels, campuses, complexes), NOT the other way round. My earlier
recommendation on bd-10s2 -- "full intersection cover for membership plus a single
deterministic anchor cell" -- is right in intent but inverted in emphasis, and applying it
naively with polygon_to_cells would have silently produced empty membership for nearly every
building. Correct it there.

== FINDING 3: OUR OWN SOURCES CARRY LICENSE OBLIGATIONS. bd-pq5w IS SCOPED TOO NARROWLY. ==
I framed license containment entirely around the CLIENT's licensed parcel layer. The landed
research shows OUR side has obligations too, and they differ per source:
    Overture buildings, divisions      ODbL-1.0            <-- SHARE-ALIKE
    Overture places                    per-source mix of CDLA-Permissive-2.0, Apache-2.0,
                                       CC0-1.0; source license must be retained
    Overture addresses                 source-specific, incl. NAD Access and Usage License
    FEMA USA Structures                CC-BY-4.0, attribution to ORNL and FEMA Geospatial
                                       Response Office REQUIRED
    Microsoft GlobalML                 CDLA-Permissive-2.0 current release; older vintages
                                       need per-release revalidation
bd-30ho states plainly: "License segmentation by source array is REQUIRED before any derived
product ships. Treat as a build-time gate, not a later cleanup."

ODbL SHARE-ALIKE IS THE COMMERCIAL ISSUE AND IT NEEDS AN OPERATOR DECISION, NOT AN
ENGINEERING ONE. A tile is a derived product. If it mixes ODbL Overture buildings with
everything else, the derived tile may inherit share-alike obligations that are
incompatible with a paid distribution model. Options to evaluate deliberately:
  (a) segregate ODbL-derived features into a separately-licensed layer of the tile, with
      the license class carried per feature -- note OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_EXT ALREADY HAS
      LICENSE_CLASS AND LICENSE_TERMS COLUMNS, so the substrate for this exists;
  (b) build the commercial tile from the permissive sources only (FEMA CC-BY, Microsoft
      CDLA) and treat Overture as an internal enrichment;
  (c) accept share-alike and publish the tile openly.
REQUIRED IN bd-pq5w AND bd-1uld: license class per FEATURE in the tile artifact, and a
declared per-tile license posture that composes our obligations with the client's. The
artifact license boundary now has TWO directions, not one.

== FINDING 4: THE ATTRIBUTE CHANNELS FOR bd-272d ARE REAL, AND ONE IS MODELLED ==
Attribute anchoring needs class, size, floors, year. What is actually arriving:
    FEMA        OCC_CLS, PRIM_OCC (occupancy class), SQFEET, PROP_ADDR, UUID, BUILD_ID
    Overture    building class, height, num_floors, GERS id
    Microsoft   height (subset only), confidence, NO ID
    MapPLUTO    BLDGCLASS, LANDUSE, BLDGAREA, LOTAREA, NUMBLDGS, NUMFLOORS, YEARBUILT
So the six-field client contract has a counterpart on the tile side for every field except
YEAR BUILT, which only MapPLUTO supplies -- meaning year-built anchoring works in NYC and
degrades outside it until a national year source exists. Record that as a known national
limitation rather than discovering it later.

CRITICAL: FEMA OCCUPANCY IS MODELLED, NOT SURVEYED. bd-1ssr requires a provenance flag
"so downstream never treats it as surveyed." Attribute anchoring MUST carry that flag into
the evidence and weight modelled attributes below observed ones. A modelled occupancy class
driving a hard eliminative filter (bd-2zdz's assemblage type filter) would be a silent error
generator -- the filter is HARD, so a wrong modelled class removes the correct candidate
before anything is scored. Use modelled occupancy as SUPPORT evidence, never as a hard
filter, unless corroborated.

== FINDING 5: NO STABLE ID CONFIRMED FOR TWO SOURCES ==
Microsoft has no id at all -- bd-3fyv derives "a deterministic feature hash because no
stable id." Overture ADDRESSES are alpha with no stable GERS id either. This confirms
bd-2cbs rule 4 (alias-less participants) and extends it: the alias-less set is Microsoft
footprints AND Overture addresses, not just Microsoft.
A derived feature hash is NOT an alias and must not be minted into a registry -- it will
change whenever the geometry changes, which violates the tile identifier stability contract
in bd-12gh.

== FINDING 6: OVERTURE ADDRESSES CANNOT BE THE ADDRESS-SET SOURCE ==
bd-30ho: "Addresses theme is ALPHA -- do not build a contract against it yet," no stable
GERS id, multi-source licensing including NAD terms. US count 127,719,691.
So bd-35qg's address-set acquisition is NOT solved by Overture. NYC PAD or the per-BIN
addresses in the landed footprints file (bd-397d) remain the path, and the national story
stays open. Do not let the size of the Overture addresses count create false confidence.

== WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE WORKED-CASE CORPUS (bd-tccn) ==
The corpus can now stage its non-MapPLUTO pulls against REAL TABLE NAMES rather than
placeholders:
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.FEMA_USA_STRUCTURES_HOT              partially loaded (DC, AK, AL)
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.MICROSOFT_GLOBALML_BUILDING_FOOTPRINTS_HOT   partially loaded
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_HOT           DDL applied, 0 rows
    plus the *_FEATURE_H3_COVERAGE tables for each
NEW YORK IS NOT YET LOADED IN ANY OF THE THREE. FEMA is alphabetical by state and is at AR;
Microsoft is 179/2415 files; Overture has not started landing. So the full-tile version of
every case remains blocked, exactly as the corpus bead predicted -- but the blocker is now
a KNOWN COMPLETION DATE rather than an unlanded dataset, and the table names and column
shapes are already fixed enough to write the extraction queries against.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
ARCHITECTURE SUPERSEDED 2026-08-15 — see docs/PLAN_CANON_GEO.md.

An adversarial multi-model design session produced a materially different architecture,
which then survived a red team that destroyed two intermediate designs. The tile is modelled
as a BOUNDED UNIVERSE and every piece of evidence is a CONSTRAINT; propagation runs to a
fixpoint; the residual model set IS the answer. There is no proposer channel.

THE THREE PROPERTIES THAT MATTER:
- CONFLUENCE. The fixpoint is independent of the order constraints are applied (Tarski 1955;
  Cousot & Cousot 1977; Apt 1999), so determinism is a theorem rather than an engineering
  effort.
- MONOTONICITY. Constraints only add and domains only shrink, so a tile resolved with four
  sources today and six next year yields a TIGHTER residual, never a contradicting one. The
  earlier answer was never wrong, only less resolved.
- STRUCTURAL ABSTENTION. The residual model set is the answer. No threshold anywhere.

THE KEY DESIGN RULE IS rho, THE SOUNDNESS DISCIPLINE. Every source attribute enters the
solver only through a declared versioned relaxation mapping it to the WEAKEST constraint the
source can actually support. An interpolated geocode becomes a 150m disc rather than a
location. A parcel ADDRESS becomes "one of this lot's addresses" rather than functional
equality. OWNERNAME equal PERMITS an assemblage; OWNERNAME different constrains NOTHING.
Every noisy channel is admitted only in its sound direction — which is what dissolved the
proposer dilemma that broke the two earlier designs.

AND THE COMMERCIAL CONSEQUENCE: if every rho is sound, the true assignment is in the model
set, so AN EMPTY MODEL SET IS A PROOF that a named source violated its own published error
model — attributable, falsifiable, and mailable to the vendor.

Read PLAN_CANON_GEO.md before starting any geo work. Section 11 carries the bead-by-bead
supersession table. Appendix A covers frozen-weight observers and imagery sources. APPENDIX
B RECORDS THE FIRST HARD MEASUREMENT, WHICH FALSIFIED A LOAD-BEARING CLAIM — read it before
trusting any performance number in the plan.

Raw session artifacts, including the red team and the adversarial reviews, are preserved
under docs/geo_design_session/ with a reading guide.

title: Implement staged org solver and reconciliation
description:
Implement the staged org solver and reconciliation engine.

Use the exact staged solver from the plan: seeds, reciprocal-best backbone merges, direct attachments with winner margins, abstentions, incumbent reconciliation, and escrow actions. Enforce the BDC-first rules around positive name evidence, no attachment chaining, single-best witness pairs, single-incumbent inheritance, multi-incumbent conflict abstention, and promotable-new gating by trusted anchor or distinct document count.

Keep the work in `src/org/solve.rs` only, with inline unit tests built from direct in-memory edge/result fixtures.

## Acceptance Criteria
`src/org/solve.rs` emits the scaffolded solve/run artifact types with deterministic entity ordering, inheritance, contradictions, and proposed escrow actions.

title: [SPLINK-STEAL/S8] diagnostics: unlinkables report (intrinsic match ceiling per surface)
description:
## Problem this solves
Some records can never auto-link regardless of threshold tuning: their populated fields are too sparse or degraded to reach backbone/attach thresholds even against a perfect duplicate of themselves. Knowing that fraction up front (a) sets honest auto-accept expectations per corpus BEFORE the grind (so "82% auto-accept" is recognized as the data ceiling, not a strategy failure), and (b) routes structurally hopeless records straight to enrichment or the inbox instead of wasting review passes on them.

## Build
canon entity diagnose unlinkables (or a report section in run/link artifacts):
- Per prepared surface, compute the maximum attainable support score: score the surface against a hypothetical perfect twin under the active strategy (every configured operator fires at full strength given the fields actually populated on that surface).
- Report the distribution of max-attainable scores vs the solver thresholds; list surfaces whose ceiling < attach/backbone thresholds, with missing-field reasons (which absent fields cost how many units).
- Surface the result as ranking context for the inbox (bd-fung consumes it as one more deterministic signal).

## Splink reference (clone at /Users/zac/Source/opensource/splink)
- splink/internals/unlinkables.py — self-match ceiling concept ("proportion of records with insufficient information to link to themselves")
- docs/topic_guides/evaluation/overview.md — how unlinkables frames intrinsic data-content limits

## How to test
- Sparse-row fixture (name-only, no anchors, no context) flagged with correct ceilings and correct missing-field attributions.
- Ceiling correctness property: for each surface, ceiling equals the evidence stage's actual score for (surface, exact clone of surface) under the same strategy.
- Determinism replay across runs and shuffles.
- Report-only: no artifact chain or outcome semantics change (byte-identical run artifacts with the feature unused).

## Doctrine constraints
Deterministic read-only diagnostics; integer units; no solver or outcome changes.

title: [CANON-V1/P05.1] Define bitemporal identity facts with provenance and trust
description:
## Background
Identity claims change over time: names change, identifiers retire or recycle, objects merge or split, data arrives late, and sources correct earlier assertions. A timeless alias map cannot answer what was believed when or valid as of a date.

## Technical Approach
Define domain-neutral `canon.identity.fact.v1` with subject/object IDs, typed predicate, valid interval, recorded-at interval or transaction sequence, source locator, materialization digest, assertion status, trust-policy reference, supersession/retraction linkage, and optional scope. Specify boundaries, open ends, canonical serialization, fact identity, and conflict representation.

## Success Criteria
- The model distinguishes event validity from when Canon learned/corrected it.
- Accepted, retracted, and superseded facts retain immutable provenance.
- Equivalent facts deduplicate; contradictory facts coexist explicitly.
- Current date or file mtime never affects semantics.

## Test Plan
Round-trip invented facts across boundaries, late arrivals, corrections, duplicate/conflicting sources, and clock-independent serialization; property-test interval and supersession invariants.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/temporal/mod.rs`
- `src/temporal/fact.rs`
- `schemas/canon.identity.fact.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/temporal_fact.rs`

## Considerations
Facts are assertions, not automatically trusted truth. Acceptance policy and compiled snapshots remain explicit.

title: Registry diff and changelog (canon registry diff)
description:
## Summary

Add `canon registry diff` to compare two registry versions and report what changed. Essential operational tooling for materialized registries — when you re-materialize from OpenFIGI weekly, you need to know what changed before you start resolving against the new version.

## Motivation

Materialized registries are snapshots. When you re-materialize, identifiers get added (new instruments issued), removed (instruments delisted), or changed (corporate actions — ticker changes, mergers). Without diff, you are resolving against a new registry version blind. With diff, you know exactly what shifted and can assess impact before updating your pipeline.

This also feeds the spine: `canon registry diff` output can be piped to `rvl` for materiality analysis — "of the 47 mappings that changed, which ones affect positions I actually hold?"

## Design

### Subcommand

```bash
canon registry diff \
  --old registries/openfigi-cusip-v2026.02/ \
  --new registries/openfigi-cusip-v2026.03/ \
  [--emit json|summary]
```

### Output (JSON)

```json
{
  "version": "canon_registry_diff.v0",
  "old": { "id": "openfigi-cusip", "version": "2026.02.28" },
  "new": { "id": "openfigi-cusip", "version": "2026.03.05" },
  "summary": {
    "total_old": 4183,
    "total_new": 4210,
    "added": 34,
    "removed": 7,
    "changed": 12,
    "unchanged": 4157
  },
  "added": [
    { "input": "92936U101", "canonical_id": "BBG01ABCDEF0", "canonical_type": "composite_figi", "rule_id": "OPENFIGI_CUSIP_TO_FIGI" }
  ],
  "removed": [
    { "input": "78462F103", "canonical_id": "BBG000BVG4K0", "canonical_type": "composite_figi", "reason": "not_in_new_registry" }
  ],
  "changed": [
    {
      "input": "931142103",
      "old": { "canonical_id": "BBG000BJ2GK0", "canonical_type": "composite_figi" },
      "new": { "canonical_id": "BBG00XXXXXXX", "canonical_type": "composite_figi" },
      "change_type": "figi_change"
    }
  ]
}
```

### Summary mode

```bash
$ canon registry diff --old v2026.02/ --new v2026.03/ --emit summary
openfigi-cusip: 2026.02.28 → 2026.03.05
  +34 added, -7 removed, ~12 changed, =4157 unchanged
  Notable: 3 ticker changes (corporate actions), 7 delistings
```

### Composability with the spine

```bash
# What changed in the registry?
canon registry diff --old v2026.02/ --new v2026.03/ > evidence/registry-diff.json

# Which changes affect my positions?
# (extract changed input IDs, filter positions file, run rvl)
canon registry diff --old v2026.02/ --new v2026.03/ \
  | jq -r '.changed[].input' > /tmp/changed-cusips.txt

# Seal the evidence
pack seal evidence/ --note "Registry update 2026.02 → 2026.03"
```

## Acceptance criteria

- `canon registry diff --old <dir> --new <dir>` compares two registry versions
- Reports added, removed, changed, unchanged counts
- JSON output includes full detail for each category
- Summary mode (--emit summary) gives human-readable one-liner
- Both registries must have the same id (refuse if comparing apples to oranges)
- Handles registries with different mapping file sets (old has cusip-to-figi.json only, new adds cusip-to-ticker.json)
- Deterministic output: same two registries = same diff, always
- Tests: known registries with specific additions, removals, and changes
close_reason: Implemented canon registry diff with deterministic effective-entry comparisons, summary output, refusals, and tests

title: [CANON-V1/P02.2] Lock all project inputs, packages, strategies, and policy hashes
description:
## Background
A manifest can point at mutable tags and local inputs, so it is not by itself a reproducibility proof. Identity decisions must be replayable months later against the exact source bytes, strategy, registry, policy, extension packages, and executable contract.

## Technical Approach
Define `canon.project.lock.v1` as a deterministic sorted lockfile containing content digests and resolved identities for every input, registry, strategy, provider snapshot, profile, ontology/vocabulary, policy, schema, and relevant Canon build. Add generation, verification, stale detection, and explicit refresh; ordinary runs never rewrite it.

## Success Criteria
- Equivalent projects produce byte-identical lockfiles independent of enumeration order.
- Changed bytes, retagged packages, missing dependencies, and tool-contract drift fail before execution with actionable diffs.
- Refresh is explicit and leaves an auditable before/after receipt.
- No credential, host-local absolute path, nondeterministic timestamp, or private raw value contaminates the lock hash.

## Test Plan
Use shuffled manifests and copied workspaces; mutate one dependency class at a time; assert exact stale reasons; and prove read-only lock checking leaves content, mtimes, and directory inventory unchanged.

- `schemas/canon.project.lock.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/project_lock.rs`

## Considerations
Distinguish a human-edited manifest from a machine-generated lock. Mutable tags may be recorded for provenance, but execution pins resolved digests.

title: [CANON-V1/P05.5] Compile as-of identity facts into immutable exact lookup snapshots
description:
## Background
Production lookup must remain exact and fast even when source truth is temporal and contested. Runtime traversal of a fact graph would violate Canon's deliberately boring lookup kernel.

## Technical Approach
Implement a deterministic compiler that accepts fact packages, trust/conflict policy, scope, `--as-of`, `--known-as-of`, and parent snapshot; selects valid accepted identity aliases; abstains on unresolved conflicts; and emits a normal immutable registry package plus a compilation proof. Relationships are emitted as sidecars/projections and never affect exact mapping unless policy accepted an identity fact.

## Success Criteria
- A frozen fact set and policy compile to byte-identical registry snapshots.
- Every emitted mapping points to the exact facts, intervals, scope, and policy clause that authorized it.
- Ambiguous/conflicting facts are omitted with structured diagnostics, never last-write-wins.
- The resulting registry works through unchanged exact lookup, row-preserving apply, dbt seed, and searchable index backends.

## Test Plan
Compile boundary dates, known-as-of corrections, scope subsets, conflicts, retractions, and relation-only facts; compare exact query results and proof references. Shuffle inputs and repeat.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/temporal/compile.rs`
- `schemas/canon.temporal.compile.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/temporal_compile.rs`

## Considerations
Compilation turns rich evidence into boring exact truth for a declared slice. It must never claim that one snapshot is timeless.

title: [CANON-V1/P08.6] Specify the filesystem-first publication backend seam
description:
## Background
Existing wrapper-managed object-store sync exposed the real requirement: registry publication must detect divergent writers. The open-source engine does not need built-in awareness of any cloud provider, and the prior decision was to remain filesystem-first and cloud-free by default.

## Technical Approach
Specify the minimal publication backend trait used by immutable package and channel operations: read by digest, create immutable object if absent, inspect head, compare-and-swap channel/head, list declared ancestry where supported, and return typed capability/refusal information. Implement the local filesystem backend as default with atomic rename/create semantics. Evaluate an optional generic object-store/OCI backend only after CAS and OCI contracts are stable; do not shell out to vendor CLIs or add provider SDKs to the default binary.

## Success Criteria
- Core lookup and local project execution have no cloud dependency or ambient network access.
- Registry mutations require expected base digest regardless of backend.
- Backends that cannot enforce required CAS refuse mutation rather than race.
- External wrappers can use immutable package push/pull safely because mutable head changes are an explicit transaction.
- The design records why native provider-specific URI handling remains deferred.

## Test Plan
Run the backend conformance suite against filesystem and the local OCI test backend; exercise create-if-absent, identical writes, stale/divergent heads, crash boundaries, read-only mode, capability refusal, and concurrent subprocess writers. Log operations, expected/actual digests, and filesystem/object inventories.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/distribution/backend.rs`
- `src/registry/transaction.rs`
- `tests/publication_backend_conformance.rs`
- `docs/OCI_ARTIFACTS.md`

## Considerations
This resolves the original S3-versus-wrapper question in favor of generic correctness: filesystem-first core, immutable OCI distribution, and a narrow capability seam. A provider-specific backend is future optional work only if repeated external demand justifies its dependency and maintenance cost.

Evidence: cargo test --test publication_backend_conformance (8 passed); cargo test --test registry_concurrency_e2e (6 passed); cargo fmt --check passed; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings passed. Full cargo test was started and progressed through many suites with no failures, then interrupted per coordinator closeout request to release reservations promptly.

comments.text: Decision update: do not implement native s3:// registry read/write in core right now. The part that is in canon's public OSS spirit is registry write correctness, not cloud transport. A stronger public version of this bead would be generic registry transaction safety: expected base registry.version/content hash before mutation, refusal on divergence, atomic next-version write where the backend supports it, and an internal backend seam with local filesystem as the only default backend. Avoid AWS SDK/object_store dependencies in the normal binary, and avoid an aws-cli wrapper as first-class canon behavior. Treat S3/object-store publishing as future optional backend work only if repeated real users need it; until then, keep canon filesystem-first and cloud-free by default.

title: canon geo: condo ledger-representation bridge — unit-BBL <-> billing-BBL <-> BIN crosswalk with block/geometry confirmation

title: canon geo D6: NYC orthoimagery tile pins and the named NYC observer error population
description:
PACKET PK-D6a-pins (stage D6 entry condition) from docs/PLAN_CANON_GEO.md §18.4 and §19.5 row D6, minted 2026-09-02 in the coverage pass. This bead carries the full design so no implementer needs the plan document. It owns the two D6 ENTRY CONDITIONS that had no owner: (1) NYC ortho tile pins recorded with URL, byte range, ETag or SHA-256, vintage, and license text hash; (2) the named NYC error population declared before any observer runs. bd-ci1n owns the pin TYPE and its validator; this bead owns the recorded pin MANIFEST and the population declaration, both of which are inputs every D6 module (bd-ci1n, bd-36sc, bd-101v, the null observer bead, the count observer bead) reads.

== WHY ==
§18.4: every image tile is pinned by URL, byte range, ETag or SHA-256, vintage, and license text hash. Without recorded pins nothing in D6 can be replayed (I07) and no adjudication crop (bd-36sc), evidence card (bd-101v), or observer row (bd-ci1n) has a tile digest to bind to. §18.4 third use: solver input is allowed "only after the observer's error is characterized on a named population"; §19.5 D6 entry: "the named NYC error population declared before any observer runs". Declaring the population after seeing observer output is the reward-hacking pattern the plan forbids (TH20 proof-class inflation, and selection bias in the characterization). Network acquisition is outside Canon's deterministic offline build (AGENTS.md, PROVIDER_SDK.md): the fetch is a script under scripts/, the recorded manifest is what Canon consumes.

== SOURCES (§18.4, in order of first use) ==
NYS and NYC 6-inch orthoimagery (CC BY, even years 2006 to 2024, byte-range capable with ETags) for the proving ground. 3DEP lidar for measured height. NAIP through the Planetary Computer mirror as the national fallback. NOAA emergency response imagery for event-scoped change. Overture or OSM data for street context, never a rendered commercial tile. This bead records NYC ortho pins first; 3DEP, NAIP (Franklin tier 2 under bd-s07o), and NOAA ERI pins reuse the same manifest shape and the same script with a different source profile, and are recorded when the stage that consumes them starts.

== DELIVERABLES ==
1. scripts/geo_observer/pin_tiles.sh (network acquisition, outside the canon binary). Inputs: a source profile file (scripts/geo_observer/sources/nyc_ortho.json: base URL template, vintage list, license id, path to the committed license text), a window list (H3 r9 cells or bounding boxes in EPSG:2263 for the population subjects). For each tile: HTTP HEAD to capture ETag and Content-Length; ranged GET of the bytes actually used; BLAKE3 of the bytes; record `{url, byte_range, etag, blake3, vintage: {start, end} (closed interval, calendar year of the flight), license_id, license_text_blake3}`. The script never writes into src/ or tests/; it writes scripts/geo_observer/pins/nyc_ortho_<vintage>.pins.json.
2. The committed pin manifest scripts/geo_observer/pins/nyc_ortho_2024.pins.json (and 2022 or 2020 for the change-event pair) with `version: "canon_geo_image_tile_pin.v0"` rows exactly matching bd-ci1n's GeoImageTilePin field list: `url`, `byte_range: Option<(u64, u64)>`, `etag: Option<String>`, `blake3`, `vintage: GeoValidTimeInterval`, `license_id`, `license_text_blake3`. Also the committed license text scripts/geo_observer/licenses/cc_by_4_0.txt whose BLAKE3 is the `license_text_blake3` every NYC row carries.
3. The named NYC error population artifact scripts/geo_observer/populations/nyc_h7_observer_population.v0.json, contract `canon_geo_error_population.v0` (an additive contract owned by observer.rs under the §19.3 shared shape: `CANON_GEO_ERROR_POPULATION_VERSION`, `canonical_error_population_bytes`, `validate_error_population_artifact`, schemas/canon.geo.error_population.v0.schema.json, one `error_population_schema_matches_a_real_instance` test in tests/geo_schemas.rs). Fields: `version`, `population_id` (string, e.g. `nyc.h7.observer.2026-09`), `region` (`nyc`), `selection_seed: u64`, `selection_query_blake3` (BLAKE3 of the checked-in SQL or of the H.7 population artifact the subjects were drawn from), `source_population_blake3` (BLAKE3 of the `canon_geo_h7_population.v0` or `canon_geo_population_request.v0` artifact), `subjects: Vec<{ subject_id, truth_plane: GeoTruthPlane, window_blake3, parcel_ids: Vec<String> }>` sorted by `subject_id`, `declared_before_observer_ids: Vec<String>` (observer contract ids that MUST NOT exist yet when this file is committed; enforced by the test below), `stratum_counts: BTreeMap<String, u64>` per truth plane. Selection rule: seeded deterministic sample (splitmix64 over the sorted subject ids, seed recorded) of at least 40 subjects from the D1 H.7 cohort stratified per truth plane so that `NonRoundAmountDateLegalBorough` and `RoundExactLenderParty` are both represented and never pooled (I09); the seed and the SQL are committed alongside so the selection is reproducible and cannot be re-drawn to flatter an observer.
4. Validation: `validate_error_population_artifact` refuses `invalid_input` with `detail["field"]` when `subjects` is empty, unsorted, has duplicate ids, has a subject whose `window_blake3` is empty, or when `selection_seed` and `selection_query_blake3` are absent. A pin manifest validation test parses every committed pin row with serde_json, checks every field non-empty (byte_range and etag may be None only when the source does not support ranges, recorded in the source profile), recomputes the license text BLAKE3 from the committed license file and asserts equality with every row's `license_text_blake3`.

== ORDERING GUARANTEE (the point of the entry condition) ==
The population file carries `declared_before_observer_ids`. The observer contract (bd-ci1n `GeoObserverContract.error_population_id`) must name this `population_id`, and the characterization artifact (count observer bead) must carry `population_blake3` equal to the canonical bytes digest of this file. A test in tests/geo_observer.rs (shipped by the count observer bead, referenced here) asserts that the population file's git-recorded first commit precedes the observer contract file's first commit is NOT a test Canon can run offline; instead the digest chain is the enforcement: a characterization whose `population_blake3` does not match the committed population refuses `observer_error_uncharacterized` (§19.4 row). Do not weaken this to a warning.

== ERROR CODES ==
| `invalid_input` | `validate_error_population_artifact`, pin manifest test | missing or malformed field; `detail["field"]` names it | refusal |
| `observer_license_forbidden` (bd-ci1n) | `admit_observations` | any pin row whose `license_id` is in `forbidden_license_ids` or whose `license_text_blake3` is empty | refusal; the manifest test asserts no NYC row can trigger it |

== CONTRACTS AND THREATS THIS BEAD SERVES ==
C09 (license gate inputs), C10 (digest chain starts at the pin), C22 (shared shape for the new contract), C23 (pins from live NYC sources carry `source_dataset` `nyc.ortho.<vintage>`; fixture pins used by T13, T14, T24 carry `fixture.` and are never these rows), N10 (no commercial basemap tile: the source profile list is the only allowed source list and is committed), TH09, TH20 (population declared with seed before observer output exists).

== TESTS (tests/geo_observer_pins.rs, new binary; each test logs on failure) ==
| T28 (bead-defined, extends §19.6) | D6 | unit | every row of scripts/geo_observer/pins/*.pins.json | every field present; `license_text_blake3` equals BLAKE3 of scripts/geo_observer/licenses/cc_by_4_0.txt; `vintage.start <= vintage.end`; no `url` host in the committed forbidden host list (google, mapbox, arcgis, apple) | a scratch manifest row with `license_id = "commercial_basemap_tos"` fails; a row whose `license_text_blake3` is recomputed from a one-byte-different license fails | LOG on failure: the row index, `url`, expected vs actual `license_text_blake3`, the license file path and length |
| T29 (bead-defined) | D6 | unit | scripts/geo_observer/populations/nyc_h7_observer_population.v0.json | `validate_error_population_artifact` is `Ok`; `subjects.len() >= 40`; both truth planes present in `stratum_counts`; `canonical_error_population_bytes` is byte-identical across two serialize passes | an unsorted or duplicated subject list refuses `invalid_input` with `detail["field"] = "subjects"`; a population with `selection_seed` absent refuses with `detail["field"] = "selection_seed"` | LOG on failure: `population_id`, `selection_seed`, `subjects.len()`, `stratum_counts`, the first out-of-order pair, canonical bytes BLAKE3 from each pass |
| T30 (bead-defined) | D6 | determinism | rerun the selection rule (splitmix64 over sorted ids with the recorded seed) from the committed source population artifact | reproduces exactly the committed `subjects` list | a different seed yields a different list (so the test proves the seed is load-bearing) | LOG on failure: seed, source population BLAKE3, first differing subject id and index, both list lengths |

== E2E SCRIPT (scripts/geo_observer/e2e_pins.sh; logs every step with `set -euo pipefail`, echoes each command, its exit code, and the BLAKE3 of every artifact it reads or writes into <work-dir>/run.log) ==
1. `b3sum scripts/geo_observer/licenses/cc_by_4_0.txt` and compare with every row's `license_text_blake3` via jq; log the digest and the row count.
2. `cargo test --test geo_observer_pins -- --nocapture` (T28 to T30).
3. `cargo test --test geo_schemas error_population_schema_matches_a_real_instance`.
4. `jq -e '.title == "canon.geo.error_population.v0" and .properties.version.const == "canon_geo_error_population.v0" and .additionalProperties == false' schemas/canon.geo.error_population.v0.schema.json`.
5. Optional live step, clearly labeled ACQUISITION and never run in CI: `bash scripts/geo_observer/pin_tiles.sh --source nyc_ortho --vintage 2024 --windows <population>.json --out scripts/geo_observer/pins/` followed by `git diff --stat scripts/geo_observer/pins/` so a changed ETag or digest is visible as a source drift, not a silent replacement.
6. Whole-tree gates: `cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test`.

== RESERVATIONS (Agent Mail; reserve only these files) ==
scripts/geo_observer/pin_tiles.sh, scripts/geo_observer/sources/nyc_ortho.json, scripts/geo_observer/pins/*.pins.json, scripts/geo_observer/licenses/cc_by_4_0.txt, scripts/geo_observer/populations/nyc_h7_observer_population.v0.json, scripts/geo_observer/e2e_pins.sh, tests/geo_observer_pins.rs, schemas/canon.geo.error_population.v0.schema.json. Shared append-only touch points, reserve for the edit only: tests/geo_schemas.rs (one include_str and one test). The `canon_geo_error_population.v0` type lives in src/geo/observer.rs, owned by bd-ci1n: coordinate on thread bd-ci1n before adding it there, or land it first in this bead as the sole edit to that file if bd-ci1n has not started.

== NON-NEGOTIABLES THAT BIND ==
N02 (pins are byte digests, no wall clock in the manifest; the acquisition timestamp lives only in the script log), N07 (the committed NYC pins are live retained evidence, never fixtures; fixture pins are separate and prefixed `fixture.`), N09, N10, I06, I07.

ANTI-REWARD-HACKING (AGENTS.md, binding): no population re-drawn after an observer runs; no pin row edited by hand to match a digest; a changed upstream tile is a recorded drift with a new manifest, never an overwrite of the old rows; code and tests ship together; no new todo!() scaffolds.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
== ACCEPTANCE (round 2: gate as acceptance criterion, D6 entry: pins and the named population) ==

GATE G6 first clause (verbatim from section 19.5 row D6): "observer error characterized on a named NYC population". The population is this bead's; the characterization is bd-3ufk's.

PROOF COMMANDS: `cargo test --test geo_observer_pins` green with T28, T29, T30 in the test names; `cargo test --test geo_schemas error_population_schema_matches_a_real_instance`; the jq pin for `error_population`; `bash scripts/geo_observer/e2e_pins.sh --work-dir <dir>`; whole-tree `cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test`.

DECLARED DENOMINATOR: population `subjects.len() >= 40` with both exact-lender planes present in `stratum_counts` and never pooled (I09); the pin manifest row count logged; the license digest equality holds on every row.

ORDERING GUARANTEE MADE CHECKABLE: the population file's `declared_before_observer_ids` lists `observer.null_footprint` and `observer.count.frozen`; the e2e script asserts with `git ls-files` that neither contract file exists at the commit that adds the population; the digest chain is enforced by bd-3ufk's `observer_error_uncharacterized`.

C IDS THAT MUST HOLD: C09, C10, C22, C23 (NYC pins carry `nyc.ortho.<vintage>`, never `fixture.`), N07, N10. T IDS: T28, T29, T30.

NEGATIVE CASES (round 2 rewrite of T28, whose halves read only "fails"): a scratch manifest row with `license_id = "commercial_basemap_tos"` is refused by `admit_observations` with `observer_license_forbidden` and `detail["field"] = "license_id"`; a row whose `license_text_blake3` was computed over cc_by_4_0.txt with one byte changed fails the manifest test with the expected and actual digests printed; a naive manifest test that compares `license_id` strings only accepts the altered license and fails T28. comments.text:
== HONEST CREDIT (round 3: reward-hacking resistance, proof classes, feature-first ratio; D6 entry: pins and the named population) ==

Cheapest false close: hand-typed pin rows, a population drawn after the observer has run, and a license digest copied from the row rather than recomputed. Exploit / guard pairs:

(2) Proof-class inflation / selection bias. EXPLOIT: declare the population after seeing which subjects the count observer gets right. GUARD (in bead): seeded splitmix64 selection over sorted ids with the seed and SQL committed; declared_before_observer_ids; the e2e asserts with git ls-files that neither observer contract file exists at the commit that adds the population; T30 proves the seed is load-bearing; bd-3ufk refuses a characterization whose population_blake3 differs.

(3) Golden regeneration. EXPLOIT: edit a pin row's blake3 to match a re-downloaded tile. GUARD (in bead): a changed upstream tile is a recorded drift with a new manifest file, never an overwrite; git diff --stat after acquisition. ADDED: pin manifests are append-only by file name (nyc_ortho_<vintage>.pins.json); a row edited in place fails T28 against the acquisition run log digest committed alongside.

(1) Gate self-weakening. EXPLOIT: turn the population validation into a warning. GUARD (in bead): "Do not weaken this to a warning"; observer_error_uncharacterized is a refusal.

(11) Dependency smuggling. EXPLOIT: fetch tiles from inside the canon binary. GUARD: pin_tiles.sh is outside; Canon consumes the manifest only. ADDED: T28 also asserts every url host is in the committed source profile's allow list, not only outside the forbidden list, so an unlisted mirror cannot slip in.

(5) Tautological tests. GUARD (in bead): T28 recomputes the license digest; T29 unsorted or duplicate subjects refuse; T30 seed + 1 differs.

(12) Demo-path hard-coding. EXPLOIT: a vintage or URL literal in observer.rs. GUARD: T27.

(8) Scope-splitting check: the canon_geo_error_population.v0 type lives in observer.rs (bd-ci1n); this bead ships the acquisition script, the manifests, the license text, the population artifact, the schema, T28 to T30, and the e2e. Not a type-only slice. No fold.

FEATURE-FIRST RATIO: this bead is a data capability (retained pins, a typed population artifact with a validator) gating bd-ci1n, bd-35zz, bd-3ufk, bd-36sc, bd-101v (the whole of D6); it is not a process item. It stays.

PROOF CLASS (N07, C23): the NYC pin manifests are retained evidence (acquired live by the script, byte digests, ETags); the population is a seeded retained selection over the observed_snapshot H.7 cohort. They may be cited as the D6 entry condition; they may NOT be cited as a characterization, an observation, or G6.

USER VALUE: every dated observation a buyer later sees is bound to a tile whose URL, bytes, vintage, and license are pinned, and the observer's error was measured on a population chosen before the observer existed, so "absent in the 2024 ortho" cannot be a cherry-picked claim.

comments.text:
== RESOLUTION (round 4) ==

The description's C23 line says NYC pins "carry source_dataset nyc.ortho.<vintage>", but deliverable 2's pin row field list omits it because bd-ci1n's GeoImageTilePin had no such field. bd-ci1n's round-4 resolution adds `source_dataset` to the pin type and controls. comments.text:
== TREE RECONCILIATION (round 5) ==

Verified: GeoTruthPlane variants NonRoundAmountDateLegalBorough and RoundExactLenderParty (src/geo/evaluation.rs:216-222); canon_geo_h7_population.v0 and canon_geo_population_request.v0 exist; the GeoImageTilePin type is bd-ci1n's with the round-4 source_dataset field; scripts/geo_observer/ does not exist yet (owned here).

TREE: GeoValidTimeInterval is { start_day: i64, end_day: i64 } in whole UTC days since 1970-01-01 (src/geo/evidence.rs:94-101). CORRECTION (adopt): rows carry vintage: { start_day, end_day } (the flight year mapped to its first and last day numbers, computed in pin_tiles.sh from the source profile); T28 asserts start_day <= end_day and both within the source profile's year list; no calendar-year field exists on the pin.

MISMATCH 2 (tooling). CLAIM: e2e step 1 runs b3sum. TREE: b3sum is not installed on the development machine. CORRECTION (adopt): step 1 uses the T28 Rust recomputation as the digest check and treats b3sum as optional (skipped with a logged line when absent); no gate depends on b3sum.

comments.text:
== DECISION (round 6) == tooling: `b3sum` replaced; `vintage.start/end` replaced

(1) `b3sum` is not installed, no `canon` subcommand prints a file digest, python3 has no `blake3` module, and the Cargo dependency `blake3 = "1"` (Cargo.toml:18) is reachable only from Rust. BLAKE3 values appear in scripts only as Canon artifact fields (`license_text_blake3`, `blake3` on each pin). This replaces every `b3sum` mention on this bead.

(2) `GeoValidTimeInterval` is `{ start_day: i64, end_day: i64 }` in whole UTC days since 1970-01-01 (src/geo/evidence.rs:98-101). Every pin row carries `vintage: { start_day, end_day }`; T28 asserts `start_day <= end_day` and both inside the source profile's year list; the description's `vintage.start <= vintage.end` and "calendar year of the flight" fields are replaced by these names (round 5 mismatch 1 stands, restated as the controlling wording).

title: [CONVERGENCE/P0] Prove direct resolve-decision parity on unchanged link inputs
description:
## Evidence
The current bd-24l9 parity helpers rewrite historical rows by adding generic profile fields before public entity link execution, and no longer directly compare the preserved internal legacy decision projection with the public link decision artifact. This can hide source-mapping and parity gaps.

## Work
Build a frozen neutral parity fixture or explicit source-mapping artifact that both the internal legacy decision producer and public canon entity link consume without runtime mutation. Hash inputs before and after. Compare decisions, matched/unmatched/ambiguous cases, gold metrics, refusal codes, deterministic bytes, mutation intent, write-back effects, and exact replay. Keep the legacy producer test-only/internal; do not restore a public resolve alias. Any necessary new fixture must be narrowly named, documented, and reserved exactly.

## Success
- The same unchanged input bytes drive both decision paths.
- The comparator freezes every accepted field mapping or explicitly justified rejection.
- Read-only runs leave registry/input bytes unchanged.
- Write-back is separately proven and exact replay succeeds.
- Focused resolve end-to-end and golden tests pass.
- No files are deleted.

## RESERVATIONS
- tests/resolve_end_to_end.rs
- tests/resolve_golden.rs
- exact tests/fixtures/resolve parity files created or edited

title: Funds registry: deterministic mint from NPORT structured IDs — string workbench explicitly deferred
description:
Decision record (2026-07-07, operator + assessment): do NOT run the string entity-resolution workbench on fund names. NPORT-P provides a native identity spine — registrant CIK -> seriesId (S000...) -> LEI at registrant AND series level (regName/regLei/seriesName/seriesId/seriesLei all already extracted in edgar-elt stg_edgar_nport) — so fund identity is deterministic-key territory, not fuzzy-matching territory. Fund names are also maximally collidable ('Growth Fund', 'Income Fund II'): pointing the workbench at them is the false-merge corpus par excellence (NEWMARK lesson) with no upside when keys exist.

What to build instead (when demand arrives, not before — depth-before-breadth gates): a deterministic funds registry, deal-registry pattern: mint from (CIK, seriesId, LEI); accumulate seriesName/regName variants as time-stamped aliases KEYED BY structured id as filings arrive (fund renames become alias history, zero matching judgment); registry then rides the standard rails — dbt-seed export (bd-t1ay), search-index (bd-2mwa), IRI->holon front door (cmdrvl-context bd-2pmk).

Where string ER WOULD earn its keep later, demand-driven: (1) NPORT holdings issuer names where lei/cusip/isin are N/A (loans, repos, swaps, privates) -> canon ORGs; (2) external name-only sources joining into the funds registry. Neither is scheduled.

The high-value cross-product needs NO name ER: NPORT holdings -> CUSIP/FIGI -> unified bond table -> deal_ref = which funds hold which CMBS deals — pure identifier joins riding edgar-ddp br-k3y + edgar-elt br-2yun/br-2fnd. Capture-only: no build scheduled.
notes: This remains an operator deployment decision, not a Canon-core feature. It is related to the generic out-of-tree extension acceptance bead bd-doe2, but it does not block the open-source program and must not introduce fund, filing, or structured-finance semantics into Canon.

title: [CANON-V1/P04.10] Prove the unresolved-to-exact accretion flywheel end to end
description:
## Background
The defining accretive behavior is a closed loop: operational misses become prioritized evidence work, reviewed knowledge becomes a new registry, and the next exact run improves demonstrably.

## Technical Approach
Build a neutral subprocess journey beginning with multiple projects and an intentionally incomplete registry. Capture misses, group them, attach impact, rank, project into shared review, simulate change, promote a new version, replay exact lookup/apply, and compare metrics. Include an alias, a new entity, a related-but-distinct pair, and a deferred ambiguity.

## Success Criteria
- Highest-value work is selected explainably and accepted changes resolve only intended rows.
- Related-distinct and deferred cases remain safely unresolved or relational.
- A second inbox pass deduplicates history and shows measurable recurrence/coverage improvement.
- Commands, reviews, hashes, metrics, filesystem deltas, and refusals are logged.

## Test Plan
Run offline in a clean workspace, repeat with shuffled events/sources, query final exact/dbt/searchable outputs, and validate that impact simulation predicted all deltas.

## RESERVATIONS
- `tests/accretion_end_to_end.rs`
- `tests/fixtures/accretion/neutral-identity`
- `README.md`

## Considerations
Success is compounding trusted exact knowledge, not 100% resolution or domain-specific scoring.

title: [SPLINK-STEAL/S5] external-candidate decision-import recipe (disposable Splink bridge; docs+fixtures only)
description:
## Problem this solves
Until S1/S3/S6 land, multi-column corpora (BDC loan/investment names: issuer + coupon + maturity + type — the shape Splink is genuinely good at) can use Splink's EM-calibrated scoring as a BOOTSTRAP candidate oracle. What canon lacks is a documented, fixture-tested recipe for importing externally-authored decisions through the EXISTING review import — with zero new runtime surface — so the bridge is disposable and core stays standalone. Keeps bd-3ofg (generic adapter contract) correctly deferred: no adapter runtime enters canon.

## Build (docs + fixtures only — no core code)
A doc (docs/EXTERNAL_CANDIDATE_IMPORT.md) specifying the full recipe:
1. Run canon entity run/link to produce artifacts + review queue as normal.
2. External scorer runs OUTSIDE canon (Splink, fully seeded: estimate_u(seed=...), EM from deterministic rules; the saved model JSON committed next to the decisions for provenance).
3. A conversion script (operator-owned, out of tree) authors decision files (match/distinct/defer) ONLY for items above an operator-set probability with no cannot-link conflict; everything else stays defer.
4. canon entity review import validates hashes and applies; audit + promote exactly as normal.
5. Sampled spot-check protocol: operator reviews N% of mechanically-authored decisions before promotion; document the sampling rule.
Include: a committed fixture pair (tiny corpus + pre-scored decisions file) proving the import path end-to-end offline; an explicit caveat that Splink is unsuitable for single-column vocabularies per its own docs ("not designed for a single bag-of-words column") — servicers, sponsors, instrument types stay pure canon; and a retirement clause: this recipe is scaffolding to be retired once S1/S3/S6 close the calibration gap.

## Splink reference (clone at /Users/zac/Source/opensource/splink)
- splink/internals/linker_components/training.py — estimate_u seed parameter (reproducibility requirement for any run feeding decisions)
- splink/internals/linker_components/misc.py — save_model_to_json (provenance artifact to commit)
- splink/internals/realtime.py — compare_records (scoring review-queue pairs directly)
- docs/index.md — the single-column unsuitability statement to quote

## How to test
- Fixture decisions import cleanly through the existing validator; receipts correct.
- Tampered/stale decision file -> atomic refusal (proves external authorship gets no special trust).

title: [SPLINK-STEAL/S2] review export: evidence-signature grouping (decide patterns, not pairs)
description:
## Problem this solves
Review queues scale with item count, but most escrowed items share a handful of evidence signatures (same lanes/operators hit, same score band, same contradiction class). Reviewing item-by-item makes the CMBS tenant long tail humanly infeasible; deciding per-signature collapses thousands of decisions to dozens. This is the review-ergonomics half of the grind problem (S1 is the calibration half).

## Build
- Deterministic evidence-signature computation per review item: sorted (lane, operator, view/field) hit vector + banded score + contradiction class. Signature definition documented in the artifact schema.
- --group-by signature on canon entity review export (both queue and native-review artifacts): items grouped; each group carries signature, member count, deterministic sample members (first-N by stable ID), and aggregate score stats.
- Import side: accept group-level decisions that expand to per-member decisions inside the typed patch receipt — every member listed individually, per-item decision IDs and hash bindings preserved, per-member overrides win over the group decision.
- No new renderer or import format: extend the bd-14m6 native review substrate exactly as bd-fung mandates (single renderer, single validator).

## Splink reference (clone at /Users/zac/Source/opensource/splink)
- splink/internals/splink_comparison_viewer.py + comparison_vector_distribution.py — browse distinct agreement patterns with example rows; one look covers hundreds of pairs. This is the concept to port into the review artifact itself.

## How to test
- Fixture where 500 synthetic pairs collapse to <= 10 signatures; assert group counts and sample determinism.
- Group-decision import expands to exact per-member patches; replay import -> identical receipt.
- Tamper one member's binding -> atomic import refusal (existing staleness semantics unchanged).
- Per-member override coexists with group decision and wins.
- Signature stability under input row-order shuffle.
- Offline HTML projection renders groups with a network-disabled browser.

## Doctrine constraints
Grouping changes presentation and import ergonomics only — zero auto-accept, no change to decision authority, audit gates, or patch semantics.

## RESERVATIONS
- src/entity/review_export.rs
- src/entity/review_import.rs
- src/entity/review.rs
- tests/entity_review_signature_groups.rs
Note: S7 (waterfall) also touches review_export.rs — serialize if both in flight.

title: [CONVERGENCE/P0] Make entity-link suite and row-format contracts executable
description:
## Evidence
The bd-24l9 adversarial review found EntityLinkCli.suite parsed and documented but absent from successful execution, and found operator/help advertising CSV, TSV, JSONL, and NDJSON while the native materializer uses a comma-only CSV reader. Public subprocess parity also lacks explicit max-candidates, max-rows, max-bytes, and no-write assertions.

## Work
Make the normative entity link contract truthful without compatibility theater. An accepted --suite must execute the existing deterministic entity audit path and surface a stable audit artifact/receipt under the work directory, or refuse before writes on invalid suites; it must never be silently ignored. Materialize CSV, TSV, JSONL, and NDJSON through existing format/delimiter detection with deterministic row/value preservation and stable source provenance. Add public subprocess tests for all advertised formats, valid/invalid suite behavior, candidate/row/byte budget refusals, and registry no-mutation when --write-back is absent. Keep entity link domain-neutral and preserve gold, write-back, witness, outcome, and refusal semantics.

## Success
- Every EntityLinkCli flag maps to observable behavior or a structured pre-write refusal.
- CSV, TSV, JSONL, and NDJSON inputs reach the shared native pipeline and preserve row values deterministically.
- Unsupported/malformed input refuses actionably.
- Public subprocess tests cover all three budgets and read-only no-write behavior.
- Operator/help match implementation.
- Focused fmt, clippy, cli_smoke, resolve_end_to_end, and resolve_golden gates pass.
- No files are deleted.

## RESERVATIONS
- src/cli.rs
- src/lib.rs
- src/entity/link.rs
- operator.json
- tests/cli_smoke.rs
- tests/fixtures/canon_v1/help/entity_help.txt
- tests/fixtures/canon_v1/help/entity_link_help.txt
close_reason: Implemented executable entity-link suite auditing, truthful CSV/TSV/JSONL/NDJSON materialization, public budget and no-write coverage, and repaired the native-link integration fixture. Independent focused rustfmt, Clippy, 25 tests across cli_smoke/resolve/native-link, operator JSON validation, diff check, and adversarial review all green; evidence in comments 304-305 and Agent Mail msgs 6676/6680/6681.

title: canon geo D3: event exposure at loan grain, wind-radii rings against exact ledger building geometry
description:
PACKET PK-D3b (stage D3) from docs/PLAN_CANON_GEO.md §18/§19, course correction 2026-09-01. This bead carries the full design so no implementer needs the plan document.

== WHY ==
§18.2: 'these 214 loans in these 31 deals have a building inside the 64-knot wind radius' within hours of an advisory, computed against exact building polygons from the ledger, not address centroids (I11). The cmdrvl-geo MCP already computes storm exposure against the live NHC/CPHC advisory geometry with source hashes; this bead consumes a pinned advisory (GeoAdvisoryPin with wind_radii rings and source_blake3s) offline and joins it to ledger building sets. Rating agency surveillance, servicers, and bond desks rebuild this by hand from address strings today. Ships tests/fixtures/geo/advisory_synthetic_adv12.json (34/50/64 knot square rings placed per T08). Stale advisories (a later advisory_number for the same storm in the archive) refuse; buildings without geometry are listed, never guessed.

== STAGE ROW (§19.5; entry condition, gate, contracts) ==
| D3 | Ledger output surface, event exposure join, cross-deal collision | G1 passed (D2 not required: no ledger field reads an explanation artifact); one full public deal's loans mapped to H.7 subjects with accession and loan ids; `tests/fixtures/geo/advisory_synthetic_adv12.json` shipped by the exposure bead; modules `ledger.rs`, `exposure.rs`, `collision.rs` | G3: one full public deal materializes as ledger rows with claim classes; exposure runs against one archived advisory; collision runs across two deals | C13 to C16, C22, C23, C25; T07, T08, T09, T23, T26, T27 | new beads, bd-kwmc, bd-67wx |

== MODULE SURFACE (§19.3; field lists are the required minimum, add #[serde(default)] fields only, never remove or rename) ==
**Dependency direction.** New modules depend on the existing `composition`, `evidence`,
`control`, `discovery`, `evaluation`, `geometry`, `geometry_value`, and `run` modules,
never the reverse. `src/geo/composition.rs` and `src/geo/evidence.rs` are not modified by
D2 to D6: `propagate` and `explain` call `solve_composition` as a black box and narrow or
re-solve `GeoCompositionRequest` values. Within the new set: `explain` consumes
`propagate`; `card`, `next_evidence`, and `inspect` consume `explain`; `exposure` and
`collision` consume `ledger`; `adjudicate` and `card` consume `observer`; nothing consumes
`inspect`.

**Shared shape.** Each module is `pub mod` in `src/geo/mod.rs` with `pub use module::*`.
Each defines `Geo<Module>Error { code: Geo<Module>ErrorCode, message: String, detail:
BTreeMap<String, String> }` with a `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` code enum that
carries the generic `UnsupportedVersion`, `InvalidInput`, `BudgetExceeded`,
`ArithmeticOverflow` variants plus the module's rows from §19.4. Each artifact type has a
`version: String` constant `CANON_GEO_<NAME>_VERSION`, `canonical_<name>_bytes`, and
`validate_<name>_artifact`. Each module ships `schemas/canon.geo.<name>.v0.schema.json`, a
`--describe` entry, a `canon geo <subcommand>`, and `tests/geo_<module>.rs`.

**`exposure.rs`**

| Item | Definition |
|---|---|
| Consumes | `GeoCollateralLedger` building sets, `GeoCanonicalPolygonMm` and `GeoLinearRingMm` building geometry from `GeoGeometryTileArtifact`, geometry.rs predicates |
| `GeoWindRadiusRing` | `knots: u16`, `ring: GeoCanonicalPolygonMm` |
| `GeoAdvisoryPin` | `advisory_id`, `storm_id`, `advisory_number: u32`, `issued: GeoValidTimeInterval`, `source_blake3s: Vec<String>`, `wind_radii: Vec<GeoWindRadiusRing>` |
| `GeoExposedBuilding` | `accession`, `loan_id`, `building_id`, `knots_band: u16` (highest ring containing the building) |
| `GeoEventExposure` | `version`, `advisory: GeoAdvisoryPin`, `ledger_blake3`, `exposed: Vec<GeoExposedBuilding>`, `buildings_without_geometry: Vec<String>` |
| `pub fn join_exposure(ledger: &GeoCollateralLedger, advisory: &GeoAdvisoryPin, geometry: &BTreeMap<String, GeoCanonicalPolygonMm>, archive_blake3s: &[String]) -> Result<GeoEventExposure, GeoExposureError>` | polygon-in-ring by exact geometry, never centroids (I11); `archive_blake3s` must contain every `source_blake3s` entry |

== ERROR CODES (§19.4; class is exactly one of refusal / abstention / typed fallback; detail always carries the named ids) ==
| `exposure_advisory_stale` | `exposure::join_exposure` | a `source_blake3s` entry is missing from `archive_blake3s`, or a later `advisory_number` for the same `storm_id` exists in the archive | refusal | T08 |
| `exposure_geometry_missing` | `exposure::join_exposure` | a ledger building has no `GeoCanonicalPolygonMm`; centroid or point input offered instead (I11) | abstention per building: id listed in `buildings_without_geometry`; refusal when every building lacks geometry | T08 |

== CONTRACTS (§19.9) ==
| C15 | `join_exposure` tests building polygons against wind radius rings by exact geometry, refuses centroid or point input, requires every `source_blake3s` entry in `archive_blake3s`, and refuses a superseded `advisory_number` | `exposure.rs` | I11 |
| C22 | Every artifact type declares `CANON_GEO_<NAME>_VERSION`, `canonical_<name>_bytes`, `validate_<name>_artifact`, and a `schemas/canon.geo.<name>.v0.schema.json`; canonical bytes are byte-identical across platforms | all §19.3 modules | N02, §19.3 shared shape |
| C25 | D2 to D6 do not modify `src/geo/composition.rs` or `src/geo/evidence.rs`; new modules call `solve_composition` as a black box, and generic modules carry no fixture, demo, or county literal | all §19.3 modules | §19.3 dependency direction, G7 |

== THREATS THIS BEAD MUST DEFEAT (§19.9) ==
| TH13 | Event exposure computed on centroids or address points, so a building on the ring edge is misclassified | Polygon-in-ring by exact geometry; point input refuses; missing geometry is listed, never guessed | C15; T08; `exposure_geometry_missing` |
| TH21 | Demo-path hard-coding: a generic module special-cases Demo 0 ids, the chimera constraint ids, or Franklin County names to pass its tests | Case-insensitive literal scan over the twelve generic modules; property tests on seeded random components | C25; T27, T03, T16 |
| TH23 | A stale advisory joined after a later advisory number exists in the archive | Latest-advisory check per `storm_id`; every source hash must be in the archive | C15; T08; `exposure_advisory_stale` |

== TESTS (§19.6; ship in tests/geo_<module>.rs with the T ids in test names; each row's Negative case is mandatory) ==
| T08 | D3 | e2e | ledger from Demo 0 case 4 (buildings `1006494` to `1006499`); advisory fixture `tests/fixtures/geo/advisory_synthetic_adv12.json` (shipped by the D3 bead) with 34, 50, and 64 knot square rings placed so `1006494` lies inside the 64 knot ring and `1006499` lies outside all rings; `archive_blake3s` containing every `source_blake3s` entry | `exposed` contains `{ building_id: "1006494", knots_band: 64 }` and no entry for `1006499`; `advisory.source_blake3s` is nonempty and equals the fixture pins | a `geometry` map that supplies a point for every building refuses `exposure_geometry_missing`; an `archive_blake3s` missing one pin refuses `exposure_advisory_stale` | C15; TH13, TH23 | `exposure_advisory_stale`, `exposure_geometry_missing` |
| T27 | D2 to D7 | adversarial | the twelve generic module files listed in §19.3 | a case-insensitive scan finds none of the literals `1004540041`, `chimera_wrongly_admitted`, `asserted_address_core`, `case_4`, `franklin`, `solve_composition` (the last only in `inspect.rs`), or any hosted-model client symbol in `observer.rs` replay code | the scan must also match `Franklin` and `CASE_4`; a scan that is case-sensitive fails on a seeded scratch copy | C18, C25; TH16, TH21 | none |

== NON-NEGOTIABLES AND INVARIANTS ==
### 19.1 Non-negotiables

- N01 Runtime lookup stays exact registry replay. Geo is a build-time workbench.
- N02 Same input plus same pinned sources reproduce byte-identical artifacts on every
  platform. No wall clock, locale, hash-map order, or float comparison in a decision path.
- N03 Every source value enters the solver only through a declared, versioned `rho`.
- N04 Adding admitted hard evidence may only narrow the model set or make it empty.
- N05 Source count is provenance, never evidence weight or confidence.
- N06 Candidate reach, admission, solver exactness, reconciliation, truth quality, and
  cost are reported as separate planes and never pooled.
- N07 Fixtures, retained evidence, and mocked providers are never presented as live proof.
- N08 Abstention is a legitimate output; an abstention-only module is not a delivered
  feature.
- N09 No vision or statistical model proposes a location. Models are observers with
  characterized error.
- N10 No commercial basemap imagery or tiles enter any artifact.
- N11 Gates are frozen in tests. A gate is passed by meeting it, never by editing it.
- N12 Every feature bead ships its code and its tests together, including at least one
  negative case a naive implementation fails.

### 19.2 Invariants for the new artifacts

- I01 A propagator prunes a value only with a typed reason naming constraint id and
  evidence ids; pruning is sound: enumeration with propagation equals enumeration without.
- I02 Propagator fixpoint is order-independent; tests run every permutation of propagator
  order on each fixture and compare bytes.
- I03 A minimal core is minimal: removing any one member restores satisfiability; tests
  verify by re-solving each deletion.
- I04 A correction set hits every enumerated core; when core enumeration hits its ceiling
  the artifact says `cores_complete=false` and no minimality claim is made.
- I05 Explanation artifacts name source record ids and rho contract ids, never internal
  indices.
- I06 An observer observation carries image tile digest, vintage, license hash, model or
  rule identity, weight or prompt digest, and the error-population digest; missing any
  field refuses.
- I07 Observer output is stored, never regenerated at replay; replay verifies the stored
  digest chain only.
- I08 A ledger row binds accession, loan id, parcel set, building set, truth plane,
  claim class, model count, exactness flags, and every source release pin; rows with
  candidate reach `none` carry the reason and no sets.
- I09 A ledger row never pools truth planes; non-round and round exact-lender evidence
  stay labeled.
- I10 The retry loop is bounded by a declared pass count; each pass is a normal pinned
  run and the loop artifact lists every pass with its abstention reason.
- I11 Event exposure joins building geometry, not centroids; advisory source hashes travel
  with the result.
- I12 Cross-deal collision reports a parcel or building shared by more than one trust
  with both accessions; pari passu participation is a labeled explanation, not a suppressed
  row.
- I13 `geo inspect` reads only emitted artifacts and receipts; it computes nothing that
  changes an answer.
- I14 Next-evidence recommendations expose the nondominated frontier and never manufacture
  a total ranking without a declared loss model.

== COMMANDS ==
### 19.7 Commands

Whole-tree gates run on every commit in every stage. Per-module binaries are the
`tests/geo_<module>.rs` files from §19.3; each stage runs its own set before claiming its
gate. `rg` exit status 1 means no match, which is the pass for the literal scans, so
they are written with a leading `!`.

```bash
# Whole-tree gates
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test

# Frozen E4 gate (T17, C24): expected red until G1, green from G1 on
cargo test --test geo_adjudication e4_acceptance_gate_requires_the_full_population_to_be_reachable -- --ignored

# Per-module test binaries (stage: test ids)
cargo test --test geo_propagate           # D2: T01 to T04, T19
cargo test --test geo_explain             # D2: T05, T06, T20, T21
cargo test --test geo_ledger              # D3: T07, T23, T26
cargo test --test geo_exposure            # D3: T08
cargo test --test geo_collision           # D3: T09
cargo test --test geo_retry               # D4: T10
cargo test --test geo_condo               # D4: T11
cargo test --test geo_inspect             # D4: T12, T25
cargo test --test geo_next_evidence       # D5: T18
cargo test --test geo_observer            # D6: T13, T14, T15
cargo test --test geo_adjudicate          # D6: T22 (new binary; distinct from the existing geo_adjudication)
cargo test --test geo_card                # D6: T24, T26
cargo test --test geo_e5_franklin_parcel  # D7: T16 plus the existing literal scan

# One test by name with output
cargo test --test geo_propagate soundness_holds_on_every_e4_fixture -- --nocapture

# Schema drift guard (C22). tests/geo_schemas.rs include_str!s each schema file, pins
# title, properties.version.const, and additionalProperties == false, then walks a real
# serialized instance against the schema; there is no jsonschema crate. Each new
# artifact adds one <name>_schema_matches_a_real_instance test there and one
# include_str! of schemas/canon.geo.<name>.v0.schema.json.
cargo test --test geo_schemas
cargo test --test geo_schemas propagation_schema_matches_a_real_instance
for s in propagation explanation separation_request separation observer observation_rows \
         image_tile_pin adjudication_request adjudication_receipt evidence_card \
         collateral_ledger event_exposure cross_deal retry_loop inspection next_evidence \
         condo_bridge_request ledger_bridge; do
  jq -e --arg s "$s" '.title == "canon.geo.\($s).v0"
    and .properties.version.const == "canon_geo_\($s).v0"
    and .additionalProperties == false' "schemas/canon.geo.${s}.v0.schema.json"
done

# --describe entries for geo subcommands (C22: one per new module, named after it:
# geo propagate, geo explain, geo observer, geo adjudicate, geo card, geo ledger,
# geo exposure, geo collision, geo retry, geo inspect, geo next-evidence, geo condo)
cargo run --bin canon -- --describe \
  | jq -r '.subcommands[] | select(.name | startswith("geo ")) | "\(.name)\t\(.status)\t\(.output_schema)"'
cargo run --bin canon -- --describe \
  | jq -e '[.subcommands[] | select(.name == "geo propagate" and .status == "implemented")] | length == 1'

# T27 literal scan (C25, G7). Mirrors tests/geo_e5_franklin_parcel.rs
# franklin_instance_names_do_not_enter_the_generic_geo_engine, which lowercases each
# generic source file and asserts it contains no instance literal.
GEO_GENERIC="src/geo/propagate.rs src/geo/explain.rs src/geo/observer.rs src/geo/adjudicate.rs \
  src/geo/card.rs src/geo/ledger.rs src/geo/exposure.rs src/geo/collision.rs src/geo/retry.rs \
  src/geo/inspect.rs src/geo/next_evidence.rs src/geo/condo.rs"
! rg -i -n 'franklin|39049|epsg:3735|1004540041|chimera_wrongly_admitted|asserted_address_core|case_4' $GEO_GENERIC
! rg -n 'solve_composition' src/geo/inspect.rs
! rg -i -n 'reqwest|hyper::|openai|anthropic|gemini|bedrock|invoke_model' src/geo/observer.rs
cargo test --test geo_e5_franklin_parcel franklin_instance_names_do_not_enter_the_generic_geo_engine

# Demo 0, capabilities, measurement plan, beads
bash scripts/geo_demo/demo0.sh --work-dir /tmp/demo0
cargo run --bin canon -- geo capabilities --emit json
cargo run --bin canon_geo_measurements -- --emit plan
br ready --json && br dep cycles --json
```

ANTI-REWARD-HACKING (AGENTS.md, binding):
- Code and tests ship in this bead; no scope-splitting into type/impl/test closures.
- No new todo!()/unimplemented!() scaffolds. Refusal-only implementation earns partial credit and never closes this bead (label refusal-only + follow-up bead if that is the honest state).
- Fixtures and Demo 0 outputs are never presented as live proof (C23). Gate thresholds are never edited to pass (C24, N11).
- Every feature test includes at least one negative case a naive implementation fails (the Negative case column below).
- Generic modules carry no fixture, demo, or county literal (C25, T27).

comments.text:

RESERVATIONS (thread bd-2k98): src/geo/exposure.rs, tests/geo_exposure.rs, tests/fixtures/geo/advisory_synthetic_adv12.json, schemas/canon.geo.event_exposure.v0.schema.json, scripts/geo_demo/e2e_exposure.sh. == ACCEPTANCE (round 2: gate as acceptance criterion, PK-D3b) ==

GATE G3 clause (verbatim from section 19.5 row D3): "exposure runs against one archived advisory". The live half (a real landed NHC/CPHC advisory) is bd-2ocv's; this bead ships exposure.rs, the synthetic advisory fixture, and T08.

title: Refusal system (10 codes)
description:
Implement the refusal type system and helper constructors in src/refusal.rs.

This module defines types and serialization only. It does NOT decide which stream (stdout/stderr) to write to — that routing is the caller's responsibility (run() checks emit mode).

Types:
- RefusalCode enum with all 10 codes (E_IO, E_ENCODING, E_CSV_PARSE, E_BAD_REGISTRY, E_COLUMN_NOT_FOUND, E_PARSE, E_EMPTY_INPUT, E_TOO_LARGE, E_EMIT_FORMAT, E_COLUMN_EXISTS). Serializes to string (e.g. "E_IO").
- Refusal struct: code (RefusalCode), message (String), detail (serde_json::Value), next_command (Option<String>).

JSON envelope: wraps Refusal into a full CanonOutput with outcome=REFUSAL, registry=null, summary=null, mappings=[], unresolved=[], refusal=Some({...}). Uses the shared CanonOutput type from lib.rs.

Helper constructors for each code, e.g.:
- Refusal::column_not_found(column: &str, available: &[String]) -> Refusal
- Refusal::bad_registry(path: &str, reason: &str) -> Refusal
- Refusal::io_error(path: &str, err: &str) -> Refusal
- etc.

Each constructor populates message, detail, and next_command with actionable recovery guidance per PLAN_CANON.md.

Convenience method: Refusal::to_canon_output() -> CanonOutput (wraps into the full envelope for serialization).
acceptance_criteria: TARGET FILE: src/refusal.rs only. Include #[cfg(test)] mod tests. Test: each RefusalCode serializes correctly (E_IO etc), helper constructors populate message/detail/next_command, to_canon_output() envelope structure. VERIFICATION: cargo test -- refusal

title: [CANON-V1/P03.4] Put strategy audit behind a bounded, isolated execution runner
description:
## Background
Current strategy audit executes scripts without a complete timeout, resource, environment, filesystem, or network boundary. That is too much ambient authority for a standalone package that may ingest third-party procedures.

## Technical Approach
Create one strategy runner with explicit runtime allowlist, wall and CPU deadlines, memory/output/process/file limits, empty-by-default environment, owned scratch directory, read-only package and fixtures, closed stdin, and network denied by policy. Capture deterministic stdout/stderr digests and structured termination reasons. Refuse platforms where the declared isolation contract cannot be enforced rather than silently degrading.

## Success Criteria
- Infinite loops, fork/process storms, oversized output, filesystem escape, network access, and environment reads terminate or refuse within documented bounds.
- Audit cannot mutate strategy packages, fixtures, registries, project inputs, or arbitrary host paths.
- Termination artifacts distinguish fixture failure from timeout, resource limit, policy denial, and runner failure.
- Normal audited fixtures remain deterministic and usable offline.

## Test Plan
Run adversarial fixture executables for each capability and limit; inspect process trees and filesystem deltas; repeat under read-only and concurrent audits. Log runner policy, commands, exit status, signal/limit reason, and artifact hashes.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/strategy/audit.rs`
- `src/strategy/runner.rs`
- `tests/strategy_sandbox.rs`

## Considerations
Portable isolation is difficult. State the enforceable contract per supported platform and fail closed; do not advertise a sandbox based only on conventions.
close_reason: Implemented isolated strategy audit runner; focused validation green, repo-wide clippy/test blocked by unrelated unreserved temporal/inventory drift
