title: canon geo D2: propagators over the extensional kernel (additive band, cardinality, source exclusivity) with sound typed prunings
description:
PACKET PK-D2a (stage D2) from docs/PLAN_CANON_GEO.md §18/§19, course correction 2026-09-01. This bead carries the full design so no implementer needs the plan document.

== WHY ==
The shipped solver (src/geo/composition.rs) is an extensional exact kernel: incidence-graph factorization, exhaustive mask enumeration under a budget, pruned DFS fallback, exact counts and backbones. None of the plan's §7 global propagators exist. Propagators are the first half of the solver middle layer (§18.5): they run to a fixpoint per component BEFORE enumeration, prune values with a typed reason naming the constraint and evidence ids, and never change the model set. They shrink the search space (component maxima of 109 to 128 raw nodes have been measured) and produce the explanation skeleton that PK-D2b consumes. Soundness is not assumed: every fixture and 200 seeded random components are solved with and without propagation and compared (T03).

### 18.5 The solver middle layer

The extensional kernel is kept as the exact backend. Three additions make it the product:

1. **Propagators as pre-search filters.** Each runs to a fixpoint over the component's
   domains before enumeration, prunes values with a typed reason naming the constraint and
   the evidence ids, and never changes the model set (soundness is checked in tests by
   comparing enumeration with and without propagation on every fixture). They shrink the
   search space and produce the explanation skeleton for free.
2. **Minimal cores and repairs.** On an empty model set, compute one minimal
   unsatisfiable subset of admitted constraints by deletion under the declared reliability
   order, then enumerate correction sets as minimal hitting sets while the core count stays
   under a deterministic ceiling. The artifact names source records, not constraint
   indices. Oversized cases return a typed superset with `explanation_complete=false`.
3. **Counterfactual separation.** For a declared prospective observation with an
   exhaustive outcome domain, report the exact model count under each outcome. Never call
   it expected value without calibrated probabilities (architecture §9).

== STAGE ROW (§19.5; entry condition, gate, contracts) ==
| D2 | Propagators and explanation artifacts | G1 passed; D1 residual artifacts committed; `src/geo/composition.rs` and `src/geo/evidence.rs` frozen at their D1 digests (C25); modules `propagate.rs`, `explain.rs` | G2: I01 to I05 hold on every E4 fixture; at least one real cohort conflict yields a minimal core naming source records | C01 to C08, C22, C25; T01 to T06, T19, T20, T21, T27 | new beads |

== MODULE SURFACE (§19.3; field lists are the required minimum, add #[serde(default)] fields only, never remove or rename) ==
**Dependency direction.** New modules depend on the existing `composition`, `evidence`,
`control`, `discovery`, `evaluation`, `geometry`, `geometry_value`, and `run` modules,
never the reverse. `src/geo/composition.rs` and `src/geo/evidence.rs` are not modified by
D2 to D6: `propagate` and `explain` call `solve_composition` as a black box and narrow or
re-solve `GeoCompositionRequest` values. Within the new set: `explain` consumes
`propagate`; `card`, `next_evidence`, and `inspect` consume `explain`; `exposure` and
`collision` consume `ledger`; `adjudicate` and `card` consume `observer`; nothing consumes
`inspect`.

**Shared shape.** Each module is `pub mod` in `src/geo/mod.rs` with `pub use module::*`.
Each defines `Geo<Module>Error { code: Geo<Module>ErrorCode, message: String, detail:
BTreeMap<String, String> }` with a `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` code enum that
carries the generic `UnsupportedVersion`, `InvalidInput`, `BudgetExceeded`,
`ArithmeticOverflow` variants plus the module's rows from §19.4. Each artifact type has a
`version: String` constant `CANON_GEO_<NAME>_VERSION`, `canonical_<name>_bytes`, and
`validate_<name>_artifact`. Each module ships `schemas/canon.geo.<name>.v0.schema.json`, a
`--describe` entry, a `canon geo <subcommand>`, and `tests/geo_<module>.rs`.

**`propagate.rs`**

| Item | Definition |
|---|---|
| Consumes | `GeoCompositionRequest`, `GeoCompositionUniverse`, `GeoHardConstraint`, `GeoHardConstraintKind::{IntegerSumBand, Cardinality, AllowedSets, Require, Forbid, AllOrNone, Requires}`, `GeoEntityRef`, `GeoEntityLevel`; optional `GeoEvidenceCompilationArtifact` whose `admissions[].contract.source_dataset` and `generated_ids` group constraints by source for exclusivity |
| `GeoPropagatorKind` | `AdditiveBand`, `Cardinality`, `SourceExclusivity` |
| `GeoPropagationBudget` | `max_fixpoint_rounds: u64`, `max_hall_subset_size: usize`, `max_subset_sum_states: u64` |
| `GeoPrunedValue` | `Excluded`, `Forced` |
| `GeoPruning` | `member: GeoEntityRef`, `value: GeoPrunedValue`, `propagator: GeoPropagatorKind`, `constraint_ids: Vec<String>`, `evidence_ids: Vec<String>` (observation ids when evidence is supplied, else empty) |
| `GeoPropagationFallback` | `propagator: GeoPropagatorKind`, `counter: String`, `configured: u64`, `guidance: String` |
| `GeoPropagationArtifact` | `version`, `request_blake3`, `prunings: Vec<GeoPruning>` (sorted by member then value), `rounds: u64`, `fixpoint_reached: bool`, `budget_fallback: Option<GeoPropagationFallback>`, `counters: BTreeMap<String, u64>` |
| `pub fn propagate(request: &GeoCompositionRequest, evidence: Option<&GeoEvidenceCompilationArtifact>, budget: &GeoPropagationBudget) -> Result<GeoPropagationArtifact, GeoPropagationError>` | runs all three propagators to a fixpoint per incidence component; every pruning cites at least one constraint id |
| `pub fn apply_prunings(request: &GeoCompositionRequest, artifact: &GeoPropagationArtifact) -> Result<GeoCompositionRequest, GeoPropagationError>` | returns a narrowed request: `Excluded` becomes `GeoHardConstraintKind::Forbid`, `Forced` becomes `Require`, ids prefixed `prune:`; universe and `max_assignments` unchanged so `model_satisfies_request` stays comparable |
| `pub fn check_soundness(request: &GeoCompositionRequest, artifact: &GeoPropagationArtifact) -> Result<GeoSoundnessReport, GeoPropagationError>` | solves original and narrowed requests with `solve_composition`, compares `residual_models` and `summary.residual_model_count`; `GeoSoundnessReport { sound: bool, model_count_before: u64, model_count_after: u64, differing_models: Vec<GeoCompositionModel> }` (I01, T03) |

== ERROR CODES (§19.4; class is exactly one of refusal / abstention / typed fallback; detail always carries the named ids) ==
| `propagation_unsound_detected` | `propagate::check_soundness` | residual model set or count differs between the original and narrowed request | refusal; also fails T03 in CI | T03 |
| `propagation_budget_exhausted` | `propagate::propagate` | `max_fixpoint_rounds`, `max_hall_subset_size`, or `max_subset_sum_states` reached before fixpoint | typed fallback: `fixpoint_reached = false`, prunings so far retained (each is individually justified), `budget_fallback` set | T19 |

== CONTRACTS (§19.9) ==
| C01 | Every `GeoPruning` carries at least one `constraint_ids` entry and, when evidence is supplied, the `evidence_ids` of the observations that justify it; a pruning with empty `constraint_ids` fails validation | `propagate.rs` | I01, I05 |
| C02 | `check_soundness` compares `residual_models` and `summary.residual_model_count` between the original and narrowed request and reports `sound == false` on any difference; propagation never changes the model set | `propagate.rs` | I01, N04 |
| C03 | The propagation fixpoint is order-independent: `canonical_propagation_bytes` is identical under every permutation of `GeoPropagatorKind`; no `HashMap` iteration reaches an artifact | `propagate.rs` | I02, N02 |
| C04 | Budget exhaustion is a typed fallback, never a silent fixpoint: `fixpoint_reached == false`, `budget_fallback` names the counter and configured value, retained prunings remain individually sound | `propagate.rs` | I01, §19.4 typed fallback class |
| C22 | Every artifact type declares `CANON_GEO_<NAME>_VERSION`, `canonical_<name>_bytes`, `validate_<name>_artifact`, and a `schemas/canon.geo.<name>.v0.schema.json`; canonical bytes are byte-identical across platforms | all §19.3 modules | N02, §19.3 shared shape |
| C25 | D2 to D6 do not modify `src/geo/composition.rs` or `src/geo/evidence.rs`; new modules call `solve_composition` as a black box, and generic modules carry no fixture, demo, or county literal | all §19.3 modules | §19.3 dependency direction, G7 |

== THREATS THIS BEAD MUST DEFEAT (§19.9) ==
| TH01 | A propagator over-prunes and silently removes a true model (unsound domain filter presented as exact) | Soundness check on every fixture and seeded random component; unsound result is a refusal and a CI failure | C02; T03, T01, T02; `propagation_unsound_detected` |
| TH02 | Propagator output depends on propagator order or on `HashMap` iteration, so two platforms emit different bytes | Permutation byte compare; `BTreeMap` only; sorted `prunings` | C03; T04 |
| TH03 | Budget exhaustion reported as a reached fixpoint, or prunings dropped without a fallback record | Typed fallback with counter name and configured value; retained prunings re-checked for soundness | C04; T19; `propagation_budget_exhausted` |
| TH20 | Proof-class inflation: Demo 0 output, fixtures, or retained evidence cited as a live measurement or gate pass | `fixture.` pins on every fixture-derived artifact; G-gate tests read only their frozen fixtures; measurement receipts require runtime-selected subjects with a recorded seed | C23, N07; T26, T16 |
| TH21 | Demo-path hard-coding: a generic module special-cases Demo 0 ids, the chimera constraint ids, or Franklin County names to pass its tests | Case-insensitive literal scan over the twelve generic modules; property tests on seeded random components | C25; T27, T03, T16 |

== TESTS (§19.6; ship in tests/geo_<module>.rs with the T ids in test names; each row's Negative case is mandatory) ==
| T01 | D2 | unit | universe `p1`, `p2`, `p3` built with `universe()` from `tests/geo_evidence_compilation.rs`; `IntegerSumBand` on `semantic_id "fixture:computed-area"` with contributions `p1=100`, `p2=200`, `p3=5000`, band `[5000, 5200]` | `prunings == [{ member: p3, value: Forced, propagator: AdditiveBand, constraint_ids: [band id] }]`; `fixpoint_reached == true` | `p1` is not `Excluded` (`p3 + p1 = 5100` is inside the band); an implementation that prunes it fails | C01, C02; TH01 | none |
| T02 | D2 | unit | Demo 0 `case4-warehouse-rows.json` universe (7 parcels `1004540041` to `1004540047`, buildings `1006494` to `1006500`, one building per parcel); `Cardinality` at building level `min 6, max 6` plus `Forbid` parcel `1004540047` | `1006500` is `Excluded` with `constraint_ids` containing both the cardinality id and the forbid id; the other six buildings are `Forced` | a count that ignores `parcel_ids` incidence forces `1006500` too; that output fails | C01, C02; TH01 | none |
| T03 | D2 | property | all six `e4_worked_cases.json` requests, the Demo 0 `negative-hard-chimera-composition.json`, and 200 seeded iterations of `random_constraints` from `tests/geo_composition.rs` | `check_soundness(...).sound == true` and `differing_models.is_empty()` on every input; `model_count_before == model_count_after` | a test-local propagator that unconditionally `Excluded`s the first universe member returns `sound == false` and `Err` code `propagation_unsound_detected` with `detail["member"]` set | C02; TH01 | `propagation_unsound_detected` |
| T04 | D2 | property | same inputs as T03; all six permutations of `[AdditiveBand, Cardinality, SourceExclusivity]` | `canonical_propagation_bytes` identical across permutations; `rounds` may differ, `prunings` may not | a permutation-dependent `prunings` order is caught by the byte compare | C03; TH02 | none |
| T19 | D2 | unit | one 200-iteration `random_constraints` component from `tests/geo_composition.rs` with `GeoPropagationBudget { max_fixpoint_rounds: 1, max_hall_subset_size: 1, max_subset_sum_states: 1 }` | `fixpoint_reached == false`; `budget_fallback.is_some()` and `budget_fallback.counter` is one of the three budget field names with `configured == 1`; `check_soundness` on the retained `prunings` still returns `sound == true`; exit is zero | `max_fixpoint_rounds: 0` refuses `invalid_input` with `detail["field"] = "max_fixpoint_rounds"` (mirrors `zero_assignment_budget_refuses_validation`) | C04, C02; TH03 | `propagation_budget_exhausted` |
| T27 | D2 to D7 | adversarial | the twelve generic module files listed in §19.3 | a case-insensitive scan finds none of the literals `1004540041`, `chimera_wrongly_admitted`, `asserted_address_core`, `case_4`, `franklin`, `solve_composition` (the last only in `inspect.rs`), or any hosted-model client symbol in `observer.rs` replay code | the scan must also match `Franklin` and `CASE_4`; a scan that is case-sensitive fails on a seeded scratch copy | C18, C25; TH16, TH21 | none |

== NON-NEGOTIABLES AND INVARIANTS ==
### 19.1 Non-negotiables

- N01 Runtime lookup stays exact registry replay. Geo is a build-time workbench.
- N02 Same input plus same pinned sources reproduce byte-identical artifacts on every
  platform. No wall clock, locale, hash-map order, or float comparison in a decision path.
- N03 Every source value enters the solver only through a declared, versioned `rho`.
- N04 Adding admitted hard evidence may only narrow the model set or make it empty.
- N05 Source count is provenance, never evidence weight or confidence.
- N06 Candidate reach, admission, solver exactness, reconciliation, truth quality, and
  cost are reported as separate planes and never pooled.
- N07 Fixtures, retained evidence, and mocked providers are never presented as live proof.
- N08 Abstention is a legitimate output; an abstention-only module is not a delivered
  feature.
- N09 No vision or statistical model proposes a location. Models are observers with
  characterized error.
- N10 No commercial basemap imagery or tiles enter any artifact.
- N11 Gates are frozen in tests. A gate is passed by meeting it, never by editing it.
- N12 Every feature bead ships its code and its tests together, including at least one
  negative case a naive implementation fails.

### 19.2 Invariants for the new artifacts

- I01 A propagator prunes a value only with a typed reason naming constraint id and
  evidence ids; pruning is sound: enumeration with propagation equals enumeration without.
- I02 Propagator fixpoint is order-independent; tests run every permutation of propagator
  order on each fixture and compare bytes.
- I03 A minimal core is minimal: removing any one member restores satisfiability; tests
  verify by re-solving each deletion.
- I04 A correction set hits every enumerated core; when core enumeration hits its ceiling
  the artifact says `cores_complete=false` and no minimality claim is made.
- I05 Explanation artifacts name source record ids and rho contract ids, never internal
  indices.
- I06 An observer observation carries image tile digest, vintage, license hash, model or
  rule identity, weight or prompt digest, and the error-population digest; missing any
  field refuses.
- I07 Observer output is stored, never regenerated at replay; replay verifies the stored
  digest chain only.
- I08 A ledger row binds accession, loan id, parcel set, building set, truth plane,
  claim class, model count, exactness flags, and every source release pin; rows with
  candidate reach `none` carry the reason and no sets.
- I09 A ledger row never pools truth planes; non-round and round exact-lender evidence
  stay labeled.
- I10 The retry loop is bounded by a declared pass count; each pass is a normal pinned
  run and the loop artifact lists every pass with its abstention reason.
- I11 Event exposure joins building geometry, not centroids; advisory source hashes travel
  with the result.
- I12 Cross-deal collision reports a parcel or building shared by more than one trust
  with both accessions; pari passu participation is a labeled explanation, not a suppressed
  row.
- I13 `geo inspect` reads only emitted artifacts and receipts; it computes nothing that
  changes an answer.
- I14 Next-evidence recommendations expose the nondominated frontier and never manufacture
  a total ranking without a declared loss model.

== COMMANDS ==
### 19.7 Commands

Whole-tree gates run on every commit in every stage. Per-module binaries are the
`tests/geo_<module>.rs` files from §19.3; each stage runs its own set before claiming its
gate. `rg` exit status 1 means no match, which is the pass for the literal scans, so
they are written with a leading `!`.

```bash
# Whole-tree gates
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test

# Frozen E4 gate (T17, C24): expected red until G1, green from G1 on
cargo test --test geo_adjudication e4_acceptance_gate_requires_the_full_population_to_be_reachable -- --ignored

# Per-module test binaries (stage: test ids)
cargo test --test geo_propagate           # D2: T01 to T04, T19
cargo test --test geo_explain             # D2: T05, T06, T20, T21
cargo test --test geo_ledger              # D3: T07, T23, T26
cargo test --test geo_exposure            # D3: T08
cargo test --test geo_collision           # D3: T09
cargo test --test geo_retry               # D4: T10
cargo test --test geo_condo               # D4: T11
cargo test --test geo_inspect             # D4: T12, T25
cargo test --test geo_next_evidence       # D5: T18
cargo test --test geo_observer            # D6: T13, T14, T15
cargo test --test geo_adjudicate          # D6: T22 (new binary; distinct from the existing geo_adjudication)
cargo test --test geo_card                # D6: T24, T26
cargo test --test geo_e5_franklin_parcel  # D7: T16 plus the existing literal scan

# One test by name with output
cargo test --test geo_propagate soundness_holds_on_every_e4_fixture -- --nocapture

# Schema drift guard (C22). tests/geo_schemas.rs include_str!s each schema file, pins
# title, properties.version.const, and additionalProperties == false, then walks a real
# serialized instance against the schema; there is no jsonschema crate. Each new
# artifact adds one <name>_schema_matches_a_real_instance test there and one
# include_str! of schemas/canon.geo.<name>.v0.schema.json.
cargo test --test geo_schemas
cargo test --test geo_schemas propagation_schema_matches_a_real_instance
for s in propagation explanation separation_request separation observer observation_rows \
         image_tile_pin adjudication_request adjudication_receipt evidence_card \
         collateral_ledger event_exposure cross_deal retry_loop inspection next_evidence \
         condo_bridge_request ledger_bridge; do
  jq -e --arg s "$s" '.title == "canon.geo.\($s).v0"
    and .properties.version.const == "canon_geo_\($s).v0"
    and .additionalProperties == false' "schemas/canon.geo.${s}.v0.schema.json"
done

# --describe entries for geo subcommands (C22: one per new module, named after it:
# geo propagate, geo explain, geo observer, geo adjudicate, geo card, geo ledger,
# geo exposure, geo collision, geo retry, geo inspect, geo next-evidence, geo condo)
cargo run --bin canon -- --describe \
  | jq -r '.subcommands[] | select(.name | startswith("geo ")) | "\(.name)\t\(.status)\t\(.output_schema)"'
cargo run --bin canon -- --describe \
  | jq -e '[.subcommands[] | select(.name == "geo propagate" and .status == "implemented")] | length == 1'

# T27 literal scan (C25, G7). Mirrors tests/geo_e5_franklin_parcel.rs
# franklin_instance_names_do_not_enter_the_generic_geo_engine, which lowercases each
# generic source file and asserts it contains no instance literal.
GEO_GENERIC="src/geo/propagate.rs src/geo/explain.rs src/geo/observer.rs src/geo/adjudicate.rs \
  src/geo/card.rs src/geo/ledger.rs src/geo/exposure.rs src/geo/collision.rs src/geo/retry.rs \
  src/geo/inspect.rs src/geo/next_evidence.rs src/geo/condo.rs"
! rg -i -n 'franklin|39049|epsg:3735|1004540041|chimera_wrongly_admitted|asserted_address_core|case_4' $GEO_GENERIC
! rg -n 'solve_composition' src/geo/inspect.rs
! rg -i -n 'reqwest|hyper::|openai|anthropic|gemini|bedrock|invoke_model' src/geo/observer.rs
cargo test --test geo_e5_franklin_parcel franklin_instance_names_do_not_enter_the_generic_geo_engine

# Demo 0, capabilities, measurement plan, beads
bash scripts/geo_demo/demo0.sh --work-dir /tmp/demo0
cargo run --bin canon -- geo capabilities --emit json
cargo run --bin canon_geo_measurements -- --emit plan
br ready --json && br dep cycles --json
```

ANTI-REWARD-HACKING (AGENTS.md, binding):
- Code and tests ship in this bead; no scope-splitting into type/impl/test closures.
- No new todo!()/unimplemented!() scaffolds. Refusal-only implementation earns partial credit and never closes this bead (label refusal-only + follow-up bead if that is the honest state).
- Fixtures and Demo 0 outputs are never presented as live proof (C23). Gate thresholds are never edited to pass (C24, N11).
- Every feature test includes at least one negative case a naive implementation fails (the Negative case column below).
- Generic modules carry no fixture, demo, or county literal (C25, T27).

== 2026-09-02 TEST LOGGING, E2E SCRIPT, RESERVATIONS (coverage pass round 1) ==

Every test in tests/geo_propagate.rs carries its T id in the function name and, on failure, panics with a message assembled from the values below (use a local `fail!(test_id, key = value, ...)` macro that also `eprintln!`s them so `-- --nocapture` shows them even when the assertion is deep in a helper). Logging is not optional; a bare `assert_eq!` on a bool is a tautological test under AGENTS.md pattern 5.

T01 (additive band forces p3): log `request_blake3`, the band constraint id and `[min, max]`, every contribution `(member, value)`, the full serialized `prunings` list, `fixpoint_reached`, `rounds`, `counters`. Negative half: log why p1 would be excluded (the sum the wrong implementation computed).
T02 (cardinality plus forbid on Demo 0 case 4): log the universe (7 parcel ids, 7 building ids), the building-to-parcel incidence the propagator used, the pruning for `1006500` with its `constraint_ids`, and the six `Forced` prunings. Negative half: log the incidence map the naive count ignored.
T03 (soundness on every fixture and 200 seeded components): per input log input name or seed, `model_count_before`, `model_count_after`, `differing_models` (first 10 serialized plus the total), the pruning responsible (member, propagator, `constraint_ids`, `evidence_ids`), and the `detail` map of `propagation_unsound_detected`. Log the seed on every iteration so a failure is reproducible with one number.
T04 (order independence): per permutation log the order, the BLAKE3 of `canonical_propagation_bytes`, `rounds`, and on mismatch the index and content of the first differing pruning between the two permutations.
T19 (budget fallback): log the `GeoPropagationBudget` values, `budget_fallback.counter`, `configured`, `guidance`, the full `counters` map, the count of retained prunings, and the `GeoSoundnessReport` on the retained prunings. Negative half: log `detail["field"]`.
T27 (literal scan): log file, line number, and the matched literal, and the seeded scratch file path for the case-insensitivity check.

E2E script scripts/geo_demo/e2e_propagate.sh (`set -euo pipefail`; echoes each command, its exit code, and the BLAKE3 of every artifact it reads or writes into <work-dir>/run.log; exits nonzero on the first failed jq assertion):

comments.text:
== ORCHESTRATOR CORRECTION 2026-09-02 to the priority note above ==
The note cites "residual model counts median 8,373,880,557,142,016, 19 cases saturated". That median
is NOT evidence and should not be repeated. Of the 38 full-reach cases, 19 carry residual_model_count
= 18,446,744,073,709,551,615 = u64::MAX, which is a SATURATION SENTINEL (a declared lower bound per
evaluation.rs:267), not a measurement. A median over a field where half the values are the ceiling
is dominated by the ceiling. The orchestrator computed it without looking at the distribution first.

WHAT THE DISTRIBUTION ACTUALLY SHOWS, and this DOES support the priority: every non-saturated
residual_model_count is exactly 2^k, 2^k-1, or a small multiple (3*2^k, 15*2^k) -- values like 4,
32, 4095, 262144, 16777215, 2^31, 2^42-1, 2^52-1. That is the signature of the extensional kernel
enumerating every subset of the FREE nodes in a component: residual = 2^(nodes nothing constrains).
So residual_model_count measures how many nodes are unconstrained, not evidential closeness. With
one PAD observation per case, almost every node stays free, and components of 53+ free nodes
overflow. That is precisely what propagators are for (this bead's WHY: "None of the plan's section 7
global propagators exist"). The conclusion stands; the statistic was wrong.

The public CLI/operator manifest exposes only project init, validate, and describe even though internal next_command fields advertise non-existent project lock refresh, plan, and run commands.

The substrate is valuable but not yet safe as Geo semantic state:
- ProjectModeKind and the compiled DAG are cluster/link shaped.
- ProjectRunNodeReceipt hashes duration_millis and resource_observations, so identical semantic outputs can produce different dependency receipt hashes.
- write_node_receipt uses direct fs::write although the schema claims atomic publication.
- max_parallelism bounds a serial loop; actual multi-agent execution belongs to bd-3oj1.
- invalidated receipts are reported but filtered out of execution, while next_actions can still suggest their command.
- max_runtime_seconds must remain cancellation telemetry/policy, not a semantic cutoff that changes an answer.

DELIVER

Expose and harden the shared project execution substrate so Geo plan/run are thin typed projections, not a second scheduler.

Add truthful public project lock/plan/run surfaces or remove every dangling next command; preferred result is:
  canon project lock refresh ...
  canon project plan ...
  canon project run ...

Provide a domain-neutral extension-node/DAG validation interface through which canon geo plan can emit Geo stages and bind a canon_geo_plan.v0 semantic overlay to canon.project.plan.v1. canon geo run delegates workspace safety, receipts, resume, invalidation, review/mutation gates, and lifecycle to the shared substrate through a Geo node executor that dispatches only declared internal leaf capabilities or validated extension entrypoints, never an ambient shell string.

Split semantic dependency identity from observational execution telemetry. Semantic hashes cover node contract, declared inputs/policy, dependency semantic hashes, outcome class where relevant, and output content digests. Duration, observed resource use, host/worker, and publication path remain integrity-protected telemetry but cannot invalidate downstream semantic work.

ACCEPTANCE

- Project help, operator manifest, schemas, and actual lock/plan/run commands agree; every emitted next command is executable or is removed.
- Geo planner output embeds/references one validated canon.project.plan.v1 DAG; Geo does not own a parallel cache, scheduler, receipt store, or workspace policy.
- Geo run output is a typed projection over canon.project.run.v1 receipts and can trace every Geo phase to one or more shared plan nodes.
- Same semantic node inputs/outputs with different duration/resource observations produce the same semantic dependency hash and downstream artifacts, while telemetry tampering is still detectable.
- Node receipts and run publication are atomic; interruption cannot leave a parseable partial receipt treated as completion.
- An invalidated node has an executable recovery path in a new immutable revision and unchanged nodes are reusable. It is never both non-runnable and advertised as directly runnable.
- Runtime seconds can cancel/pause and resume but cannot convert exact, partial, empty, or fallback semantics.
- Project core remains domain-neutral: no vendor, BBL, CMBS, NYC, parcel, or footprint special cases.
- Negative test: a Geo extension node cannot request undeclared network or mutation side effects.
- Existing entity project plan/run/resume tests keep their behavior; Geo integration adds deterministic overlay/delegation tests.
- bd-3oj1 remains the owner of actual concurrent multi-agent claims and merge; this bead provides the correct shared serial/resumable substrate.
close_reason: Delivered the accepted public serial/resumable project execution substrate with typed Geo reuse, semantic/telemetry separation, immutable manifest lineage, verified artifact CAS restoration, safe publication, and full quality-gate evidence; concurrent claiming remains explicitly owned by bd-3oj1.

title: JSON output emission (canon.v0 schema)
description:
Implement JSON output emission in src/output/json.rs.

TARGET FILE: src/output/json.rs ONLY. Do not touch src/output/csv.rs or src/output/mod.rs.

Takes a ResolveResult + RegistryMeta, builds a CanonOutput, and serializes to JSON.

IMPORTANT: Mapping.input and Mapping.canonical_id in the ResolveResult hold RAW values. This module MUST apply identifier encoding before JSON serialization:
- u8:<value> if the value is valid UTF-8 with no ASCII control bytes (0x00-0x1F, 0x7F)
- hex:<lowercase-hex-bytes> otherwise

This means you CANNOT just derive(Serialize) on CanonOutput and call serde_json::to_string. You need a wire/serialization struct (or custom Serialize impl) that transforms Mapping fields at serialization time.

UnresolvedEntry.input: same encoding rules. If None (special reasons), serialize as JSON null.

Outcome derivation:
- summary.resolved > 0 && summary.unresolved == 0 => RESOLVED
- summary.resolved > 0 && summary.unresolved > 0 => PARTIAL
- summary.resolved == 0 && summary.unresolved > 0 => UNRESOLVED

For REFUSAL outcomes: use Refusal::to_canon_output() from the refusal module. This module only handles RESOLVED/PARTIAL/UNRESOLVED.

Output is a single JSON object on stdout (compact, no trailing newline). The same format is used for --map-out sidecar files (CSV mode's JSON artifact).

UNIT TESTS: Include #[cfg(test)] mod tests in src/output/json.rs. Test:
- encode_identifier() for u8: and hex: cases
- Outcome derivation from summary counts
- Full JSON serialization round-trip for a known ResolveResult
- Refusal envelope structure

VERIFICATION: cargo test -- output::json
acceptance_criteria:
Emits single JSON object to stdout matching canon.v0 schema exactly.
version field is always 'canon.v0'.
outcome derived from summary: RESOLVED if unresolved==0, UNRESOLVED if resolved==0, PARTIAL otherwise.
registry object populated from RegistryMeta (id, version, source as CLI arg verbatim).
summary.total == summary.resolved + summary.unresolved (invariant enforced).
Identifier encoding: u8:<val> for valid UTF-8 with no ASCII control bytes, hex:<lowercase-hex> otherwise.
mappings[] has one entry per resolved unique input value.
unresolved[] has one entry per unresolved unique value (input=null JSON for special reasons).
refusal is null for non-REFUSAL outcomes; populated for REFUSAL with registry=null, summary=null, mappings=[], unresolved=[].
Exports pub fn emit(result: ResolveResult, registry: RegistryMeta) -> Result<String, Error>.
close_reason: Implemented JSON emission with identifier encoding, deterministic ordering, outcome derivation; added unit tests; cargo test -- output::json passed

title: Resolve v0 registry write-back
description:
Implement explicit registry write-back for canon resolve matched ID pairs.

title: [CANON-V1/P09] Deferred matcher techniques and reconciliation interoperability
description:
## Background
Canon must ship a strong native entity-resolution core without waiting for a decision about Dedupe, Splink, OpenRefine, learned models, active learning, email, or another review client. Those tools and techniques may later add value, but choosing among them before P12 empirical acceptance would let speculative integration work outrun measured matching failures.

## Scope
Maintain a post-core decision space with four options: port a technique or model into Rust using a source-pinned oracle-parity program; integrate a bounded external matcher; expose standard reconciliation interoperability such as the W3C Entity Reconciliation API; or do nothing if native quality and scale are sufficient. Review delivery transports are similarly optional. Concrete OpenRefine, Splink, and Dedupe adapter beads remain closed as historical superseded proposals.

## Technical Approach
Block this epic and every open child on final Canon v1 acceptance. Preserve only transport-neutral observation, candidate, evidence, review, decision-ledger, and promotion contracts in core. Revisit an option only from a reproducible P12 failure slice, measured scale limit, real operator model/workflow, or compelling interoperability need. A selected option receives a new or reopened packet with pinned sources, files, invariants, errors, test matrices, commands, and lift gates.

## Success Criteria
- No P09 issue blocks release preflight, final acceptance, sec10d, or native offline operation.
- Canon v1 passes with no named matcher, model runtime, reconciliation client, email provider, or UI.
- The option register documents native-port, adapter, standard-protocol, and no-integration choices without claiming one is selected.
- A later option has zero promotion authority and must prove marginal lift on the sealed P12 methodology.
- Terminology, dependencies, and priorities consistently describe this lane as post-v1.

## Test Plan
Validate the graph is acyclic; verify all open P09 children are blocked by final v1 acceptance; run release planning with all P09 functionality absent; scan active docs and bead notes for claims that a concrete integration or email workflow is committed.

## RESERVATIONS
- docs/DECISION_PORT_TECHNIQUES_OVER_ADAPTERS.md
- docs/DECISION_REVIEW_VIA_EMAIL_CROWDSOURCING.md

## Considerations
Deferral preserves optionality without promising parity. A full Rust port may live in a separate repository, following the cmdrvl-tabfm source-pin, oracle, parity, provenance, discrepancy, and negative-evidence discipline.

title: [SPLINK-STEAL/S6] entity calibrate em: unsupervised weight suggestion emitting proposed strategy YAML
description:
## Problem this solves
When gold labels are thin (new corpus families with no benchmark yet), support-evidence weights are pure guesswork. Fellegi-Sunter expectation-maximisation over agreement patterns estimates how discriminating each evidence operator actually is in THAT corpus — unsupervised — turning weight authoring into weight review. Complements S1: S1 selects thresholds when gold exists; S6 proposes weights when it does not.

## Build
canon entity calibrate em <EVIDENCE.jsonl> --strategy <YAML> [--emit json|summary]
- Collapse per-pair lane evidence into agreement vectors; aggregate to distinct-pattern counts (Splink's key perf trick: EM iterates over pattern counts, never raw pairs).
- Run EM for m/u per evidence operator: fixed iteration cap, documented convergence epsilon, deterministic iteration order, fixed-point/integer-scaled arithmetic so results are platform-stable (no float drift across artifact boundaries).
- Report: per-operator m/u, implied log-odds weights mapped onto NAMEKIT_SCORE_SCALE-compatible integer scores, convergence diagnostics, degenerate-cell warnings.
- Emit a PROPOSED strategy YAML fragment (support scores only). Operator reviews, edits, freezes. Nothing executes from it automatically.

## Splink reference (clone at /Users/zac/Source/opensource/splink)
- splink/internals/expectation_maximisation.py — EM over aggregated agreement patterns (count_agreement_patterns_sql; convergence default 1e-4, max 25 iterations)
- splink/internals/em_training_session.py — session mechanics, blocking-adjusted lambda (:367)
- splink/internals/estimate_u.py — u estimation approach (here: derive from full evidence artifacts or deterministic hash-sample, never RNG)
- docs/topic_guides/training/training_rationale.md — hybrid regime rationale (direct u, EM for m)

## How to test
- Synthetic corpus with planted ground-truth m/u: EM recovers parameters within declared tolerance.
- Determinism: byte-identical report across runs, platforms (integer arithmetic), and shuffled input order.
- Degenerate fixtures: constant field, zero-count cell, non-convergence -> typed warnings and NO weight proposal for the affected operator (never silent bad weights).
- Proposed YAML fragment round-trips through existing strategy validation.
- Leakage guard: command refuses if pointed at a sealed acceptance/holdout suite path (mirror bd-20vz tournament hygiene).

## Doctrine constraints
Offline; consumes existing evidence artifacts only — no new scoring runtime, no runtime evidence operator. THIS IS NOT bd-1rlk: bd-1rlk is the deferred full Fellegi-Sunter/EM *evidence operator* with per-pair uncertain evidence at solve time; this bead is an offline calibration assist with zero runtime presence and zero authority, and must not grow into bd-1rlk.

## RESERVATIONS
- src/entity/calibrate.rs (shared with S1 — serialize if both in flight)
- tests/entity_calibrate_em.rs

title: canon geo: E3 — pairwise candidate test, the headroom number (section 17)
description:
Section 17 stage E3 — the architecture's claim in measurable form: for the labeled failures, does JOINT evidence rank the true lot strictly above the wrong PIP lot?

Rebuild the Gate V2 labeled set (GROUNDTRUTH_ACRIS_BD179B.md exact CTEs). For each lot-incorrect point (and a matched sample of lot-correct points as control), build the PAIR (pip_lot, true_lot) — for multi-BBL truth, score against the nearest/best true member and report multi-BBL cases as a separate slice. Then score BOTH lots of each pair on every landed evidence row from section 16.3 EXCEPT ACRIS (row 8 is the truth source — using it as evidence is circular and forbidden here):
  - geocode: point-to-lot distance / containment depth under the tier's disc radius
  - address: parsed street matches lot's address street; house number within lot's observed range; house-number exact agreement (use the Appendix E normalizer; grammar-lite is acceptable, record its limits)
  - footprints: NYC footprint majority-linked on lot; footprint count vs NUMBLDGS agreement; FEMA count where covered
  - asserted attributes: SF band-consistency asserted-vs-BLDGAREA per lot (coordinate with E1+E2 bead comments for the discovered field names; do not block on it — discover independently if needed)
  - parcel attributes: NUMBLDGS, units consistency where fields exist
Per evidence row report the pairwise 3-way split over pairs: true lot wins / tie / PIP lot wins. Then the JOINT readouts: (1) simple vote across rows; (2) any-single-row-decisive rate; (3) the headline — fraction of incorrect points where the joint evidence ranks true strictly above PIP (ties broken by nothing — a tie is a residual doubleton, which is an honest abstention, count it separately). Control check: on the correct-point sample the PIP lot (which IS the true lot) must not lose to a random same-component neighbor — run that as the null comparison so the test has a falsification arm.

INTERPRETATION GATE: your headline number is folded only alongside E1's taxonomy (some failure classes are unaddressable by tile evidence — gross geocode errors with the true lot outside the tile must be reported as out-of-scope-for-pairwise, not as losses). title: [CANON-V1/P06.14] Compile external domain facts into immutable registry packages
description:
## Background
The useful output of an external deployment is an exact reusable registry, but Canon should compile it without understanding the domain's authorities, vocabulary, or data.

## Technical Approach
Implement a generic domain-registry compiler over pinned ontology, namespace, vocabulary, fact, review, trust/conflict, temporal, and projection packages. Emit exact aliases/IDs, relationship sidecars, unresolved conflicts, proof chains, license/provenance inventory, and reproducible build recipe. Support redistributable thin packs and larger local/private packs.

## Success Criteria
- Every mapping is justified by generic fact/review/policy references.
- Unknown domain IDs round-trip without core interpretation.
- Rebuild is byte-stable and semantic diff exposes additions, remaps, conflicts, and package changes.
- Restricted inputs can produce local packs without leaking into manifests, logs, or public fixtures.

## Test Plan
Compile two invented domains and one externally supplied private conformance deployment; rebuild offline, verify, lint/audit, query hard negatives, compile time slices, and compare exports.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/registry/domain_compile.rs`
- `schemas/canon.registry.build.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/registry_domain_compile.rs`

## Considerations
Canon knows how to compile packages, not which real-world facts deserve promotion.

title: canon geo incremental accretion — dependency-directed invalidation and reuse by affected section/component
description:
WHY

Evidence stacking is economically useful only if adding one source row or release does not force the entire geography through acquisition and solving again. Reuse must also be sound: stale rho, profile, or release bindings cannot survive unnoticed.

DELIVER

Materialize the run dependency DAG and an incremental invalidation engine. New evidence creates a new immutable run revision. It identifies touched source adapter outputs, home cells plus controlled halos, candidate sets, admitted constraints, incidence components, solver representations, reconciliation decisions, and evaluation rows. Unaffected artifacts retain their semantic hashes and are reused.

Define explicit invalidation for new rows, a new source instance, release replacement, rho contract change, query-as-of change, entity-level/profile change, backend/order/vtree policy change, and presentation-only changes. Inspect comparison reports what was reused, recomputed, added, removed, narrowed, emptied, or changed claim class.

ACCEPTANCE

- Two disconnected components fixture: add evidence touching one; only that section/component and downstream reconciliation/evaluation recompute.
- Boundary fixture: a feature change invalidates every controlled-halo section that could include it, not only its home tile.
- Negative test: a rho version change cannot reuse admissions compiled under the old contract.
- Negative test: a release replacement with stable record ids cannot reuse old geometry/evidence by id alone.
- Presentation-budget-only change reuses an already exact residual/backbone.
- Added hard evidence can narrow or empty the model set and the prior run remains reproducible as its own snapshot.
- Reuse decisions are deterministic, content-addressed, explainable, and covered by byte-parity tests.
- Resource report separates saved acquisition/materialization/solve work from estimated national extrapolation.

title: [CANON-V1/P12.10] Publish downstream migration conformance protocol and consumer contract
description:
## Background
A downstream migration is not proven by an in-repository fixture or a helper that happens to compile against private internals. sec10d currently demonstrates the danger: its helper emits removed canon org commands while Canon tests reject that surface, and static tests still approve the stale invocation. Consumers need a capability-negotiated, artifact-pinned protocol that fails before mutating data.

## Technical Approach
Publish a public-binary migration protocol covering capability discovery, version compatibility, extension-package loading, project initialization, exact-first lookup, unresolved-tail preparation and execution, review export and import, promotion, audit, application or projection, and registry replay. Define a machine-readable consumer manifest that pins Canon version, command-contract version, artifact schemas, package digest, profile and ontology identifiers, registry digest, projection contract, resource budgets, and rollback snapshot. Provide dry-run and dual-run modes plus a conformance kit that invokes only the installed public executable. Unknown flags, removed command families, incompatible schemas, missing capabilities, and ignored arguments must be hard errors.

## Success Criteria
- A consumer can determine compatibility from machine output before running a project.
- The protocol preserves generate-dbt-seed and generate-searchable-index as registry projections rather than removing them.
- Canonical registry strategy, immutable snapshots, exact lookup, review, promotion, and replay remain the center of the migration.
- Public subprocess tests catch the current stale org-command class and any silently ignored option.
- Extension packages and consumer projections remain outside core while their versions and digests appear in artifacts.
- Dry-run reports exact filesystem and output mutations; rollback selects a prior immutable registry and package digest.
- At least one out-of-tree consumer completes conformance without importing Canon source modules or using repository-relative defaults.

## Test Plan
Run the kit against compatible, too-old, too-new, unknown-profile, missing-package, tampered-package, stale-registry, removed-command, unknown-flag, partial-output, interrupted, and read-only cases. Compare dual-run outputs byte-for-byte where parity is required. Execute from a clean installed-binary environment with no Canon source checkout present.

## RESERVATIONS
- src/cli.rs
- src/entity/describe.rs
- schemas/canon.consumer.manifest.v1.schema.json
- tests/entity_consumer_conformance.rs
- docs/ENTITY_MIGRATION_PROTOCOL.md
- docs/CLI_CONTRACT.md

## Considerations
This protocol may break obsolete pre-v1 helpers rather than preserve compatibility shims. The migration seam is artifacts and declared capabilities, not downstream knowledge inside Canon.
notes:
## Cross-repository acceptance
sec10d bd-277 freezes the compatibility matrix, bd-2az migrates the helper to exact-first plus a deduplicated unresolved tail, and bd-14w replaces stale org documentation and static-only tests. This Canon bead is not operationally complete until the public conformance kit catches the currently stale org commands and sec10d can execute from an installed binary without sibling-repository defaults.

title: strategy v1 contract: typed keys, grades, and lifecycle semantics
description: Define the canonical contract before code changes. This bead updates docs/PLAN_CANON.md, the source of truth for canon behavior, so future implementation beads do not invent strategy v1 behavior. The contract must cover typed strategy keys, task-key syntax, grade values, attestation provenance, lifecycle states, update semantics, deprecate/remove semantics, promotion semantics, resolve outcomes, registry version bumps, deterministic ordering, and refusal behavior. Background: existing docs specify schema-shape plus skill hash and proof-gated register only; bd-a43 requires intent-keyed champions and operator-attested grade in the same registry. RESERVATIONS: docs/PLAN_CANON.md.
design:
Recommended contract: strategy entries have entry_schema_version = canon_strategy_entry.v1 and a typed key object with key.type = schema or task. Schema entries preserve current schema_fingerprint plus schema plus skill_hash behavior. Task entries use exact task string after ASCII trim plus skill_hash; no fuzzy matching, aliases, normalization, or shape tiers. Grade strings are exactly operator-attested and proof-attested in JSON. Status strings are exactly active and deprecated.

Operator-attested entries require provenance: operator, attested_at, reason, script content hash, and attestation hash. Proof-attested entries require existing verify/assess/airlock references and hashes. Existing pre-v1 entries load as schema-keyed proof-attested active entries through an explicit compatibility/migration rule, not a loose best-effort parser.

Active resolution ignores deprecated entries. Update, promote, and deprecate are in-place registry mutations with explicit next-version; entries are never physically deleted. Mutating commands emit deterministic receipts with before/after registry hashes and append witness records under canon's normal witness policy. Read-only resolve/list/explain never execute scripts and do not append mutation witness records.

Operator discovery is part of the contract: strategy list and strategy explain, or exactly equivalent named commands, must expose registry entries, provenance, grade/status, source file/entry order, and active-resolution reasoning.

title: [CANON-V1/P07.R6a] Preserve record-grain comparison views across source mapping and prepare
description:
## Background
The deterministic structured comparison primitives cannot prove R6 while all prepared views are derived from the primary entity surface and same-name rows collapse before evidence. Multi-assignment records need a separate, hash-bound comparison input that never becomes identity.

## Technical Approach
Compile source-mapped observations and typed assignments into a domain-neutral canon.entity.record_link_input.v1 sidecar. Preserve one stable record per source row with source-side/scope IDs, issuer observation reference, opaque assignment reference, typed comparison views, declared units/scale, source-mapping/profile/input digests, and privacy-safe provenance. Keep entity surfaces and assignment records separate; comparison fields must never create aliases, canonical IDs, or assignment-as-identity behavior. The sidecar must preserve multiple same-issuer records and deterministic ordering under shuffled source rows.

## Success Criteria
- Independent numeric/date/categorical source fields survive intake at record grain.
- Same issuer plus multiple assignments remains multiple comparison records while pointing to one issuer observation.
- Units and scale are explicit and caller-owned; no conversion is inferred.
- Missing, malformed, duplicate, unknown, and incomparable fields fail closed or quarantine under declared policy.
- Output is byte-stable, hash-bound, schema-validated, and contains no BDC-specific fields/defaults.

## Test Plan
Use neutral two-source fixtures with same-name multi-assignment rows, shuffled order, missing/overflow values, explicit scale mismatch, duplicate record IDs, and assignment/identity firewall negatives. Validate source-mapping digest continuity and byte-identical sidecars.

## RESERVATIONS
- src/extensions/source_mapping.rs
- src/entity/profile.rs
- src/entity/prepare.rs
- src/evidence/types.rs
- src/evidence/mod.rs
- schemas/canon.entity.record_link_input.v1.schema.json
- tests/entity_record_link_input.rs

## Considerations
This bead only preserves faithful record-link inputs. It does not score, solve, promote, or run private BDC data.

title: canon geo D3: cross-deal collateral collision and adjacency concentration with pari passu labeling
description:
PACKET PK-D3c (stage D3) from docs/PLAN_CANON_GEO.md §18/§19, course correction 2026-09-01. This bead carries the full design so no implementer needs the plan document.

== WHY ==
§18.2: the same parcel in two trusts is legitimate for pari passu notes and a defect otherwise; nobody runs the check because nobody has the parcel sets. Adjacent-parcel concentration across deals ('these six loans in four deals are one city block') is the same query. A declared pari passu match is a labeled explanation on a kept row, never a suppressed row (I12, TH14).

== STAGE ROW (§19.5; entry condition, gate, contracts) ==
| D3 | Ledger output surface, event exposure join, cross-deal collision | G1 passed (D2 not required: no ledger field reads an explanation artifact); one full public deal's loans mapped to H.7 subjects with accession and loan ids; `tests/fixtures/geo/advisory_synthetic_adv12.json` shipped by the exposure bead; modules `ledger.rs`, `exposure.rs`, `collision.rs` | G3: one full public deal materializes as ledger rows with claim classes; exposure runs against one archived advisory; collision runs across two deals | C13 to C16, C22, C23, C25; T07, T08, T09, T23, T26, T27 | new beads, bd-kwmc, bd-67wx |

== MODULE SURFACE (§19.3; field lists are the required minimum, add #[serde(default)] fields only, never remove or rename) ==
**Dependency direction.** New modules depend on the existing `composition`, `evidence`,
`control`, `discovery`, `evaluation`, `geometry`, `geometry_value`, and `run` modules,
never the reverse. `src/geo/composition.rs` and `src/geo/evidence.rs` are not modified by
D2 to D6: `propagate` and `explain` call `solve_composition` as a black box and narrow or
re-solve `GeoCompositionRequest` values. Within the new set: `explain` consumes
`propagate`; `card`, `next_evidence`, and `inspect` consume `explain`; `exposure` and
`collision` consume `ledger`; `adjudicate` and `card` consume `observer`; nothing consumes
`inspect`.

**Shared shape.** Each module is `pub mod` in `src/geo/mod.rs` with `pub use module::*`.
Each defines `Geo<Module>Error { code: Geo<Module>ErrorCode, message: String, detail:
BTreeMap<String, String> }` with a `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` code enum that
carries the generic `UnsupportedVersion`, `InvalidInput`, `BudgetExceeded`,
`ArithmeticOverflow` variants plus the module's rows from §19.4. Each artifact type has a
`version: String` constant `CANON_GEO_<NAME>_VERSION`, `canonical_<name>_bytes`, and
`validate_<name>_artifact`. Each module ships `schemas/canon.geo.<name>.v0.schema.json`, a
`--describe` entry, a `canon geo <subcommand>`, and `tests/geo_<module>.rs`.

**`collision.rs`**

| Item | Definition |
|---|---|
| Consumes | two or more `GeoCollateralLedger` values, `GeoEntityRef` |
| `GeoCollisionKind` | `SharedParcel`, `SharedBuilding`, `Adjacent` |
| `GeoPariPassuDeclaration` | `entity: GeoEntityRef`, `accessions: Vec<String>`, `source_record: GeoEvidenceRecordRef` |
| `GeoCollision` | `kind`, `entity: GeoEntityRef`, `accessions: Vec<String>`, `loan_ids: Vec<String>`, `pari_passu: bool`, `explanation: String` |
| `GeoCrossDealArtifact` | `version`, `ledger_blake3s: Vec<String>`, `collisions: Vec<GeoCollision>`, `adjacency_concentration: Vec<{ block_id, deal_count: u64, accessions }>` |
| `pub fn find_collisions(ledgers: &[GeoCollateralLedger], declarations: &[GeoPariPassuDeclaration], adjacency: &BTreeMap<String, String>) -> Result<GeoCrossDealArtifact, GeoCollisionError>` | `adjacency` maps parcel id to block id; a declared pari passu match sets `pari_passu = true` and keeps the row (I12) |

== ERROR CODES (§19.4; class is exactly one of refusal / abstention / typed fallback; detail always carries the named ids) ==
| `collision_pari_passu_labeled` | `collision::find_collisions` | a shared entity is covered by a `GeoPariPassuDeclaration` for every colliding accession | not an error: the row is kept with `pari_passu = true` and `explanation` (I12); listed here so no implementer suppresses it | T09 |

== CONTRACTS (§19.9) ==
| C16 | `find_collisions` reports every parcel or building shared by more than one accession with all accessions and loan ids; a declared pari passu match sets `pari_passu == true` with an `explanation` and the row is kept | `collision.rs` | I12 |
| C22 | Every artifact type declares `CANON_GEO_<NAME>_VERSION`, `canonical_<name>_bytes`, `validate_<name>_artifact`, and a `schemas/canon.geo.<name>.v0.schema.json`; canonical bytes are byte-identical across platforms | all §19.3 modules | N02, §19.3 shared shape |
| C25 | D2 to D6 do not modify `src/geo/composition.rs` or `src/geo/evidence.rs`; new modules call `solve_composition` as a black box, and generic modules carry no fixture, demo, or county literal | all §19.3 modules | §19.3 dependency direction, G7 |

== THREATS THIS BEAD MUST DEFEAT (§19.9) ==
| TH14 | A pari passu collision suppressed as a false positive, or an undeclared shared parcel hidden | Row kept with `pari_passu == true` and an explanation; undeclared rows flagged | C16; T09; `collision_pari_passu_labeled` |
| TH21 | Demo-path hard-coding: a generic module special-cases Demo 0 ids, the chimera constraint ids, or Franklin County names to pass its tests | Case-insensitive literal scan over the twelve generic modules; property tests on seeded random components | C25; T27, T03, T16 |

== TESTS (§19.6; ship in tests/geo_<module>.rs with the T ids in test names; each row's Negative case is mandatory) ==
| T09 | D3 | e2e | two ledgers whose rows share parcel `1004540041` and parcel `1004540042`; one `GeoPariPassuDeclaration` for `1004540041` only | `collisions` has exactly two `SharedParcel` rows; the `1004540041` row has `pari_passu == true` and a nonempty `explanation`; the `1004540042` row has `pari_passu == false`; both carry both accessions | an implementation that drops the declared row leaves one collision; that output fails | C16; TH14 | `collision_pari_passu_labeled` |
| T27 | D2 to D7 | adversarial | the twelve generic module files listed in §19.3 | a case-insensitive scan finds none of the literals `1004540041`, `chimera_wrongly_admitted`, `asserted_address_core`, `case_4`, `franklin`, `solve_composition` (the last only in `inspect.rs`), or any hosted-model client symbol in `observer.rs` replay code | the scan must also match `Franklin` and `CASE_4`; a scan that is case-sensitive fails on a seeded scratch copy | C18, C25; TH16, TH21 | none |

== NON-NEGOTIABLES AND INVARIANTS ==
### 19.1 Non-negotiables

- N01 Runtime lookup stays exact registry replay. Geo is a build-time workbench.
- N02 Same input plus same pinned sources reproduce byte-identical artifacts on every
  platform. No wall clock, locale, hash-map order, or float comparison in a decision path.
- N03 Every source value enters the solver only through a declared, versioned `rho`.
- N04 Adding admitted hard evidence may only narrow the model set or make it empty.
- N05 Source count is provenance, never evidence weight or confidence.
- N06 Candidate reach, admission, solver exactness, reconciliation, truth quality, and
  cost are reported as separate planes and never pooled.
- N07 Fixtures, retained evidence, and mocked providers are never presented as live proof.
- N08 Abstention is a legitimate output; an abstention-only module is not a delivered
  feature.
- N09 No vision or statistical model proposes a location. Models are observers with
  characterized error.
- N10 No commercial basemap imagery or tiles enter any artifact.
- N11 Gates are frozen in tests. A gate is passed by meeting it, never by editing it.
- N12 Every feature bead ships its code and its tests together, including at least one
  negative case a naive implementation fails.

### 19.2 Invariants for the new artifacts

- I01 A propagator prunes a value only with a typed reason naming constraint id and
  evidence ids; pruning is sound: enumeration with propagation equals enumeration without.
- I02 Propagator fixpoint is order-independent; tests run every permutation of propagator
  order on each fixture and compare bytes.
- I03 A minimal core is minimal: removing any one member restores satisfiability; tests
  verify by re-solving each deletion.
- I04 A correction set hits every enumerated core; when core enumeration hits its ceiling
  the artifact says `cores_complete=false` and no minimality claim is made.
- I05 Explanation artifacts name source record ids and rho contract ids, never internal
  indices.
- I06 An observer observation carries image tile digest, vintage, license hash, model or
  rule identity, weight or prompt digest, and the error-population digest; missing any
  field refuses.
- I07 Observer output is stored, never regenerated at replay; replay verifies the stored
  digest chain only.
- I08 A ledger row binds accession, loan id, parcel set, building set, truth plane,
  claim class, model count, exactness flags, and every source release pin; rows with
  candidate reach `none` carry the reason and no sets.
- I09 A ledger row never pools truth planes; non-round and round exact-lender evidence
  stay labeled.
- I10 The retry loop is bounded by a declared pass count; each pass is a normal pinned
  run and the loop artifact lists every pass with its abstention reason.
- I11 Event exposure joins building geometry, not centroids; advisory source hashes travel
  with the result.
- I12 Cross-deal collision reports a parcel or building shared by more than one trust
  with both accessions; pari passu participation is a labeled explanation, not a suppressed
  row.
- I13 `geo inspect` reads only emitted artifacts and receipts; it computes nothing that
  changes an answer.
- I14 Next-evidence recommendations expose the nondominated frontier and never manufacture
  a total ranking without a declared loss model.

== COMMANDS ==
### 19.7 Commands

Whole-tree gates run on every commit in every stage. Per-module binaries are the
`tests/geo_<module>.rs` files from §19.3; each stage runs its own set before claiming its
gate. `rg` exit status 1 means no match, which is the pass for the literal scans, so
they are written with a leading `!`.

```bash
# Whole-tree gates
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test

# Frozen E4 gate (T17, C24): expected red until G1, green from G1 on
cargo test --test geo_adjudication e4_acceptance_gate_requires_the_full_population_to_be_reachable -- --ignored

# Per-module test binaries (stage: test ids)
cargo test --test geo_propagate           # D2: T01 to T04, T19
cargo test --test geo_explain             # D2: T05, T06, T20, T21
cargo test --test geo_ledger              # D3: T07, T23, T26
cargo test --test geo_exposure            # D3: T08
cargo test --test geo_collision           # D3: T09
cargo test --test geo_retry               # D4: T10
cargo test --test geo_condo               # D4: T11
cargo test --test geo_inspect             # D4: T12, T25
cargo test --test geo_next_evidence       # D5: T18
cargo test --test geo_observer            # D6: T13, T14, T15
cargo test --test geo_adjudicate          # D6: T22 (new binary; distinct from the existing geo_adjudication)
cargo test --test geo_card                # D6: T24, T26
cargo test --test geo_e5_franklin_parcel  # D7: T16 plus the existing literal scan

# One test by name with output
cargo test --test geo_propagate soundness_holds_on_every_e4_fixture -- --nocapture

# Schema drift guard (C22). tests/geo_schemas.rs include_str!s each schema file, pins
# title, properties.version.const, and additionalProperties == false, then walks a real
# serialized instance against the schema; there is no jsonschema crate. Each new
# artifact adds one <name>_schema_matches_a_real_instance test there and one
# include_str! of schemas/canon.geo.<name>.v0.schema.json.
cargo test --test geo_schemas
cargo test --test geo_schemas propagation_schema_matches_a_real_instance
for s in propagation explanation separation_request separation observer observation_rows \
         image_tile_pin adjudication_request adjudication_receipt evidence_card \
         collateral_ledger event_exposure cross_deal retry_loop inspection next_evidence \
         condo_bridge_request ledger_bridge; do
  jq -e --arg s "$s" '.title == "canon.geo.\($s).v0"
    and .properties.version.const == "canon_geo_\($s).v0"
    and .additionalProperties == false' "schemas/canon.geo.${s}.v0.schema.json"
done

# --describe entries for geo subcommands (C22: one per new module, named after it:
# geo propagate, geo explain, geo observer, geo adjudicate, geo card, geo ledger,
# geo exposure, geo collision, geo retry, geo inspect, geo next-evidence, geo condo)
cargo run --bin canon -- --describe \
  | jq -r '.subcommands[] | select(.name | startswith("geo ")) | "\(.name)\t\(.status)\t\(.output_schema)"'
cargo run --bin canon -- --describe \
  | jq -e '[.subcommands[] | select(.name == "geo propagate" and .status == "implemented")] | length == 1'

# T27 literal scan (C25, G7). Mirrors tests/geo_e5_franklin_parcel.rs
# franklin_instance_names_do_not_enter_the_generic_geo_engine, which lowercases each
# generic source file and asserts it contains no instance literal.
GEO_GENERIC="src/geo/propagate.rs src/geo/explain.rs src/geo/observer.rs src/geo/adjudicate.rs \
  src/geo/card.rs src/geo/ledger.rs src/geo/exposure.rs src/geo/collision.rs src/geo/retry.rs \
  src/geo/inspect.rs src/geo/next_evidence.rs src/geo/condo.rs"
! rg -i -n 'franklin|39049|epsg:3735|1004540041|chimera_wrongly_admitted|asserted_address_core|case_4' $GEO_GENERIC
! rg -n 'solve_composition' src/geo/inspect.rs
! rg -i -n 'reqwest|hyper::|openai|anthropic|gemini|bedrock|invoke_model' src/geo/observer.rs
cargo test --test geo_e5_franklin_parcel franklin_instance_names_do_not_enter_the_generic_geo_engine

# Demo 0, capabilities, measurement plan, beads
bash scripts/geo_demo/demo0.sh --work-dir /tmp/demo0
cargo run --bin canon -- geo capabilities --emit json
cargo run --bin canon_geo_measurements -- --emit plan
br ready --json && br dep cycles --json
```

ANTI-REWARD-HACKING (AGENTS.md, binding):
- Code and tests ship in this bead; no scope-splitting into type/impl/test closures.
- No new todo!()/unimplemented!() scaffolds. Refusal-only implementation earns partial credit and never closes this bead (label refusal-only + follow-up bead if that is the honest state).
- Fixtures and Demo 0 outputs are never presented as live proof (C23). Gate thresholds are never edited to pass (C24, N11).
- Every feature test includes at least one negative case a naive implementation fails (the Negative case column below).
- Generic modules carry no fixture, demo, or county literal (C25, T27).

title: [ENTITY-ATOMICITY] Publish multi-file v1 stage sets transactionally
description:
## Background
The v1 entity workbench publishes block, evidence, solve, and run as multi-file stage sets. Validation and tamper refusals are preflighted before writes, but a late filesystem failure can still leave a mixed stage set because files are written sequentially to stable final paths. Per-file atomic rename does not make the whole set atomic. Warm-cache execution intentionally reruns in the same work_dir, so requiring final stage directories to be absent is not acceptable.

## Technical approach
Design and implement a versioned, recoverable stage-set publication protocol that preserves current public artifact paths or introduces an explicitly versioned migration. It must support same-work-dir warm-cache reruns, deterministic replay, concurrent readers, interruption recovery, and truthful writes_performed reporting. Explore append-only/content-addressed generations plus a verified commit marker or another portable transaction design. Do not rely on unsafe platform-specific directory swaps. Any cleanup or deletion behavior requires explicit written permission and a documented ownership boundary.

## Success criteria
- Readers observe either the complete previous stage set or the complete next stage set, never a mixed generation.
- I/O failure and process interruption at every publication boundary produce an actionable, truthful refusal and recover without corrupting the last committed stage.
- Warm enabled/disabled cache reruns in the same work_dir remain supported.
- Manual block/evidence/solve and full run retain byte/semantic parity.
- Publication is offline, deterministic, portable, and hash-bound.
- No hidden garbage collection or file deletion is introduced without explicit authorization.

## Test plan
Add fault injection at every write/sync/commit boundary, crash-restart recovery tests, concurrent reader/writer tests, same-work-dir cache replay, stale staging/commit marker tests, and full fmt/clippy/test gates.

## Reservations
Reserve exact implementation and test files after the publication protocol is approved; likely src/entity/run.rs plus a dedicated existing integration harness.
close_reason: Transactional content-addressed stage publication now provides complete committed generations, warm no-write replay, stale-parent refusal, failpoint recovery, concurrent reader/writer safety, and committed-byte consumers; 28 protocol tests and full quality gate pass.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text: PROTOCOL APPROVED FIRST SLICE 2026-07-14: implement the append-only content-addressed publication protocol in exact files src/entity/publication.rs, src/entity/mod.rs, and tests/entity_publication_protocol.rs. Immutable objects plus a self-hashed generation manifest must be fully written, synced, read-back validated, then exposed by one atomic commit-marker creation. Readers snapshot one generation and resolve every logical path by manifest hash. Warm replay is idempotent and no-write; cache mode/status participate in generation identity; failures report writes_performed and committed state truthfully; orphan attempts are ignored and never deleted; no garbage collection or cleanup. Include deterministic fault-injection, concurrent reader/writer, same-generation race, tamper, crash-state, and warm-rerun tests. Do not touch run.rs/lib.rs or claim stable legacy paths are transactional in this slice. Worker uses Agent Mail thread bd-2vct and does not mutate Beads, commit, or push.

title: [CANON-V1/P10.1] Stabilize an embeddable Rust API around immutable artifacts
description:
## Background
CLI-first design is valuable, but applications and agents also need exact lookup, verification, artifact reading, planning, and explanation without spawning a process for every row. The library boundary should not expose internal modules as accidental API.

## Technical Approach
Define public Rust types and traits for package open/verify, exact batch lookup, row-preserving mapping, project plan/run events, artifact/evidence/explanation readers, and read-only registry metadata. Use explicit versioned request/response types, bounded iterators/streams, stable refusal codes, and feature boundaries. Keep mutation behind higher-level transaction APIs.

## Success Criteria
- Documented public API covers supported embedding use cases without importing internal engine modules.
- CLI and SDK call the same authoritative implementations and produce equivalent artifacts.
- Semver and artifact-version responsibilities are explicit despite early-development direct changes.
- Default features remain small, safe, offline, and free of optional adapter/cloud dependencies.

## Test Plan
Compile public-API examples, run CLI/SDK conformance on the same fixtures, test batch/stream bounds, refusal parity, thread-safety declarations, and minimal/default feature builds.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/lib.rs`
- `src/sdk.rs`
- `tests/sdk_conformance.rs`
- `README.md`

## Considerations
Do not promise stability for internal solver/operator structs; stabilize artifact and operation boundaries first.

title: [CANON-V1/P10.7] Enforce cross-interface conformance and embedding examples
description:
## Background
Additional interfaces are accretive only if they expose the same truth. Divergent exit/refusal semantics or ID encoding across CLI, SDK, RPC, MCP, portable lookup, and exports would create new correctness risks.

## Technical Approach
Build one conformance corpus and runner that invokes every enabled interface against the same verified registry/project artifacts, normalizes transport envelopes only, and compares mappings, unresolved reasons, types, provenance references, plans, explanations, pagination, and mutation declarations. Compile and execute minimal consumer examples.

## Success Criteria
- All enabled read interfaces agree on semantic results and registry digest.
- Feature-disabled interfaces report clean capability absence without affecting default build.
- Examples compile from the documented public API rather than private modules.
- Conformance failures identify the field/interface delta and preserve raw outputs.

## Test Plan
Run default/minimal/all-feature matrices, CLI subprocess, Rust consumer crate, JSON-RPC/MCP client, service, portable reader, and independent export queries. Include Unicode/binary identifiers, large batches, errors, and stale artifacts.

## RESERVATIONS
- `tests/interface_conformance.rs`
- `examples/embedded_lookup.rs`
- `examples/project_plan.rs`
- `README.md`

## Considerations
Conformance compares semantics where byte envelopes necessarily differ; canonical artifacts themselves remain byte-stable.

title: [CANON-V1/P12.5] Run entity-disjoint and time-forward discovery benchmarks
description:
## Background
Withheld aliases test attachment to known entities, but Canon must also cluster previously unseen entities and generalize to future sources. Random row splits cannot prove either behavior.

## Technical Approach
Run two sealed benchmark families through the public binary. Entity-disjoint trials place all observations for a canonical entity exclusively in tune or holdout and evaluate novel clustering plus related-distinct safety. Time-forward trials build a registry and policy only from observations available before a cutoff, then evaluate later documents, renamed surfaces, new firms, and changed relationships without future leakage. Include directional cross-source linkage where a reference and target dataset have different fields. Report results by evidence availability, source family, name difficulty, entity frequency, and relation class.

## Success Criteria
- No holdout entity or future observation contributes aliases, anchors, thresholds, dictionaries, or patches to the evaluated snapshot.
- Novel-cluster and time-forward metrics meet the quality contract or produce a versioned failure report that blocks release claims.
- Hard-negative hierarchy and lookalike cases have zero severity-critical false merges.
- Results expose head-versus-tail and easy-versus-hard performance rather than one aggregate score.
- The benchmark can run on an invented public corpus and an operator-owned private corpus through the same command.

## Test Plan
Create planted leakage and temporal-reversal controls; run clean entity-disjoint and chronological splits; shuffle physical rows; repeat with exact cache disabled/enabled; test missing timestamps and conflicting temporal facts. Verify public subprocess commands, hashes, exit codes, and output queries.

## RESERVATIONS
- src/evaluation/generalization.rs
- tests/entity_generalization.rs
- tests/fixtures/extensions/neutral-domain/time_forward/

## Considerations
An entity-disjoint test asks whether Canon can form a new cluster, not whether it can invent a globally authoritative identity from names alone. Promotion still requires policy and review.
notes:
## Demanding-deployment acceptance
Owns the time-forward evaluation side of R5. Include rename and temporal-alias cases where only evidence available as of the cutoff may be used. Report identity continuity, abstention, and false-link behavior across time rather than collapsing all aliases into an atemporal gold.

title: Witness protocol
description:
Implement the witness protocol in src/witness.rs. ~100-150 LOC.

Purpose: append an immutable ledger record for every canon run, enabling audit trail and reproducibility verification.

Hashing:
- input_hash: BLAKE3 hash of the input file bytes (read the file once, hash all bytes).
- output_hash: BLAKE3 hash of the output bytes. JSON mode: hash the entire JSON string. CSV mode: hash the CSV bytes incrementally as they stream through stdout (wrap the stdout writer in a BLAKE3 hashing tee).

Ledger record (one JSON line appended to .canon-witness.jsonl):
{
  "tool": "canon",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "timestamp": "2026-02-25T12:34:56.789Z",
  "input_path": "tape.csv",
  "input_hash": "blake3:abc123...",
  "output_hash": "blake3:def456...",
  "registry_id": "cusip-isin",
  "registry_version": "3.2.1",
  "outcome": "PARTIAL",
  "summary": { "total": 100, "resolved": 95, "unresolved": 5 }
}

Ledger location: .canon-witness.jsonl in the current working directory.

Error handling: witness failures NEVER block the main pipeline. If the ledger file can't be opened/written, log a warning to stderr and continue. The tool's primary output (JSON or CSV) is never affected by witness failure.

--no-witness: if set, skip the entire witness step (no hashing, no file write).
acceptance_criteria: TARGET FILE: src/witness.rs only. Include #[cfg(test)] mod tests. Test: ledger record JSON structure, BLAKE3 hash computation, --no-witness skips entirely, witness failure does not affect exit code. VERIFICATION: cargo test -- witness

title: [CANON-V1/P06.3] Make identifier namespaces, validators, and trust policy extensible
description:
## Background
Strong identifiers differ across domains and authorities. Baking a list of identifiers into Canon would make the open-source tool opinionated and permanently incomplete.

## Technical Approach
Define identifier-namespace packages with opaque namespace URI/ID, applicable object types, normalization and format/checksum validator references, exclusivity/reuse/temporal metadata, display/redaction policy, and source trust hints. Expose a safe validator primitive interface and pin trust/conflict policy separately from the namespace definition.

## Success Criteria
- A project can introduce an unknown namespace and validator without changing core identity types.
- Bare strings are never guessed into a namespace; field mappings must declare one.
- Conflicting exclusive identifiers yield typed anti-merge/conflict evidence.
- Namespace, validator, and trust-policy changes independently invalidate the correct artifacts.

## Test Plan
Test invented numeric, alphanumeric, checksum, recycled, scoped, redacted, and conflicting namespaces. Fuzz validator inputs and prove no package can invoke undeclared code or escape resource limits.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/extensions/identifier.rs`
- `schemas/canon.extension.identifier.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/extensions_identifier.rs`

## Considerations
Provide reusable validator primitives, not built-in registries of real authorities or product-specific precedence.
