title: canon geo D6: frozen-weight structure-count observer, NYC error characterization, and the G6 measurement
description:
PACKET PK-D6a-count (stage D6, gate G6 owner) from docs/PLAN_CANON_GEO.md §18.4, §18.5, §19.5 row D6, minted 2026-09-02 in the coverage pass. §19.5 D6 work names "one frozen-weight count observer" and gate G6 reads: "observer error characterized on a named NYC population; observations admitted through rho on the D1 cohort change at least one residual or are shown redundant; card artifact validates". No bead owned the observer or the G6 measurement. This bead owns both. It carries the full design so no implementer needs the plan document.

== WHY ==
§18.4 kinds table, first row: `structure_count_in_window` with error band reads soundly as a `gcc` lower/upper bound on latent structures inside the parcel or window and feeds the cardinality propagator (bd-2ofm). This is the first imagery observation that can tighten a real multi-parcel residual: on an H.7 subject whose candidate universe carries seven buildings and whose residual is a doubleton, a count band of [5, 6] from the 2024 ortho excludes the 7-building model. §18.4 observer contract: "A vision model with frozen hashed weights in controlled arithmetic qualifies." Appendix A rule: a model is a source, not a solver; nondeterminism is banned, models are not. The observer never proposes a location (N09); its output enters only through `rho` (N03) after its error is characterized on the named NYC population (pins bead), with the null observer (null observer bead) as the redundancy baseline.

== OBSERVER RUNTIME (outside the canon binary, like every acquisition) ==
scripts/geo_observer/count_observer/ holds: `run_count_observer.py` with pinned dependencies (uv lock), an ONNX model file referenced only by BLAKE3 (`weights/<blake3>.onnx`, never by name), and a fixed preprocessing spec (crop window in pixel coordinates derived from the pin byte range and the window polygon by integer arithmetic, fixed resize to the model input size with a named integer resampler, no random augmentation). Arithmetic contract string recorded on the identity: `arithmetic_contract = "onnxruntime-cpu-<version>-int8-single-thread"`; the runner asserts single thread and integer quantized weights so two machines produce the same logits bytes; the runner records the logits BLAKE3 as `label_blake3`. Output: `canon_geo_observation_rows.v0` rows, one per window: `{ id: "obs:count:<subject_id>:<vintage>", observer_id: "observer.count.frozen", tile_pins: [pin], window_blake3, kind: StructureCountInWindow, payload: CountBand { min, max } (min = max = raw count at emission; the band is widened at ADMISSION by the characterization, never by the runner), crop_blake3 (BLAKE3 of the crop bytes written next to the row), label_blake3 }`. Canon never invokes the runner (I07, C10); replay verifies the digests.

== IDENTITY AND CONTRACT ==
`GeoObserverIdentity::FrozenWeight { model_id: "count.<arch>", weight_blake3: <blake3 of the onnx file>, arithmetic_contract }`. `GeoObserverContract { id: "observer.count.frozen", output_kinds: [StructureCountInWindow, PresentAtVintage, AbsentAtVintage], error_population_id: <pins bead population_id>, characterization_blake3: <digest of the characterization artifact>, rho_contract_ids: ["rho.structure_count.v0"] }`. The rho contract `rho.structure_count.v0` is a `GeoRhoContract` (existing evidence.rs type) declaring the `IntegerSumBand` reading: unit `structure`, value 1 per building candidate whose majority area lies in the window, band `[count - lower_slack, count + upper_slack]` with the slacks taken from the characterization, `value_origin: SourceAsserted`. Derived vintage kinds, deterministic and recorded by the runner from the same raw count: `PresentAtVintage` when raw count >= 1 for the window, `AbsentAtVintage` when raw count == 0; both are listed in `diagnostic_only_ids` by `to_rho_observation` (C11, T15) and consumed only by the dated-existence bead and by bd-1oy8 when its trigger fires.

== CHARACTERIZATION (the G6 first clause) ==
`pub fn characterize(contract: &GeoObserverContract, rows: &[GeoObservationRow], population: &GeoErrorPopulationArtifact, reference: &BTreeMap<String, u64>) -> Result<GeoObserverCharacterization, GeoObserverError>` in src/geo/observer_count.rs (generic module; add to the T27 scan). `reference` is the per-window landed footprint count computed by the null observer bead (the plane count is the reference, honestly labeled `reference = landed_footprint_plane`, not ground truth about the world). For every population subject with a row: signed error `raw - reference`; the artifact records `compared`, `exact_agreement`, `max_abs_error`, `error_band { lower_slack = max(0, max(reference - raw)), upper_slack = max(0, max(raw - reference)) }` (integers only), the per-truth-plane breakdown (never pooled, I09), `population_blake3` (must equal the committed population's canonical digest, else refuse `observer_error_uncharacterized`), `rows_outside_population: Vec<String>` (rows for subjects not in the population are listed and EXCLUDED from the error computation, so no post-hoc selection can improve the band), `is_null_baseline: false`. The band widens the admitted `IntegerSumBand` at admission time. A subject with no row is counted under `missing` with a declared denominator.

== THE G6 MEASUREMENT (second clause: "change at least one residual or are shown redundant") ==
`pub fn measure_effect(before: &[(String, GeoCompositionArtifact)], after: &[(String, GeoCompositionArtifact)]) -> Result<GeoObserverEffect, GeoObserverError>` producing `canon_geo_observer_effect.v0` (additive contract, shared shape): per case `{ case_id, model_count_before, model_count_after, backbone_gained: Vec<GeoEntityRef>, backbone_lost: Vec<GeoEntityRef> (must be empty; N04 hard evidence only narrows, a lost backbone member refuses `propagation_unsound_detected`-style code `observer_effect_widened`), status_before, status_after, redundant: bool }` and totals `{ cases: u64, changed: u64, redundant: u64, conflict_introduced: u64, per_truth_plane: ... }` with a declared denominator equal to the number of D1 cohort cases that had both a row and a solvable universe. G6 passes when `changed >= 1` or every case is `redundant` with a recorded reason, and the characterization exists. G6 is a measurement receipt over runtime-selected D1 cohort cases (the pins bead population seed), never over Demo 0 or fixtures (C23, TH20). `conflict_introduced > 0` is not a failure: it is a P2 explanation opportunity handed to bd-o0co and recorded.

== ERROR CODES (additions to the observer module enum; class per §19.4) ==
| `observer_error_uncharacterized` (existing bd-ci1n row) | `characterize`, `admit_observations` | `population_blake3` mismatch, empty characterization, kind not in `output_kinds` | refusal |
| `observer_band_not_from_characterization` | `admit_observations` when the rho band on a row is narrower than `[raw - lower_slack, raw + upper_slack]` | refusal; `detail["observation_id"]`, `detail["band"]`, `detail["characterized_band"]` |
| `observer_effect_widened` | `measure_effect` | any case with `model_count_after > model_count_before` or nonempty `backbone_lost` | refusal (violates N04; signals an unsound rho) |
| `observer_runtime_invoked` | any code path in src/geo/observer_count.rs that would spawn or import the runner | refusal by construction: T27 scan plus a test that the module has no `std::process::Command` symbol |

== CONTRACTS AND THREATS SERVED ==
C09, C10, C11 (count enters only via `to_rho_observation`; vintage kinds diagnostic), C22, C23, C25, N03, N04, N05, N09 (no location kind exists in `GeoObservationKind`; the runner outputs counts and vintages only), I06, I07, TH08 (replay never re-runs), TH10, TH20, TH21.

== TESTS (tests/geo_observer_count.rs; each test logs on failure) ==
| T34 (bead-defined, extends §19.6) | D6 | unit | a synthetic population of 5 subjects with `reference` counts `[6, 1, 3, 2, 4]` and rows with raw counts `[6, 2, 3, 1, 4]` | `compared == 5`, `exact_agreement == 3`, `max_abs_error == 1`, `error_band == {lower_slack: 1, upper_slack: 1}`; a sixth row for a subject outside the population is in `rows_outside_population` and does not change the band | a characterization computed against a population whose canonical digest differs from the contract's `error_population_id` file refuses `observer_error_uncharacterized` with `detail["population_blake3"]` naming both digests | LOG on failure: per subject id the reference, raw, signed error; the computed band; `rows_outside_population`; both population digests |
| T35 (bead-defined) | D6 | unit | T34 characterization; a row with raw count 6 for a window with 7 building candidates; `to_rho_observation` then compile and solve through `solve_composition` on the Demo 0 case 4 universe (7 parcels, 7 buildings, `fixture.` pins) with no other constraints | the compiled `IntegerSumBand` is `[5, 7]` (unit `structure`, 7 contributions of 1); `residual_model_count` drops from the unconstrained count to the count of subsets of size 5 to 7; `measure_effect` reports `changed == 1`, `backbone_lost.is_empty()` | a row whose band was narrowed to `[6, 6]` by hand refuses `observer_band_not_from_characterization`; a test-local "effect" where after > before refuses `observer_effect_widened` with `detail["case_id"]` | LOG on failure: the compiled band, the universe size, model counts before and after, the differing models, the observation id, the rho contract id |
| T36 (bead-defined) | D6 | e2e | `GeoObservationRowsArtifact` with one count row and the derived `PresentAtVintage` row, `bytes_by_blake3` with the tile, crop, and logits bytes | `verify_replay` is `Ok`; the vintage row id is in `diagnostic_only_ids`; the count row id is in `rho_observations` | flipping one byte of the logits bytes refuses `observation_regenerated_at_replay` with `detail["observation_id"]` (bd-ci1n T14 code) | LOG on failure: each digest expected vs recomputed, byte lengths, which map key failed |
| T37 (bead-defined) | D6 | adversarial | src/geo/observer_count.rs | no `std::process::Command`, `reqwest`, `hyper::`, `onnx`, `ort::`, `tract`, `openai`, `anthropic`, `gemini`, `bedrock`, `invoke_model` symbol; no T27 literal | a seeded scratch copy with `Command::new` fails | LOG on failure: file, line, literal |

== E2E SCRIPT (scripts/geo_demo/e2e_observer_count.sh; `set -euo pipefail`; logs each command, exit code, artifact BLAKE3 into <work-dir>/run.log) ==
1. `bash scripts/geo_demo/demo0.sh --work-dir <dir>`.
2. Fixture path (CI): copy tests/fixtures/geo/observer_count_fixture_rows.json (raw counts and pre-recorded logits bytes under `fixture.` pins) into <dir>; `canon geo observer characterize --contract <dir>/count-contract.json --rows <dir>/count-rows.json --population tests/fixtures/geo/fixture_population.json --reference <dir>/null-reference.json --emit json > <dir>/count-characterization.json`; log band and counts.
3. `canon geo observer admit --contract ... --rows ... --rho <dir>/rho.structure_count.json --forbidden scripts/geo_observer/forbidden_licenses.json --emit json > <dir>/count-admitted.json`; log `rho_observations` and `diagnostic_only_ids` counts.
4. `canon geo compile-evidence` and `canon geo solve` with and without the admitted rows; `canon geo observer effect --before <dir>/solve.json --after <dir>/solve-with-count.json --emit json > <dir>/count-effect.json`; log `changed`, `redundant`, `conflict_introduced`, and per case the before and after counts.
5. `canon geo observer verify-replay --rows <dir>/count-admitted.json --bytes-dir <dir>/bytes`; log every digest checked.
6. `cargo test --test geo_observer_count -- --nocapture`; `cargo test --test geo_schemas observer_effect_schema_matches_a_real_instance observer_characterization_schema_matches_a_real_instance`; whole-tree gates.
7. Live G6 run (not CI, ACQUISITION labeled): `uv run scripts/geo_observer/count_observer/run_count_observer.py --pins scripts/geo_observer/pins/nyc_ortho_2024.pins.json --population scripts/geo_observer/populations/nyc_h7_observer_population.v0.json --out <dir>/nyc-count-rows.json`, then steps 2 to 5 against the D1 residual artifacts; commit the characterization and effect artifacts as retained evidence with the run log; the G6 receipt names the population seed, the D1 residual artifact digests, and the per-truth-plane denominators.

== RESERVATIONS ==
src/geo/observer_count.rs, tests/geo_observer_count.rs, scripts/geo_demo/e2e_observer_count.sh, scripts/geo_observer/count_observer/*, scripts/geo_observer/forbidden_licenses.json, tests/fixtures/geo/observer_count_fixture_rows.json, schemas/canon.geo.observer_effect.v0.schema.json, schemas/canon.geo.observer_characterization.v0.schema.json (if the null observer bead has not landed it). Shared append-only touch points, reserve for the edit only: src/geo/mod.rs, src/geo/cli.rs (`geo observer characterize`, `admit`, `effect`, `verify-replay` under bd-ci1n's `geo observer` family), src/operator.rs, tests/geo_schemas.rs, the T27 scan list in tests/geo_e5_franklin_parcel.rs.

Depends on bd-ci1n (contract and admission), the pins bead (NYC pins, population), the null observer bead (reference counts and redundancy baseline), and bd-1g4x (the D1 residual artifacts the G6 second clause is measured on). Feeds the dated-existence bead (vintage rows), bd-101v (a real card), bd-1oy8 (trigger).

ANTI-REWARD-HACKING (AGENTS.md, binding): the band is never narrowed by hand; the population is never re-drawn; fixture rows are never cited for G6; the runner is never called from Canon; a G6 claim names the seed, the cohort digests, and per-plane denominators or it is not a G6 claim. Code and tests ship together. No new todo!() scaffolds.

title: canon geo [ambition-5]: entropic OT / Sinkhorn soft assignment — highest determinism risk, likely correctly rejected
description:
LAST IN THE AMBITION LANE, LOWEST PRIORITY, AND THE ONE MOST LIKELY TO BE CORRECTLY
REJECTED. Written down so the decision is deliberate rather than forgotten.

BLOCKED ON THE RESIDUAL HARNESS AND ON THE THREE AMBITION BEADS BEFORE IT. If exact
assignment, constellation consistency and correlation clustering have not exhausted the
tie population, this is what remains.

bd-2kjx names "Sinkhorn assignment" in its ambition list. OC-0047 already uses the same
family — iterative proportional fitting / entropic optimal transport — for holder
attribution, so the technique is not foreign to the estate.

WHAT IT WOULD BUY: entropic optimal transport produces a SOFT assignment — a doubly
stochastic coupling — rather than a hard one, under explicit MARGINAL CONSTRAINTS. The
marginals are exactly the cardinality prior the epic already names: "a tile has
approximately N buildings; a clustering producing 3N is wrong by construction." Sinkhorn
lets that prior be a CONSTRAINT ON THE SOLUTION rather than a diagnostic applied afterward,
and the entropic regularizer makes genuine ambiguity visible as a spread-out coupling row
instead of an arbitrary winner. A row of the coupling that is flat IS an abstention signal,
and a well-calibrated one.

WHY IT IS RANKED LAST — THREE REASONS, ALL STRUCTURAL:

1. DETERMINISM RISK IS THE HIGHEST OF ANY METHOD IN THE LANE. Sinkhorn is an iterative
   float algorithm whose output depends on iteration count, convergence tolerance,
   regularization strength, and floating-point accumulation ORDER. Every one of those is a
   replay hazard. To make it deterministic: FIXED iteration count (never a convergence
   tolerance), fixed regularization, a specified summation order, and integer quantization
   at the artifact boundary per src/entity/score.rs. Even then, cross-platform f64
   reproducibility must be PROVEN on the CI matrix, not assumed. If it cannot be proven,
   THIS METHOD DOES NOT SHIP — determinism is the product promise and no amount of
   elegance overrides it.

2. IT SOLVES A PROBLEM THAT MAY NOT EXIST AT THIS SCALE. Entropic OT earns its keep when
   exact assignment is computationally infeasible. At ~167 nodes per tile, Hungarian/JV is
   EXACT and costs ~4.6M operations. The regularized approximation is strictly worse than
   the exact answer unless the SOFTNESS ITSELF is the point. So the honest question is
   narrow: does a soft coupling produce BETTER-CALIBRATED ABSTENTION than the
   margin-to-next-best number the assignment bead already reports for free? MEASURE THAT
   SPECIFIC CLAIM. If margin-to-next-best is as good a tie detector, close this bead unbuilt.

3. THE CARDINALITY MARGINALS ARE NOT ACTUALLY KNOWN. The prior says a tile has
   APPROXIMATELY N buildings. Sinkhorn wants marginals, and supplying guessed marginals as
   if they were constraints would manufacture false confidence — the model would enforce a
   count nobody measured. Unbalanced OT variants relax this, at the cost of another
   hyperparameter to fix deterministically. Note also the 2026-08-14 correction to the
   epic: the cardinality prior applies PER ENTITY TYPE, and is unbounded for overlapping
   legal parcels once condos are included. So for parcels there may be no usable marginal
   at all.

title: canon geo: re-pull tiles WITH polygons and re-measure decomposition — settles whether exact compilation survives
description:
BLOCKS THE COMPILATION STRATEGY. The measurement that would settle it is cheap and has not
been run.

Appendix B of PLAN_CANON_GEO.md falsified the plan's component-size claim using centroid
proximity: on a real dense Manhattan tile there is NO radius at which components land in the
claimed 6-20 range. The distribution goes from mostly-singletons straight to a single
193-variable component percolating at ~60m.

But centroid proximity was never the intended filter. The architecture says a footprint can
only be a slot when it is geometrically compatible with a parcel — which means POLYGON
CONTAINMENT AND OVERLAP, not centre-to-centre distance. That measurement could not be run
because the extract carried only centroids, distances and areas. No polygons.

TASK: re-pull the tile WITH geometry and re-run the decomposition.

  SELECT ..., ST_ASWKT(GEOM_GEOG) FROM EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.NYC_DCP_MAPPLUTO_HOT ...
  SELECT ..., ST_ASWKT(GEOM_GEOG) FROM EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.NYC_BUILDING_FOOTPRINTS_HOT ...

Then build the compatibility graph on real predicates — footprint within parcel, footprint
intersects parcel, overlap area ratio — and measure the component distribution again.

WHAT THE ANSWER DECIDES:
- If polygon containment DOES decompose the tile into small components, section 6's exact
  compilation strategy survives and the 0.5s budget can be re-estimated honestly.
- If it does NOT, exact compilation is affordable only in sparser geographies and dense
  urban tiles need a different strategy. That is a real possibility and it must be priced
  before any engineering commits.

STRATIFY, DO NOT REPEAT n=1. The falsification stands for dense urban only. Pull at least:
one Midtown/Upper East Side dense block, one outer-borough residential block, one Queens
grid block, one suburban agency-multifamily tile outside NYC once a second geography lands.
Report the component distribution per stratum. A strategy that works in Staten Island and
fails in Midtown is still worth knowing precisely.

ALSO MEASURE, since the geometry makes them free:
- The true centroid-to-boundary distance per parcel, to replace the equal-area disc LOWER
  BOUND used in Appendix B with the actual figure.
- The half-diagonal from LOTFRONT/LOTDEPTH where present, to validate the
  normalise-by-extent filter this bead's sibling requires.
- The null and stale rate of MAPPLUTO_BBL across the footprint rows. A stale bridge is worse
  than an absent one — components look clean and are wrong — and on a tile whose answer is
  an assemblage lot, merger-induced staleness is exactly the failure mode in play.
- How many footprints whose centroid falls outside a 150m parcel window belong to parcels
  inside it, which bounds the edge effect instead of merely flagging it.

DO NOT DRAW THE WINDOW AROUND THE ANSWER. Every statistic measured so far is conditioned on
a 150m window centred on the rooftop geocode of the CORRECT building. Production tiles are
centred on bad geocodes. Select tiles by H3 cell, not by proximity to a known answer.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- Component-size distribution under real polygon predicates, per stratum, published
- A written verdict on whether exact compilation survives, and where
- Actual centroid-to-boundary distances replacing the equal-area bound
- MAPPLUTO_BBL null/stale rate quantified
- Edge effect bounded with a count

title: [CANON-V1/P03.5] Bind strategy audit, promotion, selection, and use with receipts
description:
## Background
A strategy registry should answer not only which champion is selected, but exactly why that executable was eligible, what corpus and runner policy audited it, and which projects consumed it.

## Technical Approach
Unify register, audit, compare, promote, deprecate, select, explain, and diff around hash-linked v1 receipts. Promotion binds package digest, typed selection key, fixture corpus, audit results, thresholds, runner policy, and registry parent digest. Project locks select champions by digest and record the selection proof. Require explicit mutation and optimistic concurrency.

## Success Criteria
- A selected champion always has a verifiable audit and promotion chain.
- Stale audits, changed thresholds, altered runners, deprecated packages, and registry races refuse promotion or use.
- Explain identifies champion, alternatives, compatibility level, evidence, and exact project impact.
- Read-only selection never mutates registry state or audit caches inside it.

## Test Plan
Exercise full lifecycle, stale/tampered receipts, concurrent promotions, rollback-by-new-version, deprecated champion, project pin, and offline selection. Verify all receipts and exact registry ancestry.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/strategy/registry.rs`
- `src/strategy/promotion.rs`
- `src/strategy/explain.rs`
- `tests/strategy_lifecycle.rs`

## Considerations
Deprecation and rollback create new immutable registry versions; they do not rewrite historical evidence.

title: [CANON-V1/P06] Domain-neutral extension contracts and out-of-tree deployment proof
description:
## Background
Canon should be useful in demanding industries without knowing any industry's ontology. The initiating deployment needs large-scale counterparty resolution, but that knowledge belongs to the operator's out-of-tree project—not to the open-source engine.

## Scope
Create generic, content-addressed extension contracts for identity classes, role/relationship vocabularies, identifier namespaces and validators, profiles, normalization bundles, evidence policies, provider materializers, source mappings, review semantics, corpus manifests, registry compilation, and export projections. Prove the boundary with neutral public fixtures plus a private or external conformance deployment.

## Success Criteria
A previously unknown domain can define all semantics and data outside Canon, run clustering and cross-dataset linkage through the same engine, compile exact registries, review related/distinct cases, and produce dbt/search outputs without adding a Rust branch, enum variant, built-in identifier, or product-specific default.

## Test Plan
Schema and package conformance, unknown-extension round trips, malicious package/path fixtures, source scans for domain vocabulary in core modules, a neutral reference extension, and an out-of-tree deployment acceptance run whose private assets are not required to build or test Canon.

title: [SPLINK-STEAL/S10] audit/review ranking: cluster shape metrics (density, bridges, diameter)
description:
## Problem this solves
After solve, bad merges hide in low-density clusters held together by single bridge edges (A-B strong, B-C strong, A-C absent -> chain risk). Reviewing clusters in arbitrary order wastes attention on dense obvious cliques. Deterministic cluster-shape metrics rank clusters by structural suspicion so audit/review attention lands on likely false merges first — and give bd-fung inbox ranking one more deterministic signal. This is the deterministic sibling of deferred bd-tv1m (active-learning prioritization): same goal, zero learning.

## Build
Post-solve per-cluster metrics derived purely from existing solve/evidence artifacts:
- size; edge density (scored evidence edges / possible pairs); bridge edges (edges whose removal disconnects the cluster); diameter; minimum internal edge score.
- Expose in run/link artifact summaries and as a review-export sort option (--order-by suspicion: low-density-first, mirroring Splink Cluster Studio lowest_density_clusters_by_size sampling).
- Document each metric definition and the exact tie-break order in the artifact schema.

## Splink reference (clone at /Users/zac/Source/opensource/splink)
- splink/internals/graph_metrics.py — node/edge/cluster metric frames (density, centralisation)
- splink/internals/edge_metrics.py — is_bridge computation (:28-75)
- splink/internals/cluster_studio.py — lowest_density_clusters_by_size sampler (:246): the review-prioritization use of these metrics

## How to test
- Barbell fixture (two dense subclusters joined by one bridge edge): ranks first, bridge edge flagged, diameter correct.
- Dense clique fixture ranks last.
- Metric correctness against hand-computed values on a small fixture graph.
- Deterministic ordering with documented tie-breaks, stable under input row shuffle.
- Presentation-only guard: solver outputs byte-identical with and without metrics enabled.

## Doctrine constraints
Pure derivation from existing artifacts; deterministic; ranking/presentation only — no solver behavior change, no decision authority.

## RESERVATIONS
- src/entity/graph.rs
- src/entity/audit.rs (metrics surfacing in audit summaries)
- tests/entity_cluster_metrics.rs

title: canon geo: BYOP integration harness — synthetic client layer with deliberate degradations, scored against PLUTO
description:
THE PROVING GROUND TESTS A DIFFERENT CONFIGURATION THAN THE PRODUCT. FOUND BY REALITY
CHECK 2026-08-14.

bd-bmee scores the cascade on NYC CMBS collateral with US SUPPLYING MapPLUTO. That is the
right cascade proof — NYC is the adversarial geography, PLUTO is free ground truth, and
anyone can spot-check a BBL on ZoLa. It is NOT the shipping configuration.

THE SHIPPING CONFIGURATION (operator decision 2026-08-14, bd-2kjx) is bring-your-own-parcel:
the CLIENT supplies licensed parcel geometry that may be partial, in an unknown CRS, from a
vendor with unknown semantics, under a license that forbids it coming back to us. NONE OF
THAT IS EXERCISED BY bd-bmee. If the first real client run is also the first BYOP run, the
failures will be discovered in front of a paying customer.

TASK: an integration harness that exercises the BYOP path end to end, using a SYNTHETIC
CLIENT LAYER DERIVED FROM MapPLUTO so ground truth is preserved and results stay scoreable.

DERIVE THE SYNTHETIC LAYER BY DEGRADING MapPLUTO DELIBERATELY, one property at a time, so
each failure mode is attributable:
1. COVERAGE HOLES. Remove whole counties and whole H3 tiles. Assert that removed regions
   produce SourceCoverageGap abstentions and NOT no-match abstentions, and that the
   four-number report (coverage / precision-within-coverage / abstention / multi-candidate)
   attributes them correctly.
2. PARTIAL TILES. Cut the coverage boundary THROUGH tiles. Exercises the partial-coverage
   semantics decision.
3. A DIFFERENT CRS. Re-project a copy to EPSG:2263 and supply it without a declared CRS —
   assert REFUSAL, not a guess. Then supply it WITH a declared CRS and assert the results
   match the WGS84 run within the tolerance the predicate-regime bead establishes.
4. VENDOR SIMPLIFICATION. Generalize the polygons at ~2 m, mirroring the real defect
   recorded on bd-1uld where simplified shapes no longer supported the containment result
   full-precision ST_CONTAINS returns. Assert the simplification flag is required and that
   simplified geometry is REFUSED as decision geometry without explicit acknowledgement.
5. VENDOR IDENTIFIERS INSTEAD OF AUTHORITY IDENTIFIERS. Replace BBL with a synthetic
   attom:parcel:* style id. Assert role-and-issuer namespacing holds and that the vendor id
   is NOT silently treated as an APN.
6. MUTUAL-EXCLUSIVITY MISDECLARATION. Supply the NYC condo-overlap population while
   DECLARING the layer mutually exclusive. Assert canon surfaces the contradiction rather
   than suppressing the true part_of relations — this is the failure mode bd-gs6n's
   2026-08-14 comment warns about, and a client WILL misdeclare this.
7. LICENSE POSTURE. Mark the synthetic layer redact-always. Assert that the default output
   is redacted, that `canon geo redact` produces a digest-linked shareable projection, and
   that the redacted artifact cannot reconstruct the client geometry.
8. VINTAGE MISMATCH. Supply a layer whose vintage predates the as-of of the book. Assert
   refusal rather than silent extrapolation.

SCORING: because the synthetic layer is derived from MapPLUTO, PLUTO ground truth still
applies wherever coverage exists. So this harness produces a REAL precision number for the
BYOP path, comparable to bd-bmee's, with the delta attributable to the specific degradation
applied. That comparability is the point.

RELATIONSHIP TO bd-bmee: bd-bmee owns the cascade proof and the kill criterion. This bead
owns the shipping-path proof. Neither substitutes for the other, and this one must not be
used to claim the kill criterion has been met.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- Synthetic client layer generator with each degradation independently toggleable
- All eight scenarios asserted, each failing loudly today and passing after its owning bead
  lands
- A BYOP precision number scored against PLUTO, with the delta from bd-bmee attributed
- Runs in CI on a small fixture tile set; full-borough runs on demand

title: [BDC/P0 BLOCKER] Project directional link abstentions into native review export
description:
## Goal
Make ambiguous and unmatched directional entity-link decisions first-class, deterministic review-export inputs without forcing them into generic cluster-solve semantics or adding BDC behavior to Canon core.

## Root cause
canon entity link currently computes resolve::produce_entity_link_decisions for directional matches and separately runs the native entity workbench for run/solve artifacts. The link JSON preserves matches, unmatched, and ambiguous decisions, but the advertised review command points at solve/solve.json. Native review export builds only from solve diagnostics, so include escrow can exit 0 with zero items while the directional link decision artifact contains an ambiguity. This violates the documented rule that ambiguous cases enter escrow or review and the promise that link mode participates in the same artifact-backed workbench.

## Required behavior
- Persist or accept a hash-bound canon_entity_link.v0 result containing the directional decision projection.
- Teach canon entity review export to project directional ambiguous and unmatched decisions into deterministic escrow review items with stable review IDs, generic reason codes, candidate references, source row IDs, and provenance digests/counts.
- include resolved or all may expose matched links as audit-only review items; include escrow must expose the directional abstentions.
- Preserve existing native solve/run review export, v1 routing, legacy fallback, exact link decisions, and no-write-on-refusal behavior.
- Do not add BDC-specific branches, schemas, vocabulary, issuer/tranche/FIGI behavior, or DERA dependencies.

## Acceptance
1. A neutral public fixture produces at least one matched, one ambiguous, and one unmatched target.
2. The exact advertised review-export handoff executes with exit 0. include escrow JSON and CSV contain exactly the ambiguous/unmatched directional items, stable review IDs, deterministic reasons, and JSON/CSV ID parity.
3. include all contains resolved audit items plus escrow items; include resolved does not collapse or hide the escrow partition.
4. The result is hash-bound to the directional link decision source and refuses stale/tampered inputs atomically.
5. Existing solve/run review exports and generic quality gate remain green.

## RESERVATIONS
- src/lib.rs
- src/entity/link.rs
- src/entity/review.rs
- tests/entity_link.rs
- tests/cli_smoke.rs

## Evidence
PurpleDune Agent Mail 6878 provides the read-only source diagnosis. Public-safe runtime facts: link decisions report 3 matched, 1 ambiguous, 1 unmatched; exact advertised include escrow review export exits 0 with 0 items; include all emits only 2 resolved_existing audit items.
close_reason: Completed generic directional-link review handoff. title: strategy lifecycle: update, deprecate/remove-from-active-resolution, and promote
description: Add lifecycle operations for registered strategy champions. bd-a43 requires register, update, deprecate-remove, and promote. The implementation must not physically delete entries. Remove means remove from active resolution by marking status deprecated while preserving registry history. RESERVATIONS: src/cli.rs, src/lib.rs, src/strategy_registry.rs.
design: Behavior: update locates one active entry by typed key and skill, replaces script metadata and provenance/proofs as appropriate, requires next-version, keeps key identity stable, and emits before/after receipt state. Deprecate locates one active entry, sets status deprecated, records operator/reason/timestamp, requires next-version, emits receipt state, and makes resolve ignore it without deleting the entry. Promote locates an operator-attested entry, validates verify/assess/airlock using existing proof logic, attaches proof references, changes grade to proof-attested, requires next-version, and emits receipt state. All lifecycle operations refuse ambiguous duplicate active keys; prefer in-place registry mutation over append-only duplicate entries unless the spec deliberately says otherwise.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: updating an operator-attested task champion changes script hash and registry version and resolve sees the update; deprecating makes resolve return UNRESOLVED exit 1 without deleting the entry; promoting records proof references and grade proof-attested and lint accepts it; every successful mutation emits before/after registry hashes and source file/entry order in the receipt; invalid lifecycle operations refuse for missing key, not found, deprecated key update without policy, stale next-version, malformed proof, missing operator/reason for deprecate, and ambiguous duplicate active keys; schema-keyed entries follow the documented lifecycle policy.
notes: Prefer command name deprecate over remove; docs can say deprecate is the safe remove-from-active-resolution operation.
close_reason: Implemented strategy v1 typed keys, operator/proof attestation grades, lifecycle, catalog/explain, receipts/witness, lint/diff/docs/tests; verified cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test, cargo build --release --locked, and UBS on changed files.

description:
Resolve currently matches on the bare 'input' string. identity_scope::qualify_exact_lookup(query, candidate) already implements the correct comparison: identifier_value AND canonical_type AND namespace AND scope must agree, returning an ExactLookupQualification.

description:
Once a registry declares scope dimensions, a bare 'canon --column x file.csv' lookup must NOT silently match an entry from an arbitrary scope - that is the 26-deal false merge in slow motion.

BOUNDED: when the registry declares scope dimensions and the query carries none, return outcome REFUSAL with a new typed code and a next_command naming the scope flag. Follows the existing refusal envelope (see E_BAD_REGISTRY, E_CSV_PARSE).

title: Add --scope to registry mint / add-entry / resolve
description:
CLI surface for the scope dimension. mint and add-entry must be able to write a scoped alias; the resolve path must be able to supply the query scope.

BOUNDED: repeatable --scope DIMENSION=VALUE on 'canon registry mint', 'canon registry add-entry', and the top-level resolve invocation, mapping to ScopeDimensionBinding.

WORKED EXAMPLE (the case that motivated this):
  canon registry mint --registry r --canonical-type cmbs_property --prefix PROP \
    --scope deal=CIK1690255 --with-alias 'properties.json=41-001:absee_property_alias'
resolves 41-001 only within CGCMT 2016-P6, leaving the other 25 deals that use the same asset number untouched.

title: Wire authorize_cross_scope_alias for deal-scoped alias to global property promotion
description:
identity_scope::authorize_cross_scope_alias(left, right, policy, evidence_ref) exists and is unused. It is the gate for the genuinely valuable cross-deal question: the same physical building securing loans in two different CMBS deals.

The asymmetry to preserve: the ALIAS is deal-scoped ('41-001' means nothing outside its deal); the PROPERTY is global (a self-storage facility in Bentonville AR is one building regardless of which deal financed it). Promoting a deal-scoped alias to a global property identity is a cross-scope operation and must carry evidence, not be inferred from string equality.

BOUNDED: call authorize_cross_scope_alias on that promotion path with an explicit CrossScopeAliasPolicy and a required evidence_ref. Refuse rather than merge when evidence is absent.

title: [CANON-V1/P00.7] Ship entity apply as exact, row-preserving replay
description:
## Background
Exact replay is the architectural payoff: uncertain workbench evidence becomes a versioned registry, then every production row resolves through deterministic lookup. Apply exists as native code and in runbooks but is not a complete public command.

## Technical Approach
- Implement CSV and JSONL apply requests against a verified registry snapshot and optional project/run artifact.
- Append canonical ID, status, registry ID/version/hash, rule/provenance, and profile-scoped fields while preserving raw values and ordering.
- Support full-resolution gating and an explicit partial-output policy with unambiguous exit semantics.
- Write output atomically or stream safely according to format; refuse existing output columns unless explicitly named.

## Success Criteria
- The advertised canon entity apply command exists and is shell-composable.
- Promoted aliases replay exactly over original rows.
- Raw parser/source evidence remains byte- or value-preserved according to the format contract.
- Unresolved/full-resolution failures create no misleading final output.

## Test Plan
- CSV byte-preservation and JSONL append-only tests.
- Partial/full resolution exit-code matrix.
- Stale registry and profile mismatch refusals.
- Large streaming replay, batch equivalence, and end-to-end promotion/apply tests.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/entity/apply.rs`
- `src/entity/stream.rs`
- `src/output/csv.rs`
- `tests/entity/apply_cli.rs`

## Considerations
- Core canon --emit csv remains unchanged.
- Never perform fuzzy matching during apply.
- Document output atomicity for stdout versus file destinations.

title: [CANON-V1/P08.7] Support offline mirrors, export bundles, and verified restoration
description:
## Background
Long-lived identity knowledge must survive registry outages, laptop loss, retention changes, and air-gapped operation. A cache is not a backup if dependencies and ancestry are missing.

## Technical Approach
Implement dependency-closure export of selected package roots into a deterministic OCI layout/bundle with inventory and optional trust roots. Add mirror verify, import into external cache, and restore-to-local-package operations. Detect missing ancestors/blobs/attestations and support incremental bundles by digest set without rewriting history.

## Success Criteria
- A bundle contains the complete declared dependency and ancestry closure or refuses creation.
- Restore recreates byte-identical package digests and verification results.
- Incremental mirrors never require mutable state to understand included content.
- Read/verify/import do not overwrite unrelated cache entries.

## Test Plan
Create full/incremental bundles, remove random blobs/parents, reorder storage, corrupt inventory, restore offline, compare digests, and test existing-cache collisions and read-only verification.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/distribution/mirror.rs`
- `tests/package_mirror.rs`

## Considerations
Deletion and retention policy are deliberately outside this bead and require explicit authorization under repository rules.

title: canon geo: identifier scheme for the geo mart — minted cluster IDs per entity type, aliases as members
description:
DESIGN DECISION. Operator question 2026-08-13: 'what are we gonna do for keys in our geomart? Membership paradigm, more columns on a crosswalk, or mint our own identifier? Assuming canon resolves a couple of our properties to the same, what's our ID scheme?'

RECOMMENDATION: membership AND minting -- they are not alternatives. Reject the wide crosswalk as authoritative.

== THERE IS NOT ONE ENTITY HERE. THERE ARE THREE, AND THEY NEST ==
  PARCEL    legal/tax unit        -- BBL, APN
  BUILDING  physical structure    -- BIN, Overture building GERS, FEMA UUID
  PROPERTY  underwriting unit     -- what a loan is secured by; may span parcels
                                     AND buildings, or be a fraction of one (condo)
The ID question is therefore first a question of WHICH ENTITY you are keying.
Answer: mint separately per type. cmdrvl:parcel:*, cmdrvl:building:*.

RECOMMEND DEFERRING cmdrvl:property:* IN v1. Parcel and building are objectively
defined by external authorities (BBL, BIN) and independently verifiable. 'Property'
is an underwriting construct whose boundaries vary by deal -- the loan document
defines its own collateral. Treat property as a COLLECTION defined by the source
document, not a resolved entity, until there is evidence we can adjudicate its
boundaries. Do not invent an entity we cannot verify.

== WHY THE WIDE CROSSWALK IS WRONG AS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH ==
1. CARDINALITY. One parcel -> many buildings; one building -> many POIs; one
   building can span parcels. A wide row forces either fan-out (duplicated rows,
   broken joins, double-counted exposure) or collapse (relationship destroyed).
   Both are wrong answers, not tradeoffs.
2. SCHEMA COUPLING. A column per source bakes the source list into the schema.
   Adding Overture addresses or a new vendor becomes a migration.
3. NO PER-LINK CONFIDENCE. A crosswalk row implies uniform certainty. In reality
   the BBL link may be 0.98 and the fsq_place_id link 0.61. One row cannot carry
   both, and collapsing them loses the abstention signal that makes this
   trustworthy.
4. NO TEMPORAL DIMENSION. BBLs change on lot merger and apportionment; buildings
   are demolished. A column holds one value; OC-0046 requires as-of.

The crosswalk is still USEFUL -- materialize it as a DERIVED CONVENIENCE VIEW off
the registry, regenerable, never authoritative. Ergonomics without the pathology.

== THE SCHEME ==
CLUSTER IS THE IDENTITY, matching the settled identity doctrine (clusters are the
unit of identity; source IDs are participants bound by evidence, not primary keys).

  minted id   cmdrvl:building:01J7X...   opaque, stable
  aliases     parcel:nyc:bbl:1009950001
              building:nyc:bin:1234567
              building:overture:gers:08b2a...
              building:fema:uuid:...
              cmbs:annexa:<deal>:<property_id>
              hud:project:<hud_project_number>
  relations   building X part_of parcel Y   (typed edge, NOT a column)

WORKED ANSWER TO THE OPERATOR'S QUESTION -- Annex A property P1 and HUD project H1
resolve to the same building:
  - building cluster cmdrvl:building:01J7X... exists or is minted at promotion
  - cmbs:annexa:...:P1 and hud:project:H1 are added as ALIASES with evidence
  - registry gains two exact-lookup rows, both -> the same canonical id
  - the BBL rides the part_of relation to the parcel cluster, not a column
  - NEITHER P1 NOR H1 BECOMES THE KEY. Both are participants.

== ID DESIGN RULES ==
1. OPAQUE, NOT SEMANTIC. Do not encode BBL, geography or type-hierarchy meaning
   into the identifier. Semantic IDs become WRONG when the meaning changes (lot
   merger). ULID / UUIDv7 shape -- sortable, opaque.
2. ROLE-NAMESPACED ALIASES, consistent with the settled crm:primary:* rather than
   crm:hubspot:* decision. The namespace states the ROLE the identifier plays,
   not merely who issued it.
3. MINTING IS A PROMOTION EVENT, NOT A RESOLUTION SIDE EFFECT. canon doctrine:
   workbench proposes, review promotes. An id is minted when a cluster is
   ACCEPTED. Minting on every solver run mints garbage.
4. SPLITS AND MERGES ARE FIRST-CLASS AND ARE WHERE THIS BITES LATER.
   MERGE: retain both prior ids as aliases pointing at the survivor. NEVER reuse
   an id, NEVER silently reassign.
   SPLIT: harder. The prior id must be deliberately retired or assigned to one
   side, with a tombstone so downstream references fail loudly rather than
   resolving to the wrong thing. entity/patches.rs and anti_merge.rs exist for
   exactly this class of correction -- reuse them.
5. BITEMPORAL. As-of resolution, consistent with OC-0046's no-lookahead
   requirement. 'Which cluster did this alias belong to in 2019' must be
   answerable.

== RUNTIME SHAPE ==
This preserves canon's core promise unchanged: the REGISTRY is flat and exact
(alias -> canonical id, versioned, replayable), and the cluster/relation graph is
WORKBENCH output carrying the why, the confidence and the as-of. Queries hit the
registry. Nothing probabilistic reaches runtime lookup.

REALITY CHECK 2026-08-14 — TWO CORRECTIONS: A SPEC CONFLICT WITH OC-0048, AND A MISSING
TWO-REGISTRY MODEL.

1. DIRECT CONTRADICTION WITH OC-0048 ON THE PROPERTY ENTITY — MUST BE RESOLVED BEFORE
   bd-3ccc.
   This bead says: "RECOMMEND DEFERRING cmdrvl:property:* IN v1 ... Treat property as a
   COLLECTION defined by the source document, not a resolved entity ... Do not invent an
   entity we cannot verify."
   OC-0048 (Keying section, table 'Mint in v1?') says: "Property | the loan document |
   no external authority | **Yes** — cmdrvl:property:*", and states explicitly:
   "Property is nevertheless first-class, by operator decision 2026-08-14. An earlier
   draft deferred it on the grounds that we cannot adjudicate its boundaries. That
   reasoning was sound about VERIFICATION and wrong about SCOPE: the CMBS tape IS a list
   of properties, every corpus this outcome keys is a property list, and the buyer's file
   is a property list."
   OC-0048 IS THE LATER DECISION AND IT SUPERSEDES THIS BEAD'S RECOMMENDATION. This bead
   must be updated to mint property in v1. The reconciliation is not cosmetic: it changes
   the skeleton's entity-type set (bd-3ccc), the blocking strategy (property is not
   spatially local the way parcel and building are — a property can span tiles), and the
   abstention semantics (OC-0048: property is "the one entity type where abstention is
   about MEMBERSHIP rather than location").
   A dedicated bead has been cut for property-entity resolution because it is genuinely
   different work, not a third instance of the same pattern.

2. THE MODEL ASSUMES ONE REGISTRY. BYOP HAS TWO. (operator decision 2026-08-14, bd-2kjx)
   This bead's scheme — minted cluster ID, aliases as members, relations as typed edges —
   is correct and should not change. What is missing is that under bring-your-own-parcel
   there are TWO registries in play:
     OURS    ships inside the tile. Contains minted cmdrvl:building:* clusters for our
             footprint sources, pre-promoted by us before the client ever runs.
     THEIRS  lives on the client's machine. Contains their parcel aliases (from their
             licensed layer), their property book aliases, and their own minted IDs.
   OC-0048 is explicit that "the client mints their own IDs in their own registry. We
   supply evidence; we never impose an identifier." That is coherent, but this bead does
   not model how the two compose. Required additions:
     - How a client cluster references a tile-shipped building cluster (alias? typed
       relation? foreign-registry reference?) without our ID becoming their primary key.
     - Whether tile-shipped clusters are IMMUTABLE from the client's perspective, and
       what happens when the client disagrees with one of our building clusters.

3. TILE-REFRESH ID STABILITY IS AN UNSTATED HARD REQUIREMENT.
   This bead's rule 3 says "MINTING IS A PROMOTION EVENT, NOT A RESOLUTION SIDE EFFECT."
   Correct. But tile-shipped cmdrvl:building:* IDs are minted at OUR promotion, at tile
   build time, before any client run. IF A TILE REFRESH REASSIGNS THEM, EVERY CLIENT
   REGISTRY BREAKS SILENTLY — their aliases now point at a different building.
   Rules 4 (splits/merges: never reuse, never silently reassign) and 5 (bitemporal) are
   exactly the right machinery, but they were written for a single local registry. They
   must be RESTATED AS A PUBLISHED CONTRACT ON THE TILE: a refreshed tile may add
   clusters, may retire clusters with a tombstone, and MAY NEVER reassign an existing
   minted ID to different geometry. That contract needs a conformance test that diffs
   consecutive tile vintages and fails on reassignment — the same shape as the MapPLUTO
   version-archive diff (cmdrvl-curves bd-33t6) that produces the BBL change ledger.

4. THE SIX-FIELD CLIENT INPUT CONTRACT IS THE ALIAS SOURCE (operator decision
   2026-08-14): geocode, address, geometry, building size, year built, property type.
   The client's own row identifiers become aliases under a role-namespace consistent with
   rule 2. Note that under BYOP their parcel identifiers may be VENDOR identifiers
   (attom:parcel:*, regrid:ll_uuid:*) rather than authority identifiers (bbl, apn) — the
   namespace must state the ROLE and the ISSUER distinctly, because a vendor's parcel ID
   is not the county's APN and conflating them will produce wrong joins across vendors.

RETAINED UNCHANGED AND STILL CORRECT: opaque not semantic IDs (ULID/UUIDv7); cluster is
the identity and source IDs are participants; wide crosswalk rejected as authoritative
but materialized as a derived convenience view; splits/merges first-class with
tombstones; bitemporal as-of. The registry stays flat and exact; the cluster/relation
graph is workbench output. None of that changes under BYOP.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
OPERATOR INSIGHT 2026-08-14 — PROPERTY IS CONSTITUTED, NOT RESOLVED. THIS SETTLES THE
WOBBLE AND CHANGES THE ID CONSTRUCTION.

THE OBSERVATION: "property" is singular and plural at once — a property is one asset, my
property is a holding. The domain word carries both because THE THING IS A SET.

WHAT FOLLOWS, AND IT RESOLVES WHAT bd-67wx AND OC-0048 KEPT DISAGREEING ABOUT:

PARCEL and BUILDING are RESOLVED ENTITIES. They have external authorities (BBL, BIN,
Overture GERS, FEMA UUID), so "is this the same one as that one?" is a real question with
a checkable answer. canon geo resolves them, and that is where all the uncertainty lives.

PROPERTY HAS NO AUTHORITY. The document names it. So THERE IS NO IDENTITY QUESTION TO
ADJUDICATE at the property layer — only MEMBERSHIP. OC-0048 already says property
abstention is about membership rather than location; this explains why, and the why is
what makes it designable.

bd-67wx's original instinct ("do not invent an entity we cannot verify") and OC-0048's
correction ("property is first-class; the CMBS tape IS a list of properties") are BOTH
RIGHT and were only in tension because both treated property as a third instance of the
same pattern. It is not the same pattern:

  cmdrvl:parcel:*    a CLUSTER of aliases     identity IS the cluster; source IDs are
  cmdrvl:building:*                            participants bound by evidence
  cmdrvl:property:*  a SET of clusters         members are already-minted cluster IDs;
                                               constituted by a document, not resolved

First-class does NOT mean resolved-independently. Property gets minted and it is the unit
the client cares about, AND it is derived from members that were resolved beneath it.

== THE RESULT THAT FALLS OUT: PROPERTY IDENTITY REDUCES TO SET EQUALITY ==

If the property IS the set, then two documents describe the same property IF AND ONLY IF
their member sets are equal, over stable minted IDs. That is EXACT.

  same property            member sets equal
  refi that added a lot    superset — exactly computable
  two deals overlapping    exact intersection, no adjudication
  collateral released      subset

THERE IS NO PROBABILISTIC MATCHING AT THE PROPERTY LAYER AT ALL. All uncertainty is spent
below, resolving parcels and buildings. Above that line it is set algebra over stable IDs.
canon's runtime promise survives completely intact, because nothing at the property layer
needs to guess.

This also makes bd-1oid's "second assertion, not an overwrite" posture TRIVIAL rather than
hard: you do not reconcile conflicting documents, you mint two sets and let set algebra
describe their relationship. Conflict detection becomes a set operation, not a decision.

MINTING RULE THAT FOLLOWS: mint one cmdrvl:property:* PER DOCUMENT ASSERTION. A 2015 deal
and a 2022 refi describing the same collateral get two IDs, which is CORRECT — they are
two collateral packages. If their member sets happen to be equal, that is DISCOVERABLE
EXACTLY at query time and needs no resolution step. Do not attempt to adjudicate "same
property across documents"; that would reintroduce the identity question this construction
just eliminated.

== IT GENERALIZES UPWARD ==
A portfolio is a set of properties — same construction one level up, same `contains`
relation (bd-3soj), no new entity type. That the construction generalizes without
special-casing is evidence it is the right one.

== WHAT IT ADDS: TWO DIFFERENT TEMPORAL SHAPES ==
A parcel cluster's IDENTITY is stable and its ALIASES accrete over time. A property's
MEMBERSHIP changes — collateral released, adjacent lot acquired, parcel split. Those
version differently and bd-12gh must model BOTH shapes, not one. "Which cluster did this
alias belong to in 2019" and "what were this property's members in 2019" are different
queries against different mechanisms.

== CONSEQUENCE FOR THE OUTPUT SURFACE (bd-kwmc) ==
The genuinely valuable queries are set operations over minted IDs, and they are exact:
does deal A's collateral intersect deal B's; is this HUD project a subset of this CMBS
property; what is the union of parcels a sponsor touches. That is the whole cross-corpus
join OC-0048 promises, and it is arithmetic rather than inference.

comments.text:
VERIFIED FACTS FROM STRUCTURED TOOL OUTPUT 2026-08-14. Method: `cmdrvl --json orchestrator
query --tenant salt --raw`, reading `.data.response.tool_responses[].structuredContent`
rather than Loom's prose answer. The underlying tool is `data__edgar_data_run_query`, which
returns the literal SQL it ran plus `{ok, columns, rows}` or `{ok:false, error}`. Every
fact below is a literal returned value.

THIS METHOD CHANGE IS THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST. Three claims earlier in this session
came from Loom's prose and were wrong. The structured path caught the third one
immediately, and the skill documentation already prescribed it ("prefer
tool_responses[*].structuredContent from --raw over prose"). ALL CORPUS EXTRACTS MUST USE
THE STRUCTURED PATH AND RECORD THE EMITTED SQL.

=========================================================================
1. THE LANDED MapPLUTO TABLE PROJECTS A SUBSET OF FIELDS. `UNITSTOTAL` DOES NOT EXIST.
=========================================================================
A prior extract reported "UNITSTOTAL 178" for BBL 1014477501. The structured output shows
that query FAILED: `invalid identifier 'UNITSTOTAL'`. The value was fabricated in prose.

LITERAL COLUMN LIST of EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.NYC_DCP_MAPPLUTO_HOT:
  RELEASE, RELEASE_DT, VARIANT, SOURCE_ROW_NUMBER, VALID_FROM_RELEASE_DT,
  VALID_TO_RELEASE_DT, IS_CURRENT_RELEASE, COUNTRY, STATE, BOROUGH_PARTITION, OBJECTID,
  BOROUGH, BLOCK, LOT, BBL, ADDRESS, BLDGCLASS, LANDUSE, YEARBUILT, LOTAREA, BLDGAREA,
  NUMBLDGS, NUMFLOORS, OWNERNAME, PLUTOMAPID, GEOM_GEOG, CENTROID_GEOG, CENTROID_LON,
  CENTROID_LAT, BBOX_XMIN, BBOX_YMIN, BBOX_XMAX, BBOX_YMAX, H3_R7, H3_R8, GEOM_CRS,
  SOURCE_GEOM_CRS, SOURCE_CHANNEL, SOURCE_FILENAME, ROW_PAYLOAD, LOADED_AT

CONSEQUENCES:
- MapPLUTO publishes roughly ninety fields; the landed table projects about twenty and puts
  the remainder in ROW_PAYLOAD. Anything not projected requires digging into ROW_PAYLOAD,
  which is a different access pattern and a different cost.
- THE SIX-FIELD CLIENT CONTRACT IS SATISFIED BY PROJECTED COLUMNS, which is good news:
  building size -> BLDGAREA, year built -> YEARBUILT, property type -> BLDGCLASS + LANDUSE.
  No ROW_PAYLOAD dig needed for the core cascade.
- UNIT COUNTS (UnitsTotal, UnitsRes) ARE NOT PROJECTED. Assemblage subset-sum for
  multifamily (case 7) may want them. Confirm they exist in ROW_PAYLOAD before designing
  around them.

=========================================================================
2. BBL IS STORED AS A STRING WITH A TRAILING ".0" AND IS NOT JOIN-READY.
=========================================================================
Literal returned value: "BBL": "1014477501.0"

This is a direct problem for canon. Core lookup is EXACT BYTE MATCH AFTER ASCII-TRIM, so
"1014477501" would NOT resolve against "1014477501.0". Any registry built from this column
without normalization silently fails to match the identifier every other NYC source uses,
and every downstream join against ACRIS, PLUTO, or the footprints file has the same
exposure.
REQUIRED: BBL normalization is a declared, versioned step in the ingest, not an incidental
cast. It belongs in the geo profile's normalization vocabulary alongside the geometry
canonicalization, and it needs a negative test.

=========================================================================
3. CASE 6 IS A CONDO, AND THE CONDO TRAP IS LIVE IN IT.
=========================================================================
Literal rows for BBL prefix 10144775:

  BBL 1014477501.0  "305 EAST 72 STREET"  BLDGCLASS RM  LOTAREA 37,800
                    BLDGAREA 194,949  NUMBLDGS 2  NUMFLOORS 17  YEARBUILT 1961
                    OWNERNAME "305/72 CONDOMINIUM"
  BBL 1014477502.0  "1355 1 AVENUE"       BLDGCLASS RM  LOTAREA  5,100
                    BLDGAREA 102,719  NUMBLDGS 1  NUMFLOORS 31  YEARBUILT 2009
                    OWNERNAME "UNAVAILABLE OWNER"

FOUR THINGS THIS ESTABLISHES:
a) OWNERNAME "305/72 CONDOMINIUM" and the 75xx lot range confirm these are CONDO BILLING
   BBLs. The condo trap named in OC-0048 and measured in the multi-lot fan-out is present
   in the very property picked to illustrate a different case.
b) A PRIOR CLAIM IS CORRECTED. I wrote that five asserted addresses "resolve to ONE BBL."
   Not established. At least two condo BBLs sit here with DIFFERENT street frontages —
   East 72 Street and 1 Avenue. The property's a/k/a set names E 72nd, 2nd Avenue and
   E 73rd; 1 Avenue is a fourth frontage not in that set. The containment test still has to
   be run properly.
c) YEARBUILT 1961 vs 2009 ON ADJACENT CONDO LOTS IS A LIVE REDEVELOPMENT SIGNAL — exactly
   the case hypothesised on bd-gs6n, that a large year-built spread on overlapping or
   adjacent footprints is a TEMPORAL finding rather than a match failure. It is real and it
   is in the first property examined closely.
d) NUMBLDGS 2 on one condo BBL. The building level is still needed and the BBL-to-BIN
   bridge (landed, bd-397d) is still the next pull.

=========================================================================
4. THE TABLE IS STRUCTURALLY BITEMPORAL ALREADY.
=========================================================================
RELEASE, RELEASE_DT, VALID_FROM_RELEASE_DT, VALID_TO_RELEASE_DT, IS_CURRENT_RELEASE are all
present. The landing contract (cmdrvl-curves bd-qbno) was built for multiple releases even
though OC-0048 records that only the current one is loaded.
CONSEQUENCE: the as-of machinery bd-12gh and bd-1oy8 need does not require a schema change,
only additional releases. Check `SELECT DISTINCT RELEASE, RELEASE_DT` before assuming case
9's temporal arc is blocked — cmdrvl-curves bd-33t6 may be closer to done than the outcome
document states.

=========================================================================
5. REPROJECTION PROVENANCE IS ALREADY RECORDED. THIS DIRECTLY SERVES bd-3nc7.
=========================================================================
GEOM_CRS and SOURCE_GEOM_CRS are projected columns. So the EPSG:2263 -> WGS84 transform
that the predicate-regime bead has to reason about is documented in the table itself rather
than needing archaeology. Read those columns first when starting bd-3nc7.

=========================================================================
6. H3_R7 AND H3_R8 ARE PRESENT. H3_R9 IS NOT.
=========================================================================
The epic's default tile is res-9. It is not precomputed. Canon computes it itself, which is
what bd-2b9d already requires for a separate reason — the Snowflake H3 helpers returned
malformed boundaries and a bad k-ring (edgar-elt br-2wir). Both reasons now point the same
way: compute r9 in canon with a vetted Rust H3 library, and treat the warehouse H3 columns
as a coarse prefilter at most.

=========================================================================
7. GEOCODIO SOURCE SEMANTICS — CONFIRMED BY OPERATOR.
=========================================================================
Geocodio reports the underlying address dataset that produced each match. So SOURCE values
like "TIGER/Line(R) dataset from the US Census Bureau" and "City of New York" are
per-result attribution from ONE service, not competing vendors — and MULTIPLE SOURCED
GEOCODES PER PROPERTY ARE EXPECTED AND NORMAL.
This VINDICATES the capability in bd-1a12 while keeping the retraction of the mechanism.
SOURCE becomes usable EVIDENCE: a local authoritative dataset and a national interpolated
one carry different reliability.
BUT NOTE THE COUNTEREXAMPLE ALREADY IN HAND: on "241/249 West 74th Street" the
"City of New York" sourced row is the WRONG one (W 49th St, rooftop, score 0.92) and the
TIGER/Line row is right (W 74th St, range_interpolation, score 1.00). So SOURCE is not a
safe selector either, any more than ACCURACY_TYPE or ACCURACY_SCORE are. Three fields, none
individually decisive, all disagreeing — which is precisely the argument for letting the
tile adjudicate.

title: canon geo: coverage-aware abstention — distinguish 'layer does not cover' from 'nothing matched'
description:
THE SHARPEST NEW REQUIREMENT BRING-YOUR-OWN-PARCEL CREATES. FOUND BY REALITY CHECK
2026-08-14.

THE FINDING: EntityMultisourceAbstentionReason (src/entity/multisource.rs:198) has
EXACTLY ONE VARIANT: AnchorConflict. Under BYOP (bd-2kjx) the client's licensed parcel
layer may be PARTIAL — clipped to a subscription footprint, county-limited, or simply
missing a tile. The cascade MUST distinguish:

  "THE CLIENT'S LAYER DOES NOT COVER THIS TILE"      (we cannot answer; not their fault,
                                                      not a resolution failure, and it is
                                                      FIXABLE by extending their license)
  "THE LAYER COVERS IT AND NO PARCEL CONTAINS THIS"  (a genuine finding about the world —
                                                      likely an interpolated geocode in
                                                      the right-of-way)
  "TWO PARCELS CONTAIN IT AND WE CANNOT CHOOSE"      (genuine ambiguity — the 237 Park
                                                      case, 157 such points in NYC CMBS)
  "CANDIDATES EXIST BUT THE CHANNELS DISAGREE"       (geometry says A, address says B —
                                                      abstain, and say why)

CONFLATING THE FIRST WITH THE OTHERS IS A SILENT-ERROR MODE and it is precisely the class
OC-0048 forbids ("Abstention is acceptable; silent error is not"). It is also
commercially material: "we could not key 30% of your book" reads as a product failure
when the actual cause is "your ATTOM subscription does not cover those counties," which
the client can fix in an afternoon.

TASK:
1. EXTEND THE ABSTENTION VOCABULARY. Add typed reasons covering at minimum:
   SourceCoverageGap, NoCandidateInCoverage, AmbiguousCandidates, ChannelDisagreement,
   InputChannelMissing (the six-field contract's absent-field case), GeometryRefused.
   Each carries the tile id, the source(s) implicated, and the evidence refs that led
   there. Version the artifact contract when the enum grows.
2. COVERAGE PREDICATE PER SOURCE PER TILE. Every source in a run declares, per tile,
   whether it covers that tile. For our tiles this is known by construction (the subset
   predicate, bd-1uld). For the client's layer it must be DERIVED AT INGEST — see the
   client-layer H3 ingest bead — and it must distinguish "covered and empty" from "not
   covered." A county with genuinely zero parcels in a water tile is COVERED AND EMPTY.
3. COVERAGE IS NOT BINARY AT TILE GRANULARITY. A tile may be PARTIALLY covered when the
   client's layer boundary cuts through it. Specify the semantics: RECOMMEND treating
   partial coverage as NOT COVERED for decision purposes (conservative — abstain rather
   than answer from a truncated layer) while REPORTING it distinctly, because a book
   concentrated on a coverage edge is a different conversation than one outside coverage
   entirely. Measure the partial-tile rate before fixing the rule.
4. REPORT COVERAGE AS A FIRST-CLASS RATE, ALONGSIDE PRECISION AND ABSTENTION. bd-bmee
   already elevates abstention rate and multi-lot rate to first-class metrics. Coverage
   rate joins them. The headline for a BYOP run is four numbers, not one:
     coverage rate | precision within coverage | abstention rate within coverage |
     multi-candidate rate
5. RENDER IT. bd-101v requirement 8: the card must show "the client's layer does not
   cover this tile" as a visually distinct state from "canon declined to decide." An
   empty layer and a tie look nothing alike and must not render alike.
6. REFUSE THE TEMPTING SHORTCUT. Do not fall back to OUR parcel data (e.g. MapPLUTO in
   NYC) when the client's layer is missing, unless the client EXPLICITLY declares a
   fallback source order. Silently substituting a different parcel authority produces
   answers keyed to a layer the client does not hold and cannot verify — and in a
   licensed context it may also be the wrong thing legally. If fallback is declared, the
   answering source MUST be recorded per decision.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- Typed abstention vocabulary implemented, versioned, and carried into the artifact
- Per-source per-tile coverage predicate, with covered-and-empty distinguished from
  not-covered
- Partial-tile semantics specified after measuring the partial-tile rate on a fixture
- Four-number reporting wired into the run summary
- Fixture with deliberate coverage holes proving each abstention reason fires correctly
- A negative test: a run with a coverage gap must NOT report those rows as unresolved-
  by-geometry, and must NOT silently fall back to another parcel source
close_reason: SUPERSEDED per PLAN_CANON_GEO.md section 11 + section 17 E5 doctrine (2026-08-16): abstention is the residual model set, reason codes become MUS/MCS output, and 'layer does not cover' vs 'nothing matched' is absorbed into the evidence-tier doctrine — resolver runs on any subset of section 16.3 inventory rows; coverage narrows, precision holds, abstention absorbs. The coverage-tier curve is E5's deliverable (new E5 bead). EmpiricalHighCoverage evidence is already structurally diagnostic-only in src/geo/evidence.rs. Force-closed over open deps: superseding doctrine + code landed.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
ARCHITECTURE SUPERSEDED 2026-08-15 — see docs/PLAN_CANON_GEO.md.

An adversarial multi-model design session produced a materially different architecture,
which then survived a red team that destroyed two intermediate designs. The tile is modelled
as a BOUNDED UNIVERSE and every piece of evidence is a CONSTRAINT; propagation runs to a
fixpoint; the residual model set IS the answer. There is no proposer channel.

THE THREE PROPERTIES THAT MATTER:
- CONFLUENCE. The fixpoint is independent of the order constraints are applied (Tarski 1955;
  Cousot & Cousot 1977; Apt 1999), so determinism is a theorem rather than an engineering
  effort.
- MONOTONICITY. Constraints only add and domains only shrink, so a tile resolved with four
  sources today and six next year yields a TIGHTER residual, never a contradicting one. The
  earlier answer was never wrong, only less resolved.
- STRUCTURAL ABSTENTION. The residual model set is the answer. No threshold anywhere.

THE KEY DESIGN RULE IS rho, THE SOUNDNESS DISCIPLINE. Every source attribute enters the
solver only through a declared versioned relaxation mapping it to the WEAKEST constraint the
source can actually support. An interpolated geocode becomes a 150m disc rather than a
location. A parcel ADDRESS becomes "one of this lot's addresses" rather than functional
equality. OWNERNAME equal PERMITS an assemblage; OWNERNAME different constrains NOTHING.
Every noisy channel is admitted only in its sound direction — which is what dissolved the
proposer dilemma that broke the two earlier designs.

AND THE COMMERCIAL CONSEQUENCE: if every rho is sound, the true assignment is in the model
set, so AN EMPTY MODEL SET IS A PROOF that a named source violated its own published error
model — attributable, falsifiable, and mailable to the vendor.

Read PLAN_CANON_GEO.md before starting any geo work. Section 11 carries the bead-by-bead
supersession table. Appendix A covers frozen-weight observers and imagery sources. APPENDIX
B RECORDS THE FIRST HARD MEASUREMENT, WHICH FALSIFIED A LOAD-BEARING CLAIM — read it before
trusting any performance number in the plan.

Raw session artifacts, including the red team and the adversarial reviews, are preserved
under docs/geo_design_session/ with a reading guide.
