title: canon geo D4: bounded abstain, re-geocode, retry loop as a pinned acquisition step
description:
PACKET PK-D4a (stage D4) from docs/PLAN_CANON_GEO.md §18/§19, course correction 2026-09-01. This bead carries the full design so no implementer needs the plan document.

== WHY ==
Appendix L.5 operator doctrine: abstention is a reacquisition trigger, not a terminal state. When the tile refutes its input ('this address is nowhere in here', the M.2 street-absence refuter now fires on a tiny high-signal population), re-geocode and retry in the right tile as a bounded deterministic outer loop, each pass pinned like any other run. L.6 measured the recovery ceiling from already-landed geocodes at 0/40: recovery requires a NEW geocode pass or entry through the address channel, so this is an acquisition step outside the deterministic build (PROVIDER_SDK.md). The loop emits GeoAcquisitionRequest values and never geocodes itself (I10, C17). G4 measures the recovery rate on the 40 gross-class E1 points with fresh geocodes. This bead absorbs the retained parts of bd-1a12 (geocode plausibility: the tile refuting its own input) which is closed as superseded.

== STAGE ROW (§19.5; entry condition, gate, contracts) ==
| D4 | Retry loop, condo bridge, `geo inspect` | G1 passed for `retry.rs` and `condo.rs`; G2 passed before `inspect.rs` starts (it reads `GeoExplanationArtifact`); a Demo 0 work directory reproduces from `scripts/geo_demo/demo0.sh`; the E1 gross-class and condo point lists committed as fixtures; modules `retry.rs`, `condo.rs`, `inspect.rs` | G4: recovery rate of the retry loop measured on the 40 gross-class points with fresh geocodes; condo flips independently confirmed on the 31 points; inspect answers the eight questions in architecture §1 from artifacts alone | C17, C18, C20, C22, C25; T10, T11, T12, T25, T27 | new bead, bd-2fed, bd-1g18 |

== MODULE SURFACE (§19.3; field lists are the required minimum, add #[serde(default)] fields only, never remove or rename) ==
**Dependency direction.** New modules depend on the existing `composition`, `evidence`,
`control`, `discovery`, `evaluation`, `geometry`, `geometry_value`, and `run` modules,
never the reverse. `src/geo/composition.rs` and `src/geo/evidence.rs` are not modified by
D2 to D6: `propagate` and `explain` call `solve_composition` as a black box and narrow or
re-solve `GeoCompositionRequest` values. Within the new set: `explain` consumes
`propagate`; `card`, `next_evidence`, and `inspect` consume `explain`; `exposure` and
`collision` consume `ledger`; `adjudicate` and `card` consume `observer`; nothing consumes
`inspect`.

**Shared shape.** Each module is `pub mod` in `src/geo/mod.rs` with `pub use module::*`.
Each defines `Geo<Module>Error { code: Geo<Module>ErrorCode, message: String, detail:
BTreeMap<String, String> }` with a `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` code enum that
carries the generic `UnsupportedVersion`, `InvalidInput`, `BudgetExceeded`,
`ArithmeticOverflow` variants plus the module's rows from §19.4. Each artifact type has a
`version: String` constant `CANON_GEO_<NAME>_VERSION`, `canonical_<name>_bytes`, and
`validate_<name>_artifact`. Each module ships `schemas/canon.geo.<name>.v0.schema.json`, a
`--describe` entry, a `canon geo <subcommand>`, and `tests/geo_<module>.rs`.

**`retry.rs`**

| Item | Definition |
|---|---|
| Consumes | `GeoRun` (`status`, `blockers`, `next_actions`, `semantic_hash`), `GeoAcquisitionRequest`, `GeoAcquisitionReceipt` |
| `GeoRetryPolicy` | `max_passes: u8`, `regeocode_request_template: GeoAcquisitionRequest` |
| `GeoRetryPass` | `index: u8`, `plan_blake3`, `run_blake3`, `abstention_reason: String`, `regeocode: Option<GeoAcquisitionRequest>`, `receipt_blake3: Option<String>` |
| `GeoRetryTerminal` | `Resolved`, `AbstainedAtCeiling`, `Blocked` |
| `GeoRetryLoopArtifact` | `version`, `subject_id`, `policy: GeoRetryPolicy`, `passes: Vec<GeoRetryPass>`, `terminal: Option<GeoRetryTerminal>` |
| `pub fn next_retry_pass(loop_state: &GeoRetryLoopArtifact, latest_run: &GeoRun) -> Result<Option<GeoAcquisitionRequest>, GeoRetryError>` | `Some` only while `passes.len() < max_passes` and the run abstained; the loop emits requests and never geocodes (I10) |
| `pub fn record_pass(loop_state: &mut GeoRetryLoopArtifact, run: &GeoRun, receipt: Option<&GeoAcquisitionReceipt>) -> Result<(), GeoRetryError>` | appends one pass; sets `terminal` |

== ERROR CODES (§19.4; class is exactly one of refusal / abstention / typed fallback; detail always carries the named ids) ==
| `retry_pass_ceiling` | `retry::next_retry_pass` | `passes.len() == max_passes` and the latest run still abstains | abstention: `terminal = AbstainedAtCeiling`, last `abstention_reason` preserved (I10) | T10 |
| `retry_policy_unbounded` | `retry::record_pass`, schema validation | `max_passes == 0` or absent | refusal | T10 |

== CONTRACTS (§19.9) ==
| C17 | The retry loop is bounded by `max_passes > 0`; every pass records `plan_blake3`, `run_blake3`, and `abstention_reason`; `next_retry_pass` emits acquisition requests and never geocodes | `retry.rs` | I10 |
| C22 | Every artifact type declares `CANON_GEO_<NAME>_VERSION`, `canonical_<name>_bytes`, `validate_<name>_artifact`, and a `schemas/canon.geo.<name>.v0.schema.json`; canonical bytes are byte-identical across platforms | all §19.3 modules | N02, §19.3 shared shape |
| C25 | D2 to D6 do not modify `src/geo/composition.rs` or `src/geo/evidence.rs`; new modules call `solve_composition` as a black box, and generic modules carry no fixture, demo, or county literal | all §19.3 modules | §19.3 dependency direction, G7 |

== THREATS THIS BEAD MUST DEFEAT (§19.9) ==
| TH15 | The retry loop runs unbounded or geocodes inside the loop, breaking pinned reproducibility | `max_passes > 0` required; each pass is a normal pinned run; loop emits requests only | C17; T10; `retry_policy_unbounded`, `retry_pass_ceiling` |
| TH21 | Demo-path hard-coding: a generic module special-cases Demo 0 ids, the chimera constraint ids, or Franklin County names to pass its tests | Case-insensitive literal scan over the twelve generic modules; property tests on seeded random components | C25; T27, T03, T16 |

== TESTS (§19.6; ship in tests/geo_<module>.rs with the T ids in test names; each row's Negative case is mandatory) ==
| T10 | D4 | e2e | `GeoRetryPolicy { max_passes: 2, .. }`; two `GeoRun` values whose `status` abstains with `blockers` naming `geocode_ambiguous` | after two `record_pass` calls: `passes.len() == 2`, `terminal == Some(AbstainedAtCeiling)`, `passes[1].abstention_reason == "geocode_ambiguous"`, every pass has `plan_blake3` and `run_blake3` set; `next_retry_pass` returns `Ok(None)` | `max_passes: 0` refuses `retry_policy_unbounded` with `detail["field"] = "max_passes"` | C17; TH15 | `retry_pass_ceiling`, `retry_policy_unbounded` |
| T27 | D2 to D7 | adversarial | the twelve generic module files listed in §19.3 | a case-insensitive scan finds none of the literals `1004540041`, `chimera_wrongly_admitted`, `asserted_address_core`, `case_4`, `franklin`, `solve_composition` (the last only in `inspect.rs`), or any hosted-model client symbol in `observer.rs` replay code | the scan must also match `Franklin` and `CASE_4`; a scan that is case-sensitive fails on a seeded scratch copy | C18, C25; TH16, TH21 | none |

== NON-NEGOTIABLES AND INVARIANTS ==
### 19.1 Non-negotiables

- N01 Runtime lookup stays exact registry replay. Geo is a build-time workbench.
- N02 Same input plus same pinned sources reproduce byte-identical artifacts on every
  platform. No wall clock, locale, hash-map order, or float comparison in a decision path.
- N03 Every source value enters the solver only through a declared, versioned `rho`.
- N04 Adding admitted hard evidence may only narrow the model set or make it empty.
- N05 Source count is provenance, never evidence weight or confidence.
- N06 Candidate reach, admission, solver exactness, reconciliation, truth quality, and
  cost are reported as separate planes and never pooled.
- N07 Fixtures, retained evidence, and mocked providers are never presented as live proof.
- N08 Abstention is a legitimate output; an abstention-only module is not a delivered
  feature.
- N09 No vision or statistical model proposes a location. Models are observers with
  characterized error.
- N10 No commercial basemap imagery or tiles enter any artifact.
- N11 Gates are frozen in tests. A gate is passed by meeting it, never by editing it.
- N12 Every feature bead ships its code and its tests together, including at least one
  negative case a naive implementation fails.

### 19.2 Invariants for the new artifacts

- I01 A propagator prunes a value only with a typed reason naming constraint id and
  evidence ids; pruning is sound: enumeration with propagation equals enumeration without.
- I02 Propagator fixpoint is order-independent; tests run every permutation of propagator
  order on each fixture and compare bytes.
- I03 A minimal core is minimal: removing any one member restores satisfiability; tests
  verify by re-solving each deletion.
- I04 A correction set hits every enumerated core; when core enumeration hits its ceiling
  the artifact says `cores_complete=false` and no minimality claim is made.
- I05 Explanation artifacts name source record ids and rho contract ids, never internal
  indices.
- I06 An observer observation carries image tile digest, vintage, license hash, model or
  rule identity, weight or prompt digest, and the error-population digest; missing any
  field refuses.
- I07 Observer output is stored, never regenerated at replay; replay verifies the stored
  digest chain only.
- I08 A ledger row binds accession, loan id, parcel set, building set, truth plane,
  claim class, model count, exactness flags, and every source release pin; rows with
  candidate reach `none` carry the reason and no sets.
- I09 A ledger row never pools truth planes; non-round and round exact-lender evidence
  stay labeled.
- I10 The retry loop is bounded by a declared pass count; each pass is a normal pinned
  run and the loop artifact lists every pass with its abstention reason.
- I11 Event exposure joins building geometry, not centroids; advisory source hashes travel
  with the result.
- I12 Cross-deal collision reports a parcel or building shared by more than one trust
  with both accessions; pari passu participation is a labeled explanation, not a suppressed
  row.
- I13 `geo inspect` reads only emitted artifacts and receipts; it computes nothing that
  changes an answer.
- I14 Next-evidence recommendations expose the nondominated frontier and never manufacture
  a total ranking without a declared loss model.

== COMMANDS ==
### 19.7 Commands

Whole-tree gates run on every commit in every stage. Per-module binaries are the
`tests/geo_<module>.rs` files from §19.3; each stage runs its own set before claiming its
gate. `rg` exit status 1 means no match, which is the pass for the literal scans, so
they are written with a leading `!`.

```bash
# Whole-tree gates
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test

# Frozen E4 gate (T17, C24): expected red until G1, green from G1 on
cargo test --test geo_adjudication e4_acceptance_gate_requires_the_full_population_to_be_reachable -- --ignored

# Per-module test binaries (stage: test ids)
cargo test --test geo_propagate           # D2: T01 to T04, T19
cargo test --test geo_explain             # D2: T05, T06, T20, T21
cargo test --test geo_ledger              # D3: T07, T23, T26
cargo test --test geo_exposure            # D3: T08
cargo test --test geo_collision           # D3: T09
cargo test --test geo_retry               # D4: T10
cargo test --test geo_condo               # D4: T11
cargo test --test geo_inspect             # D4: T12, T25
cargo test --test geo_next_evidence       # D5: T18
cargo test --test geo_observer            # D6: T13, T14, T15
cargo test --test geo_adjudicate          # D6: T22 (new binary; distinct from the existing geo_adjudication)
cargo test --test geo_card                # D6: T24, T26
cargo test --test geo_e5_franklin_parcel  # D7: T16 plus the existing literal scan

# One test by name with output
cargo test --test geo_propagate soundness_holds_on_every_e4_fixture -- --nocapture

# Schema drift guard (C22). tests/geo_schemas.rs include_str!s each schema file, pins
# title, properties.version.const, and additionalProperties == false, then walks a real
# serialized instance against the schema; there is no jsonschema crate. Each new
# artifact adds one <name>_schema_matches_a_real_instance test there and one
# include_str! of schemas/canon.geo.<name>.v0.schema.json.
cargo test --test geo_schemas
cargo test --test geo_schemas propagation_schema_matches_a_real_instance
for s in propagation explanation separation_request separation observer observation_rows \
         image_tile_pin adjudication_request adjudication_receipt evidence_card \
         collateral_ledger event_exposure cross_deal retry_loop inspection next_evidence \
         condo_bridge_request ledger_bridge; do
  jq -e --arg s "$s" '.title == "canon.geo.\($s).v0"
    and .properties.version.const == "canon_geo_\($s).v0"
    and .additionalProperties == false' "schemas/canon.geo.${s}.v0.schema.json"
done

# --describe entries for geo subcommands (C22: one per new module, named after it:
# geo propagate, geo explain, geo observer, geo adjudicate, geo card, geo ledger,
# geo exposure, geo collision, geo retry, geo inspect, geo next-evidence, geo condo)
cargo run --bin canon -- --describe \
  | jq -r '.subcommands[] | select(.name | startswith("geo ")) | "\(.name)\t\(.status)\t\(.output_schema)"'
cargo run --bin canon -- --describe \
  | jq -e '[.subcommands[] | select(.name == "geo propagate" and .status == "implemented")] | length == 1'

# T27 literal scan (C25, G7). Mirrors tests/geo_e5_franklin_parcel.rs
# franklin_instance_names_do_not_enter_the_generic_geo_engine, which lowercases each
# generic source file and asserts it contains no instance literal.
GEO_GENERIC="src/geo/propagate.rs src/geo/explain.rs src/geo/observer.rs src/geo/adjudicate.rs \
  src/geo/card.rs src/geo/ledger.rs src/geo/exposure.rs src/geo/collision.rs src/geo/retry.rs \
  src/geo/inspect.rs src/geo/next_evidence.rs src/geo/condo.rs"
! rg -i -n 'franklin|39049|epsg:3735|1004540041|chimera_wrongly_admitted|asserted_address_core|case_4' $GEO_GENERIC
! rg -n 'solve_composition' src/geo/inspect.rs
! rg -i -n 'reqwest|hyper::|openai|anthropic|gemini|bedrock|invoke_model' src/geo/observer.rs
cargo test --test geo_e5_franklin_parcel franklin_instance_names_do_not_enter_the_generic_geo_engine

# Demo 0, capabilities, measurement plan, beads
bash scripts/geo_demo/demo0.sh --work-dir /tmp/demo0
cargo run --bin canon -- geo capabilities --emit json
cargo run --bin canon_geo_measurements -- --emit plan
br ready --json && br dep cycles --json
```

ANTI-REWARD-HACKING (AGENTS.md, binding):
- Code and tests ship in this bead; no scope-splitting into type/impl/test closures.
- No new todo!()/unimplemented!() scaffolds. Refusal-only implementation earns partial credit and never closes this bead (label refusal-only + follow-up bead if that is the honest state).
- Fixtures and Demo 0 outputs are never presented as live proof (C23). Gate thresholds are never edited to pass (C24, N11).
- Every feature test includes at least one negative case a naive implementation fails (the Negative case column below).
- Generic modules carry no fixture, demo, or county literal (C25, T27).

title: [CANON-V1/P08.3] Publish and pull packages by immutable OCI digest
description:
## Background
Remote reuse needs a standard, optional workflow that never makes network access part of exact lookup or ordinary local execution.

## Technical Approach
Add explicit `canon package push` and `pull` against OCI Distribution-compatible registries, always verify locally, push blobs idempotently, resolve tags to digests, pin pulled dependencies, and materialize into an external content cache. Network operations require explicit commands/policy; project runs use locked local digests and refuse missing artifacts unless acquisition was planned.

## Success Criteria
- Pull by digest yields a semantically verified local package and receipt.
- Mutable tag resolution is recorded once in the project lock; execution never follows tag drift.
- Interrupted/retried uploads and downloads are idempotent and do not expose incomplete packages.
- Offline and read-only execution cannot initiate network access.

## Test Plan
Use a disposable local OCI registry for auth/no-auth, push/pull, tag movement, missing blob, corrupt proxy response, retry/interruption, concurrent push, offline refusal, and cache reuse.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/distribution/remote.rs`
- `src/distribution/cache.rs`
- `tests/oci_remote_e2e.rs`

## Considerations
Keep remote transport optional and isolated. Do not add cloud-provider SDKs to the default lookup path.

title: canon geo: residual measurement harness — the gate that justifies or kills the ambition lane
description:
THE GATE ON THE ENTIRE AMBITION LANE. NOTHING BELOW IT MAY START WITHOUT ITS OUTPUT.

bd-2kjx's discipline is explicit and correct: "NO HEAVY MATH IN v1. At ~167 nodes
exhaustive evaluation is affordable, hard constraints prune most pairs, and the evidence is
near-dispositive rather than fuzzy. Ship a DETERMINISTIC OPERATOR CASCADE with abstention.
Then MEASURE THE RESIDUAL. Only if the residual justifies it, add permutation
synchronization / correlation clustering / Sinkhorn assignment — and only in the workbench
as candidate generation and scoring, never in runtime."

That discipline was never given an instrument. This bead is the instrument. Without it,
"measure the residual" is a sentence rather than a gate, and the ambition lane becomes
either vaporware or reward hacking — building sophisticated machinery because it is
satisfying rather than because a measured defect demands it.

WHAT THE RESIDUAL IS: the population the deterministic cascade CANNOT resolve — every
abstention and every error, classified by CAUSE. Not a single number. A taxonomy with
counts, because different causes justify completely different machinery, and some justify
none.

REQUIRED CLASSIFICATION OF EVERY UNRESOLVED ROW:
  a) COVERAGE      the client's layer does not cover the tile. Justifies NO math. Fixed by
                   licensing. Must be reported separately or it inflates the apparent
                   residual and motivates machinery that cannot help.
  b) INPUT         a required channel is absent (no geocode, no address, `Various`,
                   Ginnie-with-no-address). Justifies NO math. Fixed upstream.
  c) TIE           two or more candidates score identically and no channel breaks it. The
                   237 Park case. THIS is what constellation consistency and assignment
                   methods address.
  d) DISAGREEMENT  channels conflict — geometry says A, address says B. May justify better
                   evidence weighting; may simply be correct abstention.
  e) NO-CANDIDATE  layer covers the tile, candidates were generated, none passed. The
                   interpolated-geocode population. Addressed by the address channel and by
                   proximity candidate generation, not by clustering math.
  f) SILENT ERROR  the cascade answered CONFIDENTLY AND WRONGLY. The most important
                   category and the hardest to measure — requires ground truth. In NYC,
                   PLUTO provides it. The nearest_rooftop_match tier (688 rows, 100% lot-hit
                   rate, worst house-number agreement) is the prime suspect population and
                   must be reported as its own slice.

ONLY (c) AND ARGUABLY (d) AND (f) JUSTIFY THE AMBITION LANE. If the residual is dominated
by (a) and (b) — which is entirely plausible given that PROPERTY_MART.PROPERTY_DIM is 51%
geocoded — then correlation clustering and Sinkhorn would be sophisticated answers to a
question nobody asked, and the correct next investment is geocoding and licensing.
THAT IS A REAL POSSIBLE OUTCOME AND THIS BEAD MUST BE WILLING TO REPORT IT.

REQUIRED OUTPUTS:
1. Residual taxonomy with counts and rates, per corpus, sliced by geocode tier.
2. For category (c): the TIE STRUCTURE. How many candidates, how far apart in score units,
   and whether the tie is within-source or cross-source. A tie between two condo lots is a
   different problem from a tie between two vendors' versions of one lot.
3. For category (f): a ground-truth-scored silent-error rate, with the confident-and-wrong
   cases enumerated for inspection. This is the number that determines whether the product
   is trustworthy at all.
4. A WRITTEN GATE DECISION naming which ambition-lane beads (if any) the measured residual
   justifies, with the counts that justify them. Each ambition bead is BLOCKED ON THIS
   DECISION and must cite it to start.
5. RE-RUNNABLE. The residual is measured again after each ambition-lane bead lands, so the
   marginal value of each addition is visible. A method that does not move the residual gets
   reverted, not defended.

ANTI-REWARD-HACKING NOTE, per AGENTS.md: this bead is a HARD GATE for named feature work,
which is what makes it legitimate process rather than process porn. It must not become a

comments.text:
REFINEMENT 2026-08-14 — THIS BEAD MEASURES; IT ALSO HAS TO BE TESTED. Adding the
verification requirements it was missing.

THE RISK SPECIFIC TO A MEASUREMENT HARNESS: it can be silently wrong in a way that looks
authoritative, and the whole ambition lane is gated on its output. A miscategorized
residual either builds machinery nobody needed or kills work that was justified.

REQUIRED TESTS:
1. TAXONOMY EXHAUSTIVENESS. Every unresolved row must land in exactly one of the six
   categories. Assert count(categorized) == count(unresolved) on every run, and REFUSE to
   emit a report if it does not balance. This is the same discipline as canon's core
   summary invariant (summary.total == resolved + unresolved) and should be enforced as
   hard, not warned.
2. SYNTHETIC INJECTION. Construct a fixture where each of the six causes is present in a
   KNOWN quantity — n coverage gaps, n missing-input rows, n ties, n channel
   disagreements, n no-candidates, n deliberately-wrong confident answers — and assert the
   harness recovers those exact counts. A residual harness that cannot recover injected
   counts cannot be trusted on real data.
3. SILENT-ERROR DETECTION IS THE HARDEST AND NEEDS ITS OWN TEST. Inject rows where the
   cascade will confidently produce a known-wrong answer (a nearest_rooftop_match-style
   point placed just inside the neighbour's lot) and assert category (f) catches them.
   If the harness cannot detect a planted silent error, its silent-error rate is
   meaningless and must not be published.
4. DETERMINISM. Two runs over the same scored artifact produce byte-identical reports.
5. COMPARISON MODE. Assert residual movement is computed correctly between two runs,
   including the sign — a method that makes things worse must show as worse.

LOGGING: the harness must emit per-category row identifiers, not only counts, so a human
can inspect why a row landed where it did. A count without traceable membership cannot be
audited and will be argued with rather than acted on.

title: [CANON-V1/P07.6] Generalize linkage from two tapes to N named sources
description:
## Background
Real identity programs reconcile more than a reference and target file. Repeated pairwise linking can create order-dependent transitive errors and discards cross-source context.

## Technical Approach
Extend generic entity link projects to N named sources with explicit source roles, comparison graph, field maps, anchor namespaces, pairwise candidate budgets, cross-source consistency constraints, and optional designated canonical reference. Emit source-aware evidence and decisions; abstain on contradictory cycles. Preserve the simple two-source CLI as a manifest shorthand, not a separate engine.

- Results are invariant to source enumeration where the declared comparison graph is equivalent.
- Conflicting A-B, B-C, A-C evidence is surfaced rather than transitively forced.
- Budgets prevent accidental Cartesian growth and diagnostics identify hot source pairs.
- Two-source behavior remains a strict covered subset.

## Test Plan
Test 2/3/5-source fixtures, source permutation, sparse comparison graphs, duplicate local IDs, anchor conflicts, transitive traps, budget refusal, and shard/restart determinism.

title: canon strategy: intent-keyed champions + operator-attested grade
description:
Umbrella feature for making canon strategy fit real operator workflows where the reusable artifact is an intent-triggered script, not a script tied to a columnar input profile.

Current state:
- canon strategy is implemented as a versioned local registry under _strategy/*.json.
- Existing entries are keyed by (schema_fingerprint, skill_hash).
- Existing register requires verify, assess, and airlock proof artifacts.
- Existing resolve can return EXACT, COMPATIBLE, PARTIAL, or UNRESOLVED by comparing schema shapes.

Target state:
- The same strategy registry supports typed keys: schema-shape keys and task/intent keys.
- Task/intent keys are scoped by skill hash: (key_type=task, task=<declared intent>, skill_hash=<BLAKE3 skill hash>).
- Task-keyed resolve is exact: EXACT when an active champion exists, UNRESOLVED otherwise. Schema tiers are not applicable for task keys.
- Entries carry an attestation grade: operator-attested or proof-attested.
- Operator-attested registration is the lightweight v1 path for a new user: save a script that just worked, without requiring verify/assess/airlock or any external tooling.
- Proof-attested registration remains the heavier path using audit/proof artifacts.
- Lifecycle operations support register, update, deprecate/remove-from-active-resolution, and promote operator-attested entries to proof-attested entries by attaching proof artifacts later.

Non-goals for this graph:
- No tournament or NTM multi-agent implementation.
- No script execution during strategy resolve.
- No deletion of registry entries. Remove means mark deprecated/inactive so git history and registry auditability remain intact.
design:
Use the existing strategy registry instead of building a side registry. The correct implementation path is to generalize the current entry schema and registry operations while preserving existing proof-attested, schema-keyed behavior as a first-class mode.

The graph is intentionally ordered so contract/spec work comes first, then the data model and CLI validation, then behavior paths, then lint/diff/docs/tests/quality. This keeps later beads self-contained and prevents implementers from guessing about JSON shape or CLI semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
The feature is complete only when a human can run and inspect a standalone flow on a fresh machine:
1. Register a task-keyed script with operator identity, timestamp, and one-line reason, with no fixture suite and no verify/assess/airlock inputs.
2. Resolve the same task and skill to the frozen script with EXACT exit 0, and UNRESOLVED exit 1 when no active task entry exists.
3. List and explain registered strategy champions, including typed key, grade, status, provenance, source file, entry order, and why resolve would choose or ignore an entry.
4. Update the champion with a version bump and a deterministic mutation receipt.
5. Deprecate/remove the champion from active resolution without deleting registry history.
6. Promote an operator-attested champion to proof-attested by attaching audit/proof artifacts later.
7. Emit deterministic receipts and witness records for mutating strategy commands without recording raw script bytes or secrets.
8. Run existing proof-attested schema-keyed strategy workflows unchanged as intentional product behavior.
9. Prove the mixed registry contract through reusable matrix coverage for schema proof, task operator, task promoted proof, and deprecated task entries.
10. Pass registry lint, strategy diff, README/operator docs checks, CLI smoke tests, br graph validation, and the full Rust quality gate.

title: Add registry seed audit reporting for batch registry authoring workflows

title: canon registry add-entry: atomic single-alias-entry write + semver bump + lint
description:
Add `canon registry add-entry` as the safe single-alias writer for self-authored registries.

Purpose:
- Replace hand-editing mapping JSON with a deterministic write path that validates one new alias, bumps registry metadata, and leaves the registry in a state the normal exact lookup path can consume.
- This is registry maintenance, not a resolution workbench: no matching, no suggestions, no fuzzy behavior.

CLI:
`canon registry add-entry --registry <DIR> --alias-file <FILE> --canonical-id <ID> --input <INPUT> --rule-id <RULE> [--canonical-type <TYPE>] [--bump patch|minor|major | --next-version <VER>] [--no-lint] [--emit json|plain]`

Behavior:
- `--alias-file` must be an existing root-level mapping file name ending in `.json`; reject paths, subdirectories, `registry.json`, and `_build.json`.
- Parse all root mapping files using the existing flat registry rules before planning the write.
- Refuse if `--input` is empty after ASCII trim or is not already in trimmed form. The value written should be exactly what future lookup receives after input trim.
- Refuse if any existing mapping entry anywhere in the registry already has the same `input`, regardless of `rule_id`. First-match-wins lookup makes duplicate inputs unsafe for this writer.
- `--canonical-type` is required for a new canonical ID. If omitted for an existing canonical ID, infer it only when all existing entries for that canonical ID use exactly one canonical_type; otherwise refuse.
- If `registry.json.default_id_scheme` exists, validate `--canonical-id` against that scheme unless the command is later extended with an explicit override flag. Do not silently write out-of-scheme IDs for self-authored registries.
- Version update: accept either `--next-version <VER>` or `--bump patch|minor|major`, but not both. Default is `--bump patch`. If the current version cannot be parsed as numeric `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, refuse and require `--next-version`.
- Increment `entry_count` by one and preserve all other `registry.json` fields, including unknown metadata.
- Validate proposed output before commit. If `--no-lint` is not set, run the standard lint check and abort on lint errors; warnings/info are reported in the JSON receipt but do not block.
- Write mapping file and `registry.json` using temp-file-then-rename or an equivalent restore-on-failure sequence. A failed validation, lint error, or write error must leave the original files byte-for-byte intact.
- Do not directly mutate `_index.sqlite`; the version change should cause normal registry loading to rebuild the derived index.
- Do not add new witness behavior in this bead. Keep registry command side effects limited to the documented registry file writes.

Output:
- Default `--emit json`: emit `canon_registry_add_entry.v0` with registry before/after, alias entry, touched files, lint summary, and warnings.
- `--emit plain`: emit a concise one-line success summary.
acceptance_criteria:
- Successful add-entry appends exactly one mapping object to the chosen alias file and updates `registry.json.version` and `entry_count`.
- Duplicate `input` anywhere in the registry refuses before writing and leaves all files unchanged.
- Missing `--canonical-type` is accepted only when it can be inferred unambiguously from existing entries for the canonical ID.
- Patch/minor/major bumps work for numeric three-part versions; non-bumpable versions require `--next-version`.
- `registry.json` unknown fields survive the write unchanged.
- Alias-file validation rejects path traversal, subdirectories, missing files, `registry.json`, and `_build.json`.
- Lint errors abort the write and leave all files byte-for-byte unchanged; lint warnings/info appear in the receipt.
- JSON receipt shape is covered by a golden fixture for `canon_registry_add_entry.v0`.
- A round-trip test proves a subsequent normal `canon <INPUT> --registry ...` resolves the newly added alias.
- Quality gate passes: `cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test`.
notes:
Target files:
- src/registry/add_entry.rs (new)
- src/registry.rs (add module/export only; there is no src/registry/mod.rs in this repo)
- src/cli.rs (wire subcommand and emit/version options)
- src/lib.rs (minimal dispatch only)
- operator.json (add command contract if implemented in this bead)
- tests/registry_add_entry.rs (new)

Implementation notes:
- Prefer an internal planning function that returns proposed file bytes plus a receipt before writing. `mint` should reuse that planner instead of shelling out or reimplementing add-entry logic.
- Treat lint as data: `registry_lint::lint(..., Standard)` returns a report even with findings; only severity `error` should block by default.
- Preserve the exact-match lookup contract. This command only authors exact aliases.
close_reason: Implemented canon registry add-entry with exact alias planning, atomic write/restore behavior, metadata version and entry_count updates, canonical_type inference, default_id_scheme validation, optional lint receipt, operator contract, golden JSON receipt, round-trip lookup coverage, and refusal/unchanged-file tests. Evidence: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test; target/debug/canon --describe includes registry add-entry; br dep cycles --json returned count 0.

title: [CANON-V1/P06.4] Define portable entity profile packages for cluster and link modes
description:
## Background
A reusable deployment needs to bundle its object types, field roles, normalization, blocking, evidence, constraints, review thresholds, and canonical-ID conventions without turning those settings into engine branches.

## Technical Approach
Specify a `canon.entity.profile.v1` package that references ontology, namespace, vocabulary, normalization, evidence, and policy digests; maps declared observation fields; selects cluster or cross-dataset link modes; declares limits and expected outputs; and supports explicit project overrides. Core dispatch is identical for all profile IDs.

## Success Criteria
- A third-party profile runs through public CLI/SDK contracts with no source changes.
- One profile can support both clustering and directional linkage where declared.
- Every default and override is visible in artifact headers and project locks.
- Wrong object types, missing capabilities, incompatible packages, and unknown fields refuse deterministically.

## Test Plan
Run two unrelated neutral profiles through prepare/index/block/evidence/solve-or-link/review/promote/apply. Test override invalidation, missing capabilities, package tampering, and byte-stable artifacts.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/extensions/profile.rs`
- `schemas/canon.entity.profile.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/extensions_profile.rs`

## Considerations
Profiles are external executable configuration with strict schemas; they are not free-form hooks into Rust internals.

title: canon geo: NYC proving-ground harness — BBL on CMBS collateral, scored against PLUTO
description:
The OC-0048 proving ground and the kill criterion.

TASK: assign a BBL to CMBS collateral in New York City and score against PLUTO's
address-to-BBL ground truth.

BASELINE FIRST: run plain address-string matching and record its precision and
recall. That is the number the deterministic cascade must beat. Without the
baseline the result is unfalsifiable.

REPORT BOTH precision AND ABSTENTION RATE. Abstention is acceptable; SILENT
ERROR IS NOT. The abstention rate is a first-class success metric, not a
footnote.

KILL CRITERION (from OC-0048): if the deterministic cascade cannot beat
address-string matching on the NYC scored set, the tile distribution work does
not start.

WHY NYC: hardest geography (multi-building lots, air rights, buildings spanning
lots, hyphenated ranges), free ground truth, densest CMBS market, publicly
checkable via ZoLa, and ACRIS makes it the OC-0047 ground-truth county too.

GEOMETRY; tabular PLUTO cannot support point-in-polygon) and NYC Building

cmdrvl-curves.

SCOPE. NYC CMBS geocode rows, county_fips in (36005,36047,36061,36081,36085), from EDGAR_DB.DBT_WRANGLING_EDGAR.WRGL_EDGAR_CMBS_GEOCODES__STRUCTURED: 6,682 rows total, ~10% of the 68,603-row national geocode book.
  36061 Manhattan 3,420 | 36047 Brooklyn 1,563 | 36081 Queens 873 | 36005 Bronx 755 | 36085 Staten Island 71

GEOCODE TIER DISTRIBUTION (Geocodio accuracy_type):
  rooftop 5,436 (81.4%) | nearest_rooftop_match 688 (10.3%) | range_interpolation 404 (6.0%) | street_center 79 (1.2%) | place 51 (0.8%) | intersection 24 (0.4%)

GEOMETRY-ONLY BASELINE — ST_CONTAINS into NYC_DCP_MAPPLUTO_HOT current release, hit rate by tier:
  rooftop 5,063/5,067 = 99.92%
  nearest_rooftop_match 648/648 = 100.00%
  range_interpolation 196/388 = 50.52%
  street_center 24/79 = 30.38%
  place 40/50 = 80.00%
  intersection 2/23 = 8.70%
  OVERALL 5,973/6,255 = 95.49% land inside at least one lot

IMPLICATION FOR THIS BEAD'S FRAMING. Point-in-polygon alone already produces AN answer for 95.5% of the NYC book. COVERAGE IS THEREFORE NOT THE PROBLEM AND MUST NOT BE THE HEADLINE METRIC. The cascade's claim has to be PRECISION and honest ABSTENTION — separating correct BBLs from confident-looking wrong ones — not raising a hit rate. Score accordingly.

TIER TO DISTRUST: nearest_rooftop_match, 688 rows, hits a lot 100% of the time (Geocodio substituted a nearby rooftop when the exact address was not found), yet agrees with the lot's house number least often of the rooftop tiers. Geometry is maximally confident here and may be pointing at the neighbour. This is the silent-error population.

CAVEAT ON GEOCODIO SEMANTICS: the tier meanings above (rooftop = on structure, range_interpolation = street-centreline interpolation, nearest_rooftop_match = substituted nearby rooftop) are asserted from general knowledge of Geocodio, NOT verified against their documentation. Confirm before this framing hardens.

comments.text:
MULTI-LOT FAN-OUT OBSERVED 2026-08-14 — the condo trap is real and measurable, not hypothetical.

Across four Loom query formulations of the same NYC join, the row counts did not agree: 6,682 total rows / 6,255 distinct geocoded points / 6,388 rows landing in a lot. Worse, the by-borough breakdown reported 5,494 Manhattan rows landing in a lot against a Manhattan total of only 3,420 rows.

A single point is landing inside MORE THAN ONE MapPLUTO polygon. The expected cause is condo unit billing BBLs overlapping the condo parent lot — the trap already named in this bead's NYC TRAPS section and in OC-0048 — plus any query that INNER JOINs without collapsing produces fan-out.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE HIT RATE. It means 'which BBL' is GENUINELY AMBIGUOUS for a real population, and no improvement in geometry resolves it: both polygons legitimately contain the point. This is the strongest empirical argument yet for what canon geo adds over a spatial join — typed output (bd-3soj), within-source mutual exclusion via anti_merge, and abstention as a reported rate. A naive pipeline silently picks whichever row the join returns first.

REQUIRED OF THE HARNESS:
- Report the multi-lot rate as a first-class number alongside precision and abstention.
- Never collapse multi-lot hits with an arbitrary pick (MAX, LIMIT 1, first-returned). Either resolve via condo parent/unit semantics or abstain.
- The baseline in the prior comment must be re-derived on a de-duplicated, fan-out-aware basis before it is quoted as the number to beat. TREAT THE 95.49% AS DIRECTIONAL, NOT EXACT.

FOLLOW-ON CORPORA (operator 2026-08-14): after CMBS, the same NYC exercise runs for HUD, Fannie, Ginnie and Freddie property tables — roughly equivalent size and shape each. Build the harness to take a corpus as a parameter rather than hardcoding the CMBS geocode table.

comments.text:
REALITY CHECK 2026-08-14 — THE KILL CRITERION CANNOT CURRENTLY BE EVALUATED. THREE
DEFECTS.

DEFECT 1: THE COMPARATOR HAS NEVER BEEN MEASURED.
This bead says: "BASELINE FIRST: run plain address-string matching and record its
precision and recall. That is the number the deterministic cascade must beat. Without
the baseline the result is unfalsifiable."
What the 2026-08-14 comment actually recorded is a GEOMETRY-ONLY point-in-polygon hit
rate (95.49% overall, broken out by Geocodio tier). That is a useful and honest number
and it is NOT the address-string baseline. It is a different baseline for a different
claim.
Meanwhile OC-0048 states Phase 0 is "Not yet run" while this bead's comments show a
baseline WAS run. Both are half right. The half that matters — ADDRESS-STRING PRECISION
AND RECALL — does not exist. Until it does, the kill criterion is unfalsifiable exactly
as this bead warned.
OC-0048 asks for TWO baselines, and that is correct: naive address-string matching, and
geometry-only PIP. The cascade must beat both, and specifically must recover the
interpolated tier that geometry alone cannot reach.
ACTION: the address-string baseline is cut as its own bead with NO DEPENDENCIES. It is
SQL only — no canon, no code, no landing. See defect 3.

DEFECT 2: PREDICATE-REGIME MISMATCH. NOT PREVIOUSLY NOTED ANYWHERE.
The measured baseline used Snowflake ST_CONTAINS against NYC_DCP_MAPPLUTO_HOT, whose
geometry is stored as GEOGRAPHY — a SPHERICAL predicate. MapPLUTO was landed by
reprojecting source EPSG:2263 (NY State Plane feet) to WGS84 (bd-35ae receipt). canon
will compute PLANAR exact predicates (Shewchuk-style, bd-15ba) on WGS84 degrees.
THAT IS THREE DIFFERENT GEOMETRY REGIMES: State Plane source, spherical warehouse
predicate, planar canon predicate.
Determinism of canon's predicate DOES NOT IMPLY AGREEMENT WITH THE BASELINE. Worse, the
disagreement will concentrate precisely on BOUNDARY-ADJACENT POINTS — which is the entire
population this outcome cares about, and the population the 157 multi-lot cases live in.
If the cascade is scored against a baseline computed under a different predicate, some
apparent "cascade errors" will be predicate disagreements and some apparent "cascade
wins" will be luck.
ACTION: a predicate-regime reconciliation bead is cut. This bead must not quote a
precision number until the regimes are reconciled or the disagreement rate is measured
and reported alongside.

DEFECT 3: THE CHEAPEST FALSIFYING EXPERIMENT SITS AT THE BOTTOM OF A FOUR-DEEP CHAIN.
This bead is blocked on bd-2b9d + bd-gs6n + bd-1zph, which are blocked on bd-3ccc, which
is blocked on bd-67wx and (transitively for bd-gs6n) bd-15ba. So the work that would tell
us NOT TO BUILD is gated behind the entire build. You cannot fail fast on this plan.
OC-0048's own Sequencing section says Phase 0 is "No canon, no landing, read-only" —
correctly identifying it as unblocked work — yet it lives inside this bead, which is
maximally blocked.
ACTION: baseline measurement is extracted into standalone READY beads. This bead retains
the SCORED CASCADE COMPARISON, which genuinely does depend on the cascade existing.

RETAINED AND REINFORCED:
- Report precision AND abstention rate. Abstention acceptable, silent error not.
- Report the MULTI-LOT RATE as a first-class number. The fan-out is real and measured
  (6,682 rows / 6,255 distinct points / 6,388 in-lot; Manhattan by-borough 5,494 against
  a 3,420 total). Never collapse multi-lot hits with MAX/LIMIT 1/first-returned.
- The 95.49% is DIRECTIONAL, not exact; re-derive on a de-duplicated fan-out-aware basis.
- COVERAGE IS NOT THE HEADLINE METRIC. PIP alone answers 95.5% of the NYC book. The
  claim is PRECISION and HONEST ABSTENTION.
- TIER TO DISTRUST: nearest_rooftop_match, 688 rows, 100% lot-hit rate but worst house-
  number agreement. This is the silent-error population and deserves its own reported
  slice.
- CAVEAT still open: Geocodio tier semantics are asserted from general knowledge, not
  verified against documentation. Confirm before the framing hardens.
- Corpus as a PARAMETER, not hardcoded to the CMBS geocode table — HUD, Fannie, Ginnie,
  Freddie follow.

NEW: BYOP MEANS THIS PROVING GROUND TESTS A DIFFERENT CONFIGURATION THAN THE PRODUCT.
Operator decision 2026-08-14 (bd-2kjx): clients bring their own parcel layer. Here WE
supply MapPLUTO. That is legitimate as a CASCADE proof — NYC is the adversarial geography
and PLUTO is free ground truth — but it does not exercise the shipping path: client-
supplied partial-coverage geometry, two-registry composition, license containment. A
separate BYOP integration test is cut, using an ATTOM-shaped synthetic layer with
deliberate coverage holes derived from MapPLUTO so ground truth is preserved.

NEW: DENOMINATOR HONESTY HAS A CEILING THIS BEAD SHOULD STATE. PROPERTY_MART.PROPERTY_DIM
is 50,593 rows with 25,884 geocoded (51%), and the backfill is blocked on a frozen
Geocodio account (br-ppnr blocked on br-1zo6). Annex A `Various` addresses never geocoded.
Ginnie's native key is a pool number with NO ADDRESS FIELD AT ALL. Report these as
excluded-and-counted, per OC-0048's denominator-honesty criterion, and note that for the
agency corpora this ceiling binds BEFORE canon geo does any work.

comments.text:
AMENDMENT 2026-08-14 — THE METRIC CAN PASS WHILE THE PRODUCT FAILS. FOURTH DEFECT.

OPERATOR CASE: a parcel that is bare in year 0 and carries seven buildings in year 1, where
building one goes into a REIT, building two into a CMBS trust, and building three carries an
RCA sales comp.

ALL THREE POSITIONS RESOLVE TO THE SAME, CORRECT BBL. Under this bead's metric — "assign a
BBL to CMBS collateral, scored against PLUTO" — all three score as CORRECT, while the
question that actually matters (WHICH BUILDING?) is never tested at all.

So the kill criterion as scored could be satisfied by a system that cannot do the thing the
product is for. BBL is what can be scored cheaply against free public ground truth. BUILDING
is what the client needs in order to join a REIT holding, a CMBS position and a comp
without merging them. Those are not the same target and this bead currently conflates them.

WORSE — PARCEL-LEVEL RESOLUTION ACTIVELY CREATES FALSE MERGES ACROSS CORPORA. Collapsing
three distinct collateral positions onto one BBL double-counts exposure, corrupts holder
attribution (OC-0047) and corrupts pool composition (OC-0046). The cross-corpus join this
whole outcome exists to enable would be poisoned by the key it ships. A BBL column that
merges them is not a partial answer; it is a wrong one.

REQUIRED CHANGES TO THIS BEAD:
1. SCORE AT TWO LEVELS, REPORT BOTH SEPARATELY.
   PARCEL level against PLUTO — cheap, public, verifiable on ZoLa. Keep it; it is the
   honest proving-ground metric and it is what makes the result checkable by a stranger.
   BUILDING level — the product metric. Ground truth is harder: NYC BIN via the landed
   building footprints file (bd-397d) is the BBL-to-BIN bridge and is the obvious source.
2. REPORT THE MULTI-BUILDING-PARCEL POPULATION AS A FIRST-CLASS SLICE, alongside the
   multi-lot rate this bead already elevates. How many CMBS positions share a BBL with
   another position from ANY corpus (CMBS, REIT Schedule III, HUD, GSE, RCA)? That count is
   the size of the false-merge exposure, and it is computable today from landed data without
   any resolution existing.
3. ADD A FALSE-MERGE RATE TO THE HEADLINE NUMBERS. The reporting set becomes:
   coverage | precision-within-coverage | abstention | multi-candidate | FALSE-MERGE
   A false merge is worse than an abstention and worse than a miss, because it silently
   corrupts a downstream join rather than failing visibly. It deserves its own number and
   arguably its own weight in the cost-sensitive calibration (bd-1vcw).
4. THE PROVING GROUND MUST INCLUDE AT LEAST ONE MULTI-CORPUS SHARED-PARCEL CASE in its
   scored set, deliberately selected. If the NYC CMBS book has none, source one from REIT
   Schedule III or RCA — the case is the whole argument for the entity-level model
   (bd-2cbs) and for building-level resolution, and an evaluation that omits it proves
   nothing about the product.

TEMPORAL INTERACTION (see the entity-lifecycle bead): scoring a 2019 assertion against a
current MapPLUTO release will attribute it to a containment graph that did not exist at the
time. Bind every scored row to the tile vintage matching its as-of, or exclude it from the
denominator and count it separately.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-14 — THE GEOCODE TABLE'S GRAIN, AND WHY "241/249 WEST 74TH STREET" HAS
TWO ROWS. Operator questioned the earlier claim; the earlier claim was wrong about the
mechanism.

WHAT I SAID: "one property, two geocode rows that disagree — the row-to-point relation is
many-to-many AND INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT," framed as a single geocoder behaving
inconsistently.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE (verified against the table): the two rows are the output of TWO
DIFFERENT GEOCODING SERVICES run at different times. The ETL APPENDS results rather than
upserting them.

  GRAIN: PROPERTY_NAME + PROPERTY_ADDRESS + PROPERTY_CITY + PROPERTY_STATE + SOURCE + ASOF
  There is NO deal, loan, or property identifier column in this table AT ALL.

THREE CONSEQUENCES, ALL MORE USEFUL THAN THE CLAIM THEY REPLACE:

1. THE ROW COUNT IS NOT A PROPERTY COUNT. 68,603 rows nationally and 6,682 in the five
   boroughs are property x SOURCE x ASOF, not properties. The previously observed
   6,682 rows / 6,255 distinct points gap is partly this, not solely multi-lot fan-out.
   EVERY DENOMINATOR IN bd-14co AND bd-bmee MUST DEDUPLICATE TO A DECLARED GRAIN FIRST and
   state which grain it used. A coverage or precision rate computed over appended
   geocoder outputs is not a rate over the book.

2. THE TABLE CANNOT BE ATTRIBUTED TO A DEAL ON ITS OWN. With no loan or deal identifier,
   this table cannot answer "which CMBS position does this resolution belong to." bd-bmee's
   scored set, and the whole false-merge analysis in bd-1oy8 (which turns on positions from
   DIFFERENT corpora sharing a parcel), require joining upstream to a table that carries
   deal identifiers. IDENTIFY THAT UPSTREAM TABLE BEFORE THE SCORED SET IS BUILT — this is
   a prerequisite nobody had noticed.

3. INDEPENDENT GEOCODERS DISAGREEING IS BETTER EVIDENCE THAN ONE GEOCODER WAVERING.
   The finding survives and gets stronger. Two INDEPENDENT services producing points ~25
   blocks apart for the same asserted address is a strong, free disagreement signal, and it
   is exactly what the tile can adjudicate (see the geocode-plausibility bead). The usual
   remedies — take the highest ACCURACY_SCORE, the most recent ASOF, or a preferred SOURCE
   — all pick a winner WITHOUT EVIDENCE. Canon can do better by asking the tile which point
   its own neighbourhood supports.

WHAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED FROM THE ORIGINAL FINDING: one of the two points is ROOFTOP tier
and parses to "241 W 49th St" against a source address of "241/249 West 74th Street" — a
confident, high-tier, ~25-block error. The silent-error population is still larger than the
single nearest_rooftop_match tier bd-bmee identified, and calibration keyed only on
accuracy_type still misses it.

CORRECTION 2026-08-14 — THE "51% GEOCODED" FIGURE IS WRONG. I cited it repeatedly this
session, including in this bead. Operator questioned it and was right.

WHAT I REPEATED, sourced from OC-0048: "PROPERTY_MART.PROPERTY_DIM holds 50,593 rows with
only 25,884 geocoded (51%) ... that is a hard coverage ceiling."

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MEASURED (edgar-elt br-ppnr, 2026-07-23, against
WRGL_EDGAR_CRE_PROPERTIES__DEDUPED, applying the br-351x identity normalization and the
committed placeholder seed list):
    total_distinct_properties   38,365
    placeholder_excluded         4,245   DEFEASED, VARIOUS, -, N/A, NA, UNKNOWN
    geocodable_denominator      34,120
    geocoded                    33,219
    COVERAGE                    97.36%   of geocodable

THE REAL REMAINING GAP IS ABOUT 901 PROPERTIES, NOT ~24,700.

WHY THE FIGURES DIVERGE. The 51% number counts a denominator that includes addresses which
CAN NEVER GEOCODE -- defeased and placeholder entries whose address field is blank or
literal "VARIOUS". Excluding them is not generosity; it is the same denominator definition
br-1ni6's geo_coverage_pct uses, pinned to the same normalization macros so the two cannot
drift. A coverage rate computed over ungeocodable rows is not a coverage rate.
The 50,593 row count is also a different grain from 38,365 distinct properties, so the two
statements were never comparable to begin with.

WHAT THIS CHANGES IN THIS BEAD AND ACROSS THE EPIC:
1. GEOCODE COVERAGE IS NOT THE BINDING CONSTRAINT ON THE PROPERTY BOOK. I described it as a
   ceiling that "binds before canon geo does any work." At 97.36% of geocodable it does not.
   Strike that framing wherever it appears.
2. WHAT REMAINS A REAL LIMIT, UNCHANGED:
   - `Various` addresses genuinely never geocoded, and there are 4,245 placeholder identities.
     They still need the Annex A parse (edgar-elt br-6iii), not geometry, and they are still
     excluded-and-counted per OC-0048's denominator-honesty criterion.
   - Ginnie Mae still has no address field at its native pool grain.
   - The AGENCY tables are a separate and much larger population that is genuinely NOT
     geocoded yet -- cmdrvl-curves bd-25xz covers roughly 90,000 records (15,579 Ginnie
     street addresses plus 74,349 HUD FHA multifamily at city/state/zip). THAT is the real
     coverage gap for the agency corpora, and it is ON HOLD (bd-13mx).
3. bd-14hu's argument IMPROVES. Pre-resolving our own corpora looked weaker when half the
   property book appeared ungeocoded. At 97.36% the CMBS side is effectively ready to
   pre-resolve now, and the work concentrates on the agency tables rather than on backfill.

MEASURED GEOCODE HISTORY, for anyone sizing this work (2026-08-14, literal query):
WRGL_EDGAR_CMBS_GEOCODES__STRUCTURED -- 68,603 rows, 54,690 distinct PROPERTY_ADDRESS,
4,149 addresses appearing under more than one ASOF because the ETL appends rather than
upserts. Dominated by the 2025-01 initial load (45,114 rows) and an unexplained 2026-08
batch (14,714 rows / 14,242 distinct).

PROCESS NOTE: this is the fourth claim this session that came from prose rather than a
measured value, and the third that was wrong. The 51% figure was in a document I trusted;
the 97.36% figure was in a bead comment recording an actual query. WHEN TWO NUMBERS
DISAGREE, PREFER THE ONE WITH A RECORDED METHOD AND A DENOMINATOR DEFINITION.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
THE KILL-CRITERION COMPARATOR, MEASURED 2026-08-15. This bead's central deliverable. From
returned structured results, not prose.

== NAIVE ADDRESS-STRING BASELINE ==

Method: deduplicate to distinct (PROPERTY_ADDRESS, COUNTY_FIPS) across the five boroughs.
Map COUNTY_FIPS to MapPLUTO BOROUGH (36005=BX, 36047=BK, 36061=MN, 36081=QN, 36085=SI).
Normalize BOTH sides identically and deliberately stupidly — uppercase, strip all
non-alphanumerics, collapse whitespace. Join on exact normalized equality, scoped by
borough. Borough scoping is required: NYC reuses street names across boroughs, so an
unscoped join would manufacture matches.

  distinct CMBS addresses in scope        5,269
  matched at least one MapPLUTO lot       1,522   =  28.9%
  matched exactly one                     1,522
  matched more than one                       0
  max lots per address                        1

**NAIVE ADDRESS-STRING MATCHING ACHIEVES 28.9% COVERAGE ON THE FIVE-BOROUGH CMBS BOOK.**

The operator predicted 30-40% before any measurement. The measured answer is 28.9%.

== READING IT HONESTLY ==

1. THIS IS COVERAGE, NOT PRECISION. We do not yet know how many of the 1,522 are correct.
   But every match is an exact normalized string equality within the correct borough against
   a lot's own recorded address, so precision on the matched subset should be high. That is
   the characteristic profile of address matching: PRECISE WHERE IT FIRES, AND IT RARELY
   FIRES.

2. ZERO AMBIGUITY, WHICH IS ITSELF INFORMATIVE. No address matched more than one lot. That
   is a consequence of MapPLUTO storing exactly ONE address per lot — exact equality against
   a single stored string either hits or misses, it cannot be ambiguous. So the baseline has
   no ambiguity to resolve and no abstention to make; it simply answers 28.9% of the time
   and is silent otherwise.

3. THE 71.1% THAT DO NOT MATCH ARE THE ENTIRE PRODUCT. That population is where every
   measured failure lives — multi-address strings, Queens grid hyphenates, ranges, corner
   a/k/a alternates, and the large and corner lots whose true address is not the one
   MapPLUTO stored.

== THE TWO BASELINES SIDE BY SIDE ==

  naive address-string    28.9% coverage, unique when it fires, precision unmeasured
  geometry-only PIP       ~95% coverage (directional, needs fan-out correction on distinct
                          points), precision unmeasured, 157 five-borough points land in
                          more than one lot

These are two points on a coverage/precision plane, not two numbers to beat separately. Per
the risk-coverage framing, THE CASCADE MUST PASS ABOVE BOTH POINTS: higher precision than
geometry-alone at geometry's coverage, and materially more coverage than 28.9% at
address-grade precision. A cascade that merely raises coverage above 28.9% has beaten
nothing, because point-in-polygon already does that.

== WHAT REMAINS ON THIS BEAD ==
- Precision for both baselines, which requires the address-independent ground truth in
  bd-179b — scoring against PLUTO alone is circular because PLUTO's truth is address-to-BBL
  and the CMBS address is the thing being tested
- The geometry-only rate re-derived fan-out-aware on the 4,076 distinct points rather than
  on rows
- Tier-by-tier breakdown, with nearest_rooftop_match as its own slice
- The corrected chimera rate after two-sided normalization
- The property-cardinality distribution

title: [CANON-V1/P12.9] Extract current domain special cases through extension packages with parity
description:
## Background
Canon core currently contains Reg AB, CMBS, sec10d, BDC, tenant, and structured-finance-aware profiles, fixtures, commands, defaults, or apply assumptions. They helped bootstrap the architecture, but they make the open-source engine appear coupled to one use case and make downstream ownership ambiguous. Extraction is safe only after non-exact quality is measured and parity is explicit.

## Technical Approach
Produce a machine-readable inventory of every domain-bearing symbol, literal, profile, fixture, schema field, documentation promise, command branch, default path, and test. Classify each as generic engine capability, neutral example, external extension package, downstream adapter, historical plan, or removable duplicate. Define a versioned extension-package contract for normalization components, candidate operators, evidence extractors, relationship vocabularies, profile policy, registry namespace rules, corpus manifests, projection mappings, and quality gates. Move behavior through that contract in dependency order while preserving public artifact semantics and benchmark results. Use at least two unrelated external packages to prove that the seam is real. Do not delete files or old behavior without the separate explicit authorization required by repository policy.

## Success Criteria
- A source scan has zero unexplained CMBS, Reg AB, sec10d, BDC, or structured-finance literals in generic runtime paths and defaults.
- Every inventoried special case has one named generic destination and parity evidence.
- The engine can load unknown opaque package and profile identifiers without recompilation.
- Current Reg AB and CMBS fixtures retain exact output parity and non-exact quality within the P12 gates through external packages.
- Two neutral domains exercise the same package contract without domain branches in core.
- Canon distributions do not point by default into a sibling repository or private corpus.
- Package manifests and digests are recorded in every project artifact and evaluation report.

## Test Plan
Snapshot the inventory before extraction; run source-firewall tests and denylisted literal scans; execute all current domain fixtures through old and packaged paths; compare canonical IDs, decisions, evidence, refusals, diagnostics, performance, and registry output. Test missing, unknown, tampered, stale, and incompatible packages. Run neutral-package conformance and public-binary subprocess tests.

## RESERVATIONS
- src/cli.rs
- src/entity/profile.rs
- src/entity/apply.rs
- src/namekit/tenant.rs
- tests/entity_profile_firewall_contract.rs
- tests/entity_fixture_manifest.rs
- docs/IDENTITY_ARCHITECTURE.md
- docs/ENTITY_CONTRACT.md

## Considerations
This is extraction, not deletion-by-cleanup. Domain expertise remains valuable; ownership moves to packages maintained by the consuming domain. Generic legal-name normalization may remain core only when justified across domains and provenance-backed.
notes:
## Cross-repository acceptance
sec10d bd-26s implements the first domain-owned Reg AB firm identity extension package. Extraction parity is incomplete until that package loads through the generic contract, reproduces the existing exact surface and projection behavior, and passes the empirical non-exact quality gates without Reg AB branches in Canon core.
