title: canon geo D6: imagery observer lane, pinned licensed tiles, observer contract, rho admission, replay without regeneration
description:
PACKET PK-D6a (stage D6) from docs/PLAN_CANON_GEO.md §18/§19, course correction 2026-09-01. This bead carries the full design so no implementer needs the plan document.

== WHY ==
Appendix A stated the rule (a model is a source, not a solver; nondeterminism is banned, models are not) and Appendix J verified the sources from primary pages (NYS/NYC 6-inch orthos CC BY, 3DEP, NAIP via Planetary Computer, NOAA ERI; Google/Mapbox/Esri basemaps forbidden by their own terms). This bead makes the lane buildable: pinned image tiles (URL, byte range, ETag or digest, vintage, license text hash), an observer contract (rule-based, frozen-weight, or recorded-hosted identity with characterized regional error on a named population), typed observation kinds with their sound rho readings, and replay that verifies stored digests and never re-runs a model (I07). A vision model's label is a recorded observation with provenance; it enters the solver only through rho (N09). Screenshots of commercial basemaps and location-proposing models are CUT (§18.3).

### 18.4 The imagery and map evidence lane

Appendix A stated the rule: a model is a source, not a solver. Appendix J verified the
sources. This section makes the lane buildable.

**Sources, in order of first use.** NYS and NYC 6-inch orthoimagery (CC BY, even years
2006 to 2024, byte-range capable with ETags) for the proving ground. 3DEP lidar for measured
height. NAIP through the Planetary Computer mirror as the national fallback. NOAA
emergency response imagery for event-scoped change. Overture or OSM data for street
context, never a rendered commercial tile. Every image tile is pinned by URL, byte range,
ETag or SHA-256, vintage, and license text hash.

**Observer contract.** An observer is a deterministic function from pinned image bytes
and a pinned geometry window to typed observations. It declares: model identity and
weight hash (or "rule-based"), input tile digests, output observation kinds, the
population on which its regional error was characterized, the characterization digest, and
the `rho` band each observation kind induces. A vision model with frozen hashed weights in
controlled arithmetic qualifies. A hosted model whose output cannot be reproduced
byte-for-byte also qualifies, but only as a **recorded observation with provenance**:
Canon stores the label, the crop digest, the model version, and the prompt digest, and
replay never re-runs the model. In both cases the observation enters the solver only
through `rho`.

**Observation kinds** (each with its sound reading):

| Kind | Sound `rho` reading | Feeds |
|---|---|---|
| `structure_count_in_window` with error band | `gcc` lower/upper bound on latent structures inside the parcel or window | cardinality propagator |
| `footprint_outline` at vintage | one more footprint plane with its own within-source exclusivity; majority-parcel predicate applies | candidate universe, incidence |
| `height_or_floors` from 3DEP with density-derived error | integer band on floors; never a decider | additive band |
| `present_at_vintage` / `absent_at_vintage` | closed valid-time interval observation; diagnostic until the temporal solver lands, hard only as "absent at v implies not the 2019 structure" once dated | interval admission; later Allen/STP |
| `change_event` between two vintages | diagnostic flag that raises the next-evidence priority; never a constraint alone | next-evidence controller |

**Three uses, in order.** First, adjudication: ortho crops with candidate parcel lines
drawn on them are the cheapest stratified truth instrument for bd-179b's second source;
the crop and the label are the receipt. Second, the visual evidence card (bd-101v): ortho,
candidate parcels, forced set, ambiguous set, conflicting source records, all overlaid,
which is both the reviewer surface and the sales artifact. Third, solver input through the
kinds above, only after the observer's error is characterized on a named population.

**What stays forbidden.** A screenshot of a commercial basemap; a model answering "the
property is here"; any observer whose output is re-generated at replay; any imagery
observation admitted without a characterized error population.

== STAGE ROW (§19.5; entry condition, gate, contracts) ==
| D6 | Observer lane: NYC ortho pinning, one rule-based observer (footprint outline from a landed footprint plane as the null observer), one frozen-weight count observer, adjudication crops, evidence card | G2 passed (`card.rs` reads explanation artifacts); NYC ortho tile pins recorded with URL, byte range, ETag or SHA-256, vintage, and license text hash per §18.4; the named NYC error population declared before any observer runs; modules `observer.rs`, `adjudicate.rs`, `card.rs` | G6: observer error characterized on a named NYC population; observations admitted through rho on the D1 cohort change at least one residual or are shown redundant; card artifact validates | C09 to C12, C21, C22, C23, C25; T13, T14, T15, T22, T24, T26, T27 | new beads, bd-101v |

== MODULE SURFACE (§19.3; field lists are the required minimum, add #[serde(default)] fields only, never remove or rename) ==
**Dependency direction.** New modules depend on the existing `composition`, `evidence`,
`control`, `discovery`, `evaluation`, `geometry`, `geometry_value`, and `run` modules,
never the reverse. `src/geo/composition.rs` and `src/geo/evidence.rs` are not modified by
D2 to D6: `propagate` and `explain` call `solve_composition` as a black box and narrow or
re-solve `GeoCompositionRequest` values. Within the new set: `explain` consumes
`propagate`; `card`, `next_evidence`, and `inspect` consume `explain`; `exposure` and
`collision` consume `ledger`; `adjudicate` and `card` consume `observer`; nothing consumes
`inspect`.

**Shared shape.** Each module is `pub mod` in `src/geo/mod.rs` with `pub use module::*`.
Each defines `Geo<Module>Error { code: Geo<Module>ErrorCode, message: String, detail:
BTreeMap<String, String> }` with a `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` code enum that
carries the generic `UnsupportedVersion`, `InvalidInput`, `BudgetExceeded`,
`ArithmeticOverflow` variants plus the module's rows from §19.4. Each artifact type has a
`version: String` constant `CANON_GEO_<NAME>_VERSION`, `canonical_<name>_bytes`, and
`validate_<name>_artifact`. Each module ships `schemas/canon.geo.<name>.v0.schema.json`, a
`--describe` entry, a `canon geo <subcommand>`, and `tests/geo_<module>.rs`.

**`observer.rs`**

| Item | Definition |
|---|---|
| Consumes | `GeoRhoContract`, `GeoRhoObservation`, `GeoRhoObservationKind::IntegerSumBand`, `GeoValidTimeInterval`, `GeoEvidenceRecordRef`, `GeoIntegerMeasure`, `GeoIntegerValueOrigin::SourceAsserted`, `GeoCanonicalPolygonMm` for the window |
| `GeoImageTilePin` | `url`, `byte_range: Option<(u64, u64)>`, `etag: Option<String>`, `blake3`, `vintage: GeoValidTimeInterval`, `license_id`, `license_text_blake3` |
| `GeoObserverIdentity` | `RuleBased { rule_id, rule_version }`, `FrozenWeight { model_id, weight_blake3, arithmetic_contract }`, `RecordedHosted { model_id, model_version, prompt_blake3 }` |
| `GeoObservationKind` | `StructureCountInWindow`, `FootprintOutline`, `HeightOrFloors`, `PresentAtVintage`, `AbsentAtVintage`, `ChangeEvent` (§18.4 table) |
| `GeoObserverContract` | `id`, `version`, `identity: GeoObserverIdentity`, `output_kinds: Vec<GeoObservationKind>`, `error_population_id`, `characterization_blake3`, `rho_contract_ids: Vec<String>` |
| `GeoObservationRow` | `id`, `observer_id`, `tile_pins: Vec<GeoImageTilePin>`, `window_blake3`, `kind`, `payload: GeoObservationPayload` (one variant per kind: count band `{min, max}`, ring digest, floors band, vintage interval, vintage pair), `crop_blake3`, `label_blake3` |
| `GeoObservationRowsArtifact` | `version`, `contract: GeoObserverContract`, `rows: Vec<GeoObservationRow>`, `rho_observations: Vec<GeoRhoObservation>`, `diagnostic_only_ids: Vec<String>`, `not_admitted_ids: Vec<String>` |
| `pub fn admit_observations(contract: &GeoObserverContract, rows: &[GeoObservationRow], rho: &[GeoRhoContract], forbidden_license_ids: &[String]) -> Result<GeoObservationRowsArtifact, GeoObserverError>` | applies I06; every row's `kind` must be in `output_kinds`; every `rho_contract_ids` entry must exist in `rho` |
| `pub fn to_rho_observation(row: &GeoObservationRow, contract: &GeoObserverContract, universe: &GeoCompositionUniverse) -> Option<GeoRhoObservation>` | `StructureCountInWindow` and `HeightOrFloors` become `IntegerSumBand` (`unit` `structure` with value 1 per building candidate in the window, or `floor`; `value_origin` `SourceAsserted`); `PresentAtVintage`/`AbsentAtVintage` carry `valid_time` and are listed in `diagnostic_only_ids`; `FootprintOutline` and `ChangeEvent` return `None` (they enter through `materialize` and `next_evidence`) |
| `pub fn verify_replay(artifact: &GeoObservationRowsArtifact, bytes_by_blake3: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<u8>>) -> Result<(), GeoObserverError>` | recomputes tile, crop, and label digests; contains no call path to any identity (I07) |

== ERROR CODES (§19.4; class is exactly one of refusal / abstention / typed fallback; detail always carries the named ids) ==
| `observer_missing_provenance` | `observer::admit_observations` | any I06 field absent on the contract, a row, or a tile pin | refusal | T13 |
| `observer_error_uncharacterized` | `observer::admit_observations` | `error_population_id` or `characterization_blake3` empty, or a row `kind` not in `output_kinds` | refusal | T13 |
| `observer_license_forbidden` | `observer::admit_observations` | a tile pin `license_id` is in `forbidden_license_ids` or `license_text_blake3` is empty (N10) | refusal | T13 |
| `image_tile_digest_mismatch` | `observer::verify_replay`, `adjudicate::validate_adjudication_receipt` | bytes supplied for a pin, crop, or label hash differently from the stored `blake3` | refusal | T14 |
| `observation_regenerated_at_replay` | `observer::verify_replay` | caller supplies a row whose `label_blake3` or payload digest differs from the stored artifact, or requests identity invocation during replay (I07) | refusal | T14 |
| `observation_temporal_diagnostic` | `observer::to_rho_observation` | `PresentAtVintage` or `AbsentAtVintage` before dated composition exists | abstention: id listed in `diagnostic_only_ids`, no hard constraint (T15) | T15 |

== CONTRACTS (§19.9) ==
| C09 | `admit_observations` refuses any contract, row, or pin missing an I06 field, any `kind` outside `output_kinds`, any empty `error_population_id` or `characterization_blake3`, and any pin whose `license_id` is forbidden or whose `license_text_blake3` is empty | `observer.rs` | I06, N09, N10 |
| C10 | `verify_replay` recomputes tile, crop, and label digests from supplied bytes and contains no call path to any `GeoObserverIdentity`; a differing digest refuses | `observer.rs` | I07, N02 |
| C11 | An observation enters the solver only through `to_rho_observation` as a `GeoRhoObservation` under a declared `rho_contract_ids` entry; `PresentAtVintage` and `AbsentAtVintage` are listed in `diagnostic_only_ids` and induce no hard constraint until dated composition exists | `observer.rs` | N03, §18.4 kinds table |
| C22 | Every artifact type declares `CANON_GEO_<NAME>_VERSION`, `canonical_<name>_bytes`, `validate_<name>_artifact`, and a `schemas/canon.geo.<name>.v0.schema.json`; canonical bytes are byte-identical across platforms | all §19.3 modules | N02, §19.3 shared shape |
| C23 | Artifacts built from `tests/fixtures/geo/` or `scripts/geo_demo/` inputs carry `source_dataset` pins beginning `fixture.` and are never read by a G-gate test or cited as a measurement | all §19.3 modules | N07 |
| C25 | D2 to D6 do not modify `src/geo/composition.rs` or `src/geo/evidence.rs`; new modules call `solve_composition` as a black box, and generic modules carry no fixture, demo, or county literal | all §19.3 modules | §19.3 dependency direction, G7 |

== THREATS THIS BEAD MUST DEFEAT (§19.9) ==
| TH08 | A hosted or frozen model is re-run at replay and its fresh output replaces the stored observation | `verify_replay` has no identity call path; digest mismatch refuses | C10; T14; `observation_regenerated_at_replay`, `image_tile_digest_mismatch` |
| TH09 | A commercial basemap tile enters through a pin with a missing or mislabeled license | License gate on `license_id` and `license_text_blake3`; forbidden list is an input, never a constant a module can drop | C09; T13; `observer_license_forbidden` |
| TH10 | A vision model proposes a location, or an uncharacterized observer's output reaches the solver as a hard constraint | Observations enter only through `rho` under a characterized error population; vintage kinds stay diagnostic | C09, C11; T13, T15; `observer_error_uncharacterized`, `observation_temporal_diagnostic` |
| TH20 | Proof-class inflation: Demo 0 output, fixtures, or retained evidence cited as a live measurement or gate pass | `fixture.` pins on every fixture-derived artifact; G-gate tests read only their frozen fixtures; measurement receipts require runtime-selected subjects with a recorded seed | C23, N07; T26, T16 |
| TH21 | Demo-path hard-coding: a generic module special-cases Demo 0 ids, the chimera constraint ids, or Franklin County names to pass its tests | Case-insensitive literal scan over the twelve generic modules; property tests on seeded random components | C25; T27, T03, T16 |

== TESTS (§19.6; ship in tests/geo_<module>.rs with the T ids in test names; each row's Negative case is mandatory) ==
| T13 | D6 | unit | three `GeoObserverContract` and pin variants: `FrozenWeight` with empty `weight_blake3`; `characterization_blake3 == ""`; a tile pin with `license_id = "commercial_basemap_tos"` listed in `forbidden_license_ids` | each `admit_observations` call returns `Err` with the matching code and `detail["field"]` naming the missing or forbidden field | a complete contract and a CC BY pin admit with `not_admitted_ids.is_empty()` | C09; TH09, TH10 | `observer_missing_provenance`, `observer_error_uncharacterized`, `observer_license_forbidden` |
| T14 | D6 | e2e | a `GeoObservationRowsArtifact` with one `StructureCountInWindow` row and a `bytes_by_blake3` map holding the pinned tile, crop, and label bytes | `verify_replay` returns `Ok(())`; the T27 literal scan finds no identity invocation in `observer.rs` replay path | flipping one byte of the tile refuses `image_tile_digest_mismatch` with `detail["tile"]`; a row whose `label_blake3` differs from the stored artifact refuses `observation_regenerated_at_replay` with `detail["observation_id"]` | C10; TH08 | `image_tile_digest_mismatch`, `observation_regenerated_at_replay` |
| T15 | D6 | unit | a `PresentAtVintage` row over the universe of `temporal_occupancy_cannot_be_smuggled_in_as_timeless_property_identity` in `tests/geo_evidence_compilation.rs` | `to_rho_observation` returns `Some` with `valid_time == Some(interval)`; the row id is in `diagnostic_only_ids`; the compiled request has `hard_constraints.is_empty()` and `residual_model_count == 3` | an implementation that emits a `Require` from the vintage observation changes `residual_model_count` and fails | C11; TH10 | `observation_temporal_diagnostic` |
| T27 | D2 to D7 | adversarial | the twelve generic module files listed in §19.3 | a case-insensitive scan finds none of the literals `1004540041`, `chimera_wrongly_admitted`, `asserted_address_core`, `case_4`, `franklin`, `solve_composition` (the last only in `inspect.rs`), or any hosted-model client symbol in `observer.rs` replay code | the scan must also match `Franklin` and `CASE_4`; a scan that is case-sensitive fails on a seeded scratch copy | C18, C25; TH16, TH21 | none |

== NON-NEGOTIABLES AND INVARIANTS ==
### 19.1 Non-negotiables

- N01 Runtime lookup stays exact registry replay. Geo is a build-time workbench.
- N02 Same input plus same pinned sources reproduce byte-identical artifacts on every
  platform. No wall clock, locale, hash-map order, or float comparison in a decision path.
- N03 Every source value enters the solver only through a declared, versioned `rho`.
- N04 Adding admitted hard evidence may only narrow the model set or make it empty.
- N05 Source count is provenance, never evidence weight or confidence.
- N06 Candidate reach, admission, solver exactness, reconciliation, truth quality, and
  cost are reported as separate planes and never pooled.
- N07 Fixtures, retained evidence, and mocked providers are never presented as live proof.
- N08 Abstention is a legitimate output; an abstention-only module is not a delivered
  feature.
- N09 No vision or statistical model proposes a location. Models are observers with
  characterized error.
- N10 No commercial basemap imagery or tiles enter any artifact.
- N11 Gates are frozen in tests. A gate is passed by meeting it, never by editing it.
- N12 Every feature bead ships its code and its tests together, including at least one
  negative case a naive implementation fails.

### 19.2 Invariants for the new artifacts

- I01 A propagator prunes a value only with a typed reason naming constraint id and
  evidence ids; pruning is sound: enumeration with propagation equals enumeration without.
- I02 Propagator fixpoint is order-independent; tests run every permutation of propagator
  order on each fixture and compare bytes.
- I03 A minimal core is minimal: removing any one member restores satisfiability; tests
  verify by re-solving each deletion.
- I04 A correction set hits every enumerated core; when core enumeration hits its ceiling
  the artifact says `cores_complete=false` and no minimality claim is made.
- I05 Explanation artifacts name source record ids and rho contract ids, never internal
  indices.
- I06 An observer observation carries image tile digest, vintage, license hash, model or
  rule identity, weight or prompt digest, and the error-population digest; missing any
  field refuses.
- I07 Observer output is stored, never regenerated at replay; replay verifies the stored
  digest chain only.
- I08 A ledger row binds accession, loan id, parcel set, building set, truth plane,
  claim class, model count, exactness flags, and every source release pin; rows with
  candidate reach `none` carry the reason and no sets.
- I09 A ledger row never pools truth planes; non-round and round exact-lender evidence
  stay labeled.
- I10 The retry loop is bounded by a declared pass count; each pass is a normal pinned
  run and the loop artifact lists every pass with its abstention reason.
- I11 Event exposure joins building geometry, not centroids; advisory source hashes travel
  with the result.
- I12 Cross-deal collision reports a parcel or building shared by more than one trust
  with both accessions; pari passu participation is a labeled explanation, not a suppressed
  row.
- I13 `geo inspect` reads only emitted artifacts and receipts; it computes nothing that
  changes an answer.
- I14 Next-evidence recommendations expose the nondominated frontier and never manufacture
  a total ranking without a declared loss model.

== COMMANDS ==
### 19.7 Commands

Whole-tree gates run on every commit in every stage. Per-module binaries are the
`tests/geo_<module>.rs` files from §19.3; each stage runs its own set before claiming its
gate. `rg` exit status 1 means no match, which is the pass for the literal scans, so
they are written with a leading `!`.

```bash
# Whole-tree gates
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test

# Frozen E4 gate (T17, C24): expected red until G1, green from G1 on
cargo test --test geo_adjudication e4_acceptance_gate_requires_the_full_population_to_be_reachable -- --ignored

# Per-module test binaries (stage: test ids)
cargo test --test geo_propagate           # D2: T01 to T04, T19
cargo test --test geo_explain             # D2: T05, T06, T20, T21
cargo test --test geo_ledger              # D3: T07, T23, T26
cargo test --test geo_exposure            # D3: T08
cargo test --test geo_collision           # D3: T09
cargo test --test geo_retry               # D4: T10
cargo test --test geo_condo               # D4: T11
cargo test --test geo_inspect             # D4: T12, T25
cargo test --test geo_next_evidence       # D5: T18
cargo test --test geo_observer            # D6: T13, T14, T15
cargo test --test geo_adjudicate          # D6: T22 (new binary; distinct from the existing geo_adjudication)
cargo test --test geo_card                # D6: T24, T26
cargo test --test geo_e5_franklin_parcel  # D7: T16 plus the existing literal scan

# One test by name with output
cargo test --test geo_propagate soundness_holds_on_every_e4_fixture -- --nocapture

# Schema drift guard (C22). tests/geo_schemas.rs include_str!s each schema file, pins
# title, properties.version.const, and additionalProperties == false, then walks a real
# serialized instance against the schema; there is no jsonschema crate. Each new
# artifact adds one <name>_schema_matches_a_real_instance test there and one
# include_str! of schemas/canon.geo.<name>.v0.schema.json.
cargo test --test geo_schemas
cargo test --test geo_schemas propagation_schema_matches_a_real_instance
for s in propagation explanation separation_request separation observer observation_rows \
         image_tile_pin adjudication_request adjudication_receipt evidence_card \
         collateral_ledger event_exposure cross_deal retry_loop inspection next_evidence \
         condo_bridge_request ledger_bridge; do
  jq -e --arg s "$s" '.title == "canon.geo.\($s).v0"
    and .properties.version.const == "canon_geo_\($s).v0"
    and .additionalProperties == false' "schemas/canon.geo.${s}.v0.schema.json"
done

# --describe entries for geo subcommands (C22: one per new module, named after it:
# geo propagate, geo explain, geo observer, geo adjudicate, geo card, geo ledger,
# geo exposure, geo collision, geo retry, geo inspect, geo next-evidence, geo condo)
cargo run --bin canon -- --describe \
  | jq -r '.subcommands[] | select(.name | startswith("geo ")) | "\(.name)\t\(.status)\t\(.output_schema)"'
cargo run --bin canon -- --describe \
  | jq -e '[.subcommands[] | select(.name == "geo propagate" and .status == "implemented")] | length == 1'

# T27 literal scan (C25, G7). Mirrors tests/geo_e5_franklin_parcel.rs
# franklin_instance_names_do_not_enter_the_generic_geo_engine, which lowercases each
# generic source file and asserts it contains no instance literal.
GEO_GENERIC="src/geo/propagate.rs src/geo/explain.rs src/geo/observer.rs src/geo/adjudicate.rs \
  src/geo/card.rs src/geo/ledger.rs src/geo/exposure.rs src/geo/collision.rs src/geo/retry.rs \
  src/geo/inspect.rs src/geo/next_evidence.rs src/geo/condo.rs"
! rg -i -n 'franklin|39049|epsg:3735|1004540041|chimera_wrongly_admitted|asserted_address_core|case_4' $GEO_GENERIC
! rg -n 'solve_composition' src/geo/inspect.rs
! rg -i -n 'reqwest|hyper::|openai|anthropic|gemini|bedrock|invoke_model' src/geo/observer.rs
cargo test --test geo_e5_franklin_parcel franklin_instance_names_do_not_enter_the_generic_geo_engine

# Demo 0, capabilities, measurement plan, beads
bash scripts/geo_demo/demo0.sh --work-dir /tmp/demo0
cargo run --bin canon -- geo capabilities --emit json
cargo run --bin canon_geo_measurements -- --emit plan
br ready --json && br dep cycles --json
```

ANTI-REWARD-HACKING (AGENTS.md, binding):
- Code and tests ship in this bead; no scope-splitting into type/impl/test closures.
- No new todo!()/unimplemented!() scaffolds. Refusal-only implementation earns partial credit and never closes this bead (label refusal-only + follow-up bead if that is the honest state).
- Fixtures and Demo 0 outputs are never presented as live proof (C23). Gate thresholds are never edited to pass (C24, N11).
- Every feature test includes at least one negative case a naive implementation fails (the Negative case column below).
- Generic modules carry no fixture, demo, or county literal (C25, T27).

== 2026-09-02 TEST LOGGING, E2E SCRIPT, RESERVATIONS, AND D6 OWNERSHIP SPLIT (coverage pass round 1) ==

OWNERSHIP SPLIT. §19.5 D6 lists five work items: NYC ortho pinning, one rule-based observer (footprint outline from a landed footprint plane as the null observer), one frozen-weight count observer, adjudication crops, evidence card. This bead owns the observer CONTRACT, admission, rho conversion, tile pin type, license gate, and replay (observer.rs, T13 to T15). The other items now have owners: bd-2g4z (NYC ortho tile pins recorded with URL, byte range, ETag or SHA-256, vintage, license text hash, plus the named NYC error population declared before any observer runs; this bead depends on it, matching the D6 entry condition), bd-35zz (the rule-based null observer and the redundancy baseline), bd-3ufk (the frozen-weight count observer, its NYC characterization, and the G6 measurement), bd-1ehd (vintage observations bound into ledger rows, the §18.2 dated existence capability), bd-36sc (adjudication receipts), bd-101v (card). Three additive contracts land in observer.rs under the §19.3 shared shape and are owned here even when another bead lands them first: `canon_geo_error_population.v0` (bd-2g4z), `canon_geo_observer_characterization.v0` (bd-35zz and bd-3ufk), `canon_geo_observer_effect.v0` (bd-3ufk). The `geo observer` subcommand family (`admit`, `verify-replay`, `to-rho`, `null`, `characterize`, `effect`) is one clap subcommand tree owned here; other beads add leaves.

Every test in tests/geo_observer.rs carries its T id in the function name and, on failure, panics with a message assembled from the values below (a local `fail!` macro that also `eprintln!`s so `-- --nocapture` shows them).

T13 (three refusing variants and one admitting): per variant log the serialized `GeoObserverContract` (identity variant, `weight_blake3` or `rule_id`, `error_population_id`, `characterization_blake3`, `output_kinds`, `rho_contract_ids`), the pin (`license_id`, `license_text_blake3`, `blake3`, `vintage`), the `forbidden_license_ids` list, the returned code, and `detail["field"]`. On the admitting half log `not_admitted_ids`, `diagnostic_only_ids`, and `rho_observations.len()`.
T14 (replay by digest only): per stored digest log the key (`tile`, `crop`, `label`), the expected BLAKE3, the recomputed BLAKE3, the byte length supplied, and on the negative halves `detail["tile"]` or `detail["observation_id"]`; log the T27 scan result for the replay path (`reqwest`, `hyper::`, `openai`, `anthropic`, `gemini`, `bedrock`, `invoke_model`, `std::process::Command`).
T15 (vintage kinds are diagnostic): log the `GeoRhoObservation` returned (`valid_time`, `kind`), `diagnostic_only_ids`, the compiled request's `hard_constraints.len()`, and `residual_model_count` before and after admission (expected unchanged at 3); on the negative half log the `Require` the wrong implementation emitted.
T27: file, line, literal, scratch path.

E2E script scripts/geo_demo/e2e_observer.sh (`set -euo pipefail`; echoes each command, exit code, and the BLAKE3 of every artifact into <work-dir>/run.log):
1. `bash scripts/geo_demo/demo0.sh --work-dir <dir>`.

title: [BDC/R6] Reconcile private decisions at canonical record grain
description: The private evaluator looks up target/reference material through lane + canonical RecordLinkInput record_id, then discards that record key and reconciles only by normalized issuer-surface material. This collapses distinct tranche/assignment rows for the same issuer and raises private_identity_conflict across valid row-level match/ambiguity outcomes. Aggregate-only evidence: 1,337 canonical target records each occur once with zero record-level conflicts, while surface-only collapse produces 55 artificial conflicts. Reconcile private decisions with a privacy-safe composite bound to source lane + canonical record_id + material hash; preserve material continuity without asserting one assignment outcome per issuer surface. Acceptance: same material on distinct canonical records may carry distinct decisions; repeat decision for one canonical record must remain consistent; match reference decision is likewise bound to left lane + canonical record_id + material; focused tests/build pass; two evaluator runs produce byte-identical sanitized reports or the next genuine gate.
close_reason: Completed: private decision reconciliation now uses a privacy-safe digest bound to source lane + canonical record_id + independently bound material hash; distinct records sharing material no longer conflict while repeat inconsistent decisions still refuse; 17 focused tests passed initially and 21/21 passed with the final evaluator; two full evaluator runs emitted byte-identical sanitized reports and cleared private_identity_conflict.

title: [CANON-V1/P09.3] Add an optional Splink candidate-and-evidence adapter
description:
## Background
Splink may provide scalable probabilistic linkage and useful comparison diagnostics for some operators. Its probabilities and learned parameters must remain suggestions within Canon's evidence/review boundary.

## Technical Approach
Implement a subprocess/file adapter that exports pinned observations and comparison configuration, invokes a pinned Splink environment through the bounded runner, and imports candidate pairs plus typed comparison/evidence records. Record model/training/config/software digests and map probabilities to context/support evidence under explicit policy; never auto-promote based solely on an adapter score.

## Success Criteria
- Splink candidates and comparisons are reproducible when the external environment declares deterministic behavior.
- Every score traces to model, parameters, input, and software version.
- Adapter failures or absence do not affect native workflows or registry state.
- Canon review/explain shows Splink evidence distinctly from native and trusted-anchor evidence.

## Test Plan
Against a pinned local environment or frozen adapter output, test candidate parity, model/config changes, shuffled inputs, missing values, large outputs, timeout/resource failure, malformed probabilities, and registry no-mutation.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/adapters/splink.rs`
- `tests/splink_adapter_e2e.rs`
- `docs/ADAPTERS.md`

## Considerations
Do not expose Python objects or Splink schemas as Canon's public contract; the adapter translates at the boundary.
close_reason: Retired: Splink wraps Fellegi-Sunter + EM (textbook). Ported native as bd-1rlk. Scale backend is its only unique asset, irrelevant at our scale. Reopen only if an operator brings a trained model via generic seam bd-3ofg. See docs/DECISION_PORT_TECHNIQUES_OVER_ADAPTERS.md.

title: [CANON-V1/P12.2] Build a sealed, leakage-resistant corpus and split conformance harness
description:
## Background
Entity-resolution metrics are meaningless when the same aliases, entities, documents, or derived labels leak across tuning and holdout partitions. Canon must standardize evaluation mechanics while leaving substantive corpora under domain ownership.

## Technical Approach
Extend the generic corpus contract with entity-grouped and time-aware splits, source-family grouping, immutable train/tune/holdout manifests, label confidence and adjudicator provenance, license/redaction metadata, and cryptographic commitments to hidden labels. Validate that canonical entities, alias surfaces, derived mutations, document families, and duplicated observations cannot cross forbidden split boundaries. Support three holdout modes: alias-disjoint for incumbent attachment, entity-disjoint for novel clustering, and time-forward for future-source generalization. Report exact-known rows in a separate stratum.

## Success Criteria
- A corpus cannot be evaluated when labels, surfaces, entities, derived variants, or source documents leak across declared boundaries.
- Holdout label hashes are committed before strategy selection and the runner records whether labels were accessible.
- Private corpora and invented public corpora share the same contract without leaking private content.
- Row duplication changes prevalence telemetry, not entity-discovery denominators.
- Train/tune/holdout changes create a new corpus version and invalidate dependent results.

## Test Plan
Create planted leakage fixtures for shared entity, alias, normalized form, source document, mutation seed, and duplicate row. Exercise valid alias-disjoint, entity-disjoint, and time-forward splits. Run twice with shuffled manifest and row order and compare canonical results. Test missing license, redaction, and adjudication metadata refusals.

## RESERVATIONS
- src/evaluation/corpus.rs
- schemas/canon.evaluation.corpus.v1.schema.json
- tests/evaluation_corpus_splits.rs
- tests/fixtures/extensions/neutral-domain/evaluation/

## Considerations
The harness protects evaluation integrity; it must not prescribe what an organization, patient, product, or financial counterparty means.
close_reason: Completed reserved-file split conformance harness and leakage fixtures; validation: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --test evaluation_corpus --test evaluation_corpus_splits -- -D warnings; cargo test --quiet --test evaluation_corpus; cargo test --quiet --test evaluation_corpus_splits

title: [CANON-V1/P06.17] Prove an out-of-tree demanding deployment without Canon awareness
description:
## Background
The extension boundary is credible only if an operator can solve a complex real domain while Canon remains unaware of that domain. The initiating operator intends a large counterparty deployment, but its proprietary or industry-specific assets must stay outside the open-source product.

## Technical Approach
Create a black-box conformance journey whose external workspace supplies its ontology, roles, identifier namespaces, source mappings/providers, profiles, evidence policy, hard-negative corpus, review policy, temporal facts, registry recipe, and export projections. Canon receives only generic packages through public CLI/SDK contracts. Public CI uses an invented neutral twin; an optional local acceptance target can point at the operator's private deployment.

## Success Criteria
- No Canon source, built-in schema enum, default, fixture, or required documentation names the operator's industry.
- The external deployment can cluster entities, link datasets, preserve related/distinct and assignments, review/promote facts, compile exact snapshots, and export dbt/search outputs.
- Swapping to the neutral twin requires no engine changes.
- A source scan and command trace prove there are no domain conditionals or hidden plugin privileges.

## Test Plan
Run the public neutral journey in CI and the external local journey when assets are supplied. Exercise offline, read-only, interrupt/resume, shuffled inputs, hard negatives, package tampering, and query final outputs. Log only non-sensitive commands, digests, metrics, and filesystem deltas.

## RESERVATIONS
- `tests/extensions_end_to_end.rs`
- `tests/fixtures/extensions/neutral-domain`
- `docs/EXTENSIONS.md`

## Considerations
The application may be structured finance, healthcare, commerce, or anything else. Canon's acceptance claim is extension completeness, not built-in expertise.
notes:
## Demanding-deployment acceptance
Exercise all R1-R5 twice: license-safe invented neutral analogues in public CI and real BDC issuer cases in a private local target. The proof must include a core source scan for BDC/finance vocabulary and must succeed without a fork, domain conditional, private-data dependency, optional matcher, or transport-specific review workflow.

title: [ENT-P07] Signed-graph solver with hard cannot-link constraints
description:

Purpose:
Solve candidate surfaces into existing IDs, promotable new IDs, escrow, or contradictions using a signed evidence graph. Hard cannot-link facts are constraints, not negative weights. The solver must split, abstain, or contradict when a component contains hard negatives; it must never outscore a trusted contradiction.

- Errors: E_ENTITY_CANNOT_LINK_OVERRIDE, E_ENTITY_ARTIFACT_CONTRACT.

- Tests: EN-S001..EN-S005.

Acceptance criteria:
- `canon_entity_solve.v0` summarizes resolved existing, promotable new, escrow, contradictions, entities, review groups, and decision-ledger path.
- Solver enforces hard cannot-link constraints and stable tie-breaking.
- Component diagnostics expose strongest positive and negative cuts.
- Review groups are emitted by surface cluster or ambiguity pattern, not raw row.

title: [CANON-V1/P03] Canon strategy as canonical procedural knowledge
description:
## Background
Canon strategy is intentionally retained. Registries store canonical declarative knowledge; strategies store canonical procedural knowledge. The current lifecycle is valuable but its relation to entity/resolve YAML strategies, project manifests, packaging, and safe script execution must become explicit.

## Scope
Define typed strategy kinds; clarify identity strategy versus task/schema champion semantics; package and pin strategies; harden the audit executor with time/resource/environment/network controls; integrate receipts, signatures, lifecycle operations, project dependencies, and deterministic tournament evaluation.

## Success Criteria
Canon strategy remains a first-class command family with no capability loss. Every selected strategy is typed, pinned, explainable, safely audited, versioned, diffable, and usable as a project dependency.

## Test Plan
Mixed-kind registry fixtures, executor timeout and isolation tests, malicious/hung script cases, lifecycle mutation/no-mutation matrices, project resolution E2E, tournament holdout tests, and deterministic receipts.

title: [CANON-V1/P06.13] Standardize domain-owned gold corpora and hard-negative evaluation
description:
## Background
A generic engine needs evaluation contracts that let each operator prove precision, recall, abstention, relationships, and temporal behavior on private or redistributable domain data without checking that data into Canon.

## Technical Approach
Define corpus manifests for observations, cluster labels, cross-dataset pairs, identifiers, hard negatives, relationships, assignments, temporal changes, adjudication confidence, train/tune/holdout partitions, provenance, license, and redaction. Define generic metrics including false-merge severity and exact-replay coverage. Ensure tournament runners cannot read holdout labels during tuning.

## Success Criteria
- Private and public corpora use the same manifest while data may stay out of tree.
- Metrics work for unknown ontology and role IDs.
- Hard negatives and abstention quality are first-class, not buried under aggregate recall.
- Partition leakage, duplicates, inconsistent labels, and license gaps are detected.

## Test Plan
Ship only invented neutral corpora; run schema/consistency/leakage checks, baseline exact and native strategies, metric determinism, and private-path references that do not leak content.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/evaluation/corpus.rs`
- `schemas/canon.evaluation.corpus.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/evaluation_corpus.rs`

## Considerations
Canon standardizes evidence about quality; the operator owns substantive labels and distribution rights.

title: [CANON-V1/P04.9] Measure coverage gain, review yield, drift, and accretion velocity
description:
## Background
The flywheel must prove that each review and provider investment makes Canon more useful. Raw registry size can grow while true coverage or decision quality gets worse.

## Technical Approach
Define versioned metrics across frozen corpora and project receipts: weighted exact coverage, unique unresolved groups, ambiguity/contradiction rate, reviewed-to-promoted yield, median age, repeat recurrence after promotion, hard-negative regressions, cross-project reuse, and time/cost bands. Attribute deltas to registry and strategy versions without collecting raw identities by default.

## Success Criteria
- Metrics compare like-for-like corpora and visibly flag corpus or policy changes.
- Coverage gains are separated into new aliases, new entities, remaps, provider additions, and temporal effects.
- A promotion that improves recall but harms hard negatives or creates repeat unresolved events is visible.
- Reports are deterministic, privacy-aware, and queryable as JSON plus concise summary.

## Test Plan
Use synthetic histories containing genuine improvement, registry bloat, regression, corpus drift, and review backlog. Verify attribution math, missing intervals, redaction, and deterministic reports.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/inbox/metrics.rs`
- `schemas/canon.accretion.metrics.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/inbox_metrics.rs`

## Considerations
Metrics guide investment; they must not become thresholds that pressure reviewers to accept uncertain matches.

title: [SPLINK-STEAL/S7] review packets: additive per-pair score decomposition (evidence waterfall)
description:
## Problem this solves
Reviewers deciding escrow items need to see WHY a pair scored 31 against a backbone threshold of 32 — which operators contributed what — in one glance. canon entity explain has the data, but review artifacts do not present it additively, so reviewers context-switch to explain output per item. Fast per-item comprehension is what makes the residual (post-S1/S2) review queue cheap. The review-substrate decision doc (docs/DECISION_REVIEW_VIA_EMAIL_CROWDSOURCING.md) already names "self-contained evidence-waterfall packets" as core substrate — this bead implements that presentation.

## Build
Extend review export (queue + native-review JSON/CSV/HTML) with a per-item ordered contribution breakdown:
- Each evidence hit as (lane, operator, view/field, integer score units, running cumulative total).
- Threshold lines (backbone_score_min, attach_score_min, abstain_margin) rendered against the cumulative so the shortfall or surplus is visible at a glance.
- Static offline HTML renders it as a simple bar/waterfall table using the existing static projection (no new JS deps, no new renderer).
- Redaction follows the existing review-artifact contract; the decomposition must not leak values the artifact would otherwise redact.

## Splink reference (clone at /Users/zac/Source/opensource/splink)
- splink/internals/waterfall_chart.py and linker_components/visualisations.py waterfall_chart — additive log2 decomposition (prior + per-comparison + TF terms) with a remove_sensitive_data variant. Port the presentation concept onto canon integer score units.

## How to test
- Golden snapshot test of a review packet with decomposition.
- Integer invariant: sum of listed contributions equals the recorded pair score exactly, for every item in the fixture corpus (property test).
- Redacted variant contains no raw values (scan test).
- HTML projection renders with a network-disabled browser.
- Byte-stable ordering: (lane, operator, field) sort is deterministic under input shuffle.

## Doctrine constraints
Presentation of existing artifact data only — no new scoring, no semantics change, no new renderer or import format (bd-14m6 substrate rules apply).

## RESERVATIONS
- src/entity/review_export.rs (shared with S2 — serialize if both in flight)
- tests/entity_review_waterfall.rs

title: canon geo run — resumable offline orchestration with one content-addressed run manifest
description:
WHY

An interrupted agent currently has no single validated object saying which Geo artifacts exist, which inputs produced them, what is reusable, or where to resume. Repeating acquisition and exact solves is expensive and risks mixing releases.

DELIVER

Implement canon_geo_run.v0 and canon geo run --plan PLAN --work-dir DIR. The command orchestrates only declared offline leaf capabilities, resumes by default, and commits immutable phase outputs through atomic same-filesystem publication.

Each run revision indexes question/capability/inventory/profile/plan/budget hashes, phase and gate state, source-release receipts, typed artifact references, deterministic usage counters, blockers/abstentions/contradictions/fallbacks, current answer status, next actions, and dependency edges used for invalidation.

State transitions are DRAFTED, PREFLIGHTED, MATERIALIZED, REACH_CHECKED, COMPILED, FACTORIZED, SOLVED, RECONCILED, and EVALUATED, with WAITING_FOR_INPUT, UNSUPPORTED_GRAIN, ABSTAINED, CONTRADICTED, and BUDGET_FALLBACK as explicit non-success states.

ACCEPTANCE

- Re-running an unchanged plan reuses hash-verified artifacts and is byte-identical at the semantic layer.
- Paths, timestamps, host identity, process id, and worker completion order do not enter semantic hashes.
- A phase is recorded complete only after its artifact validates and hashes.
- Crash test interrupts between artifact write and manifest publication; resume neither loses the artifact nor double-applies the phase.
- Missing acquisition produces WAITING_FOR_INPUT and an exact continuation action; Canon never reaches the network.
- Deterministic budget exhaustion preserves completed work and emits typed fallback; a faster machine cannot change the result.
- Negative test: changed source bytes under the same claimed digest refuse rather than reuse.
- Negative test: mixed releases or an incompatible profile never resume into an old compiled residual.
- Concurrent writers cannot silently corrupt or merge one work directory.

title: canon geo: spatial evidence operators (within, intersects, distance_lt, area_ratio, iou_gt)
description:
Spatial predicates as STRATEGY OPERATORS in the existing YAML surface -- the
same shape as exact / tolerance_pct / range / prefix today. Core stays
domain-free; the spatial vocabulary lives in the strategy.

OPERATORS:
  within            point in polygon
  intersects        polygon overlap, non-empty
  distance_lt       centroid or edge distance under a bound
  area_ratio        footprint area ratio within a band (rejects wrong-size match)
  iou_gt            intersection-over-union above a threshold
  constellation_consistent   deferred to its own bead; harder and not v1

Each operator emits EVIDENCE with a score and a named reason, so explain.rs can
answer 'why did X match Y' by pointing at operator outputs. Per canon's final
rule: if you cannot explain the match by pointing at assertion scores, it does
not ship.

ALSO: within-source mutual exclusion and distance-based hard negatives should be
expressed through anti_merge rather than a bespoke mechanism.

Depends on: geometry decision, skeleton
Parent: bd-2kjx
close_reason: Superseded by §18.3 / §3 rho discipline: spatial predicates are exact geometry-kernel predicates admitted through versioned rho contracts (src/geo/geometry.rs, geometry_value.rs, evidence.rs), not YAML strategy operators with thresholds. Threshold-scored operators are the 'preferences rank, constraints prune' violation §10.1 forbids.

comments.author: zac
comments.text:
NOTE 2026-08-14 from the measured NYC baseline (see bd-bmee): a point can legitimately fall inside MORE THAN ONE lot polygon — condo unit BBL overlapping the condo parent lot — so the 'within' operator must not assume a single containing polygon.

Two consequences for this bead:
1. 'within' returns a SET, not a boolean-plus-one-winner. Emitting one match silently discards a real ambiguity.
2. Within-source mutual exclusion is NOT universally true for NYC tax lots the way it is for building footprints. Two Overture buildings are not the same building, but a condo unit lot and its parent lot are legitimately overlapping records in the SAME source. Expressing lot overlap through anti_merge as a blanket rule would be wrong; the condo parent/unit relationship is a part_of relation (bd-3soj), not a distinctness violation.

The epic bd-2kjx lists WITHIN-SOURCE MUTUAL EXCLUSION as one of the five reasons geo is easier than person ER. That claim holds for building footprints and does NOT hold for NYC tax lots. Scope the assumption per source rather than globally.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
REALITY CHECK 2026-08-14 — THE "STRATEGY OPERATOR" PREMISE IS NOT SUPPORTED BY THE CODE.

This bead says: "Spatial predicates as STRATEGY OPERATORS in the existing YAML surface --
the same shape as exact / tolerance_pct / range / prefix today. Core stays domain-free;
the spatial vocabulary lives in the strategy."

Two problems, both verified.

1. THERE IS NO DECLARATIVE OPERATOR SURFACE. The ops named
   (exact/tolerance_pct/range/prefix) live in src/resolve/strategy.rs:8 as
   `const SUPPORTED_OPERATORS: &[&str]`, dispatched by a `match spec.op.as_str()` in
   src/resolve/assertions.rs:19-28 with `_ => Outcome::fail("unsupported_operator")`.
   That is a CLOSED VOCABULARY IN CORE RUST. "The vocabulary lives in the strategy" is
   false — the strategy only SELECTS from a list core defines. Every new operator is a
   core code change.

   The entity-side equivalent is the same shape: src/entity/profile.rs:855-886 defines
   SUPPORTED_SUPPORT_OPS (6 entries), SUPPORTED_CANNOT_LINK_OPS (10),
   SUPPORTED_RELATION_HINT_OPS (8). All closed. All textual. Not one takes a number.

2. THE SURFACE THIS BEAD POINTS AT IS THE ONE THE EPIC DISAVOWS. exact/tolerance_pct/
   range/prefix are in src/resolve/ — the two-tape CMBS tape matcher that bd-2kjx
   explicitly rejects as "the wrong substrate (see bd-3g5q, closed)". Do not build the
   spatial vocabulary there.

CORRECTED SHAPE: declare geo's operator vocabularies as THEIR OWN const arrays inside
src/geo/, parallel to entity's, sharing the artifact chain but not the vocabulary. Core
does change; that is unavoidable and is now the settled call (see bd-15ba). What stays
out of core is the DOMAIN CONVENTION layer — BBL semantics, condo parent/unit rules,
locale address conventions — which belongs in profiles and strategies.

OPERATOR SET — AMENDED FOR BYOP AND FOR THE MEASURED NYC FINDINGS:

  within          POINT-IN-POLYGON. Returns a SET, not a boolean-plus-winner (see the
                  2026-08-14 comment on this bead: a point can legitimately fall inside
                  a condo unit lot AND its parent lot). Emitting one match silently
                  discards a real ambiguity.
  intersects      polygon overlap, non-empty
  distance_lt     centroid or edge distance under a bound. NOTE: this is the operator
                  that carries the interpolated geocode tier — OC-0048 establishes that
                  range_interpolation and street_center points land in the right-of-way
                  where NO lot contains them. "Snap to nearest lot" is forbidden; this
                  operator GENERATES CANDIDATES which the address channel must then
                  corroborate or the cascade abstains.
  distance_gt     NEW — the spatial hard negative. Emits ScoreLane::AntiMerge with
                  hard_cannot_link=true. This is the "hard negatives exist" claim from
                  the epic, and it is NEW CODE: anti_merge.rs is two lexical helpers and
                  transfers only the lane, not the logic.
  area_ratio      footprint area ratio within a band (rejects wrong-size match)
  iou_gt          intersection-over-union above a threshold
  centroid_within NEW — cheap prefilter before exact PIP
  bbox_overlaps   NEW — the conservative filter stage; see bd-15ba on filtered
                  predicates. Must be provably conservative.

ATTRIBUTE OPERATORS THE CLIENT INPUT CONTRACT NOW REQUIRES (operator decision
2026-08-14: the six fields are geocode, address, geometry, building size, year built,
property type). These are NOT geometry but they are how wrong matches get REJECTED, and
canon has no numeric evidence operator at all today:

  size_ratio_within   building size agreement within a band. A 12,000 sf building is not
                      a 340,000 sf building even if the footprints overlap.
  year_built_within   year-built agreement within a tolerance. Cheap, strong negative
                      signal: a 1927 building and a 2019 building on the same footprint
                      means redevelopment, which is a TEMPORAL finding, not a match.
  category_compatible property type compatibility over a declared equivalence table
                      (office/mixed-use compatible; multifamily/industrial not).
                      Table lives in the profile, not core.

REQUIREMENT — EVERY OPERATOR EMITS STRUCTURED EVIDENCE, NOT PROSE. Verified problem:
existing helpers stuff their semantics into a format! string on EdgeEvidenceHit.explanation
(e.g. "relation hint relation=part_of left=... right=..."). A renderer or a downstream
consumer would have to PARSE PROSE. Geo operators must emit typed fields — measured
value, threshold, units, and the comparison outcome — alongside the human explanation.
bd-101v's card depends on this and cannot be built against explanation strings.

REQUIREMENT — GEOMETRY IS NOT A SUPPORTED VALUE TYPE YET. src/entity/record_link.rs:153
types features as Numeric|Date|Categorical. There is no geometry variant anywhere in the
evidence model. See the new geometry-typed-value bead; this bead is blocked on it.

ANTI-MERGE SCOPING — CORRECTED (reinforces the 2026-08-14 comment already on this bead):
within-source mutual exclusion is a PER-SOURCE DECLARED PROPERTY, not a global geo
invariant. It holds for building footprints. It does NOT hold for parcel/tax-lot sources
with condo aggregation. Under BYOP this becomes sharper still: WE DO NOT KNOW THE
CLIENT'S PARCEL LAYER SEMANTICS. The client must DECLARE whether their layer is
mutually exclusive; canon must refuse rather than assume. A wrong assumption here
suppresses true part_of relations (bd-3soj).

constellation_consistent is deferred to its own bead — THAT BEAD NOW EXISTS. It was
never created before this reality check.

title: [CANON-V1/P00.3] Cut the final entity CLI and dispatch scaffold against v1 artifacts
description:
## Background
Entity behavior must not depend on optional-flag accidents, and record linkage must not remain a sibling product. One CLI contract should select one artifact-backed engine and expose supported stages plus clear cluster/link entry points.

## Technical Approach
Define the final grammar under `canon entity`. Stage commands are `prepare`, `index build`, `block`, `evidence` (or the single contract-approved replacement for legacy `edge`), `solve`, `run`, `review`, `audit`, `promote`, `apply`, and `explain`. `canon entity link <REFERENCE> <TARGET>` is the ergonomic two-source linkage entry point and compiles into the same run/stage requests; project manifests may declare cluster, two-source link, or N-source link mode. Make profile/work-directory/project context explicit, centralize output/refusal routing, and pre-create narrow dispatch seams. Remove active legacy selection directly after parity; request deletion permission for obsolete files.

## Success Criteria
- The same invocation shape always selects the same engine.
- `entity link` retains cross-dataset functionality without a top-level `resolve` engine.
- Run/project mode and explicit stage execution share typed request boundaries.
- Help contains no org wording, ambiguous mode switch, or domain-specific command/default.
- Unknown/stale shapes produce actionable structured refusals.

## Test Plan
Parse and subprocess-smoke every command/mode and mutual exclusion; snapshot help; test intent/typo diagnostics; assert dispatch request types and stdout/stderr; and prove two-source shorthand compiles to the same plan/artifacts as an equivalent project manifest.

title: [CANON-V1/P07.R6d] Bind shared prepared surfaces to every record-link source lane
description: Public record_link_surface_bindings currently reduces each PreparedSurfaceRecord to one lexicographically first source_id. When the same normalized surface occurs in both record-link source lanes, provenance contains both source systems but only one lane receives a binding; the other side then refuses at block with missing_surface_binding. Emit deterministic RecordLinkSurfaceBindingInput entries per (surface_id, source_id), with source_row_ids restricted to provenance samples from that source. Preserve the source-row identity firewall: assignment IDs and record IDs remain non-authoritative. Add a neutral regression covering an exact shared surface across both sources plus repeated rows/assignments, prove both lanes bind, native link does not refuse, and output remains deterministic. No BDC/CMBS/domain-specific behavior.
notes: Private proof reproduced missing_surface_binding when one normalized surface spans both source lanes. First fix (per-source prepared-surface bindings) exposed the next required projection rule: dedicated record-link candidates may legitimately have identical left/right surface IDs at record grain, but generic block/edge artifacts must never receive self-pairs. Exact neutral regression currently fails with E_ENTITY_ARTIFACT_CONTRACT malformed_candidate_pair. Keep dedicated candidate/evidence/alignment artifacts intact; suppress only same-surface projection into generic block candidates and generic edge records, then prove native link and deterministic artifacts.
close_reason: Shared prepared surfaces bind deterministically per source lane with fail-closed missing/ambiguous handling and no generic self-pair projection; neutral public regression and full quality gates pass.

title: [BDC/P0] Inventory local BDC datasets and select a reproducible minimal evaluation slice

None; this is read-only data inventory and Beads metadata only.

title: [CANON-V1/P06.R1-R5] Freeze demanding-deployment requirements for the extension boundary
description:
## Background
The private BDC issuer-resolution deployment is a forcing function for Canon's domain-neutral P06 extension boundary. It contains difficult identity cases—legal and operating names, SPVs and holdcos, tranches, weak identifiers, relational context, and renames—without authorizing any structured-finance behavior in core.

The normative planning artifact is docs/BDC_ISSUER_EXTENSION_REQUIREMENTS.md. This bead freezes R1-R5 and maps each requirement to generic core contracts and acceptance evidence.

## Scope
- R1: preserve raw, legal-name, dba or operating-name, and other typed views from a source observation.
- R2: model issuer identity separately from facilities, tranches, holdings, and other assignments.
- R3: preserve distinguishing features and express authoritative or reviewed negative constraints without unsafe domain heuristics.
- R4: admit generic relational context such as repeated co-observation while preventing it from becoming identity authority.
- R5: represent temporal aliases, renames, source dates, and as-of resolution explicitly.
- Exercise invented neutral analogues in public CI and the real BDC deployment in private acceptance.
- Keep all BDC vocabulary, corpora, parsing, and policy outside Canon core.
- Exclude committing to Splink, Dedupe, OpenRefine, active learning, email review, or a native model port.

## Technical approach
Wire R1-R5 into the existing P06 contracts: typed normalization views; observations, assignments, and relationships; generic evidence operators and typed evidence IR; source-schema mapping; candidate-recall evaluation; temporal/as-of semantics; and the out-of-tree deployment proof. The demanding deployment owns its source parsing, labels, thresholds, and policy.

Safety corrections are mandatory. Never blanket-strip SPV, Bidco, Holdco, numbered-company, or similar legal terms. Industry classification is contextual negative evidence, not a universal hard cannot-link. Cross-BDC co-holding is an ablation-gated context feature, never promotion authority. Hard vetoes require authoritative identifiers, explicit constraints, or reviewed adjudication.

## Acceptance Criteria
- R1-R5 each map to one or more owned implementation beads and named acceptance evidence.
- Public fixtures exercise neutral analogues without finance vocabulary in core.
- Private acceptance can exercise real BDC cases without creating a Canon dependency on private data.
- No optional matcher or review transport blocks the P00-P12 core release path.
- The requirements document and active bead notes agree on the safety boundaries.

## Test plan
- Inspect the dependency graph to ensure all affected P06 tasks and bd-doe2 consumed the frozen requirements.
- Run the P06 domain-neutrality/source scan when implemented.
- Run typed-view, assignment-separation, protected-feature, relational-ablation, candidate-recall, and temporal-alias acceptance cases.
- Compare public neutral and private BDC results at the generic contract boundary.
- Verify P09 optional decisions remain downstream of bd-2i2q.

## File and reservation boundaries
This planning bead changes only the requirements document and bead metadata. Future implementation follows the exact-file reservation rules of its owning beads. Domain packs and private corpora remain out of tree or in explicitly scoped package fixtures.

## Considerations
The goal is not to make Canon know BDCs. The goal is to ensure a demanding BDC package can be built on Canon without forks, hidden authority, or loss of evidence.
close_reason: Requirements frozen in docs/BDC_ISSUER_EXTENSION_REQUIREMENTS.md; R1-R5 are wired into generic P06 owners and bd-doe2 acceptance, unsafe veto/normalization assumptions are corrected, and optional matcher or review choices are explicitly out of scope.

title: [CANON-V1/P05.4] Keep identity, hierarchy, and role relationships semantically distinct
description:
## Background
Parents, children, brands, divisions, branches, products, successors, and time-bounded assignees are related but not necessarily the same identity. Treating every relation as `same_as` is a general source of registry corruption.

## Technical Approach
Define a generic directed relationship fact with subject/object types, valid interval, provenance, policy reference, cardinality constraints, and identity implication set to none unless a separate equality fact exists. Support namespaced extension vocabularies without embedding their substantive rules.

## Success Criteria
- Relationship edges never become aliases solely because they connect records.
- Temporal hierarchy/role queries return provenance and intervals.
- Cardinality/cycle constraints are policy-driven and reviewable.
- Review distinguishes same, distinct, related, and uncertain.

## Test Plan
Use invented parent/child, brand/operator, successor, changing assignment, graph-cycle, overlapping-exclusive, and unknown-extension cases; assert exact lookup is unchanged by relation-only facts.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/temporal/relation.rs`
- `schemas/canon.identity.relation.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/temporal_relation.rs`

## Considerations
Relationship vocabularies live in packages; the engine enforces only generic graph and identity-separation invariants.

title: canon geo: the client-facing output surface — CSV column, typed answer sidecar, derived crosswalk view
description:
THE THING THE CLIENT ACTUALLY CONSUMES. Everything else in this epic produces evidence;
this bead produces the deliverable.

OC-0048 specifies the output shape and it is already half-built: "`canon --emit csv`
appends a `location__canon` column to the operator's own file — the identifier-provider
experience, ALREADY IMPLEMENTED. Behind each row, a typed answer rather than a boolean."

  relation:        same_parcel
  apn / bbl:       1-00995-0001
  buildings:       [BIN_a, BIN_b]
  rca_resolves_to: BIN_a
  nx_range_spans:  [BIN_a, BIN_b]
  score_units:     8700 / 10000
  evidence:        [pip_parcel, address_range_match, area_ratio]

THE TENSION THIS BEAD MUST RESOLVE: canon's registry is FLAT AND EXACT — one alias, one
canonical id, one row. The answer above is NOT flat. It carries a typed relation, a set of
buildings, a score, and an evidence list. OC-0048 flags this openly for the property case
("A property spanning three parcels cannot be one registry row without either fan-out or
collapse — the same pathology this document rejects when it rejects the wide crosswalk")
and bd-3soj leaves it open at the API boundary. The property bead decides whether the
relation graph is product or workbench state; THIS bead builds whichever surface that
decision implies.

SCOPE:
1. THE CSV COLUMN PATH IS UNCHANGED AND MUST STAY THAT WAY. `canon <INPUT> --registry ...
   --column ... --emit csv` appends the canonical column by EXACT REGISTRY LOOKUP. Nothing
   probabilistic, nothing spatial, no geometry at runtime. That invariant is canon's core
   promise and geo does not get to bend it. Verify by test that the geo path introduces no
   new behaviour into src/lookup.rs.
2. THE DERIVED CROSSWALK VIEW. bd-67wx sanctions it explicitly: "The crosswalk is still
   USEFUL — materialize it as a DERIVED CONVENIENCE VIEW off the registry, regenerable,
   never authoritative. Ergonomics without the pathology." Build it. It is the wide table
   clients will ask for, generated from the registry plus the relation graph, carrying a
   generation timestamp and the source registry version so nobody mistakes it for truth.
   Its regeneration must be deterministic from pinned inputs.
3. THE TYPED ANSWER ARTIFACT. The per-row structure above, emitted as a sidecar keyed to
   the input rows — the same relationship `--map-out` already has to `--emit csv`. This is
   where relation, member sets, score_units, evidence operator ids, abstention state, and
   coverage state live. REUSE THE EXISTING SIDECAR PATTERN rather than inventing a new
   output mode.
4. THE GRAPH SURFACE. canon already depends on petgraph, and the estate already has graph
   infrastructure (data-fabric, Oxigraph). DECIDE — and record — whether canon geo emits a
   graph projection directly or whether it emits the typed answer artifact and lets
   downstream build the graph. RECOMMEND THE LATTER: canon's boundary is identity
   compilation, not graph serving, and OC-0048's non-goals already say canon does not ship
   a renderer or a web surface. The same reasoning applies to a query engine. Emit the
   artifact; let data-fabric or the client's warehouse serve it.
5. EXPORT PARITY. `canon registry export --format dbt-seed|search-index` already exists and
   preserves the registry boundary. Geo must not need a third export format. Verify the geo
   registry exports cleanly through the existing formats, and if it cannot, that is a
   finding about the identifier scheme (bd-67wx), not a licence to add a format.

WHAT MAKES THIS THE HARDEST BEAD TO KEEP HONEST: every request from a client will be for a
wider, flatter, more convenient table, and every one of those requests is a request to
reintroduce the fan-out-or-collapse pathology the identifier scheme exists to prevent. The
derived view is the pressure valve. Ship it, regenerate it, and never let it become the
source of truth.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- Test proving the runtime lookup path is unchanged by geo
- Derived crosswalk view, deterministic from pinned registry + relation graph, stamped with
  provenance and marked non-authoritative
- Typed answer sidecar reusing the existing --map-out pattern, carrying relation, members,
  score_units, evidence ids, abstention and coverage state
- A recorded decision on emit-graph vs emit-artifact
- Geo registry exports through the existing dbt-seed and search-index formats without a new
  format
- One worked end-to-end example: a client CSV in, a canonicalized CSV plus typed sidecar
  out, including at least one abstention and one multi-candidate row

title: [CANON-V1/P06.11] Reconcile cross-provider namespaces as evidence, not truth
description:
## Background
External deployments often combine multiple authorities and internal systems whose identifiers apply to different object types. Convenience crosswalks are a common source of false same-as assertions.

## Technical Approach
Define a generic cross-provider reconciliation pipeline that joins provider facts only through declared field maps and evidence policy, emits proposed identity/relationship/cannot-link evidence, preserves every native namespace and scope, and requires review/promotion. Support disagreement and one-to-many mappings without coercion.

## Success Criteria
- No provider's identifier is reinterpreted as another namespace.
- Crosswalk output is typed evidence with source/policy provenance, never an implicit registry write.
- Different object types and scopes block unsafe reconciliation.
- One-to-many, missing, stale, and conflicting links survive as reviewable states.

## Test Plan
Use three invented providers with overlapping numeric IDs, hierarchy differences, renamed objects, and contradictory links. Verify deterministic reconciliation, abstention, impact simulation, and no mutation.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/providers/reconcile.rs`
- `schemas/canon.provider.reconcile.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/provider_reconcile.rs`

## Considerations
Domain-owned trust policy may recommend authoritative sources; Canon core treats those recommendations as pinned inputs.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic provider reconcile evidence contract and passed focused validation

title: canon geo measurements: bind receipt query_id to the query that produced the rows (QUERY_TAG-ready)
close_reason: Receipt query_id is now bound to the executed statement: cmdrvl_data_live attestation requires the cited query's recorded text hash to equal executed_query_text_sha256; wrong-id and unreachable-history cases refuse/unattest. geo_measurement_runner 12 passed. Commits f6eff28, b5908bc.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
== ORIGIN 2026-09-02 ==
Found while verifying the Overture repair and reading Linear CMD-145 ("Idea: set Snowflake
QUERY_TAG per tool call in the MCP servers (data-mcp-server first) for per-key/per-tool
attribution"). Filed at the operator's direction. This bead is the CANON half; CMD-145 is the
MCP half and they are separable — see SEQUENCING.

== THE GAP, stated exactly ==
src/bin/canon_geo_measurements.rs:757 proof_attestation():

    match (proof_class.as_str(), receipt.query_id.as_ref()) {
        ("observed", None)            => "observed",
        ("cmdrvl_data_live", Some(_)) => "LiveComplete",
        (_, None)                     => "invalid_input",
        _                             => "receipt_consistent",
    }

`query_id` is a caller-supplied `Option<String>` on both Receipt (line 146) and ResultArtifact
(line 168). The attestation checks PRESENCE, not CORRESPONDENCE. Any syntactically valid string
in that field promotes a cmdrvl_data_live receipt to LiveComplete. Nothing verifies the cited
query is the query that produced the rows in the artifact.

That is the difference between "this receipt names a query" and "this receipt is bound to its
query", and LiveComplete is the strongest proof class the measurement harness can award.

== WHY IT IS NOT THEORETICAL ==
The cmdrvl-data MCP does NOT return a query id in its response. Verified 2026-09-02: the
run_query payload is {ok, query, row_count, columns, rows} and the server exposes only
list_tables / describe_table / sample_rows / run_query. Agents therefore recover the id from
Snowflake query history AFTER execution — bd-23ux's receipt records this honestly, with
"history_recovered": true on each query_receipts entry.

Recovery is by matching against history. During this session TEN agents ran similar bounded
control SQL against the same warehouse concurrently. Two agents running the same reach control
minutes apart can each recover the other's query id by text-and-timestamp matching, and both
receipts would then cite a query they did not run — while every existing check passes, because
both ids are present and well-formed. No incident of this is known to have occurred; the point
is that nothing in the harness would detect it.

== WHAT TO BUILD (canon side, no upstream dependency) ==
Bind the cited query_id to the executed statement using material the receipt ALREADY carries:
`executed_query_text_sha256`, `source_sql_sha256`, `executed_query_text_path`, `executed_at`,
`row_count`, and `result_set_sha256`.

Minimum: for proof_class cmdrvl_data_live, resolve the cited query_id against query history and
require that the recorded statement text hashes to `executed_query_text_sha256`. A mismatch is
a typed refusal naming the measurement_id, the cited query_id, the expected hash and the actual
hash — never a warning, never a downgrade-and-continue.

If history is unreachable at validation time, that is NOT a pass. It is a distinct outcome from
both "bound" and "mismatched": the receipt stays unattested rather than being promoted. Do not
let unreachable-history silently behave like success — that would reproduce the present gap
with extra steps.

== SEQUENCING WITH CMD-145 ==
CMD-145 proposes QUERY_TAG per tool call so query_history carries per-consumer/per-tool
attribution (data-mcp-server / SVC_DATA_MCP first, then evidence, geo, edgar). When that ships,
tag-based lookup makes recovery deterministic instead of a text match, and the tag can also be
bound into the receipt.

These are independent and this bead does NOT wait on CMD-145. Order:
  (a) NOW: correspondence check against executed_query_text_sha256. Works today, no MCP change.
  (b) WHEN CMD-145 SHIPS: consume the tag, prefer tag lookup over text matching, and add the
      tag to the receipt contract as an additive OPTIONAL field so existing receipts keep
      validating. Bumping the receipt contract version to make it required is a separate
      decision, not a side effect. (See bd-3o8w for the precedent: `surface` was added to
      canon_geo_capabilities.v0 as optional precisely so old consumers kept parsing.)
Note `grep -rniE "query_tag" src/ scripts/ schemas/` currently returns nothing — canon has no
tag concept at all yet.

== NEGATIVES THIS BEAD MUST PROVE ==
- A cmdrvl_data_live receipt carrying a well-formed but WRONG query_id (one belonging to a
  different statement) is refused, not attested. This is the whole bead; a test suite without
  it proves nothing.
- A receipt whose cited query's recorded text hash differs from executed_query_text_sha256 is
  refused with both hashes named.
- Unreachable/expired history produces the unattested outcome, distinct from both pass and
  mismatch, and is asserted separately.
- An "observed" receipt with query_id: None still classifies as observed and is NOT promoted.
- Relabeling proof_class from observed to cmdrvl_data_live without a bindable id stays
  invalid_input.

== BOUNDARY ==
Do not relax any existing check to make binding easier, and do not weaken proof_attestation's
current invalid_input arm. Do not fabricate a query id anywhere in canon — if an execution
path cannot produce one, the honest result is the observed class, which already exists for
exactly that case. This bead adds a gate; it must not become a way around one.

description: Implement task-keyed strategy resolve in the existing strategy registry engine. title: [CANON-V1/P11.2] Generate and execute a canonical command-contract corpus
description:
## Background
README, help, schemas, operator metadata, doctor output, and tests have drifted, including commands advertised before executable dispatch existed. The executable contract must become the source of truth.

## Technical Approach
Define a machine-readable command corpus derived from the real dispatch table with names, nesting, arguments, defaults, schemas, exit codes, side effects, examples, and availability/features. Generate or validate help/operator/docs snippets from it and execute every example against fixtures. Add a CI drift check that rejects documented commands missing from dispatch and dispatch commands missing from contracts.

## Success Criteria

title: [CANON-V1/P02.3] Implement project init, validate, and describe ergonomics
description:
## Background
The project abstraction will accrete only if a person or agent can start correctly without memorizing internal schemas. Bootstrap commands must create the smallest truthful project and explain what remains missing.

## Technical Approach
Add `canon project init`, `validate`, and `describe` with structured JSON and concise summary modes. Init accepts an explicit directory and optional external profile reference, refuses non-empty collisions, emits a minimal neutral manifest plus safe ignore guidance, and never invents source semantics. Validate reports all independent diagnostics deterministically. Describe exposes capabilities, schemas, next actions, mutation scope, and examples.

## Success Criteria
- A fresh directory reaches a valid dry-run plan through documented commands.
- Existing files are never overwritten; refused init leaves the target byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Describe/schema surfaces fully state flags, outputs, exits, side effects, and next commands.
- Human and robot output name missing requirements without stack traces.

## Test Plan
Exercise empty/non-empty/read-only/relative/Unicode directories; validate good, unknown-extension, and multi-error fixtures; snapshot output and inspect filesystem before/after refusals.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/cli.rs`
- `src/project/init.rs`
- `src/operator.rs`
- `tests/project_cli.rs`

## Considerations
Generated samples use invented neutral identifiers and point to explicit external profile/provider selection; they ship no domain ontology or placeholder real-world entities.
