title: canon geo D2: explanation artifacts, minimal unsatisfiable core, correction sets, and exact counterfactual separation
description:
PACKET PK-D2b (stage D2) from docs/PLAN_CANON_GEO.md §18/§19, course correction 2026-09-01. This bead carries the full design so no implementer needs the plan document.

== WHY ==
§18.2 names the ordered minimal-correction-set lattice as the highest-margin single artifact and the only one with a buyer other than the person asking (data vendors, trustees). A competitor can approximate a backbone; nobody can approximate the minimal set of retractions that restores consistency. Today an empty model set reports conflict_constraint_ids with no minimality and no source-record naming. This bead adds: deletion-based minimal core under the declared source-reliability order (QuickXplain semantics), correction sets as minimal hitting sets over enumerated cores under deterministic ceilings, and exact counterfactual separation for a declared prospective observation (never called expected value without calibrated probabilities). Cores name source records and rho contracts, never constraint indices, so the artifact can be sent to Overture, FEMA, or an assessor as a falsifiable claim (§3.1).

### 18.5 The solver middle layer

The extensional kernel is kept as the exact backend. Three additions make it the product:

1. **Propagators as pre-search filters.** Each runs to a fixpoint over the component's
   domains before enumeration, prunes values with a typed reason naming the constraint and
   the evidence ids, and never changes the model set (soundness is checked in tests by
   comparing enumeration with and without propagation on every fixture). They shrink the
   search space and produce the explanation skeleton for free.
2. **Minimal cores and repairs.** On an empty model set, compute one minimal
   unsatisfiable subset of admitted constraints by deletion under the declared reliability
   order, then enumerate correction sets as minimal hitting sets while the core count stays
   under a deterministic ceiling. The artifact names source records, not constraint
   indices. Oversized cases return a typed superset with `explanation_complete=false`.
3. **Counterfactual separation.** For a declared prospective observation with an
   exhaustive outcome domain, report the exact model count under each outcome. Never call
   it expected value without calibrated probabilities (architecture §9).

== STAGE ROW (§19.5; entry condition, gate, contracts) ==
| D2 | Propagators and explanation artifacts | G1 passed; D1 residual artifacts committed; `src/geo/composition.rs` and `src/geo/evidence.rs` frozen at their D1 digests (C25); modules `propagate.rs`, `explain.rs` | G2: I01 to I05 hold on every E4 fixture; at least one real cohort conflict yields a minimal core naming source records | C01 to C08, C22, C25; T01 to T06, T19, T20, T21, T27 | new beads |

== MODULE SURFACE (§19.3; field lists are the required minimum, add #[serde(default)] fields only, never remove or rename) ==
**Dependency direction.** New modules depend on the existing `composition`, `evidence`,
`control`, `discovery`, `evaluation`, `geometry`, `geometry_value`, and `run` modules,
never the reverse. `src/geo/composition.rs` and `src/geo/evidence.rs` are not modified by
D2 to D6: `propagate` and `explain` call `solve_composition` as a black box and narrow or
re-solve `GeoCompositionRequest` values. Within the new set: `explain` consumes
`propagate`; `card`, `next_evidence`, and `inspect` consume `explain`; `exposure` and
`collision` consume `ledger`; `adjudicate` and `card` consume `observer`; nothing consumes
`inspect`.

**Shared shape.** Each module is `pub mod` in `src/geo/mod.rs` with `pub use module::*`.
Each defines `Geo<Module>Error { code: Geo<Module>ErrorCode, message: String, detail:
BTreeMap<String, String> }` with a `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` code enum that
carries the generic `UnsupportedVersion`, `InvalidInput`, `BudgetExceeded`,
`ArithmeticOverflow` variants plus the module's rows from §19.4. Each artifact type has a
`version: String` constant `CANON_GEO_<NAME>_VERSION`, `canonical_<name>_bytes`, and
`validate_<name>_artifact`. Each module ships `schemas/canon.geo.<name>.v0.schema.json`, a
`--describe` entry, a `canon geo <subcommand>`, and `tests/geo_<module>.rs`.

**`explain.rs`**

| Item | Definition |
|---|---|
| Consumes | `GeoCompositionRequest`, `GeoCompositionArtifact` (`status == GeoCompositionStatus::Conflict`, `conflict_constraint_ids`, `conflict_core_complete`), `GeoEvidenceCompilationArtifact` (`GeoEvidenceAdmission { observation_id, contract, source_records, generated_ids }` maps constraint ids to `GeoEvidenceRecordRef.source_record_id` and `GeoRhoContract.id`), `GeoPropagationArtifact` (pruning skeleton), `solve_composition` |
| `GeoReliabilityOrder` | `contract_ids_most_reliable_first: Vec<String>`; every admitted contract id must appear exactly once |
| `GeoExplanationBudget` | `max_core_solves: u64`, `max_cores: u64`, `max_hitting_sets: u64` |
| `GeoMinimalCore` | `constraint_ids`, `observation_ids`, `source_record_ids`, `rho_contract_ids`, `minimal: bool` |
| `GeoCorrectionSet` | `observation_ids`, `source_record_ids`, `minimal: bool` |
| `GeoExplanationArtifact` | `version`, `request_blake3`, `evidence_blake3`, `cores: Vec<GeoMinimalCore>`, `cores_complete: bool`, `correction_sets: Vec<GeoCorrectionSet>`, `explanation_complete: bool`, `counters: BTreeMap<String, u64>` |
| `GeoProspectiveOutcome` | `outcome_id: String`, `induced: Vec<GeoHardConstraintKind>` |
| `GeoProspectiveObservation` | `id`, `contract_id`, `cost_units: u64`, `outcomes: Vec<GeoProspectiveOutcome>` (declared exhaustive) |
| `GeoSeparationRequest` | `version`, `request: GeoCompositionRequest`, `prospective: Vec<GeoProspectiveObservation>` |
| `GeoOutcomeSeparation` | `outcome_id`, `residual_model_count: u64`, `count_exact: bool` |
| `GeoSeparationArtifact` | `version`, `request_blake3`, `baseline_model_count`, `per_observation: Vec<{ observation_id, per_outcome: Vec<GeoOutcomeSeparation>, worst_case_remaining: u64, redundant: bool }>` |
| `pub fn minimal_core(request: &GeoCompositionRequest, evidence: &GeoEvidenceCompilationArtifact, order: &GeoReliabilityOrder, budget: &GeoExplanationBudget) -> Result<GeoExplanationArtifact, GeoExplanationError>` | deletion-based core under `order` (QuickXplain semantics); refuses unless the input solves to `Conflict` (I03, I05) |
| `pub fn correction_sets(artifact: &mut GeoExplanationArtifact, request: &GeoCompositionRequest, evidence: &GeoEvidenceCompilationArtifact, budget: &GeoExplanationBudget) -> Result<(), GeoExplanationError>` | enumerates further cores up to `max_cores`, then minimal hitting sets; sets `cores_complete` and `explanation_complete` (I04) |
| `pub fn separate(request: &GeoSeparationRequest, budget: &GeoExplanationBudget) -> Result<GeoSeparationArtifact, GeoExplanationError>` | one `solve_composition` per outcome with `induced` appended; exact only when the baseline residual is complete and unsaturated; never emits an expected value (§18.5 item 3) |

== ERROR CODES (§19.4; class is exactly one of refusal / abstention / typed fallback; detail always carries the named ids) ==
| `core_not_minimal` | `explain::minimal_core` | re-solving with any single core member deleted stays `Conflict` (I03 check fails) | refusal | T05 |
| `core_enumeration_ceiling` | `explain::correction_sets` | `max_cores` or `max_core_solves` reached before enumeration closes | typed fallback: `cores_complete = false`, `explanation_complete = false`, every `minimal` flag `false` (I04) | T06 |
| `explanation_not_conflict` | `explain::minimal_core` | input request solves to `Resolved` or `Ambiguous`; no core exists | refusal | T20 |
| `separation_residual_inexact` | `explain::separate` | baseline `residual_model_count_complete = false` or `residual_model_count_saturated = true`, or an outcome solve returns `BudgetFallback` | typed fallback: `count_exact = false` on the affected `GeoOutcomeSeparation`; no `redundant` claim | T21 |

== CONTRACTS (§19.9) ==
| C05 | `minimal_core` refuses unless the input solves to `Conflict`, and every emitted core with `minimal == true` has been verified by re-solving each single deletion | `explain.rs` | I03 |
| C06 | Every emitted correction set hits every enumerated core; when `max_cores` or `max_core_solves` is reached, `cores_complete == false`, `explanation_complete == false`, and no `minimal` flag is `true` | `explain.rs` | I04 |
| C07 | Cores and correction sets name `source_record_ids` and `rho_contract_ids`; constraint ids appear only as declared ids, never as positional indices | `explain.rs` | I05, §18.5 item 2 |
| C08 | `separate` reports one exact count per declared outcome and sets `count_exact == false` whenever the baseline is incomplete or saturated or an outcome solve falls back; no artifact field carries an expected value or a probability | `explain.rs` | §18.5 item 3, N05 |
| C22 | Every artifact type declares `CANON_GEO_<NAME>_VERSION`, `canonical_<name>_bytes`, `validate_<name>_artifact`, and a `schemas/canon.geo.<name>.v0.schema.json`; canonical bytes are byte-identical across platforms | all §19.3 modules | N02, §19.3 shared shape |
| C25 | D2 to D6 do not modify `src/geo/composition.rs` or `src/geo/evidence.rs`; new modules call `solve_composition` as a black box, and generic modules carry no fixture, demo, or county literal | all §19.3 modules | §19.3 dependency direction, G7 |

== THREATS THIS BEAD MUST DEFEAT (§19.9) ==
| TH04 | A superset core, or a core computed on a satisfiable input, presented as minimal | Deletion re-solve per member; refusal on non-conflict input | C05; T05, T20; `core_not_minimal`, `explanation_not_conflict` |
| TH05 | Minimality or completeness claimed after the core enumeration ceiling | `cores_complete` and `explanation_complete` forced `false`, every `minimal` forced `false` at the ceiling | C06; T06; `core_enumeration_ceiling` |
| TH06 | Explanation names internal constraint indices, so the artifact cannot be sent upstream to a source owner | Cores and correction sets carry `source_record_ids` and `rho_contract_ids` | C07; T05 |
| TH07 | Counterfactual separation smuggles in an expected value, a probability, or a `redundant` claim on an inexact count | `count_exact` gating; no expected-value field on the type | C08; T21; `separation_residual_inexact` |
| TH21 | Demo-path hard-coding: a generic module special-cases Demo 0 ids, the chimera constraint ids, or Franklin County names to pass its tests | Case-insensitive literal scan over the twelve generic modules; property tests on seeded random components | C25; T27, T03, T16 |

== TESTS (§19.6; ship in tests/geo_<module>.rs with the T ids in test names; each row's Negative case is mandatory) ==

== NON-NEGOTIABLES AND INVARIANTS ==
### 19.1 Non-negotiables

- N01 Runtime lookup stays exact registry replay. Geo is a build-time workbench.
- N02 Same input plus same pinned sources reproduce byte-identical artifacts on every
  platform. No wall clock, locale, hash-map order, or float comparison in a decision path.
- N03 Every source value enters the solver only through a declared, versioned `rho`.
- N04 Adding admitted hard evidence may only narrow the model set or make it empty.
- N05 Source count is provenance, never evidence weight or confidence.
- N06 Candidate reach, admission, solver exactness, reconciliation, truth quality, and
  cost are reported as separate planes and never pooled.
- N07 Fixtures, retained evidence, and mocked providers are never presented as live proof.
- N08 Abstention is a legitimate output; an abstention-only module is not a delivered
  feature.
- N09 No vision or statistical model proposes a location. Models are observers with
  characterized error.
- N10 No commercial basemap imagery or tiles enter any artifact.
- N11 Gates are frozen in tests. A gate is passed by meeting it, never by editing it.
- N12 Every feature bead ships its code and its tests together, including at least one
  negative case a naive implementation fails.

### 19.2 Invariants for the new artifacts

- I01 A propagator prunes a value only with a typed reason naming constraint id and
  evidence ids; pruning is sound: enumeration with propagation equals enumeration without.
- I02 Propagator fixpoint is order-independent; tests run every permutation of propagator
  order on each fixture and compare bytes.
- I03 A minimal core is minimal: removing any one member restores satisfiability; tests
  verify by re-solving each deletion.
- I04 A correction set hits every enumerated core; when core enumeration hits its ceiling
  the artifact says `cores_complete=false` and no minimality claim is made.
- I05 Explanation artifacts name source record ids and rho contract ids, never internal
  indices.
- I06 An observer observation carries image tile digest, vintage, license hash, model or
  rule identity, weight or prompt digest, and the error-population digest; missing any
  field refuses.
- I07 Observer output is stored, never regenerated at replay; replay verifies the stored
  digest chain only.
- I08 A ledger row binds accession, loan id, parcel set, building set, truth plane,
  claim class, model count, exactness flags, and every source release pin; rows with
  candidate reach `none` carry the reason and no sets.
- I09 A ledger row never pools truth planes; non-round and round exact-lender evidence
  stay labeled.
- I10 The retry loop is bounded by a declared pass count; each pass is a normal pinned
  run and the loop artifact lists every pass with its abstention reason.
- I11 Event exposure joins building geometry, not centroids; advisory source hashes travel
  with the result.
- I12 Cross-deal collision reports a parcel or building shared by more than one trust
  with both accessions; pari passu participation is a labeled explanation, not a suppressed
  row.
- I13 `geo inspect` reads only emitted artifacts and receipts; it computes nothing that
  changes an answer.
- I14 Next-evidence recommendations expose the nondominated frontier and never manufacture
  a total ranking without a declared loss model.

== COMMANDS ==
### 19.7 Commands

Whole-tree gates run on every commit in every stage. Per-module binaries are the
`tests/geo_<module>.rs` files from §19.3; each stage runs its own set before claiming its
gate. `rg` exit status 1 means no match, which is the pass for the literal scans, so
they are written with a leading `!`.

```bash
# Whole-tree gates
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test

# Frozen E4 gate (T17, C24): expected red until G1, green from G1 on
cargo test --test geo_adjudication e4_acceptance_gate_requires_the_full_population_to_be_reachable -- --ignored

# Per-module test binaries (stage: test ids)
cargo test --test geo_propagate           # D2: T01 to T04, T19
cargo test --test geo_explain             # D2: T05, T06, T20, T21
cargo test --test geo_ledger              # D3: T07, T23, T26
cargo test --test geo_exposure            # D3: T08
cargo test --test geo_collision           # D3: T09
cargo test --test geo_retry               # D4: T10
cargo test --test geo_condo               # D4: T11
cargo test --test geo_inspect             # D4: T12, T25
cargo test --test geo_next_evidence       # D5: T18
cargo test --test geo_observer            # D6: T13, T14, T15
cargo test --test geo_adjudicate          # D6: T22 (new binary; distinct from the existing geo_adjudication)
cargo test --test geo_card                # D6: T24, T26
cargo test --test geo_e5_franklin_parcel  # D7: T16 plus the existing literal scan

# One test by name with output
cargo test --test geo_propagate soundness_holds_on_every_e4_fixture -- --nocapture

# Schema drift guard (C22). tests/geo_schemas.rs include_str!s each schema file, pins
# title, properties.version.const, and additionalProperties == false, then walks a real
# serialized instance against the schema; there is no jsonschema crate. Each new
# artifact adds one <name>_schema_matches_a_real_instance test there and one
# include_str! of schemas/canon.geo.<name>.v0.schema.json.
cargo test --test geo_schemas
cargo test --test geo_schemas propagation_schema_matches_a_real_instance
for s in propagation explanation separation_request separation observer observation_rows \
         image_tile_pin adjudication_request adjudication_receipt evidence_card \
         collateral_ledger event_exposure cross_deal retry_loop inspection next_evidence \
         condo_bridge_request ledger_bridge; do
  jq -e --arg s "$s" '.title == "canon.geo.\($s).v0"
    and .properties.version.const == "canon_geo_\($s).v0"
    and .additionalProperties == false' "schemas/canon.geo.${s}.v0.schema.json"
done

# --describe entries for geo subcommands (C22: one per new module, named after it:
# geo propagate, geo explain, geo observer, geo adjudicate, geo card, geo ledger,
# geo exposure, geo collision, geo retry, geo inspect, geo next-evidence, geo condo)
cargo run --bin canon -- --describe \
  | jq -r '.subcommands[] | select(.name | startswith("geo ")) | "\(.name)\t\(.status)\t\(.output_schema)"'
cargo run --bin canon -- --describe \
  | jq -e '[.subcommands[] | select(.name == "geo propagate" and .status == "implemented")] | length == 1'

# T27 literal scan (C25, G7). Mirrors tests/geo_e5_franklin_parcel.rs
# franklin_instance_names_do_not_enter_the_generic_geo_engine, which lowercases each
# generic source file and asserts it contains no instance literal.
GEO_GENERIC="src/geo/propagate.rs src/geo/explain.rs src/geo/observer.rs src/geo/adjudicate.rs \
  src/geo/card.rs src/geo/ledger.rs src/geo/exposure.rs src/geo/collision.rs src/geo/retry.rs \
  src/geo/inspect.rs src/geo/next_evidence.rs src/geo/condo.rs"
! rg -i -n 'franklin|39049|epsg:3735|1004540041|chimera_wrongly_admitted|asserted_address_core|case_4' $GEO_GENERIC
! rg -n 'solve_composition' src/geo/inspect.rs
! rg -i -n 'reqwest|hyper::|openai|anthropic|gemini|bedrock|invoke_model' src/geo/observer.rs
cargo test --test geo_e5_franklin_parcel franklin_instance_names_do_not_enter_the_generic_geo_engine

# Demo 0, capabilities, measurement plan, beads
bash scripts/geo_demo/demo0.sh --work-dir /tmp/demo0
cargo run --bin canon -- geo capabilities --emit json
cargo run --bin canon_geo_measurements -- --emit plan
br ready --json && br dep cycles --json
```

ANTI-REWARD-HACKING (AGENTS.md, binding):
- Code and tests ship in this bead; no scope-splitting into type/impl/test closures.
- No new todo!()/unimplemented!() scaffolds. Refusal-only implementation earns partial credit and never closes this bead (label refusal-only + follow-up bead if that is the honest state).
- Fixtures and Demo 0 outputs are never presented as live proof (C23). Gate thresholds are never edited to pass (C24, N11).
- Every feature test includes at least one negative case a naive implementation fails (the Negative case column below).
- Generic modules carry no fixture, demo, or county literal (C25, T27).

comments.text:
== DECISION (round 6) == class 5: the digest chain without `composition.request_blake3`

CONTROLLING DESIGN. `GeoCompositionArtifact` (src/geo/composition.rs:448-476) has no `request_blake3`; its only digest is `evidence_compilation: Option<GeoEvidenceCompilationReference { version, request_version, blake3 }>`, set only when the solve consumed an evidence artifact (src/geo/cli.rs:699-703; src/geo/executor.rs:506-510). Therefore explain.rs computes both digests itself from the evidence compilation it is handed: `evidence_blake3 = BLAKE3(canonical_evidence_compilation_bytes(evidence))` (src/geo/evidence.rs:445) and `request_blake3 = BLAKE3(serde_json::to_vec(&canonicalize_composition_request(&evidence.composition_request)?))` (src/geo/composition.rs:2221 over the request embedded at src/geo/evidence.rs:182). `GeoExplanationArtifact` carries both; card.rs recomputes both from the same evidence artifact (bd-101v round 6). C21 is DEFINED as: (a) `composition.evidence_compilation.blake3 == explanation.evidence_blake3 == BLAKE3(canonical_evidence_compilation_bytes(evidence))`, and (b) `explanation.request_blake3 == BLAKE3(serde_json::to_vec(canonicalize_composition_request(&evidence.composition_request)))`. A composition solved from a bare request (`evidence_compilation == None`) cannot chain and is refused downstream. `minimal_core` and `correction_sets` take the evidence artifact as their request source (the `request` parameter is `&evidence.composition_request` after canonicalization) so the digests they record are the ones the card verifies.

Bead-defined T75 in tests/geo_explain.rs: `chimera_compilation_chains_through_solve_and_explain`: `canon geo solve --request` semantics in-process over that compilation yields `status == Conflict` and `evidence_compilation.blake3` equal to the fixture's canonical digest; `minimal_core` over it yields `cores[0]` per T05 and an artifact whose `evidence_blake3` equals that digest and whose `request_blake3` equals the recomputed request digest; a compilation edited by one byte after solving makes the two `evidence_blake3` values differ (logged). e2e_explain.sh step 2 writes `<dir>/chimera-evidence-compilation.json` (copy of the fixture) and `canon geo solve --request <dir>/chimera-evidence-compilation.json > <dir>/chimera-solve.json`, then `canon geo explain --composition <dir>/chimera-solve.json --evidence <dir>/chimera-evidence-compilation.json --order <dir>/order.json > <dir>/explanation.json`, and asserts `jq -e '.evidence_blake3 == input.evidence_compilation.blake3' <dir>/explanation.json <dir>/chimera-solve.json`; BLAKE3 values in the script come only from those artifact fields.

T21 (round 5 mismatch 2 stands): uses the `oversized_component_budget_fallback_is_typed_and_deterministic` request (tests/geo_composition.rs:1086-1118) copied into tests/common/geo_fixtures.rs.

title: External prerequisite: twinning REST supports OpenFIGI batch mapping OpenAPI
description:
This is a canon-side blocker representing work owned by twinning. Do not implement canon OpenFIGI robustness work against a mock-only contract until the twinning REST enhancement can execute the OpenFIGI mapping API shape.

Required twinning capability:
- Serve an OpenAPI-described `POST /v3/mapping` endpoint compatible with OpenFIGI mapping semantics.
- Accept a top-level JSON array request body of mapping jobs with at least `idType` and `idValue`.
- Return a top-level JSON array response in the same order and length as the request.
- Support per-item success via `{ "data": [...] }` and per-item failure via `{ "error": "..." }`.
- Support candidate fields used by canon: `figi`, `compositeFIGI`, `ticker`, `name`, `securityType`, and `exchCode`.
- Enforce or observe `X-OPENFIGI-APIKEY` auth shape.
- Exercise 429 responses with `Retry-After` or `ratelimit-reset` headers so canon retry behavior can be tested.
- Provide deterministic seeded/replayed cases for success, miss, provider error, ambiguity, malformed/length-mismatched response, and rate-limit retry.

Close this blocker only when a canon test or documented smoke command can point `canon registry build --source openfigi` at a twinning `base_url` and receive OpenFIGI-shaped responses without using live OpenFIGI.

title: Resolve v0 scoring and match decisions
description:
Implement deterministic candidate scoring and match decision logic for canon resolve.

Scope:
- Add src/resolve/scoring.rs.
- For each target record, score each surviving reference candidate by evaluating strategy assertions in YAML order.
- Apply assertion weights and required-assertion semantics.
- Compute total candidate score and assertion evidence details.
- Select the best candidate using deterministic ordering, including lexicographic reference ID tie-breaking when scores are equal.
- Apply match_threshold and ambiguity_gap.
- Classify each target as MATCHED, UNMATCHED, or AMBIGUOUS.
- Include runner-up data for matches and near-miss data for unmatched records.
- Detect and report v0 one-to-many conflicts where multiple target records choose the same reference record, without trying to solve global bipartite matching yet.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests cover high-confidence match, below-threshold unmatched, insufficient ambiguity gap, exact score ties, required assertion failure, runner-up gap calculation, near-miss reporting, and same-reference conflict warnings.
- Output ordering is stable across repeated runs.
- Floating-point comparisons are deterministic and avoid platform-sensitive ordering surprises where practical.
- No registry write-back occurs here; this bead only produces in-memory decision records.

Target files:
- src/resolve/scoring.rs
- src/resolve/types.rs if needed
- tests/fixtures/resolve/** only if fixture adjustments are needed

Reservation guidance:
- Reserve only scoring-related files and exact fixture files touched.

title: canon geo: artifact license containment — field classification and 'canon geo redact'
description:
BYOP MAKES THE ARTIFACT LICENSE-ENCUMBERED. FOUND BY REALITY CHECK 2026-08-14.

THE PROBLEM: bd-101v requires geometry at DECISION FIDELITY in the artifact, for every
candidate including the ones that lost, so the visual evidence card can be drawn without
a second query. Under bring-your-own-parcel (bd-2kjx) that geometry INCLUDES THE CLIENT'S
LICENSED PARCEL POLYGONS from ATTOM / Regrid / LightBox. So the artifact that makes the
decision checkable is also an artifact we may have no right to receive.

CONSEQUENCES, WHICH MUST BE DESIGNED FOR RATHER THAN DISCOVERED IN A SUPPORT TICKET:
- We cannot debug a client's run by asking them to send the artifact.
- We cannot score a client's results centrally, so our own quality telemetry has a hole
  exactly where the paying customers are.
- bd-2jfj (evidence-signature grouping) CANNOT BE A HOSTED SERVICE for licensed layers.
  Its "one card per pattern instead of per pair" economics — which OC-0048 identifies as
  what makes visual review affordable at all — must work with the card rendered
  CLIENT-SIDE.
- OC-0048's non-goal "No APN corpus is redistributed; licensed parcel data stays the
  client's" is currently a statement of intent with NO MECHANISM. This bead is the
  mechanism.

TASK:
1. FIELD-LEVEL CLASSIFICATION. Classify every field of every geo artifact as
   ENCUMBERED or SHAREABLE. First cut:
     SHAREABLE   evidence scores, operator ids, reason codes, lanes, thresholds,
                 abstention states and reasons, tile ids, halo flags, coverage states,
                 multi-containment counts, OUR geometry, our minted cluster ids,
                 candidate counts, timing/diagnostics
     ENCUMBERED  client geometry, client row values, client addresses, vendor parcel
                 identifiers, and any derived value from which the source geometry could
                 be reconstructed (note: a sufficiently precise bbox plus area plus
                 vertex count may be reconstructive — think about this, do not wave at it)
   The reconstruction question is the subtle one. A "shareable" summary that leaks the
   polygon in aggregate is not shareable.
2. `canon geo redact` — A PROJECTION, NOT A DELETION. Produce the shareable subset as a
   first-class derived artifact that PRESERVES CONTENT-ADDRESSING INTEGRITY: the redacted
   artifact must carry a verifiable link to the full artifact's digest, so a decision can
   be discussed and audited by reference without the encumbered payload travelling. This
   is the same shape as canon's existing `--explicit` / masked-by-default behaviour on
   the lookup path, which already defaults input and canonical_id to [REDACTED] with
   "redacted": true in the envelope — REUSE THAT DOCTRINE AND VOCABULARY rather than
   inventing a second redaction model.
3. DEFAULT DENY. Redaction is the DEFAULT for any artifact containing a source marked
   licensed. Sharing the full artifact requires an explicit operator action. Getting this
   backwards means the first support ticket ships us data we should not hold.
4. LICENSE DECLARATION AT INGEST. The client-layer ingest bead requires a vendor
   descriptor; extend it with a license posture: shareable / internal-only / redact-always.
   Canon must refuse to run rather than assume a default posture.
5. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE PROVING GROUND. bd-bmee uses MapPLUTO, which is public, so the
   proving ground runs UNREDACTED and is fully shareable. That is convenient and it also
   means the redaction path will be UNTESTED by the proving ground. The BYOP integration
   test bead must exercise redaction explicitly.
6. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE CARD. bd-101v's card renders from the artifact. A redacted
   artifact can still render: the tile geometry from OUR sources, the evidence waterfall,
   the abstention state, and the candidate topology are all shareable. What it cannot draw
   is the client's parcel outline. Decide whether a redacted card is USEFUL ENOUGH TO BE
   WORTH RENDERING — RECOMMEND YES, because the evidence waterfall and the tie structure
   are most of the persuasive content, and a card that says "two client parcels contained
   this point, here is why neither won" is still checkable by the client against their own
   layer.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- Written field-level classification for every geo artifact, including an explicit
  analysis of which shareable aggregates could reconstruct encumbered geometry
- `canon geo redact` producing a verifiable, digest-linked shareable projection
- Default-deny behaviour with an explicit opt-out
- License posture declared at ingest, refusal on absence
- A redacted-card fixture proving the card is still meaningful without client geometry
- A test that a redacted artifact cannot be used to reconstruct encumbered geometry

Foursquare landing. That is the POI level in bd-2cbs, and it is in the same table family as
Overture buildings.

== FINDING 1: THE LANDED H3 GRAIN IS r4 / r7 / r8. THERE IS NO r9. ==
All three sources partition by h3_r4 and carry H3_R7 and H3_R8 columns. The epic's default
tile is res-9 and it is NOT precomputed anywhere.

AND THERE IS A CONVENIENT COINCIDENCE WORTH DELIBERATELY EXPLOITING: an r8 cell is
approximately 0.737 km2 -- which is almost exactly the area the epic specifies for its WORK
UNIT (an r9 cell plus k-ring 1 = 7 cells = 0.737 km2). So the already-landed H3_R8 column is
essentially the intended work-unit size.
ACTION FOR bd-2b9d: reconsider r9-plus-k-ring versus r8-plus-k-ring as the work unit, now
that r8 is precomputed across every source and r9 is not. This does not change the
requirement to compute cells in canon with a vetted Rust library -- the Snowflake H3 helper
defects (edgar-elt br-2wir) still stand -- but it does mean the warehouse can prefilter at
r8 for free, and the resolution decision now has a third input alongside node count and
human legibility.

== FINDING 2: POLYGON-TO-CELLS RETURNS EMPTY FOR SMALL BUILDINGS. LIVE, MEASURED. ==
From bd-3fyv: "H3_POLYGON_TO_CELLS alone inserted only 116 coverage rows for 354,804 hot
rows because small buildings often contain no H3 r8 cell centroid." Fixed there by using a
guaranteed CENTROID_H3_R8 plus H3_TRY_POLYGON_TO_CELLS.

THIS IS DIRECTLY THE MEMBERSHIP QUESTION bd-10s2 AND bd-2b9d SPECIFY. At r8 or r9 a
building is much smaller than a cell, so "which cells does this polygon cover" is
degenerate: the standard polygon-to-cells contract returns cells whose CENTRES fall inside
the polygon, and for a building that set is almost always EMPTY.
CONSEQUENCE: membership must be CENTROID-ANCHORED with polygon coverage as a supplement for
the large-feature case (parcels, campuses, complexes), NOT the other way round. My earlier
recommendation on bd-10s2 -- "full intersection cover for membership plus a single
deterministic anchor cell" -- is right in intent but inverted in emphasis, and applying it
naively with polygon_to_cells would have silently produced empty membership for nearly every
building. Correct it there.

== FINDING 3: OUR OWN SOURCES CARRY LICENSE OBLIGATIONS. bd-pq5w IS SCOPED TOO NARROWLY. ==
I framed license containment entirely around the CLIENT's licensed parcel layer. The landed
research shows OUR side has obligations too, and they differ per source:
    Overture buildings, divisions      ODbL-1.0            <-- SHARE-ALIKE
    Overture places                    per-source mix of CDLA-Permissive-2.0, Apache-2.0,
                                       CC0-1.0; source license must be retained
    Overture addresses                 source-specific, incl. NAD Access and Usage License
    FEMA USA Structures                CC-BY-4.0, attribution to ORNL and FEMA Geospatial
                                       Response Office REQUIRED
    Microsoft GlobalML                 CDLA-Permissive-2.0 current release; older vintages
                                       need per-release revalidation
bd-30ho states plainly: "License segmentation by source array is REQUIRED before any derived
product ships. Treat as a build-time gate, not a later cleanup."

ODbL SHARE-ALIKE IS THE COMMERCIAL ISSUE AND IT NEEDS AN OPERATOR DECISION, NOT AN
ENGINEERING ONE. A tile is a derived product. If it mixes ODbL Overture buildings with
everything else, the derived tile may inherit share-alike obligations that are
incompatible with a paid distribution model. Options to evaluate deliberately:
  (a) segregate ODbL-derived features into a separately-licensed layer of the tile, with
      the license class carried per feature -- note OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_EXT ALREADY HAS
      LICENSE_CLASS AND LICENSE_TERMS COLUMNS, so the substrate for this exists;
  (b) build the commercial tile from the permissive sources only (FEMA CC-BY, Microsoft
      CDLA) and treat Overture as an internal enrichment;
  (c) accept share-alike and publish the tile openly.
REQUIRED IN bd-pq5w AND bd-1uld: license class per FEATURE in the tile artifact, and a
declared per-tile license posture that composes our obligations with the client's. The
artifact license boundary now has TWO directions, not one.

== FINDING 4: THE ATTRIBUTE CHANNELS FOR bd-272d ARE REAL, AND ONE IS MODELLED ==
Attribute anchoring needs class, size, floors, year. What is actually arriving:
    FEMA        OCC_CLS, PRIM_OCC (occupancy class), SQFEET, PROP_ADDR, UUID, BUILD_ID
    Overture    building class, height, num_floors, GERS id
    Microsoft   height (subset only), confidence, NO ID
    MapPLUTO    BLDGCLASS, LANDUSE, BLDGAREA, LOTAREA, NUMBLDGS, NUMFLOORS, YEARBUILT
So the six-field client contract has a counterpart on the tile side for every field except
YEAR BUILT, which only MapPLUTO supplies -- meaning year-built anchoring works in NYC and
degrades outside it until a national year source exists. Record that as a known national
limitation rather than discovering it later.

CRITICAL: FEMA OCCUPANCY IS MODELLED, NOT SURVEYED. bd-1ssr requires a provenance flag
"so downstream never treats it as surveyed." Attribute anchoring MUST carry that flag into
the evidence and weight modelled attributes below observed ones. A modelled occupancy class
driving a hard eliminative filter (bd-2zdz's assemblage type filter) would be a silent error
generator -- the filter is HARD, so a wrong modelled class removes the correct candidate
before anything is scored. Use modelled occupancy as SUPPORT evidence, never as a hard
filter, unless corroborated.

== FINDING 5: NO STABLE ID CONFIRMED FOR TWO SOURCES ==
Microsoft has no id at all -- bd-3fyv derives "a deterministic feature hash because no
stable id." Overture ADDRESSES are alpha with no stable GERS id either. This confirms
bd-2cbs rule 4 (alias-less participants) and extends it: the alias-less set is Microsoft
footprints AND Overture addresses, not just Microsoft.
A derived feature hash is NOT an alias and must not be minted into a registry -- it will
change whenever the geometry changes, which violates the tile identifier stability contract
in bd-12gh.

== FINDING 6: OVERTURE ADDRESSES CANNOT BE THE ADDRESS-SET SOURCE ==
bd-30ho: "Addresses theme is ALPHA -- do not build a contract against it yet," no stable
GERS id, multi-source licensing including NAD terms. US count 127,719,691.
So bd-35qg's address-set acquisition is NOT solved by Overture. NYC PAD or the per-BIN
addresses in the landed footprints file (bd-397d) remain the path, and the national story
stays open. Do not let the size of the Overture addresses count create false confidence.

== WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE WORKED-CASE CORPUS (bd-tccn) ==
The corpus can now stage its non-MapPLUTO pulls against REAL TABLE NAMES rather than
placeholders:
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.FEMA_USA_STRUCTURES_HOT              partially loaded (DC, AK, AL)
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.MICROSOFT_GLOBALML_BUILDING_FOOTPRINTS_HOT   partially loaded
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_HOT           DDL applied, 0 rows
    plus the *_FEATURE_H3_COVERAGE tables for each
NEW YORK IS NOT YET LOADED IN ANY OF THE THREE. FEMA is alphabetical by state and is at AR;
Microsoft is 179/2415 files; Overture has not started landing. So the full-tile version of
every case remains blocked, exactly as the corpus bead predicted -- but the blocker is now
a KNOWN COMPLETION DATE rather than an unlanded dataset, and the table names and column
shapes are already fixed enough to write the extraction queries against.

WHAT THE BODY ASSUMES: that license encumbrance flows one way — the CLIENT's licensed parcel

inherit share-alike obligations incompatible with paid distribution. Three options to
evaluate deliberately:
  (a) SEGREGATE ODbL-derived features into a separately-licensed layer, carrying license
      class PER FEATURE. The substrate already exists — OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_EXT carries
      LICENSE_CLASS and LICENSE_TERMS columns today.
  (b) Build the commercial tile from permissive sources only (FEMA CC-BY, Microsoft CDLA)
      and treat Overture as internal enrichment.
  (c) Accept share-alike and publish the tile openly.
This needs an operator decision before the tile artifact format freezes (bd-1uld).

REQUIRED ADDITIONS TO THIS BEAD:
1. LICENSE CLASS PER FEATURE in the tile artifact, not per tile. Mixed-license tiles are
   the normal case, and a per-tile label cannot express them.
2. A DECLARED PER-TILE LICENSE POSTURE that COMPOSES our obligations with the client's.
   The redaction projection must satisfy both directions simultaneously: strip the client's
   encumbered geometry when sharing outward, AND carry required attributions (ORNL, FEMA,
   Overture Maps Foundation and its sources) wherever our features travel.
3. ATTRIBUTION IS NOT REDACTABLE. CC-BY and ODbL require attribution to SURVIVE derivation.
   A redaction projection that strips provenance to protect the client would breach our own
   obligations. Attribution fields must be classified SHAREABLE-AND-REQUIRED — a third
   class, not simply "shareable".

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-14 — THE ACCRETION FLYWHEEL DOES NOT SPIN FROM CLIENT USAGE. I overstated
it, and the operator caught it.

"We're not gonna get to keep our clients' properties. We're gonna run canon on their side.
We could offer it as an empty MCP server and get the info for ourselves, but we're mostly
offering for them to run canon on their side, so we won't be picking up addresses."

WHAT I IMPLIED: that resolving corpora compounds generally, as though every run added to the
registry.
WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE: accretion is bounded to CORPORA WE HOLD AND RESOLVE OURSELVES.
Canon runs on the client's machine, their artifacts are license-encumbered (bd-pq5w), and
their book never comes back. So:

  ACCRETES     HUD, Ginnie, Fannie, Freddie, CMBS conduit, REIT Schedule III, NAIC --
               everything we acquire and resolve on our own compute.
  DOES NOT     bank balance sheets, CRE CLOs, SASBs, and every other client corpus. Every
               client BENEFITS from our accretion; NO client CONTRIBUTES to it.

THE MOAT THEREFORE COMPOUNDS WITH ACQUISITION, NOT WITH ADOPTION. That is a real flywheel and
a weaker one than I described. It grows when we land another corpus, not when we sign
another client. Worth stating plainly because it changes what investment actually widens the
lead: buying and resolving more property corpora, not selling more seats.

TWO CONSEQUENCES THAT NEED HANDLING.

1. THE ADDRESS-SET ACCRETION PATH IS BOUNDED TOO (see bd-35qg). It still works -- HUD plus
   the agencies plus CMBS conduit is a large share of US institutional CRE addresses, and it
   is genuinely national. But it will never reach the addresses that exist only in client
   books, so it cannot fully substitute for landing an authoritative address-set source.
   The two paths remain complementary rather than one superseding the other.

2. WE ARE BLIND TO OUR OWN PRODUCT'S PERFORMANCE, AND THIS IS THE SERIOUS ONE.
   This bead makes the STAGE-1 HIT RATE against a real client book "the number that decides
   how much this actually buys." UNDER CLIENT-SIDE EXECUTION WE CANNOT MEASURE IT. Same for
   precision, abstention rate, coverage and false merges on live books -- bd-pq5w already
   records that we cannot debug or score a client's run centrally, and this is the same
   blindness applied to the metrics that would tell us where to improve.

   MITIGATION, AND IT IS ALREADY SCOPED: bd-pq5w's field classification separates SHAREABLE
   from ENCUMBERED. Evidence scores, operator ids, reason codes, abstention states, coverage
   states, candidate counts and tile ids are all shareable; client geometry and row values
   are not. So an OPT-IN REDACTED RUN SUMMARY gives us hit rates, abstention distributions
   and residual taxonomy WITHOUT their data ever leaving their machine.
   REQUIRED: make that redacted telemetry a first-class, opt-in, clearly-labelled output of
   the client run rather than something bolted on later. Design it as part of the artifact
   contract, and make what it contains inspectable by the client before they send it --
   trust is the product here, and a telemetry channel that is not fully legible would cost
   more than the metrics are worth.

   PROXY IN THE MEANTIME: hold out one of our own corpora, resolve the rest, and measure
   stage-1 hit rate of the held-out set against the accreted registry. That is a real
   number we can compute without any client, and it bounds the expected benefit before the
   first deployment.

3. THE HOSTED-MCP ALTERNATIVE IS A DELIBERATE PRODUCT DECISION, NOT A FALLBACK. Offering a
   hosted server that resolves on our side WOULD let us capture addresses -- and it inverts
   the privacy posture that the client-side design exists to provide. It is a different
   product with a different trust story and a different licensing exposure (their parcel
   vendor's terms may forbid sending the layer to us at all). Do not let it arrive by
   accident as a support convenience; if it is offered, it is offered explicitly.

title: [CANON-V1/P01.4] Define deterministic registry export backend interface
description:
## Background
dbt seed and search index are successful exports but currently implemented as one command-specific module. A backend boundary lets project compilation and packages produce multiple verified projections without alternate semantics.

## Technical Approach
- Define a typed export request containing verified package snapshot, filters, namespace, canonical IRI policy, output targets, and provenance.
- Define backend metadata, deterministic write planning, output hashes, refusal behavior, and common summary fields.
- Adapt existing dbt-seed and search-index implementations without changing their user-visible semantics.
- Allow project manifests to request multiple exports atomically after promotion.

## Success Criteria
- All backends consume the same effective mapping snapshot and precedence rules.
- Filters and normalized search keys cannot diverge silently between formats.
- Existing CLI commands continue to work.
- A failed backend cannot leave another backend falsely reported as complete.

## Test Plan
- Shared conformance harness for export backends.
- Filter and precedence metamorphic tests.
- Atomic multi-export failure tests.
- Existing golden artifact parity.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/registry/export.rs`
- `src/lib.rs`
- `tests/registry_export_conformance.rs`

## Considerations
- Do not make export formats part of core lookup.
- Keep backend API narrow enough for future formats.
- Shared CLI wiring should be coordinated with P00 dispatch ownership.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic registry export backend interface with shared snapshot planning and conformance validation; focused tests/clippy green, repo-wide fmt blocked by unrelated active-tree drift

title: canon geo: name-and-region resolution — the cascade entered from the other end (Schedule III, NAIC)
description:
OPERATOR CORRECTION 2026-08-14: NAME-ONLY RESOLUTION IS A CAPABILITY, NOT AN EDGE CASE. I
recorded it as a limitation on bd-14hu and that framing was wrong.

"A Schedule III that says 'Mall of Louisiana' with a city, state and ZIP -- we should be
able to use our data sources and get that. Resolving our data sources should really be good
at helping us resolve names, especially if we have the property type and the year built. I
don't see why we couldn't get pretty close to where a human would just have to adjudicate a
few decisions."

== WHY THIS IS RIGHT, AND WHY IT INVERTS THE DESIGN ==
OC-0048 states the doctrine as: "The attributes do not FIND the match -- geometry does. They
REJECT the wrong one."
THAT IS TRUE FOR ADDRESS AND GEOCODE INPUTS AND FALSE FOR NAME-ONLY INPUTS. With no point
and no street address there is nothing for geometry to start from. The correct statement for
this population is the mirror image:

    THE NAME FINDS THE MATCH. GEOMETRY AND ATTRIBUTES REJECT THE WRONG ONE.

Same evidence, same operators, opposite order. That symmetry is the whole design, and it
means name-only resolution is not a bolt-on -- it is the cascade entered from the other end.

== A SECOND ENTRY POINT INTO THE CASCADE ==
Everything scoped so far starts: geocode -> tile -> candidates -> score -> decide/abstain.
Name-only starts:  name + region -> TILE SET -> candidate POIs and buildings -> narrow by
attributes -> descend the level ladder -> confirm with geometry.

  1. REGION RESOLVES TO A TILE SET, NOT A TILE. City/state/ZIP is a coarse spatial filter
     yielding many cells rather than one. Overture's DIVISIONS theme (division_area,
     division_boundary) is landing in bd-30ho and is exactly the source for administrative
     boundaries -> cell coverage. A ZIP is on the order of tens of r8 cells; bounded and
     tractable, especially with a name filter applied first.
  2. NAME MATCHING IS WHERE canon ENTITY'S EXISTING MACHINERY GENUINELY TRANSFERS UNCHANGED
     (bd-2cbs rule 3). namekit, rapidfuzz, tfidf_cosine, alias_patch_match, and the
     cmbs_tenant_label profile pattern all apply directly to POI and place names. This is
     the strongest instance in the whole epic of reuse actually being reuse.
  3. ATTRIBUTES NARROW HARD. Property type plus year built plus size, against a region
     rather than a tile. A mall in one ZIP is close to unique.
  4. DESCEND THE LADDER TO CONFIRM. POI -> containing building -> parcel (bd-2cbs). Then
     check the building's size and year against the assertion. Found by name, CONFIRMED by
     geometry -- and disagreement at the confirm step is a strong abstention signal, not a
     tiebreak.

== RARITY IS THE FEASIBILITY TEST, AND IT IS COMPUTABLE ==
"Mall of Louisiana" works because it is unique in its region. "Holiday Inn Express" or
"Walmart Supercenter" is not -- a metro carries dozens. So name-only resolution is feasible
exactly where the name is DISCRIMINATING IN THE REGION, and that is computable from the
region's own POI population, the same way bd-272d computes attribute rarity from the tile's
own population.
REQUIRED: score by name rarity IN THE REGION, ABSTAIN when the name is not discriminating,
and REPORT the region's discriminating power so "we could not resolve it" distinguishes
"the name is generic" from "nothing matched." Chains and brands should route to review by
construction rather than being attempted and silently mismatched.

== FOUR HARD PARTS, RECORDED HONESTLY ==
1. CHAIN AND BRAND NAMES are the failure population, per the rarity point above.
2. NAMES DRIFT. Malls are renamed and rebranded; a 2015 Schedule III name may not match a
   2026 POI name. This is the temporal problem from bd-1oy8 arriving through the name
   channel, and prior names are themselves accretable knowledge (bd-14hu).
3. THE POI IS NOT THE BUILDING. A mall POI is one point; the mall spans multiple parcels
   and multiple buildings. So "Mall of Louisiana" resolves to a SET -- which makes a mall a
   canonical instance of BOTH the property-as-set model AND corpus case 7 (M parcels to N
   buildings). Do not let the POI point become the answer.
4. OVERTURE PLACES LICENSING is a per-source mix (CDLA-Permissive-2.0 / Apache-2.0 / CC0)
   requiring source license retention, per bd-30ho. Name-only resolution leans hardest on
   the theme with the most fragmented licensing; carry license class per feature (bd-pq5w).

== WHAT IT UNLOCKS: TWO WHOLE CORPORA ==
  REIT SCHEDULE III (bd-14a8)    property NAME only, no address field. Currently
                                 unaddressable by any geometry-first design.
  NAIC SCHEDULE A/B (naic-2wt)   the insurer's own descriptor, quality varies.
Both are name/descriptor-only and both are listed in OC-0048's corpus table as things this
outcome is supposed to key. Without this path they simply never resolve.

== GINNIE MAE IS A DIFFERENT MECHANISM AND SHOULD BE VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED ==
The operator grouped Ginnie with the name cases. It is probably NOT a name problem: Ginnie's
native key is a pool number with no address and no property name, so there is no name to
match. The likely path is an IDENTIFIER JOIN rather than a name match -- Ginnie multifamily
pools reference FHA case numbers, and HUD's property inventory carries FHA numbers WITH
addresses, so GNMA -> FHA number -> HUD -> address would resolve it through a corpus we
already hold.
I HAVE NOT VERIFIED THAT CHAIN. Confirm the FHA-number linkage exists in the landed Ginnie
and HUD data before scoping work on it. If it holds, Ginnie is cheap and needs none of this
bead's machinery; if it does not, Ginnie may be genuinely unresolvable at the property level
and that should be stated plainly rather than left implied.

== SEQUENCING ==
This depends on Overture places and divisions landing (bd-30ho, not started) and on the
entity-level model (bd-2cbs). It does NOT depend on the geometry cascade being finished --
the name path can be proven independently, and proving it early de-risks two corpora that
the geometry-first design cannot touch at all.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- A name+region entry point distinct from the geocode entry point, with its own blocking
  strategy (region -> tile set, then name)
- Region-to-cell coverage derived from Overture divisions
- Name matching reusing canon entity's existing operators rather than new ones
- Name rarity computed per region, with abstention when not discriminating and the
  region's discriminating power reported
- Descend-and-confirm: POI -> building -> parcel, with attribute disagreement at the confirm
  step producing abstention rather than a tiebreak
- A worked case on a real Schedule III row -- "Mall of Louisiana" or equivalent -- resolving
  to a SET of parcels and buildings, not a point
- A negative case: a chain name in a dense metro that correctly abstains and routes to review
- The Ginnie FHA-number chain either verified and scoped, or documented as unavailable

title: canon geo: research all imagery and elevation sources from primary sources, catalog the survivors at provider and channel level
description:
Research every candidate imagery and elevation source carefully, then CATALOG THE SURVIVORS
at provider and channel level so the estate can draw on them later without re-researching.

CONTEXT: PLAN_CANON_GEO.md Appendix A establishes that a frozen-weight observer (the
cmdrvl-tabfm / FrankenWhisper / FrankenOCR pattern — open weights reimplemented in pure Rust
with hard-coded weights, bit-identical forever) satisfies canon's determinism requirement.
The model is a SOURCE, not a solver: it emits typed observations (a structure count, a roof
outline, a floor count) which enter as constraints like any other evidence. So imagery
becomes another source class, and any imagery source is admissible once it has a license
posture, a vintage, and a characterized error.

ONLY NAIP HAS BEEN VERIFIED. Everything else in Appendix A.5 is from general knowledge and
explicitly marked unverified. This bead closes that.

== WHAT TO RESEARCH, PER SOURCE ==

For each candidate below, establish from PRIMARY SOURCES (agency pages, license text, actual
bucket or endpoint listings — not blog posts, not model recall):

  1. LICENSE POSTURE, exactly. Public domain / permissive with attribution / licensed and
     resolvable but not redistributable / prohibited for our use. Quote the operative
     clause. This is the gate — see the FCC Fabric precedent, where a high-value dataset
     turned out to restrict use to "statutory broadband-related obligations" and was
     therefore unusable for commercial CRE despite ranking #4 on an earlier list.
  2. COVERAGE — national, regional, spotty. Which states/counties, and how is coverage
     reported.
  3. RESOLUTION and bands. Is it adequate to resolve an individual building footprint.
  4. VINTAGE AND CADENCE. Per-tile date, refresh schedule, and whether historical vintages
     are retained. Temporal identity depends on this (bd-1oy8, Allen interval constraints).
  5. ACCESS MECHANISM. Bulk download / COG plus HTTP range requests / STAC catalog / tile
     server / authenticated API. COG-plus-range is strongly preferred: it fetches only the
     window covering an H3 cell and needs no key or rate limit.
  6. PINNABILITY. Can a specific asset be content-addressed — object version, ETag, checksum
     — so a re-render years later is byte-identical? A source that cannot be pinned cannot
     enter a reproducible evidence artifact.
  7. COST at national scale, including egress.
  8. ERROR CHARACTERIZABILITY. Is there published accuracy metadata, and is the error
     plausibly measurable by us? Per Appendix A.3, no characterization means no rho band
     means no admission.

== CANDIDATES ==

VERIFIED ALREADY, re-confirm coverage years only:
  NAIP (USDA FPAC-BC). Public domain, 1m 2003-17 / 0.6m from 2018 / 0.3m coastal option.
  Three public S3 buckets: naip-visualization (3-band COG), naip-analytic (4-band MRF),
  naip-source (raw GeoTIFF). STAC exists. OPEN QUESTION: the AWS registry describes
  2011-2018 for one bucket while STAC catalogs claim 2010-present — confirm current coverage
  against the live bucket. Known limitation: leaf-on growing-season imagery, so canopy
  obscures structures in tree-heavy areas, which is the dominant term in its rho band and is
  seasonal and geographic.

ASSESS FIRST, AND POSSIBLY BEFORE IMAGERY AT ALL:
  USGS 3DEP LiDAR. Height is MEASURED rather than inferred; building extraction from point
  clouds is classical geometry, so there may be NO MODEL TO CHARACTERIZE — which would
  collapse the entire Appendix A.3 admission gate to ordinary sensor accuracy. Distinguishes
  building from parking lot trivially and yields floor-count estimates directly against
  NUMFLOORS. Public domain, on AWS Open Data. Coverage incomplete and vintage varies widely
  by county. THIS MAY BE THE RIGHT SENSOR AND IT IS RANKED FIRST FOR THAT REASON.

REMAINING CANDIDATES:
  Sentinel-1 SAR (ESA). ~10m radar, all-weather, free and open. Too coarse for footprints,
  but buildings have distinctive double-bounce signatures — assess for PRESENCE AND CHANGE
  DETECTION, which is what the temporal constraints currently have no observation source for.
  Sentinel-2 (ESA). ~10m optical, free and open. Change detection and land cover.
  State and municipal orthoimagery. Several states and NYC specifically fly higher resolution
  than NAIP, often public. Likely the best resolution available for the NYC proving ground —
  check NYC first.
  USGS High Resolution Orthoimagery (HRO). Public domain, higher res where covered.
  NOAA emergency response imagery. Post-disaster, high-res, public domain. Narrow but
  valuable for change events.
  Commercial: Maxar, Planet, Nearmap, Vexcel, Airbus. Better resolution and cadence,
  licensed. Record terms precisely — resolvable-under-license versus redistributable is the
  distinction that matters, and it is the same containment discipline as bd-pq5w.
  Mapbox / Google / Esri basemaps. EXPECTED TO FAIL — terms generally forbid caching, which
  is incompatible with a pinned evidence artifact. Confirm and record so nobody re-proposes
  them.

Add any source the research turns up that is not listed. The list is a starting point, not a
boundary.

== CATALOG THE SURVIVORS ==

Every source that passes scrutiny gets registered in the metadata catalog using the `catalog`
skill, at BOTH levels:
  data_provider://<agency or vendor>
  data_channel://<provider>/<dataset>/<access method>
with license_terms recorded verbatim, required attribution captured, access mechanism and
pinning strategy described, coverage and cadence stated, and a data-location plus lineage
stitched where we land anything.

title: [CANON-V1/REVIEW] Prove v1 contracts through the public crate API
description:
## Background
5.5 review found that new v1 contract modules are presented as shipped contract rows, but their tests compile source files directly instead of proving the public crate API. This can let contracts exist on disk without being importable by downstream users.

## Evidence
- `src/lib.rs` exports existing modules but not all new v1 contract modules.
- `tests/inbox_contract.rs`, `tests/temporal_fact.rs`, and `tests/strategy_contract.rs` use path inclusion/direct source compilation patterns.
- Contract inventory rows present these contracts as preserved/shipped.

## Success Criteria
- Contract tests import the intended public surface via `canon::...`, or the contract inventory explicitly marks the modules as internal/non-public with a documented access boundary.
- New v1 contract modules have a deliberate API exposure decision in code and tests.
- A failing import path would fail the quality gate.

## RESERVATIONS

- `tests/inbox_contract.rs`
- `tests/temporal_fact.rs`
- `tests/strategy_contract.rs`

title: [CANON-V1/P08.5] Enforce content-addressed publication and optimistic concurrency
description:
## Background
Two writers can otherwise publish divergent next registry versions and silently lose updates. Versioned files alone do not guarantee a single ancestry.

## Technical Approach
Require every mutation/promotion to name expected base digest and version; build the candidate package completely; verify it; then publish with compare-and-swap or create-if-absent semantics. Define backend capabilities and deterministic conflict receipts. Tags/channels update only after immutable package publication and use their own expected-current digest.

## Success Criteria
- Concurrent writers from the same base produce at most one accepted successor for a linear channel.
- The loser receives the actual head and a safe rebase/semantic-merge plan; no data is overwritten.
- Filesystem publication is atomic and crash-safe within documented platform guarantees.
- Package history remains immutable and ancestry-verifiable.

## Test Plan
Race many subprocess writers, inject crashes at every publication boundary, test stale bases, identical candidates, divergent candidates, tag races, and recovery. Verify directory/object inventories and ancestry.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/registry/transaction.rs`
- `src/distribution/backend.rs`
- `tests/registry_concurrency_e2e.rs`

## Considerations
Some stores provide weaker primitives. Backends must advertise capabilities and refuse unsafe mutation rather than emulate CAS with a race.
close_reason: Implemented filesystem-first content-addressed publication backend and registry publication transaction in reserved files only. Evidence: cargo test --test registry_concurrency_e2e passed 6/6; cargo test --test registry_concurrency passed 6/6 after rerun; cargo fmt --check passed; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings passed. Note: production wiring still requires coordinator-owned src/lib.rs module declarations for distribution::backend and registry::transaction.

title: Resolve v0 graph hydration and candidate filtering
description:
Hydrate the ephemeral two-tape graph and implement deterministic candidate selection for canon resolve.

Background:
- The plan uses petgraph as an in-process workbench graph, not as a persistent entity database.
- V0 can be simple, but the graph boundary should be explicit so v1 can add bipartite constraints and neighborhood signals later.

Scope:
- Add src/resolve/graph.rs or equivalent module.
- Build a petgraph graph from loaded reference and target records.
- Insert nodes in sorted composite-ID order for deterministic traversal.
- Apply strategy candidate_filter entries in declaration order.
- Candidate filters should narrow reference candidates per target using operators such as exact, canon_match, range, date_range, prefix, and any explicitly supported subset from the strategy parser.
- Enforce max_candidates from strategy/CLI and refuse with E_TOO_MANY_CANDIDATES when a target has too many surviving candidates.
- Emit structured candidate provenance so output/scoring can explain which filters passed.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests cover node counts, side labels, deterministic node ordering, candidate filtering by exact/range/canon_match, max-candidate refusal, and no-candidate behavior.
- Candidate filtering avoids full output cross-product in normal fixture cases but remains deterministic when filters are absent.
- The graph is ephemeral and no graph state is written to the registry or disk.

Target files:
- src/resolve/graph.rs
- src/resolve/types.rs if needed
- tests/fixtures/resolve/** only if fixture adjustments are needed

Reservation guidance:
- Reserve only graph/candidate files and exact fixture files touched.

title: [CANON-V1/P02.5] Execute project DAGs with content-addressed resumability
description:
## Background
Large identity runs will be interrupted, rerun, and extended. A monolithic all-or-nothing command wastes compute and makes partial state opaque.

## Technical Approach
Implement a deterministic runner that executes ready DAG nodes, commits each artifact atomically, records a hash-linked receipt, and resumes only when all declared inputs and tool contracts match. Support bounded parallelism for independent read-only nodes, explicit stage selection, fail-fast or collect-independent-failures policy, and cancellation without corrupting prior results.

## Success Criteria
- Interrupted runs resume from validated artifacts and never repeat a valid completed node.
- Changed inputs invalidate exactly the affected node and descendants.
- Failed/cancelled nodes leave no artifact that can be mistaken for complete.
- Receipts record node hashes, durations, resource observations, outcomes, and next actions without sensitive data.

## Test Plan
Inject failures before, during, and after artifact publication for every node class; restart and compare final bytes with uninterrupted runs; test poisoning, stale tool versions, bounded parallelism, cancellation, and disk-full refusal.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/project/run.rs`
- `src/project/receipt.rs`
- `schemas/canon.project.run.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/project_resume.rs`

## Considerations
Resumability is content validation, not existence checking. Temporary files stay inside the owned work directory and publication is atomic.
close_reason: Completed project DAG runner/resume layer in reserved files. Evidence: rustfmt --edition 2024 --check src/project/run.rs src/project/receipt.rs tests/project_resume.rs passed; cargo test --test project_resume --test project_plan passed (18 tests); cargo clippy --test project_resume --test project_plan -- -D warnings with command-line allowances for pre-existing unreserved src/project/plan.rs warnings passed. Repo-level blockers outside bd-r8sb: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings fails in src/project/plan.rs; cargo test fails tests/canon_v1_contract_inventory.rs on entity/package inventory drift; cargo fmt --check fails many active unreserved entity/inbox/project files.

title: strategy register: operator-attested task champions without proof tooling
description: Implement the lightweight v1 register path: save a script that just worked as an operator-attested strategy champion. The target user flow should stand alone on a new user's machine and require no verify, assess, airlock, fixture suite, NTM, or multi-agent tooling. RESERVATIONS: src/strategy_registry.rs, src/lib.rs.
design:
Behavior: register task-keyed operator-attested entries into the same _strategy/entries.json used by existing champions; require explicit next-version different from registry.json version; require task, skill identity, script path, script-id, language, operator identity, and one-line reason; hash skill and script bytes with BLAKE3; record operator attestation provenance including operator, attested_at, reason, script content hash, and attestation hash; allow explicit attested_at if the spec adopts it for deterministic tests, defaulting to current UTC only for live CLI; refuse duplicate active key registration and point users to update or deprecate.

Successful register emits a receipt with registry id, before/after version, before/after registry hash, typed key, grade/status, script metadata, source file/entry order, and next suggested commands. It must provide the data needed by the witness parity bead without forcing resolve/list/explain to mutate state.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: task-keyed operator-attested register succeeds without --verify, --assess, or --airlock; registry.json version and entry_count update exactly once; _strategy/entries.json remains pretty-printed deterministic JSON with entry_schema_version; registered entry immediately resolves by task and skill with EXACT; duplicate active register refuses with next_command; success JSON includes a deterministic mutation receipt; existing proof-attested schema register remains supported and proof-gated.

title: [CANON-V1/P04.4] Attach usage and blast-radius context to unresolved groups
description:
## Background
Occurrence count alone is a poor prioritizer. One missing identity used across many critical records and downstream models may matter more than a noisy high-frequency free-text label.

## Technical Approach
Define a content-addressed usage-context artifact derived from project manifests, typed field/assignment roles, exact-lookup/apply lineage, dbt/search consumers, source criticality, exposure or row-count bands, and downstream dependency counts. Join context through hashes/privacy-safe keys and make weights explicit policy inputs.

## Success Criteria
- Impact inputs trace to declared projects/artifacts rather than anecdotes.
- Missing or sensitive values are unknown/banded, never silently zero.
- The model distinguishes frequency, unique projects/subjects, critical roles, downstream consumers, and change blast radius.
- Recomputation is deterministic and does not mutate inbox evidence.

## Test Plan
Build neutral fixtures where frequency and business impact disagree; test missing lineage, redacted measures, duplicated projects, stale references, and policy changes; verify joins and contribution breakdowns.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/inbox/context.rs`
- `schemas/canon.usage_context.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/inbox_context.rs`

## Considerations
Impact is decision support, not an automatic merge threshold. Operator priorities remain explicit and external.

title: canon geo: entity-grain re-score of the labeled set + abstention-loop arithmetic (L.5 measurement)
description:
L.5 made two doctrine corrections binding: (1) abstention on wrong-location input triggers re-geocode-and-retry; (2) answers are scored at ENTITY grain, not ledger grain — a BBL is an alias projection, and the right building/parcel is a valid answer when the unit-BBL form is unavailable.

TASK: re-score the Gate V2 labeled set (233 PIP-covered: 154/79, rebuild from GROUNDTRUTH_ACRIS_BD179B.md CTEs) at entity grain, and compute the abstention-loop arithmetic.

M1 — ENTITY-GRAIN RE-SCORE. For each of the 79 ledger-grain failures, determine whether the PIP answer is entity-correct at (a) parcel grain and (b) building grain: the condo class (32) is entity-correct when the PIP parcel physically contains/matches the true property (E1 measured distance 0.00m — verify per-point with a structured predicate, e.g. ACRIS truth block equals PIP block, or true condo billing-lot relationship, or containment of the property point in the PIP parcel with truth-borough/block agreement — record the exact predicate as the entity-match definition). Report the corrected precision table: ledger-grain (154/233 known) vs parcel-grain vs building-grain, ALL and per E1 class. Classes must reconcile with E1's partition.
M2 — ABSTENTION ARITHMETIC. Compute precision-on-answered under the policy: abstain-for-retry on the E1 gross class (40) — i.e., answered = 233 - 40, correct = entity-grain correct among answered. Report with and without the 3 contamination suspects excluded. This is the honest projection of the plan's operating point, no new capability assumed beyond the two L.5 doctrines.
M3 — RETRY-LOOP CEILING (bounded probe): for the 40 gross points, does the CMBS record carry any alternate geocode rows (other sources/asof) whose point lands in a different tile? Report how many of the 40 have at least one alternate point, and of those, how many alternates PIP into a lot whose block matches ACRIS truth. That bounds the recoverable fraction of the abstain-then-re-geocode loop from data already landed. Do not call any external geocoder.

DISCIPLINE: unchanged — structured results only, exact SQL per number, ACRIS may define truth/entity-match but is never a scored evidence channel, partitions reconcile with E1 (40/32/2/2/3). Output docs/geo_design_session/ENTITY_GRAIN_RESCORE.md; bead comments per block; commit only your file; no push; no self-close.

title: canon registry export: first-class provenance-stamped seed materialization (dbt-seed format)
description:
Promote the registry->dbt-seed promotion pattern (proven 2026-07-06 in edgar-elt, cmbs_servicer_alias_map.csv, firms@1.0.12->1.1.17) from a session-driven workbench process to a first-class canon subcommand, e.g.:

  canon registry export --format dbt-seed --namespace <ctx> --out <seed.csv>

Requirements distilled from the edgar-elt promotion:
- Deterministic output: stable row ordering so git diffs of re-exports are meaningful.
- Per-row provenance stamp: registry_version + content hash (drift tripwire), match_source (canon / registry_exact / registry_brand).
- Context/namespace filtering is FIRST-CLASS, not optional: full-registry export is what produced CRM false merges (NEWMARK->ORG-006, CRED IQ->ORG-005); the fix was servicer-context-restricted matching. Related: edgar-elt br-2n9x (shared alias namespace false-merge risk).
- Confident-only inclusion; abstentions are excluded so consumers fail closed to NULL.
- Optional scaffolds: companion dbt schema.yml (column docs + not_null tests) and an anti-collapse singular test template (one normalized key -> exactly one canon id).
- dbt coupling stays thin: the format is a conventions-following CSV; no dbt runtime dependency in canon.

Why first-class: canon boundary doctrine is "judgment in the workbench, deterministic SQL downstream; registry crosses into transform tools only as a frozen versioned snapshot." This command IS that boundary, and it is generic to any dbt user with messy entity strings -- a strong OSS adoption surface.

Capture-only bead: no build scheduled.
