title: canon geo: client input contract — the six declared fields and the channel-agreement rule
description:
OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-14 — THE CLIENT INPUT CONTRACT IS SETTLED AT SIX FIELDS.

  geocode (lat/lon)   address   geometry   building size   year built   property type

These are what can reasonably be expected from ANY property source — CMBS Annex A, HUD,
Fannie, Freddie, Ginnie, REIT Schedule III, NAIC Schedule A/B, or a client's own book.
The first three drive geometry. The last three are INDEPENDENT ATTRIBUTE CHANNELS whose
job is to REJECT wrong matches rather than to find right ones. OC-0048 already states the
principle: "The attributes do not FIND the match — geometry does. They REJECT the wrong
one."

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN BEAD: the geo profile's required_fields ARE this contract. bd-3ccc
cannot declare a profile without it, and bd-gs6n cannot design attribute operators
without knowing which attributes are guaranteed. OC-0048's Client input contract section
currently lists only address + geocode + soft disambiguators and does NOT model
client-supplied geometry at all — that document must be amended in the same change.

SUPERSEDES: OC-0048 "Required: address string. Strongly preferred: geocode. Cheap
disambiguators: property type, building size, year built, property name."

== FIELD-BY-FIELD CONTRACT ==

geocode         lat/lon. REQUIRED where available; the accuracy tier MUST be declared if
                the source has one (Geocodio accuracy_type or equivalent). A geocode
                without a declared tier is treated as unknown-tier and cannot be
                auto-accepted, because the interpolated tier behaves completely
                differently from rooftop (OC-0048, Geocode quality is the hinge).
address         Raw string plus parsed components where the source has them. Locale /
                jurisdiction MUST be declarable, because hyphen semantics are
                jurisdiction-dependent (bd-1zph: Queens grid vs range).
geometry        NEW AND NOW FIRST-CLASS. Polygon or multipolygon. Under bring-your-own-
                parcel (bd-2kjx) this is how the client's licensed layer enters. MUST
                declare: CRS, vendor, vintage, and whether the geometry is source-fidelity
                or vendor-simplified. Canon REFUSES rather than assuming defaults.
building size   Square feet or square metres, UNITS DECLARED. Drives size_ratio_within.
year built      Integer year. Drives year_built_within. NOTE the temporal subtlety: a
                large year-built disagreement on an overlapping footprint is evidence of
                REDEVELOPMENT, which is a genuine temporal finding, not a match failure.
property type   Source's own category string plus a declared mapping into a neutral
                category vocabulary. The equivalence table lives in the PROFILE, not core
                (bd-15ba: predicates in core, conventions in profiles).

== HARD REQUIREMENTS ==

1. EVERY FIELD IS DECLARABLE AS ABSENT, AND ABSENCE IS NOT FAILURE. Ginnie's native key
   is a pool number with NO ADDRESS FIELD AT ALL. Annex A carries `Various` addresses that
   never geocoded. PROPERTY_MART.PROPERTY_DIM is 51% geocoded. A contract that requires
   all six fields excludes half the estate. Model each field as
   present / absent / present-but-unreliable, and make the cascade's behaviour a function
   of WHICH channels are available.
2. CHANNEL AGREEMENT, NOT CHANNEL SUM. The trustworthiness argument in bd-1zph — require
   geometry and address to AGREE or abstain — generalizes to all six. Define the agreement
   rule explicitly: which channels are independent, how many must agree for each decision
   band, and what happens when an available channel DISAGREES (that is a stronger signal
   than a missing channel and must not be averaged away).
3. UNITS AND TYPES ARE DECLARED, NEVER INFERRED. Square feet vs square metres, and a
   year-built of 0 / 1900 / NULL as sentinel values, are exactly the silent-error surface
   canon's refusal taxonomy exists to prevent.
4. THE CONTRACT IS THE PROFILE. Ship it as a built-in geo profile template
   (`canon entity profile init` equivalent for geo) so a client can generate a conforming
   file rather than reading prose. NOTE: canon currently ships only two built-in profiles
   (cmbs_tenant_label, regab_firm_identity) and `--profile <path>` file loading is
   VERIFIED WORKING, so this is a template plus a validator, not new plumbing.

== NOTE ON A CANON GAP THIS EXPOSES ==
canon has NO numeric evidence operator today. src/entity/record_link.rs:153 types features
as Numeric|Date|Categorical but SUPPORTED_SUPPORT_OPS (src/entity/profile.rs:855) is
exact_view / token_overlap / string_similarity / tfidf_cosine / alias_patch_match /
reviewed_alias — all textual. building size and year built therefore require NEW numeric
comparison operators, not just a profile entry. Scoped in bd-gs6n.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- Written six-field contract with per-field presence/absence/unreliable semantics
- A built-in geo profile template a client can generate and validate
- Declared units, CRS, locale, and category-mapping requirements with refusals for each
  missing declaration
- An explicit channel-agreement rule with decision bands
- OC-0048's Client input contract section amended to match
- Conformance fixtures: one fully-populated source, one address-only source, one
  geometry-only source, one Ginnie-shaped source with neither address nor geocode
close_reason: Client input contract landed: the six declared fields with unit/measure/value-origin/conversion compatibility, wired through capabilities and composition request schemas. geo_client_input_contract 7 passed, geo_composition and geo_cli green. Commit fbe8757.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
REFINEMENT 2026-08-14 — SIZE AND TYPE PLAY A DIFFERENT ROLE IN EACH SOLVE MODE, AND THE
MEASURE MUST BE DECLARED.

1. THE DUAL ROLE. This bead frames all three attribute channels as rejectors: "The
   attributes do not FIND the match — geometry does. They REJECT the wrong one." That is
   true in PAIRWISE mode and INCOMPLETE for assemblage mode (see the assemblage bead).

   PAIRWISE:    building size is a REJECTION FILTER. A 12,000 SF building is not a
                340,000 SF building.
   ASSEMBLAGE:  building size is an ADDITIVE CONSTRAINT OVER A SUBSET. The asserted
                property size must equal the SUM of member building areas within
                tolerance. This is what decides three buildings versus five, and it is a
                far stronger use of the same field.
   Same for property type: pairwise it is a compatibility check; in assemblage it is a
   HARD ELIMINATIVE FILTER applied before enumeration (an office property removes retail
   candidates outright), which is what collapses the combinatorics.

   Record both roles in the contract so an implementer does not build only the rejector.

2. THE SIZE MEASURE MUST BE DECLARED, AND THE MISMATCH IS SYSTEMATIC, NOT NOISE. CMBS
   building size is frequently NRA (net rentable area). PLUTO's BldgArea is gross. That is
   a structural 10-20% gap IN A KNOWN DIRECTION. A symmetric tolerance band will either
   reject correct assemblages or accept wrong ones, and at the subset level the error
   COMPOUNDS across members.
   REQUIRED: `building size` declares its MEASURE (nra | gsf | bldgarea | unknown), not
   just its units. Canon refuses to run a subset-sum across sources whose measures are
   undeclared or known-incompatible without a declared conversion posture. `unknown` is a
   legitimate declaration and must degrade to a wider band with the widening recorded,
   never silently.

3. ASYMMETRIC EVIDENCE — THIS IS WHAT WE CONTRIBUTE. In assemblage mode the client asserts
   the property's total size; OUR TILE supplies the per-lot building areas that have to sum
   to it. That asymmetry is the product: they bring the assertion, we bring the
   observations that constrain it. Worth stating explicitly because it is the clearest
   articulation of why the tile has value beyond geometry.

4. YEAR BUILT HAS THE SAME DUAL SHAPE. Pairwise it rejects. In assemblage a WIDE SPREAD of
   year-built across candidate members is evidence FOR an assemblage (older lots built over
   at different times), not against it. Do not let the pairwise rejector logic leak into
   the subset scorer with its sign flipped.

comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-14 — THE "51% GEOCODED" FIGURE IS WRONG. I cited it repeatedly this
session, including in this bead. Operator questioned it and was right.

WHAT I REPEATED, sourced from OC-0048: "PROPERTY_MART.PROPERTY_DIM holds 50,593 rows with
only 25,884 geocoded (51%) ... that is a hard coverage ceiling."

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MEASURED (edgar-elt br-ppnr, 2026-07-23, against
WRGL_EDGAR_CRE_PROPERTIES__DEDUPED, applying the br-351x identity normalization and the
committed placeholder seed list):
    total_distinct_properties   38,365
    placeholder_excluded         4,245   DEFEASED, VARIOUS, -, N/A, NA, UNKNOWN
    geocodable_denominator      34,120
    geocoded                    33,219
    COVERAGE                    97.36%   of geocodable

THE REAL REMAINING GAP IS ABOUT 901 PROPERTIES, NOT ~24,700.

WHY THE FIGURES DIVERGE. The 51% number counts a denominator that includes addresses which
CAN NEVER GEOCODE -- defeased and placeholder entries whose address field is blank or
literal "VARIOUS". Excluding them is not generosity; it is the same denominator definition
br-1ni6's geo_coverage_pct uses, pinned to the same normalization macros so the two cannot
drift. A coverage rate computed over ungeocodable rows is not a coverage rate.
The 50,593 row count is also a different grain from 38,365 distinct properties, so the two
statements were never comparable to begin with.

WHAT THIS CHANGES IN THIS BEAD AND ACROSS THE EPIC:
1. GEOCODE COVERAGE IS NOT THE BINDING CONSTRAINT ON THE PROPERTY BOOK. I described it as a
   ceiling that "binds before canon geo does any work." At 97.36% of geocodable it does not.
   Strike that framing wherever it appears.
2. WHAT REMAINS A REAL LIMIT, UNCHANGED:
   - `Various` addresses genuinely never geocoded, and there are 4,245 placeholder identities.
     They still need the Annex A parse (edgar-elt br-6iii), not geometry, and they are still
     excluded-and-counted per OC-0048's denominator-honesty criterion.
   - Ginnie Mae still has no address field at its native pool grain.
   - The AGENCY tables are a separate and much larger population that is genuinely NOT
     geocoded yet -- cmdrvl-curves bd-25xz covers roughly 90,000 records (15,579 Ginnie
     street addresses plus 74,349 HUD FHA multifamily at city/state/zip). THAT is the real
     coverage gap for the agency corpora, and it is ON HOLD (bd-13mx).
3. bd-14hu's argument IMPROVES. Pre-resolving our own corpora looked weaker when half the
   property book appeared ungeocoded. At 97.36% the CMBS side is effectively ready to
   pre-resolve now, and the work concentrates on the agency tables rather than on backfill.

MEASURED GEOCODE HISTORY, for anyone sizing this work (2026-08-14, literal query):
WRGL_EDGAR_CMBS_GEOCODES__STRUCTURED -- 68,603 rows, 54,690 distinct PROPERTY_ADDRESS,
4,149 addresses appearing under more than one ASOF because the ETL appends rather than
upserts. Dominated by the 2025-01 initial load (45,114 rows) and an unexplained 2026-08
batch (14,714 rows / 14,242 distinct).

PROCESS NOTE: this is the fourth claim this session that came from prose rather than a
measured value, and the third that was wrong. The 51% figure was in a document I trusted;
the 97.36% figure was in a bead comment recording an actual query. WHEN TWO NUMBERS
DISAGREE, PREFER THE ONE WITH A RECORDED METHOD AND A DENOMINATOR DEFINITION.

title: [CANON-V1/P13.3] Deferred kit-builder sidecar for reviewed pack scaffolding
description:
## Background
After at least two hand-built packs and the neutral/non-finance portability proof establish the package shape, explore an agent-drivable sidecar that helps operators author another pack. This is an adoption aid, not an authority or a prerequisite for Canon v1.

## Scope
- Inspect user-supplied schemas and samples.
- Suggest entity surfaces, roles, mappings, normalization views, protected features, blocking rules, evidence-policy skeletons, and candidate review pairs.
- Emit a reviewable out-of-tree scaffold matching the proven pack contract.
- Exclude unattended gold-label creation, trusted-policy authoring, registry writes, automatic promotion, source ingestion, and core changes.

## Technical approach
Use the hand-built packs only as structural examples, never as a source of assumed domain truth. Every inferred rule carries its evidence, uncertainty, and origin. Generated corpus items are unlabeled review candidates until a human adjudicates them. Training or prompt context must exclude sealed evaluation holdouts. Output is deterministic where practical and produces a manifest-level diff suitable for code review.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A new operator can scaffold a valid package without granting the sidecar registry authority.
- Every generated semantic choice is visibly marked proposed until confirmed.
- Re-running on identical inputs is reproducible or records the exact nondeterministic provenance.
- The scaffold passes package schema and static validation but cannot publish or promote itself.
- Holdout data is demonstrably absent from inference and suggestion inputs.

## Test plan
- Golden scaffold snapshots for at least three contrasting schemas.
- Negative tests proving no automatic labels, policy trust, registry writes, or package publication.
- Repeatability and provenance tests.
- Human review exercise measuring accepted, rejected, and edited suggestions.
- Leakage audit against sealed fixtures.

## File and reservation boundaries
Build as a separate sidecar or tool that emits pack files. Reserve exact sidecar and fixture files. No implementation belongs in core entity-resolution crates.

## Considerations
The sidecar may accelerate boilerplate while being confidently wrong about semantics. Its product contract is inspectable suggestion, not correctness by generation.

title: [CANON-V1/P08.1] Specify registry and strategy OCI artifact media types
description:
## Background
Content-addressed registries and strategies become accretive when they can be named, verified, cached, and promoted through standard artifact infrastructure rather than copied as mutable directories.

## Technical Approach
Define OCI artifact manifests/media types for registry packages, strategy packages, fact packages, domain-extension packages, review/promotion attestations, and optional export projections. Specify layer ordering, annotations, subject/referrer relationships, platform independence, digest semantics, semantic version tags, and a local OCI-layout representation.

## Success Criteria
- The canonical package digest and OCI manifest relationship is explicit and verifiable.
- All package kinds retain their own schema/media type while sharing distribution mechanics.
- Attestations and signatures refer to immutable subjects instead of being embedded circularly.
- Unknown extension layers can be preserved but cannot bypass semantic verify.

## Test Plan
Golden-test manifests/layouts, reordered layers, duplicate/missing layers, wrong media types, annotation changes, unknown extensions, and digest tampering against an independent OCI parser where practical.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/distribution/oci.rs`
- `docs/OCI_ARTIFACTS.md`
- `tests/oci_contract.rs`

## Considerations
OCI is transport and discovery, not the source of truth for registry semantics.

title: [SPLINK-STEAL/S11] entity score-pair: on-demand two-record scoring under a strategy
description:
## Problem this solves Triaging one escrow item or iterating on a strategy currently requires a full workbench run to see how two specific records score. A bounded primitive that scores exactly two records under a strategy — evidence hits, banded verdict, decomposition — makes strategy iteration and agent-driven spot checks cheap during the BDC/CMBS grind (e.g. "would these two tenant rows merge under the current thresholds?" answered in milliseconds). ## Build canon entity score-pair --left --right --profile

--strategy [--registry

] [--emit json|summary] - Runs prepare + evidence for exactly the two records; emits the pair evidence artifact, an advisory banded verdict (would-merge / would-attach / would-escrow / below-floor at the strategy thresholds), and the additive decomposition (S7 format if landed; inline otherwise). - No work-dir mutation. Witness behavior decided in implementation against the ambient witness parity rules (AGENTS.md invariant 8) — either append like other commands or document a read-only exemption; do not improvise. ## Splink reference (clone at /Users/zac/Source/opensource/splink) - splink/internals/realtime.py — compare_records (:44): linker-free two-record scoring with SQL cache; the ergonomic target - splink/internals/linker_components/inference.py — score_pair (:746): intermediate columns retained for waterfall explanation ## How to test - Parity property: for a pair drawn from an existing fixture corpus, score-pair reproduces exactly the evidence scores the full pipeline recorded for that same pair (byte-equal evidence hits). - Verdict banding matches solver behavior on the same fixture (a would-merge pair actually merges in the full run). - Determinism replay. - Malformed record / profile-shape mismatch -> typed refusal, exit 2. - Registry-optional: works without --registry (no registry_alias evidence) and with it (alias evidence included), both deterministic. ## Doctrine constraints Advisory only — the verdict is a banding of a hypothetical pair, grants no decision or promotion authority, writes nothing. title: [CANON-V1/P11.3] Replace virtual scale claims with real end-to-end benchmark tiers
description:
## Background
A 500k virtual probe or direct function benchmark does not prove that the installed CLI can ingest, index, match, write artifacts, resume, and export a real dataset within bounded resources.

## Technical Approach
Define reproducible small/medium/large benchmark generators and manifests, including at least 500k actual observations, skewed buckets, multi-source links, repeated aliases, sparse anchors, hard negatives, unresolved items, and exports. Run the installed binary through full project lifecycles and record cold/warm wall time, peak RSS, CPU, I/O, artifacts, cache reuse, and correctness samples.

## Success Criteria
- Published scale numbers come from complete real subprocess work, not extrapolation.
- Benchmarks validate output counts/hashes and query final artifacts, not only process exit.
- Resource budgets fail safely before memory/disk explosion and resume is measured after interruption.
- Hardware, build flags, corpus seed/version, commands, and raw results accompany every claim.

## Test Plan
Run tiers cold/warm, shuffled, low-memory, disk-constrained, interrupted/resumed, and default/minimal features where relevant. Repeat enough to report variance without hiding outliers.

## RESERVATIONS
- `benches/project_scale.rs`
- `tests/scale_end_to_end.rs`
- `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`

## Considerations
Synthetic benchmarks establish system performance. Do not infer domain accuracy from them.

title: canon geo next evidence — residual-aware reach repair, conflict diagnosis, and costed model separation
description:
WHY

Accretive evidence does not mean indiscriminately adding sources. The agent needs to know which available observation can repair reach, diagnose contradiction, separate the present residual, or raise the requested claim class at the lowest declared cost.

DELIVER

Add residual-aware recommendations to inspect --recommend-next. Candidate actions come from the regional inventory and profile and are classified as REPAIR_REACH, DIAGNOSE_CONFLICT, SEPARATE_RESIDUAL, RAISE_CLAIM_CLASS, or STOP.

For non-empty residuals, a prospective observation partitions the current model set by possible outcomes. Report counterfactual partition sizes, worst-case remaining models, redundancy with current constraints/lineage, deterministic acquisition/materialization/solve cost, and dominance relationships.

Without calibrated outcome probabilities, do not report expected value of information. With a versioned calibration and caller-supplied loss model, any expectation is explicitly named and remains separate from monetary value. Source count, vendor diversity, and nominal novelty do not become utility.

ACCEPTANCE

- Reach failure recommends reach repair before residual separation.
- Empty residual recommends evidence/source diagnosis from a deterministic conflict explanation before adding unrelated sources.
- Duplicate or logically redundant evidence has zero incremental model separation.
- Two records with shared lineage are not counted as independent outcomes.
- Dominated actions are marked, with the declared policy determining ordering rather than hidden heuristics.
- STOP is valid when the requested claim is forced, affordable actions are redundant, the grain is unsupported, ambiguity is irreducible under admitted evidence, or budget is exhausted.
- Negative test: absent probabilities cannot produce a field or prose claim named expected VoI.
- Recommendations never acquire data or mutate the run; each emits an exact bounded acquisition/continuation action.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text: POLICY BOUNDARY 2026-08-31: recommendation ranking is only globally optimal relative to an explicit versioned caller decision/loss policy. Without one, emit the nondominated frontier plus counterfactual separation/cost facts. No policy may authorize unsound hard admission, call an inexact residual exact, or trade precision away for coverage.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text: EXACTNESS BOUNDARY 2026-08-31: a prospective observation must declare an exhaustive outcome domain and the rho induced by each outcome. Exact counterfactual separation/ranking requires an exact current residual and exact outcome partitions. Saturated counts, sampled/materialized subsets, partial backbones, or budget fallback may emit labeled bounds/diagnostics only and must not masquerade as exact model separation.

title: [CANON-V1/P12.11] Execute no-theatre empirical resolution acceptance on sealed holdouts
description:
## Background
The project must not declare entity resolution complete because the architecture is elegant, tests are numerous, exact mappings replay, or an in-repository demo passes. Release acceptance must exercise the installed public product against hidden non-exact truth and make failures visible without post-hoc threshold tuning.

## Technical Approach
Run a clean-room acceptance campaign over a neutral public corpus and at least one demanding out-of-tree operator corpus when available. Seal label and split digests before the release candidate is built. Exercise withheld-alias incumbent attachment, novel clustering, directional linking, related-but-distinct hard negatives, contradictory evidence, and genuine unresolved cases. Execute exact-first lookup separately and exclude it from discovery scores. Capture candidate and union recall, rank distributions, evidence ablations, calibrated outcome bands, pairwise and cluster quality, severe-error slices, review burden, sequential accretion, wall time, peak memory, disk use, and filesystem mutations. Use only installed public commands, released schemas, declared extension packages, and immutable registry artifacts.

## Success Criteria
- Every P12.1 gate passes on sealed holdouts without changing labels, exclusions, or thresholds after reveal.
- Candidate retrieval meets its gate independently of solver and policy metrics.
- There are zero observed severity-critical false merges and every labeled case is accounted for.
- Exact-known rows are visible as an operational baseline but contribute zero weight to discovery scores.
- Sequential evaluation proves that reviewed knowledge becomes exact future coverage with reproducible snapshots.
- The out-of-tree migration reproduces its declared downstream outputs and records rollback artifacts.
- The acceptance bundle includes commands, executable version, source revision, package and registry digests, corpus manifests, split and label hashes, raw machine reports, environment, hardware, resource telemetry, and failure inventory.
- Any failed gate leaves the release epic open and creates a stage-specific remediation bead; narrative waivers alone cannot close acceptance.

## Test Plan
Perform independent cold and warm runs, shuffled input order, duplicate-row inflation attacks, no-network execution, read-only inputs, missing and tampered packages, stale registry, interruption, and replay from the captured bundle. Have a second operator reproduce summary metrics solely from raw artifacts and pinned commands.

## RESERVATIONS
- scripts/run_release_acceptance.sh
- tests/entity_release_acceptance.rs
- tests/fixtures/canon_v1/quality/acceptance_manifest.json
- docs/ENTITY_EVALS_AND_PERFORMANCE.md
- docs/ACCEPTANCE.md

## Considerations
A small honest failing benchmark is more valuable than a large exact-replay victory. Corpus labels may remain private, but manifests, methods, hashes, aggregate metrics, and failure accounting must be auditable.
notes:
## Cross-repository acceptance
sec10d bd-3t7 supplies real candidate-recall evidence, bd-16d supplies calibrated same-firm and hard-negative evidence, bd-1a4 supplies time-forward accretion evidence, and bd-u7e is the consumer cutover gate. Canon acceptance must ingest their signed manifests or record an explicit unavailable-corpus condition; exact-only sec10d replay is not evidence of non-exact discovery.

title: [CANON-V1/P07.8] Prove native entity resolution as the complete default path
description:
## Background
Before external matcher adapters are considered, Canon's own engine must provide a coherent end-to-end workflow for exact-existing matches, new clusters, cross-source links, abstention, review, promotion, and replay.

## Technical Approach
Create a neutral subprocess acceptance project exercising cluster, two-source link, N-source link, trusted anchors, support/anti-merge/context evidence, related-distinct facts, temporal inputs, review, audit, promotion, exact replay, inbox capture, and dbt/search export. Use only native features and generic extension packages.

## Success Criteria
- Every advertised native stage and lifecycle command executes through the public binary.
- Accepted knowledge resolves exactly on replay while ambiguous and related-distinct cases remain safe.
- All artifacts share one contract/provenance chain and verify offline.
- The journey succeeds with all optional adapter features absent from the build.

## Test Plan
Run clean, shuffled, interrupted/resumed, read-only, package-tampered, and resource-refusal journeys. Record commands, stdout/stderr, exit codes, hashes, metrics, and filesystem deltas.

## RESERVATIONS
- `tests/native_entity_end_to_end.rs`
- `tests/fixtures/extensions/neutral-entity-project`
- `README.md`

## Considerations
This bead is the adapter gate: adapter work stays blocked until this native acceptance is green.

Attach or comment the exact executable commands, Canon/build and dependency versions, fixture or corpus digests, environment/platform, stdout/stderr locations, exit codes, artifact/package hashes, elapsed time and peak resource observations where relevant, pre/post filesystem inventories, semantic assertions, and every failure/refusal encountered. A green test name or prose summary alone is not completion evidence.

title: [CANON-V1/P02.6] Make review, promotion, apply, and export a project state machine
description:
## Background
Evidence computation, human decisions, registry mutation, exact replay, and export currently feel like unrelated commands. The project should make their order and authorization visible without automating away judgment.

## Technical Approach
Define explicit project states and transitions from planned through evidence-ready, review-required, audited, promotable, promoted, replay-verified, and exported. Bind review bundles and promotion receipts to the plan/run hashes. Add `project status`, `review`, `promote`, `apply`, and `export` orchestration that delegates to the single entity and registry contracts and refuses stale or skipped gates.

## Success Criteria
- Every project reports one state, blockers, completed receipts, and exact next commands.
- Promotion cannot consume a review or audit from a different run, registry snapshot, policy, or strategy.
- Apply and exports are reproducible descendants of a promoted registry digest.
- Mutation commands enumerate intended paths and version changes before requiring explicit execution.

## Test Plan
Walk happy, abstention-heavy, rejected-review, stale-review, registry-race, partial-export, and recovery scenarios as subprocess journeys. Verify each illegal transition refuses with zero mutation and a useful remediation.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/project/state.rs`
- `src/project/lifecycle.rs`
- `tests/project_lifecycle.rs`

## Considerations
The state machine coordinates existing authoritative operations; it must not create a second implementation of review, promotion, lookup, or export.

title: [CANON-V1/P12] Empirical same-entity discovery quality and migration proof
description:
## Background
Canon has unusually strong architecture for deterministic artifacts, evidence, abstention, review, promotion, and exact replay. That architecture is necessary but insufficient: the product earns its keep only if it can actually discover that differently rendered observations refer to the same entity while refusing unsafe parent, subsidiary, division, successor, and lookalike collapses. Existing sec10d evidence is dominated by 127,991 rows over only 46 already-reviewed exact surfaces, so it proves replay and row preservation rather than non-exact discovery.

## Scope
Make empirical entity-equivalence quality a release-blocking lane. Separate exact-known replay from withheld-alias recovery, novel-entity clustering, cross-source linkage, related-but-distinct classification, and abstention. Build leakage-resistant corpora, candidate-recall diagnostics, counterfactual and time-forward benchmarks, evidence ablations, cost-sensitive decision gates, sequential accretion proof, domain-extraction parity, and a downstream migration protocol. Canon remains domain-neutral; real structured-finance labels, profiles, sources, and registries stay in an external operator-owned package.

## Success Criteria
- Candidate generation demonstrably retrieves true same-entity pairs before solver scoring.
- Hidden holdouts prove high-precision same-entity decisions, useful recall, safe abstention, and zero observed severity-critical false merges.
- Exact-known rows cannot inflate discovery metrics.
- Repeated projects turn reviewed decisions into exact future coverage without regression.
- Current domain-specialized behavior can leave Canon core without reducing measured quality.
- A real external consumer can migrate through public contracts and reproduce exact downstream outputs.

## Test Plan
Run public-binary evaluations over neutral public corpora and an optional operator-owned real corpus; seal holdout labels before tuning; execute shuffled, cold/warm, read-only, stale, tampered, and interrupted variants; log commands, versions, corpus and artifact hashes, stage metrics, error slices, wall time, peak memory, and filesystem mutations.

## Considerations
A correct abstention is better than a confident false merge. Name similarity alone is never proof when the available evidence is ambiguous. This epic adds empirical proof and controlled improvement work, not domain dictionaries or thresholds to Canon core.
notes:
## Cross-repository execution
The first demanding out-of-tree consumer is sec10d epic bd-u79 in /Users/zac/Source/cmdrvl/sec10d. Beads cannot encode blocking edges across repository databases, so the sec10d child descriptions carry Canon external refs and the release operators must verify both graphs. sec10d candidate retrieval bd-3t7 maps to P12.3; decision quality bd-16d maps to P12.6/P12.7; package bd-26s maps to P12.9; migration bd-2az and conformance bd-14w map to P12.10; cutover bd-u7e maps to P12.11.

## Deferred option lane
P09 is a post-v1 decision space and depends on bd-2i2q. Dedupe, Splink, OpenRefine reconciliation interoperability, a cmdrvl-tabfm-style Rust port, active learning, and email or other review delivery are all optional possibilities. None blocks the P00-P12 architecture, native quality acceptance, sec10d migration, or release. Any selected option must emit the same typed evidence, obey the same decision and promotion authority boundaries, and earn adoption through measured lift on sealed corpora.

title: [CANON-V1/P09.5] Deferred evaluation harness for a selected optional technique
description:
## Background
Native ports and external adapters should not be adopted because their underlying algorithms sound useful. A future option earns maintenance only through reproducible lift over the accepted native baseline.

## Technical Approach
After core acceptance and after one concrete option is selected, reuse the P12 sealed-corpus, candidate-recall, evidence-ablation, calibration, hard-negative, review-cost, and resource methodology. Compare the exact accepted native baseline against baseline plus the option. Keep candidate retrieval, scoring, policy, and promotion metrics separate. Bind every report to corpus/split, source or tool, model, feature, configuration, binary, policy, and registry digests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- No evaluation requires implementing every option; one selected option is evaluated at a time.
- Exact replay cannot inflate non-exact lift.
- Candidate recall, severe false merges, calibrated precision/recall, abstention, review burden, runtime, memory, and determinism are all reported.
- The option is rejected or remains experimental if lift is absent, unstable, unsafe, or not worth maintenance.
- Optional evidence never grants direct promotion authority.

## Test Plan
Run planted helpful, neutral, harmful, leakage, nondeterministic, malformed, and resource-exhausting options; verify accounting and rejection gates. Reproduce the report from raw pinned artifacts.

## RESERVATIONS
No implementation files while deferred. Reuse the future P12 evaluation interfaces rather than create a parallel scorecard.

## Considerations
Closed concrete adapter beads are historical decisions and are not dependencies of this generic future evaluation.

comments.author: HazyFalcon
comments.text:
## Shortest post-convergence BDC proof chain

Accepted model to enforce:
- Issuer is the Canon identity. The issuer registry contains accepted issuer aliases only.
- Instrument/facility/tranche is a typed assignment fact on an issuer observation, with filer/holder subject, as-of interval, source locator, and payload fields such as lien, rate, maturity, FV, cost, and par.
- Filing prose to FIGI is an out-of-tree crosswalk to an existing instrument/tranche identifier. It is not a second Canon issuer identity registry and must not write issuer aliases.

Dependency-ordered viable set:
1. Already closed generic contracts: bd-kkh5 requirements, bd-3hz3 typed normalization views, bd-3bst assignments separate from identity, bd-1092 source mapping, bd-1w3y evidence IR, bd-11ai entity link, bd-21nh candidate recall, bd-1mr6 evidence policy, bd-epmu/bd-cyjb corpus and split contracts.
2. bd-jbpo is the data prerequisite. It supplies paths, digests, schemas, label/proxy-label policy, and the minimal local slice; no private rows are copied into Canon.
3. bd-12px is the first real-data post-convergence proof. It runs on the bd-jbpo slice soon after core convergence. It should not wait on P09/P10/P13. bd-1rlk remains an optional related scorer escalation only; the first proof can use accepted native/simple deterministic scoring if it emits typed evidence and meets gates.
4. bd-doe2 is the pre-release demanding-deployment proof. It exercises the same contracts through a public neutral twin and the private BDC local target, plus source scan and command trace, without Canon awareness of BDC.
5. bd-18zf is the post-core starter pack after bd-2i2q. It packages a BDC issuer-resolution pack/corpus outside core; it is not a prerequisite for bd-12px and should consume, not block, the first proof evidence.

Canonical artifact layout, rooted outside Canon for private data:
- `work/bdc-proof/<slice-id>/source_manifest.json` from bd-jbpo with input paths, row counts, hashes, license/privacy flags.
- `bdc_parse_rows` and `dera_rows` are external/local paths or immutable locators.
- `bdc_source_mapping_profile`, `bdc_identity_strategy`, `issuer_registry`, and `bdc_gold_or_proxy_manifest` are pinned by digest.
- `figi_crosswalk_candidates.jsonl` is optional assignment/crosswalk evidence only.
- Canon outputs: `entity_link.json`, `block/candidates.json`, `block/diagnostics.json`, `candidate_recall.json`, `audit.json`, `review.csv|json`, `promote.json`, `apply.json`, `registry.diff.json`, dbt/search exports.

Exact public command chain, with paths filled from bd-jbpo:
```bash
canon entity link "$BDC_PARSE_ROWS" "$DERA_ROWS" 
  --profile "$BDC_PROFILE" 
  --strategy "$BDC_STRATEGY" 
  --registry "$ISSUER_REGISTRY" 
  --work-dir "$WORKDIR" 
  --suite "$BDC_SUITE" 
  --emit json 
  --no-witness > "$WORKDIR/entity_link.json"

jq -s . "$WORKDIR/block/candidates.jsonl" > "$WORKDIR/block/candidates.json"
jq .diagnostics "$WORKDIR/block/block.json" > "$WORKDIR/block/diagnostics.json"

canon entity candidate-recall 
  --manifest "$BDC_GOLD_OR_PROXY_MANIFEST" 
  --candidates "$WORKDIR/block/candidates.json" 
  --diagnostics "$WORKDIR/block/diagnostics.json" 
  --exact-bucket-count "$EXACT_BUCKET_COUNT" 
  --emit json > "$WORKDIR/candidate_recall.json"

canon entity audit "$WORKDIR/solve/solve.json" 
  --suite "$BDC_SUITE" 
  --emit json > "$WORKDIR/audit.json"

canon entity review export "$WORKDIR/solve/solve.json" 
  --include all 
  --emit csv > "$WORKDIR/review.csv"

canon entity review import "$WORKDIR/review.csv" 
  --registry "$ISSUER_REGISTRY" 
  --next-version "$NEXT_VERSION" 
  --audit "$WORKDIR/audit.json" 
  --emit json > "$WORKDIR/review_import.json"

canon entity promote "$WORKDIR/solve/solve.json" 
  --audit "$WORKDIR/audit.json" 
  --registry "$ISSUER_REGISTRY" 
  --next-version "$NEXT_VERSION" 
  --emit json > "$WORKDIR/promote.json"

canon entity apply "$WORKDIR/solve/solve.json" 
  --rows "$BDC_PARSE_ROWS" 
  --registry "$ISSUER_REGISTRY" 
  --column "$ISSUER_SURFACE_COLUMN" 
  --out "$WORKDIR/bdc_parse_rows.canon.csv" 
  --allow-partial-output 
  --emit json > "$WORKDIR/apply.json"

canon registry diff 
  --old "$ISSUER_REGISTRY_BEFORE" 
  --new "$ISSUER_REGISTRY" 
  --emit json > "$WORKDIR/registry.diff.json"
```

Pre-release bd-doe2 adds the domain-neutrality/source gate and reruns equivalent commands on the public neutral twin:
```bash
rg -n "BDC|business development|SOI|DERA|portfolio company|tranche|BDC issuer" 
  src schemas tests operator.json README.md docs/EXTENSIONS.md docs/IDENTITY_ARCHITECTURE.md 
  > "$WORKDIR/domain_source_scan.txt"
```
Any non-whitelisted hit in core runtime, schema, operator contract, public default, or required docs fails bd-doe2.

Post-core bd-18zf starts only after bd-2i2q and packages the out-of-tree starter pack:
```bash
canon package pack --root "$BDC_PACK_ROOT" --package "$BDC_PACK_ROOT/package.json" --out "$WORKDIR/bdc-issuer-pack.canonpkg"
canon package verify "$WORKDIR/bdc-issuer-pack.canonpkg" --emit json > "$WORKDIR/package.verify.json"
canon package inspect "$WORKDIR/bdc-issuer-pack.canonpkg" --emit json > "$WORKDIR/package.inspect.json"
canon registry export --format dbt-seed --registry "$ISSUER_REGISTRY" --namespace "$BDC_NAMESPACE" --canonical-type "$ISSUER_CANONICAL_TYPE" --out "$WORKDIR/canon_bdc_issuers.csv" --emit json > "$WORKDIR/dbt_export.json"
canon registry export --format search-index --registry "$ISSUER_REGISTRY" --out "$WORKDIR/bdc_issuers.search.sqlite" --emit json > "$WORKDIR/search_export.json"
```

Minimum metrics and failure gates:
- Candidate retrieval: union recall@50 meets the bd-21nh/P12 gate for the sealed/proxy labels; every miss has deterministic forensics and next action.
- R2 assignment separation: two tranche rows for one issuer produce one issuer observation plus N assignment facts; assignment promotion never writes an alias.
- R6 structured linkage: exact FV+cost+par+maturity/rate pseudo-labels or reviewed labels align parse rows to DERA rows with zero critical false merges and no tranche collapse.
- Identity quality: no critical false merges on hard negatives such as same-name/different-entity or Idera-style lookalikes; ambiguous cases abstain or enter review.
- FIGI crosswalk: filing prose may resolve to existing FIGI only as crosswalk/assignment evidence; treating FIGI as issuer identity or writing FIGI-derived issuer aliases fails.
- Temporal/as-of: any rename/alias accretion is intervaled and time-forward; same-quarter or holdout leakage fails.
- Boundary: private data stays out of Canon; BDC vocabulary in core runtime/schema/defaults fails bd-doe2; optional P09 matchers cannot be required to pass the first proof.

No new beads are needed now: bd-jbpo covers data inventory, bd-12px covers the first real-data proof, bd-doe2 covers pre-release demanding deployment, and bd-18zf covers post-core packaging.

title: [CANON-V1/P09.2] Add an optional OpenRefine review interchange adapter
description:
## Background
OpenRefine can offer a familiar tabular reconciliation/review surface, but Canon must remain fully usable without installing or operating it.

## Technical Approach
Implement import/export interchange between canonical review/evidence artifacts and a pinned, documented OpenRefine-compatible format or extension protocol. Preserve stable observation/candidate IDs, provenance, evidence summaries, match/new/distinct/defer actions, and hash bindings. Treat OpenRefine as a review client: it cannot directly write a registry or reinterpret Canon IDs.

## Success Criteria
- A Canon review pack can be reviewed through OpenRefine and imported without information loss for supported actions.
- Round-trip decisions remain bound to the original run, policy, and registry snapshot.
- Unsupported OpenRefine constructs are reported, not silently dropped.
- The adapter is optional and absent from default build/runtime dependencies.

## Test Plan
Use a pinned local test installation or frozen protocol fixtures; round-trip all actions, Unicode/large tables, stale/tampered IDs, unsupported decisions, duplicate imports, and network-disabled operation.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/adapters/openrefine.rs`
- `tests/openrefine_adapter_e2e.rs`
- `docs/ADAPTERS.md`

## Considerations
OpenRefine is best treated as one frontend projection, not an alternate source of canonical truth.
close_reason: Retired: OpenRefine adapter is a review-GUI interchange, not a matcher; Canon builds its own review flywheel. Clustering already native (bd-21nh). Reopen only if an operator insists on the GUI. See decision doc.
